# Groups & Functions

Whether it’s a wedding, corporate event or group function, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island offers an unforgettable setting for your next event.

Image Pinky Beach

Pinky Beach

### A place to reconnect, re-energise and see the world differently

With its rich history, incredible coastal scenes and thriving wildlife, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island offers event and function spaces like no other. A place to breathe in the abundance of space around you and connect to the environment, you leave with a new-found energy that comes from indulging in new experiences.

Whether it’s your dream wedding, corporate event, conference or a team building event, the island offers the facilities, accommodation and dining to make it a truly unforgettable experience.

If you want to make your next school trip a memorable one, give your students an exciting learning experience with a variety of educational tours as well as a surfing clinic operating on the island.

Image Samphire Rottnest

[Samphire Rottnest](/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest)

### Corporate Groups

There are many reasons why visitors come to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island: invigorating adventures in nature, mindful interactions with history, and seaside getaways spent submerged in tranquil waters.

For corporate groups, time spent on Wadjemup is all about experiencing a fresh perspective and the energy that comes from time well spent.

[Find out more about corporate groups](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/groups-functions/corporate-groups)

Image 

[Walking tours](/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours)

### Education groups

A unique learning experience that re-engages students and ignites curiosity away from textbooks, desks, and tests.

Give your students a unique and memorable learning experience that’s all around doing, seeing, experiencing and connecting. Your students can stand in the places where history was made and walk in the wilderness where native flora is regenerating.

The various educational tours and activities on the island are designed to re-engage students and ignite curiosity that they can take back with them.

[Find out more about education groups](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/groups-functions/education-groups)

Image Pinky Beach

[Pinky Beach](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach)

### Weddings

Celebrate your special day at one of Australia’s most beautiful locations.

With its stunning coastal landscapes and picture-perfect views, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island provides the perfect backdrop for your forever memories. There are unique options for both ceremony and reception to suit your style, and bring friends and families together to celebrate love.

[Find out more about weddings](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/groups-functions/weddings)

Image Isola Bar e Cibo, South Thomson Bay

### Events in public spaces

Thinking about holding a special event on Rottnest Island? All events held in public spaces on Rottnest Island require approval from Rottnest Island Authority (RIA). This includes formal gatherings or ceremonies, sporting events and festivals, or public meetings held in a public area within the limits of the island.

For more information about the application process, visit the  [Rottnest Island Authority website](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/permits-and-fees/events).

[Learn more](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/permits-and-fees/events)

# Stay

## Find your home base on the island, a place for launching explorations and decompressing in the glow of a sunset

Staying at Rottnest Island can be a chance to reconnect with nature, have a moment of indulgence, or embark on an invigorating adventure. And, it might be all of this.

Rottnest Island has accommodation options for every kind of person who ventures to the island. The [Stay Rottnest Campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-campground) being a source of stories shared over barbecues and quiet nights in nature, while the simple cosiness of a [Stay Rottnest Self-Contained](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained) unit dissolves mainland stress into island stillness.

Boutique accommodation like [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) or [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) are havens for deep relaxation, rejuvenating after island escapades.

# Little Armstrong Bay

## A gentle cove to relax and reflect

Little Armstrong Bay is one of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s quieter bays. Rocky outcrops on both sides of the bay embrace a short stretch of beach, making it feel all the more secluded. These serve to protect the shallow waters from the southerly and easterly winds, making it a calm, relaxing spot for families with young children.

But while the perfect place to relax and unwind, there’s still plenty of adventure to be had. Excellent [snorkelling conditions](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) can be found further out into the bay, and the [Karlinyah Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/karlinyah-bidi) makes its northwestern pass right by the bay, providing the ideal place to take a break from hiking and enjoy the cooling turquoise water.

### Look around and you’ll find

Image 

Rocky outcrops surrounding the beach

Image 

Snorkel the surrounding coral reefs

Image 

Uncover a rainbow of sea life

Image 

A key stop on the Karlinyah Bidi

### Where to find Little Armstrong Bay

On the northern coast of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, you can get to Little Armstrong Bay by jumping on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and getting off at Stop 17. Alternatively, hop on a [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) and take the 12-minute ride — perfect for drying off after a swim.

Image Little Armstrong Bay, Rottnest Island

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Family-friendly snorkelling

You’ll find Little Armstrong Bay in one of Wadjemup’s five [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones), making it a safe haven for marine life.

With shallower waters, it’s ideal for beginners, with deeper waters further out in the bay welcoming more experienced divers. Diving under the water and swimming out through a maze of seagrass, the natural reef creates a home for an amazing array of colourful and curious fish. And thanks to its protection, you may even come face-to-face with some species of sea life that aren’t found anywhere else along the island’s coastline.

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

Image Little Armstrong Bay, Rottnest Island

Little Armstrong Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

Are any facilities available at Little Armstrong Bay?

Due to its secluded nature, Little Armstrong Bay doesn’t feature any facilities. The closest toilets and showers can be found at Geordie Bay, just a seven-minute bike ride away (or a 30-minute walk if you’re not in a hurry).

What is the best way to get there?

Little Armstrong Bay is just a quick 12-minute bike ride from the main settlement past Geordie Bay, or Stop 17 on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus route.

Can I fish at Little Armstrong Bay?

Little Armstrong Bay is part of the Armstrong Bay Marine Sanctuary Zone, which helps to preserve the exquisite sea life population for generations to come. Shore based fishing is permitted by means of a rod and line or line held in the hand in certain areas which are sign posted. Taking of any marine flora and fauna by all other means here isn’t allowed.

* Your Guide to Surfing Rottnest Island’s Breaks

# Your Guide to Surfing Rottnest Island’s Breaks

All the advice you need to plan a surfing getaway on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

7 minutes

Image Mary Cove, Rottnest Island

Mary Cove, Rottnest Island

**Wadjemup / Rottnest Island isn’t the place for a quick surf, it’s an adventure. An all-encompassing experience that starts with the journey from the mainland. There are hidden, carefully guarded local spots, waves that test your mettle, and epic surf that makes you work for its discovery.**

And when you’re out there, taking a breather and simply floating atop the dappled blueness, looking back towards the silhouette of the island… It’s a new kind of decompression.

### An island of swell from every direction

Although the sweeping beaches of Perth are ideal for a Sunday afternoon of sunbathing and cooling dips, when it comes to surf, they don’t always hold up. Locals will often find themselves heading home early for a victory-less lunch, drowning sorrows of still waters and aching arms. Unreliability is the bane of any surfer. And that’s where you need an island.

Wadjemup’s multiple swell directions and strong conditions create a haven for gold-standard surf. There’s always an area that’s offshore. With the south side producing consistently impressive waves, the north side changing with the seasons, and raw, wild conditions finding their home at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end).

All of the breaks on the island are reef breaks, generating powerful waves that form offshore and carry their riders across the open ocean’s surface, far longer than any beach break.

> There are waves on the island that rival the quality and power of waves down in the South West around Margaret River. — Surfing WA

Image Surfing

[Surfing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing)

Image 

[Checking the surf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing)

Image 

[Surfing a wave at Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing)

### Thrilling rides: waves for the experienced surfers

As a stop on the 2021 World Surf League Championship Tour, Rottnest Island produces surf worthy of world-renowned professionals. It’s not only the intensity of the surf that makes Wadjemup most suited to experienced surfers, but also the remote locations and tiring paddle time, which mean you need to know what you’re doing.

If you’re seeking a challenging wave or a unique experience, then here are some places to hit:

**[Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay):** The spot used for international, national, and state-level surfing events. It’s a thrilling break, with a solid left and even right-handers when the conditions are suitable. As the bay has a reputation, it may be busier than other places.

**Where is it?** Strickland Bay is located on the southern side of the thin bridge of land leading over to [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), making it one of the furthest spots from the settlement. The bus stop is a fair hike away from the bay, 750 metres along a sandy track.

**Stark Bay:** Another place for serious swell. It’s an exposed reef break, offering pretty consistent waves and a quiet, lesser known location.

**Where is it?** Stark Bay is on the opposite side of the island to Strickland, but has a bus stop right at the beach.

**[West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end):** The location of the Rotto Box, a gnarly wave created by a heavy reef break that holds strong swells. Surfers have to be towed into the wave, as it’s not safe to paddle out.

**Where is it?** West End is at the far, opposite end of the island to [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) — even though there’s a bus stop, the surf is only accessible by boat.

### Softer surf: breaks for beginners

Everything that makes Wadjemup an impressive place to surf also makes it risky for new surfers. Most of the breaks on the island are too challenging for beginners, not just because of the waves themselves, but also the isolation of the spots — if inexperienced surfers come unstuck, they’re a long way from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

Luckily, there are a couple of places with softer waves that still pose a challenge, but not a hazardous one. Out towards the western tip of the island, just before [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay), is Mary Cove — a calmer spot with a steady left break, similar to [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay), but a lot more forgiving. Another accessible break is Chicken Reef, which can be found near Salmon Bay. This exposed reef break receives distant groundswells and offshore winds from the north and north-east, and is known for its consistent, clean winter waves. With both locations, check the weather to ensure the surf is accessible for your abilities before heading out.

Image 

Strickland Bay

### Accessing the surf

If you come via [the ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry) and must find your way to the surf breaks by land, then there’s a chance to interact with the beauty of the island wilderness as well as the ocean. Most of the worthwhile breaks require a hike through the bush or shrubland from the nearest bus stop — an opportunity to work up a sweat, observe stunning vistas along the coastline, and take in the surrounding flora.

**Accessible by land:**

* [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay)
* Stark Bay
* Chicken Reef
* Mary Cove
* Fairbridge Bluff

If you’re able to make the trip on a [private boat](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-private-boat), every bay is a possibility. For the breaks further offshore, a boat makes it easy to retain energy and put your full strength into an invigorating ride. The more challenging breaks are opened up to you, and you can easily pop back to [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) for a rest and a feed afterwards.

**Requires a boat:**

* [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end)
* Bullet Reef
* Radar Reef

### Planning your surfing getaway on Wadjemup

#### When to go

Surfing on Wadjemup is predominantly an off-season activity, as it’s during autumn and winter that the largest swells come rolling through. Winter mornings on the island see beautiful, light conditions, with barely a breath of wind. And when you visit Wadjemup during this peak surfing season, it’s quieter too. The wildlife is awake, the bush is vibrant, and you’ll find real peaceful moments.

If it’s possible to stay overnight or visit by boat, then you can arrive at the best time of day for surfing on the island. The rule is: the earlier the better. 6 am is perfect for summer days, but the sun will rise later in the winter, so it’ll be more like 7 or 8 am — that’s when you want to arrive. But don’t start when it’s still dark, it’s not safe to roam the wilderness areas when you can’t see where you’re going!

And if you can only come for a day trip, make sure you’re on that first morning ferry and plan ahead so you know which beach you’re heading for.

### Hiring equipment

Although you can’t hire a surfboard on the island, you can get everything else you need. Just head to [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) for a bike (or electric bike), and surfboard rack.

While you’re shopping, it’s also a good idea to stock up for your day. There aren’t many fresh water sources once you leave the settlement, so bring plenty of bottled water. If it’s summer, you’ll definitely need a hat and sunscreen, and bring a raincoat on any milder days — the weather can change quickly.

### Finding your surf spot

As you know, surfing is about adaptability; the weather is always changing and sometimes you need to plan on-the-go. So, when you get to the island, assess the situation on the day (or the night before). Don’t worry if the winds are onshore wherever you are, as on the other side of the island the conditions will be clean and offshore. Use this understanding — and the knowledge of which surf breaks are within your abilities — to pick your spot.

If you’re unsure what the weather is telling you, then you can always talk to a local. Many of the people who work on the island are surfers, like the rangers, and they know how the island operates. They may guard some local secrets, but are sure to send you in the direction of some solid surf — and away from any dangerous weather.

Image Surfing at Rottnest Island

Rottnest Island Surfing

Image Rottnest Island

Rottnest Island Surfing

Image 

Time for a surf

### Staying overnight

An [overnight stay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) is an opportunity to sink into the island rhythm. So, when you wake, early on the morning of your first surf, the stresses of the mainland have already slipped away.

Staying overnight — whether it’s on a boat or on the island — also means you can easily head to one of the nearby venues for celebratory after-surf pints and hearty pub meals, without any time restrictions from the ferry.

### Waves that bring connection to all that is here

It’s not just the surf itself that makes catching a wave on Wadjemup so special. It’s the craggy headlands and undulating landscape visible around the lip of the wave. And it’s the wildlife — the marine sanctuaries in the waters beneath you, teeming with tropical fish.

> I remember surfing many, many times on Rottnest Island when big schools of dolphins would swim under me or I'd see big schools of fish — Surfing WA.

The isolation of an island surf brings a sense of peace not found on the mainland. Surfing on Wadjemup is a way to connect with the land and the water, and all that is here. While catching some pretty amazing waves too.

**At this relaxed coastal accommodation, the Rottnest Island experience is transferred seamlessly from the outside world into every room.**

The 80 spacious rooms available at Samphire Rottnest have been thoughtfully designed to complement the natural surroundings. Experience understated modern surrounds from the comforts of your room and marvel at the island from your own private balcony or deck.

Venture outside and roam across native landscaping. Here, the stylish poolside cabanas beckon. Take a dip in the pool any time of year, with heated waters in the cooler months and refreshing cool temperatures over summer.

Once you’ve worked up an appetite, go on a food journey through the archipelagos of South East Asia at [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara). Next door you’ll find the iconic [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), offering a relaxed dining experience, or [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) for bespoke cocktails.

Samphire Rottnest is also available for event or conference hire, offering your guests a unique experience and spectacular views.

There are a number of rooms suitable for guests with mobility requirements.

For more information or to make a booking, visit the [Samphire Rottnest website](https://samphirerottnest.com.au/).

Samphire Rottnest is located in South Thomson Bay, just a short walk along the bay from the main jetty.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What time is check-in?

Check-in is available from 3 pm. You can request an early check-in by contacting the Samphire Rottnest reservations team at [reservations@samphirerottnest.com.au](mailto:reservations@samphirerottnest.com.au). Please note that early check-in is subject to availability and cannot be guaranteed.

What time is check-out?

The check-out time is 11 am. You can request a late check-out by contacting the Samphire Rottnest reservation team at [reservations@samphirerottnest.com.au](mailto:reservations@samphirerottnest.com.au). Please note this is subject to availability.

Where can I store my bike?

Samphire Rottnest has dedicated bike racks for guests, located in the courtyard on the south side of the property.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If your ferry to Rottnest Island is cancelled due to weather conditions, Samphire Rottnest can change the date of your booking to within two months of the initial booking. This booking will become non-refundable. If your ferry departing Rottnest Island has been cancelled due to weather conditions, Samphire Rottnest can extend your booking at a 50% discount on the best available rate.

If accommodation at Samphire Rottnest is not available for an extra night, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire if they have availabilities.

# Hiking the Wadjemup Bidi

## Every step tells a story

See the island from a new perspective and reconnect with nature on the Wadjemup Bidi. This incredible series of walk trails take in the spectacular coastal headlands, stunning inland lakes and breathtaking vistas of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Spanning 45 km and threading its way through the island, the Bidi — which means "trail" or "track" in Noongar — is made up of five sections. Each unique stretch displays culturally and environmentally significant landmarks, providing balanced opportunity for historical reflection and celebration of the island’s natural beauty.

Image 

[West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end)

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

### Choose from 5 different trails or do them all

With the entire Wadjemup Bidi covering 45 km, you’ll need to spread your hike over a few days if you want to do the whole thing.

For those wanting to explore at their own pace, the Wadjemup Bidi is made up of five connected trails allowing you to traverse the island in separate stages.

To make your journey even easier, download the  [WA Parks Foundation Smartreka digital maps](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/smartreka-digital-maps)  via the Avenza Maps app before you set off. These GPS-enabled maps let you track your real-time location on your smartphone, helping you stay on course while discovering Wadjemup’s stunning coastal headlands, tranquil lakes, and iconic landmarks.

Once you’ve got your [Smartreka map](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/smartreka-digital-maps) ready — or picked up a printed version from the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/visitor-centre) — and packed plenty of water, all that’s left is to choose your first trail and start exploring.

[Leave No Trace

Please help us to reduce our ecological footprint. Find more information about minimising your impact on the island here.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability)

### Guided walking tours

If you’re not sure where to start or want to learn more about the island whilst you enjoy your scenic walk, let one of the island experts show you a side of Wadjemup you’ve never seen before.

With multiple tours to choose from, including regular day tours right through to overnight retreats, the perfect adventure awaits both hiking enthusiasts and beginners alike.

# Rottnest Island Nursery

The Rottnest Island Nursery is helping to keep the native landscape alive.

Image Leaves

Leaves

### The future of flora

The natural and unique landscape of Rottnest Island is one of the main reasons why so many people come and explore it. But the environment is as delicate as it is beautiful and as tourism grows, so does the risk for native flora.

A lot of foot (and bike) traffic, especially around beach access areas, means that Rottnest Island needs a plan for revegetation. This is where the idea for the Rottnest Island Nursery came from — it’s how we plan for the future of the island’s natural landscape.

Image Rottnest Island scenery and vegetation, Samphire plant.

[Samphire by the salt lakes](/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes)

### The Rottnest Island Nursery

To maintain this unique island ecosystem, there can be up to 40,000 native seedlings propagating in the nursery at any one time, from woodland melaleuca to spinifex and everything in between. And thanks to the team of volunteers, who dedicate 2,500 hours to this project each year, the Rottnest Island Nursery is helping to keep the native landscape alive.

This nursery sets the stage for seed collection, treatment, storage, and propagation of seedlings native to the island; what you can’t see is how this land would have looked in the future without their hours of work.

Interested in volunteering some time to tree planting around Rottnest Island? Visit the Rottnest Island Authority website to find out how you can help.

[Learn more about volunteering](https://ria.wa.gov.au/about-us/volunteering-and-partnership)

Image 

The diverse plant landscape

### Experiencing the island’s flora

The work of the Rottnest Island Nursery can be seen all over the island. There’s samphire around the lakes, spinifex in the dunes at Longreach Bay, tea trees along the bike path between The Basin and Longreach Bay, and saltbush along Parker Point Road.

All of these native flora species have a home here on Rottnest Island and create the awe-inspiring landscape that attracts so many people each and every year.

[Learn more about nature experiences](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature)

# Wildlife Encounters on Wadjemup

The habitats that sprawl across Wadjemup / Rottnest Island are home to a collection of native wildlife species, each one moving naturally through this Class A Reserve.

6 minutes

Image Quokkas

Quokkas

**With 19 km of Indian Ocean between the mainland and Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, native wildlife has found its sanctuary. This island, a Class A Reserve, is a puzzle of six unique ecosystems, each one home to thriving animal, bird, and sea life.**

Some play in familiar surroundings, others cross vast distances to breed new life and sustain their own. Some are seen and not heard or heard but unseen. Some sleep, others roam.

Wadjemup wildlife is, by nature, wild. Your experience of their native refuge spots will be unlike anyone else’s. It’s not ours to control - and that’s the beauty of it.

#### The island’s six wildlife ecosystems

Every corner of Wadjemup is a biodiverse environment, purpose-made by nature for native wildlife. When you venture through each area, it’s as if you have travelled across continents to find yourself surrounded by a whole new landscape.

* Coastal. The limestone landscapes and rare bird species.
* Scrub heath. A bird and reptile respite that carpets the island’s floor.
* Wetlands. Salt lakes, swamps, and freshwater holes draw in amphibians.
* Woodlands. Native trees brush the clouds and welcome rare birds and bats.
* Ocean. A marine ecosystem for tropical fish, dolphins, seals, sea lions, and migrating whales.
* Settlement. A populated centre where the natural and man-made world co-exist. Native wildlife roams freely, gently encouraged back into their homes further afield.

> It’s unlike anywhere else in the world. These six diverse environments knit together to create the unique landscape of Wadjemup, where you can see native wildlife in their natural environment.

Image Aerial view of Geordie Bay and salt lakes

A collection of unique ecosystems

### Ngobar / Coastal

###### The crisp air and building swell

When you speak about your time on Rottnest Island, the coastline will likely play a leading role. Its sweeping beaches, sand dunes, and limestone cliffs are familiar, yet completely unique. With every gust of wind, seashell particles and quartz sand form the coastline’s ever-changing fingerprint.

This process has created the landscape for wedge-tailed shearwaters , cormorants, terns, and the impressive osprey. Along with the familiar king’s skink, these bird species are just as much part of the coastal landscape as the sand dunes.

Image Sand dunes on Wadjemup/Rottnest Island

### Ngobar djooraly / Scrub Heath

###### Amongst dense island covering

Take a deep breath and if you are smelling salty-sweet air, you have moved into the scrubland ecosystem. As one of the biggest systems on the island, scrub heath covers more than half of Wadjemup. Its dense covering is a refuge for reptiles like bobtails and the king skink.

> If you’re an early riser, you can look out into the scrub on a crisp morning and see white-fronted chat, silvereye, and scrub wren. They all live freely amongst the native bushes — prickle lily and feather speargrass grow undisturbed thanks to the quokka’s natural aversion to the plants.

### Balyan boodja / Wetlands

###### Refuge in serene spaces

An intricate network of [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), brackish swamps, and small freshwater holes (or wet spots called seeps) make up this natural ecosystem. Fed by winter rainfall and groundwater that moves to the surface from the underground aquifer, the wetlands cover more than ten per cent of the island.

While a draw for the select few, these wetlands do not pique the interest of the masses. This makes the area a secluded haven for travellers as well as native wildlife, especially amphibians. The moaning frog, motorbike frog, and squelching froglets can often be heard but rarely seen.

The same cannot be said for the wetland’s birdlife, who are visible at every turn. Rock parrots, Australian shelducks, bridled and crested terns, waders, and red-necked phalarope are all possible sightings.

> One per cent of the world’s banded stilt population is found in the island’s wetlands. It’s one of the most delightful finds for bird lovers.

### Boorn boodja / Woodlands

###### Tangled in enchanting woods

The rare and exquisite make their home in the unique woodland habitat of the island.

Three types of native trees can be found here, the Rottnest Island pine, the Rottnest Island tea tree, and wattle trees. These trees provide shelter for countless species of bush birds, including the rare and beautiful golden whistler, red-capped robin, silvereye, and the singing honeyeater.

As the heat slowly dissolves on a warm evening, a walk in the woodland will showcase the island’s white-striped free-tailed bat population. These nocturnal creatures create a sense of ethereal beauty in the woodland, quietly foraging above the tree canopy. Their unique echolocation calls reveal their presence to travellers listening from the wooded boundaries.

### Maambakoort / Ocean

###### Marine garden sanctuaries

The marine reserve is one of the most spectacular drawcards of the island. From sandy floors, seagrass meadows, coral reefs, and rocky shores, the diverse marine habitats attract 400 species of tropical fish.

Thanks to the warm Leeuwin Current that surrounds the island, the diversity of fish species — baldchin groper, harlequin fish, samson fish, and yellowtail kingfish — is often joined by the magnificent green turtle and crustaceans like the famous western rock lobster.

During winter and spring, you may even spot [humpback whales migrating through the waters](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching), particularly at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). You can also see long-nosed fur seals, bottlenose dolphins, and Australian sea lions from the Cathedral Rocks viewing platform.

### Settlement areas

###### Wildlife among historic development

The settlement of [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) is not devoid of island wildlife. As you warm up with a coffee and devour a pastry from the local bakery, you will likely be joined by quokkas, bobtail lizards, and silver gulls. These species clearly flourish in their natural habitats further afield; therefore, be mindful not to encourage their stay in the settlement with food that can be harmful to their physical and behavioural development.

The [quokka population](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) is a big island attraction. These iconic mammals can be found all over the island and while they are commonly spotted in the settlement area, head out towards the reserve to see them in their natural habitat. If you visit during August, you can see little joeys poking their heads out of their mothers’ pouches; come September, you can watch them take their first hops out into the world.

Remember, we are here to simply observe the quokkas (and all wildlife on Wadjemup) as they continue their natural movements around the island.

[Conserve the island

Wadjemup is a Class A Reserve meaning that the island is protected for both recreation and conservation. When you experience the island, by foot, flipper, or bike, there are ways to respect the land you’re on and its unique natural environment.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability)

# Aboriginal Culture & History

## The story of Wadjemup

Wadjemup, the Noongar name of the island, is often referred to as 'the place across the water where the spirits are'. This land is that of the Traditional Owners, the Whadjuk Noongar people, who know the island as a resting place of the spirits, as well as a memorial place of Aboriginal men and boys whose bodies still rest beneath the sands of Wadjemup. This is a history that we acknowledge and pay respect to.

Content Warning

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are advised that this content contains images and names of individuals who have passed away.

Visitors are also advised that this content contains material, including historical names and images, which relate to the island’s prison era and may be confronting and/or challenging.

The Rottnest Island Authority does not endorse the language and views of the past, and sincerely apologises for any distress this content may cause.

Image Sculpture at Wadjemup Museum

[Noongar Boodja who represents all Noongar men, positioned to look over the Quod and Aboriginal Burial Ground](/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum)

### A tale of two histories

For Aboriginal people across Western Australia, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a significant place. Their connection to the island is both complex and, at times, difficult.

[Learn more about Aboriginal History](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history)

Image West End

[West End](/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end)

### A deep connection to land

Wadjemup is the land of the Traditional Owners, the Whadjuk Noongar people, who have an enduring cultural and spiritual connection to the land and waters.

[Learn more about Aboriginal culture](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-culture)

### Paying your respects

Visitors to the island are encouraged to enrich their understanding of the Aboriginal perspective on the island. Pause, reflect and pay respect at the Koora-Yeye-Boordawan-Kalyakoorl (Past-Present-Future-Forever) sculpture at the end of the main jetty, learn more about the significance from a local Noongar guide on a [Go Cultural tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences), and visit the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) to learn more.

# Ricey Beach

## An invigorating space to stop and reflect

For those venturing around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s western shores, Ricey Beach is a delightful little find. A secluded beach, it’s quieter than some of the others on the island, making it perfect for a day with the kids and lazy afternoons spent lounging, swimming, and getting away from it all.

Protected by a winding coral reef, its sparkling turquoise waters provide calm refuge from the sun. In combination with the stunning white sand, it’s the ideal afternoon swimming spot.

### Look out for...

Image 

Beautiful calm waters for swimming

Image 

Audio sign sharing Nyitting (Dreaming) stories

Image 

Fishing for all levels of expertise

Image 

The Karlinyah Bidi stretch of the Wadjemup Bidi

### Where to find Ricey Beach

Hop on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and get off at Stop 15. Take the walking track down from the road and you’ll find Ricey Beach sprawled out in front of you. Alternatively, jump on your bike for a 20-minute [ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from the main Thomson Bay settlement, either around the northern coast or through the island’s central roads.

Image 

[Fishing](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing)

### One of the island’s best fishing destinations

There’s a lot of good fishing off Wadjemup beaches, so choosing the best one is difficult. But Ricey Beach has made a name for itself as having some of the island’s best fishing conditions.

Calm, tranquil waters bordered by a shallow reef create a safe haven for fish. There are fantastic reef fishing opportunities, with deep fishing holes providing homes for some of WA’s most sought-after fish species. Here you’ll be able to find mulloway, tailor, salmon, skippy, and herring, and even some silver bream, flathead, or flounder if you’re lucky that day.

Image Ricey Beach

Ricey Beach

### Frequently Asked Questions

What's the best way to get there?

It’s a long walk from the main beaches, so the best way to get to Ricey Beach is either via the Quokka Coaches Island Explorer bus (Stop 15), or cycling.

What facilities are available at Ricey Beach?

There’s a picnic bench shaded by trees to stop, relax, and unwind.

The closest toilet facilities are located at City of York Bay (four minutes by bike or 15 minutes on foot) and Stark Bay (three minutes by bike or 12 minutes on foot).

Are there accessible facilities at Ricey Beach?

The beach itself features a well-sited access ramp that allows for easy access to the beach.

What fish can you catch at Ricey Beach?

Ricey Beach is known for fishing conditions that suit a range of species, from fast-moving tailor and salmon to reef favourites like skippy and herring. Mulloway may also be found here, while silver bream, flathead and flounder can appear when the day is on your side. For more places to cast a line, explore the [guide to fishing on Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-wetting-a-line-on-rottnest-island).

# By Bus

Take advantage of the comfort and convenience of a bus and see more of the island in less time.

Image Bus driving through the lakes

Bus driving through the lakes

### Sit back and take in the sights

Whether it’s for a unique tour, or easy transport, the various bus services on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island provide convenience and connection, whatever the weather.

Enjoy onboard commentary with guided tours as you discover the island's hidden gems. Travel at your own pace with the hop-on hop-off service, allowing you to visit your favourite spots whenever you like. For a quick and convenient ride, the daily shuttle bus connects Thomson Bay, Geordie Bay, and Kingstown.

Image 

[Quokka Coaches](/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour)

### Quokka Coaches Island Explorer

Choose to ride the full island loop or explore at your own pace, hopping off whenever something catches your eye — perhaps stop at West End to watch the surging waves collide with the coastline.

 [More about Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour)

Image 

[Geordie Bay](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay)

### Quokka Coaches Shuttle Bus

Settle into island life faster by taking a shuttle bus to your accommodation on arrival.

The shuttle service is a quick and convenient way to move between the island settlements and the airport. The shuttle bus is perfect to get you to your accommodation or save your energy when moving between Thomson Bay, Geordie Bay and Kingstown.

 [More about Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour)

Image Quokka Coaches

[Bayseeker Island Tour](/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour)

### Quokka Coaches Bayseeker Island Tour

A cosy bus ride past woodland habitats, salt lakes, and beaches. This 1.75 hour bus tour is for nature-lovers who like to stay comfortable while still getting a culture fix from the commentary, with stops at various maritime and military history sites.

[More about Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour)

Image 

[Discover Rottnest Bus Tour](/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour)

### Discover Rottnest Bus Tour With Rottnest Express

This 90-minute tour takes you to the island’s most spectacular locations, stopping at Wadjemup Lighthouse and West End.

The onboard commentary delivers insights into the island’s history and native flora and fauna as you experience Wadjemup undercover.

 [More about Discover Rottnest Bus Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour)

### Accessible for all

The Discover Rottnest tour bus, and Quokka Coaches shuttle and tour buses are wheelchair accessible. However, please call ahead to ensure that seats within the bus can be removed to accommodate the wheelchair. [Read more about accessibility here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/accessibility).

### Charter bus hire

Are you planning a special event or wedding on the island?

Provide your guests with the ultimate in comfort and convenience with 28-seater and 42-seater charter buses available for hire with  [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour).

Image Bus travel on the island

Bus travel on the island

Image Quokka Coaches ticket kiosk

[Quokka Coaches ticket kiosk](/deals/visit-more-for-less-with-the-rottnest-seasonal-transport-pass)

### Quokka Coaches Seasonal Transport Pass

Are you a regular visitor to the island? Save on your next stay with a Rottnest Seasonal Transport Pass from Quokka Coaches. The pass gives you access to a discounted rate for the Island Explorer and Accommodation Shuttle service so you can see more for less.

Conditions apply.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals/visit-more-for-less-with-the-rottnest-seasonal-transport-pass)

### Frequently Asked Questions

What should I bring on a Rottnest Island bus tour?

Whether travelling by bus, bike or on foot, we advise that you bring a hat, sunscreen, comfortable walking shoes and a water bottle. Wear lightweight, breathable clothing for comfort in summer, and be sure to pack a beach towel and swimsuit to enjoy the stunning marine sanctuaries that surround the island. In autumn, winter and spring, it’s best to pack a jumper and rain jacket or umbrella. Adventurous travellers may also like to bring a wetsuit to enjoy snorkelling or surfing in the cooler months.

Does the Rottnest Island bus book out?

The [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) Island Explorer hop-on hop-off bus service and tours, as well as the [Rottnest Express Discovery Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour), often book out during peak periods. We recommend booking your bus ticket online in advance, which will make it easier to board the bus on the island.

What should I do if the bus is fully booked?

If the bus is fully booked during your visit, there are great alternative ways to explore the island. The [accommodation shuttle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) is available to all visitors, allowing easy travel between the Thomson Bay and Geordie Bay settlements. You can also [hire a bike or electric bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike), book a [private transfer with Quokka Hopper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-private-transfer), or simply [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) – there is a lot you can see on foot.

Within a 15-minute walk from the main settlement, you can find [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), a picturesque spot for snorkelling, or head to Bathurst Lighthouse which overlooks the stunning [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). Alternatively, you can discover the beauty of the island’s centre, watching quokkas in their natural habitat by Garden Lake or enjoying the panoramic view across the lakes from Vlamingh Lookout.

# The Basin

## One of nature’s best kept secrets

A bucket-list beach thanks to its naturally hollowed out reef, it’s easy to see why The Basin is one of the most popular beaches on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Located just a 10-minute [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) from the main settlement, it’s the perfect place to relax and reconnect as you feel the soft sand between your toes and the warm sun on your face.

Take a dip in the safe, protected waters or put on your mask and snorkel to discover another world below the surface with an abundance of species of fish, as well as beautiful purple, pink and brown shades of coral.

Recently refurbished, make the most of the new outdoor showers, BBQs and toilet facilities — perfect for your family fun day.

### Where to find The Basin

Located just 10 minutes from the main settlement, The Basin is easily accessible [on foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot), or [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike). Just follow the signposts and you’ll soon arrive at this world-renowned beach.

[Safety in the Water

To have the safest experience, always check the weather and tidal conditions before snorkelling and be aware of your abilities in the water.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

Image Snorkelling

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Explore a new world beneath the surface

Stunningly beautiful with crystal clear, warm waters thanks to the Leeuwin Current, The Basin is an underwater haven just waiting to be discovered.

Calm and protected when the wind blows from the south-east, south or south-west, thanks to its natural barrier, it’s the ideal place for kids or beginners to get used to snorkelling while exploring the plethora of fish attracted to the seagrass.

The natural bowl or “basin” is a great place to look for fish and crustaceans.

[Learn more about Snorkelling and Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby The Basin?

The facilities at The Basin have been recently refurbished with new outdoor showers, BBQs, drinking water and toilet facilities now available. An upgraded seating area is also in place.

What is the best way to get there?

The Basin is just a 10-minute walk or short bike ride from the main settlement. Just follow the signposts.

Are there accessible facilities at The Basin?

Accessible toilets are available.

Is The Basin good for snorkelling?

The Basin is well suited to snorkelling, especially for beginners and families when conditions are calm. Its protected water and sea life close to shore make it an easy place to pause, swim, and explore beneath the surface before discovering more [snorkelling and diving spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) on the island.

# Thomson Bay

## Thomson Bay is where your Wadjemup adventure begins

Thomson Bay is your introduction to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, and the first bay you see as you step off the ferry and onto the jetty. Stretching from north to south, it provides a vibrant backdrop for the entire main settlement.

Just off the main jetty you’ll find a roped-off swimming area for the little ones, modern amenities, and barbecue facilities ready and waiting. Everything else you need is within arm’s reach. Head into town and refuel with a coffee, or stay for a while over a mouthwatering meal at one of the waterside restaurants at [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar), and [Isola Bar e Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest). Drop in to the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) to learn more about your island stay.

So kick off your shoes, feel the soft, white sand beneath your feet, and get ready to begin your Wadjemup adventure.

### Where to find Thomson Bay

Disembark from your ferry, walk down the jetty, and you’ll arrive at Thomson Bay. Just a one-minute walk from the main settlement, it’s your first introduction to Wadjemup.

Image Thomson Bay

[Thomson Bay](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Set the tone for your time on Wadjemup

With the whole day ahead of you, wade into the calm waters and have your first experience of Wadjemup’s pristine beaches.

Travelling further out into the bay, keen-eyed observers looking below the waves might even be lucky enough to get a glimpse of the island’s friendly booyi (green turtles) and stingrays.

If you’re feeling adventurous, the jetty at Thomson Bay is one of the most popular family fishing spots. Schools of herring play between the moorings, providing just enough of a challenge for young fishers. Large numbers of squid roam the waters as the sun goes down, attracted by the jetty lights — even if you don’t fish, they’re a marvel to watch.

A lively location with space for families of all sizes, Thomson Bay is the ideal spot to relax and unwind, to settle in for a day of swimming, sun, and sandcastles, before discovering the rest of the island.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby Thomson Bay?

Thomson Bay is the gateway to Wadjemup, so there’s everything you need in one location. Public toilets and change rooms, lockers, barbecue facilities, the Visitor Centre and more.

What is the best way to get there?

When you step off the main jetty, you’re already there. You can reach Thomson Bay by walking, or make it the end point of your island ride.

Are there accessible facilities at Thomson Bay?

Accessible facilities are located close to Thomson Bay. A unisex accessible toilet is available at the Visitor Centre. An accessible toilet and shower facility is located nearby at Bedford Avenue. Access to the beach is available across the sand at North Thomson Bay. More accessibility information is available here.

# By Ferry

Travelling to Rottnest Island by ferry is the most popular way to get to the island. There are three ferry operators to choose from and multiple departure points.

Image Aerial view of ferry jetty in Thomson Bay

Aerial view of ferry jetty in Thomson Bay

## Set sail to the island

Sit back, relax and enjoy the ride as you experience the fun and freedom of a ferry — the most popular way to get to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

With transfers across to the island available through three operators, you can choose your closest departure point from Perth City, North Fremantle, Fremantle and Hillarys Boat Harbour.

Ferry travel time will depend on where you leave from, ranging from around 25 minutes from Fremantle, 45 minutes from Hillarys Boat Harbour and up to 90 minutes from Perth's Barrack Street Jetty.

Rottnest Island ferry timetables vary depending on the season and weather. Please contact your preferred ferry provider for current schedules.

Departures from Victoria Quay

Due to works at the B Shed ferry terminal at Victoria Quay in Fremantle, ticketing booths are temporarily located on the east side of E Shed. Ferries are operating as normal.

Image SeaLink WA Rottnest

Ferry leaving Thomson Bay

## Planning your journey

Rottnest Island ferry timetables vary depending on the season and weather. Choose your preferred provider based on where you will departing from.

* [Image SeaLink WA Rottnest

  SeaLink Rottnest

  With ferries departing daily from Fremantle and Perth, you’ll cruise effortlessly towards Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.](/see-do/shopping-services/sealink-rottnest)
* [Image Rottnest Fast Ferries

  Rottnest Fast Ferries

  Embark on your Wadjemup / Rottnest Island voyage from Perth’s northern suburbs on a spacious, high-speed catamaran.](/see-do/shopping-services/rottnest-fast-ferries)
* [Image Rottnest Express

  Rottnest Express

  Set sail to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island from two convenient locations in Fremantle or from the heart of Perth.](/see-do/shopping-services/rottnest-express)

### Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to get to Rottnest Island by ferry?

Rottnest Island ferries take approximately 25 minutes from Fremantle, 45 minutes from Hillarys Boat Harbour, or 90 minutes from Perth's Barrack Street Jetty.

Do we need to book?

Booking is recommended particularly in the peak summer periods to guarantee a seat on your preferred departure. Ferry tickets can also be purchased on the day, subject to availability.

Where does the ferry depart from?

Ferries depart from Northport at Rous Head in North Fremantle,  B Shed at Victoria Quay in Fremantle, Barrack Street Jetty in Perth’s city centre, and Hillarys Boat Harbour in Perth's northern suburbs.

Ferries depart from Main Jetty on the island in Thomson Bay.

How early do we need to get to the terminal?

It’s recommended that all passengers arrive at the terminal at least 30 minutes prior to departure. This allows enough time to park vehicles, label and load luggage and equipment, and collect your ferry tickets. If you’re travelling with no luggage or freight and have an e-ticket or QR code, please make your way straight to the boarding gate.

Is parking available at the terminal?

Paid parking is available at Victoria Quay in Fremantle. Secure, undercover parking is available nearby on Henderson Street.

Secure parking is available at Rous Head in North Fremantle.

Free short term and overnight vehicle parking options are available at Hillarys Boat Harbour.

Multiple paid parking options are available near Barrack Street Jetty in Perth’s city centre.

Can I get to the ferry terminals by bus or train?

Victoria Quay, Hillarys Boat Harbour and Barrack Street Jetty in Perth City are all accessible by public transport.

* B Shed, Victoria Quay, Fremantle - bus and train stops nearby
* Hillarys Boat Harbour - bus stops nearby on West Coast Drive
* Barrack Street Jetty, Perth City - bus and train stops nearby

What is the Rottnest Island Admission fee?

This fee is collected by ferry operators on behalf of the [Rottnest Island Authority](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/) and contributes to the provision of island facilities.

All visitors are required to pay an admission fee. Visitors arriving by ferry pay this fee as part of their fare at the time of booking.

Do ferries accommodate wheelchair and pram access?

Yes, in most cases ferries can accommodate wheelchairs.  Find more about [accessibility at Rottnest Island here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/accessibility).

Ferries can also accommodate prams on board, however, depending on capacity, the pram may need to be stowed. Find out more about [luggage & equipment here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/luggage-equipment).

What do I need to do if I’m taking luggage?

You will need to use luggage labels that can either be arranged in advance or organised on the day at the ferry terminal. Find out more about [luggage and equipment here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/luggage-equipment).

What if I want to bring my own equipment?

You are generally welcome to bring your own bike, SCUBA diving gear, surfboard, kayak, stand-up paddleboard and other equipment on the ferry. However, permitted items, freight charges and stowing requirements will depend on your ferry provider. Find out more about [luggage and equipment here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/luggage-equipment).

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

The friendly reservations team at your chosen accommodation will contact you to advise that all ferries have been cancelled for the day of your departure and offer an alternate solution. Please note, the conditions of booking vary for each operator.

# Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms

Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms offers rooms to rest for the night and a relaxed experience of Rottnest Island.

**The hostel and dormitories are an affordable way to get the most out of your stay on the island. Private family rooms and shared options available.**

Located in the historic Kingstown Barracks, Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms is a place to rest and meet like-minded travellers. Accommodation options range from private family rooms for larger groups to share to communal dormitories that provide the full hostel experience.

This affordable accommodation attracts the adventurous at heart, so be sure to visit the shared spaces to swap stories with your fellow island wanderers.

For more information or to make a booking at the hostel, visit the [Stay Rottnest website](http://stayrottnest.com).

To make a group booking in the dormitories, please call Stay Rottnest on (+61) 1800 111 111.

Hostel

Bunk down in these shared rooms and relax into the island lifestyle. Here, you can thaw out after a crisp surf, cool down after a day of cycling and engage in the community feel of the hostel.

The hostel features 50 comfortable beds with linens provided, plus shared kitchen and lounge spaces for preparing meals and relaxing. There is additional outside seating for those using the kitchen and barbecue areas. Communal washroom facilities are also available, with towels included.

Solo travellers can rest in a single bunk bed (shared room), while the family rooms sleep up to four adults (one double bed and one bunk bed per room).

* Kingstown Barracks

* Sleeps 1-50

* Budget friendly option

[Check availability](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates)

Image

Dormitories

This much-loved school camp destination provides a comfortable base for groups. Staying at Kingstown Barracks is a chance to stay amongst history, with its heritage clock tower and salvaged WWII gun barrel. As you move beyond the dorms, the learning can continue around the island.

There are 17 dormitory rooms available with bed configurations ranging from 2-bed to 18-bed rooms. There is also a communal bathroom. Select rooms have private bathroom facilities and are wheelchair accessible.

A pillow and blanket is provided per bed, with linens and towels available for hire. Please note that there are no kitchen facilities available for the dormitories.

* Kingstown Barracks

* Sleeps 2-18 guests

* Budget friendly option

### Frequently Asked Questions

How do I book accommodation?

Stay Rottnest accommodation is available to book online via [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) or via phone on (+61) 1800 111 111 (Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm, excluding public holidays). Bookings can be made up to nine months in advance of your stay.

**Booking online**

[Booking online](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) is the quickest and easiest way to secure Stay Rottnest accommodation and receive instant confirmation.

Special requests and notes are also able to be placed in the booking.

How do Open Days work?

Availability for bookings opens on the first working Wednesday of each calendar month, for accommodation nine months in advance.

While you can book by calling Stay Rottnest on (+61) 1800 111 111, online is the simplest and most successful way to book accommodation. As demand for bookings is high, a virtual queuing system is used to ensure a smooth experience for everyone on busy Open Days.  

**Booking for Accessibility**

If you need wheelchair accessible accommodation, please send your request after 8:30 am to [stay@rottnestisland.com](mailto:stay@rottnestisland.com) and ensure you attach a copy of your ACROD Card (front and back). These requests are processed in the order they’re received from 8:30 am onwards on Open Day, so hold your email until then. There is a limit of one booking per ACROD Card.

For more information, visit [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates)

When are Open Days scheduled?

Open Days are held on the first Wednesday of each month, to release availability for the next booking period, nine months in advance.

Visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/files/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf) to see all current scheduled Open Day dates.

How much will it cost?

The prices of Stay Rottnest accommodation vary based on the type of accommodation chosen, the time of year and availability. To check prices for available accommodation, select your preferred dates, location and accommodation type on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates).

What is the difference between the hostel rooms and a dormitory?

The hostel offers accommodation in a family room (double bed and bunk bed) or a single bed in a shared bunk room. Guests at the hostel have access to communal kitchen and barbecue areas as well as shared bathroom facilities.

The dormitory offers shared rooms for groups or schools, varying between two and 18-bed layouts. Some rooms have a private bathroom and wheelchair access, and all guests can access the shared bathroom facilities.

Can I alter or cancel my booking?

Yes, however cancellations and modifications may incur a cancellation fee.

Further details on how to cancel or alter your booking, and applicable fees, can be found in the [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

Can I transfer my booking to someone else?

You may nominate another person as authorised to check in to the accommodation, however you will remain as the owner of the booking as the original guest. As the owner of the booking, you will be liable for any costs related to the accommodation for the duration of the booking.

You can view the full [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

Where can I find an accommodation map?

You can find a accommodation map of all accommodation types on the [Stay Rottnest website here](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_accommodation_maps.pdf).

What’s included in my accommodation?

The inclusions vary by accommodation. You can see what is included for each type at [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates).

What time is check-in?

Check-in is from 2 pm. You can leave your mobile number at the Visitor Centre, who will text you if your accommodation is ready early.

What time is check-out?

The check-out time is 9 am.

Do I need to bring linen and towels?

In hostel rooms, bed linens and towels are provided with your booking.

In the dormitories, a pillow and blanket is provided, however guests need to hire linen and towels prior to arrival or bring their own.

How do I hire extra items?

If you require additional items, please complete a [Hire Items Booking Form](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/accommodation_hire_items_2026.pdf).

Please contact Stay Rottnest at least 48 hours prior to arrival for hire items.

How can I get between the Kingstown Barracks and the main settlement?

Kingstown Barracks is a 25-minute walk or 10-minute cycle from the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre). Alternatively, guests can take the Quokka Coaches accommodation shuttle bus.

When is luggage collection?

For Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms accommodation, luggage must be out for collection by 9 am for ferries departing at 10 am or later. For ferries departing before 10 am, luggage must be out for collection by 7 am and must be pre-booked by notifying the Visitor Centre 24 hours before departure.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If ferries are cancelled for the day of your departure, guests of Stay Rottnest accommodation will be contacted by reservations and given the option to:

* Leave the day prior and receive a refund for your unused night of accommodation, or
* If your accommodation is available for an extra day, you will be invited to stay for 50% of the rack rate.

If you do not wish to leave early, and your accommodation is not available for an extra night, nor is any alternate Stay Rottnest accommodation available, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire if they have availabilities.

Once you arrive on the island, make your way to the Visitor Centre to check in.

Photo ID is required for registration by the person who made the booking.

# Staying Cool at Wadjemup in Summer

A guide to staying safe and cool while embracing the warm summer temperatures on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

6 minutes

Image Couple relaxing on the beach at Rocky Baybddb239e-fdf4-4599-a7a9-0a1ff2a585d0.tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=e7f765f2_1)

Set up an umbrella

**Is the glorious summer heat starting to hamper your adventurous energy? Here are a few ways you can find some cooling relief.**

At picturesque Australian destinations like Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, [summer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) is an experience with well-established expectations. Heady, warm air that makes the cool ocean a luxurious escape. Savouring sweet [icy treats](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/chilled-bliss--discover-the-best-spots-for-cool-scoops-and-icy-treats) while overlooking stretches of white sand. A sky so blue the horizon line blurs where it meets the sea.

Along with this quintessential summer experience come a few realities of the hot weather. But with a just a few precautions and some helpful tips in mind, you can confidently settle into this languorous season on the island.

### Shaded activities

Although it’s easy to become mesmerised by sun-drenched activities, scheduling time to be in the shade is one of our main tips to stay cool in summer. By knowing when to take a break from the sun, you keep energy levels high for other adventures.

#### Recline under a beach umbrella

Escaping the heat doesn’t mean staying inside the whole time, and a beach umbrella keeps you shaded while you still enjoy views of the shimmering ocean. Bays like [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) and  [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin)  are only a short walk from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), so once you have your shade of choice in hand, stroll down to get settled in. You can bring your own beach shelter or umbrella, or hire one from [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals) when you arrive.

#### Dine at a restaurant or cafe

The settlement is full of venues that offer a chance to cool down while refuelling for further explorations. There are places like [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto), where you can revive tired young travellers with homemade pizzas, or [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), the ideal choice for an afternoon feast accompanied by chilled wine or pints amongst friends. And for lighter, [refreshingly cool treats](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/chilled-bliss--discover-the-best-spots-for-cool-scoops-and-icy-treats), take your pick from a wide variety of options, like ice cream at [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican), [Simmo’s](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/simmo-s-rottnest) and [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery), an acai bowl from [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane), a cold smoothie from the [Boost Mobeel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/boost-mobeel-rottnest), or a fresh juice at [Geordie’s Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery).

#### Picnic under shady trees or shelters

Wadjemup is a lush natural landscape, and with this comes plenty of trees to shelter under — perhaps with a picnic of fresh [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) treats or a selection of bites from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store). If you take a wander along Thomson Bay, or even through the settlement, you’ll find clumps of wattle and tea trees, shaped into cocoons of shady respite by the cool coastal winds. Alternatively, you can enjoy lunch at the shade shelters overlooking [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), North Thomson Bay, [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), or in the settlement mall.

#### Visit the museum

Another way to take a break out of the sun? Enter the cool stillness of a museum. [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) is the place to develop a deeper understanding of the history of the island, where you can wander amongst 40,000-year-old artefacts as you cool off from the day.

#### Head to the arcade

At [Rottnest Movies & Mini Gol](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf)f, there’s also an undercover play space available in the form of retro arcade. Engage in some good-natured competition and have a rest from the sun’s rays.

#### Browse the shops

Once you’ve shared sunny memories in the outdoors, venture into the shaded shops, where you can pick up some souvenirs to remind you of those moments. [Island Gypsy](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/island-gypsy) offers gifts, mementos, and beach accessories, while [Indianic Boutique](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/indianic-boutique) has swimwear and clothing that will remind you of island life with every wear.

#### Join a bus tour

Avoid cycling or walking in the heat by booking a bus tour ahead of time. The two-hour [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) Bayseeker Island Tour travels past woodland habitats, salt lakes, and beaches. Or opt for the 90-minute [Discover Rottnest Bus Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour), which visits stunning locations like [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) and [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) with onboard commentary along the way.

### Cooling ocean-based activities

There is one particularly obvious way to stay cool on Wadjemup: by going in the ocean! The sparkling clear waters that surround the island are fresh and soothing, the perfect antidote to the summer sun (other than hats, sunscreen and shade, of course).

#### Join a snorkelling tour

[Rottnest Snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-snorkel) provides a tour of the best snorkelling spots around the island. They cruise the shallow, abundant waters and pause to dive below, where hundreds of species of fish can be observed. Alternatively, hop onboard the iconic [Charter 1 snorkel and sailing tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1), complete with a drag net that allows you to relish in the cooling wake of the boat as you cruise along.

#### Head off on a self-guided snorkel

With [63 beaches and 20 bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches), you’re spoiled for choice with [places to snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/where-to-snorkel-at-rottnest-island--six-of-the-best-spots). But if you’re looking to avoid the busier beaches, head straight to [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay). Dive in and snorkel along the dappled aqua waters at this gem of a spot and you’ll encounter the unique underwater wildlife that call the island’s marine sanctuaries home.

#### Shipwrecks

Wadjemup has a rich [maritime history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history), and evidence of this lies hidden with the wrecks of 13 unfortunate vessels. Most are located in the deep water surrounding the island, but two — *Uribes* and *[Shark](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks)* — are shallow enough to explore from the sandy beaches.

#### Take an express boat tour

Climb aboard the [Eco Express Boat Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours) and prepare for an awe-inspiring trip that explores parts of Wadjemup only accessible by water. The best bit? You can catch a unique perspective of the island’s wild coastline all from under the shady roof of the Eco Express boat, with occasional cooling showers of sea spray.

Image Parker Point

[Charter 1 Snorkel & Sailing Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/charter-1?tab=see-do)

### How hot does it really get in summer on Rottnest Island?

Although the island meets the warm weather expectations of Australia, it also benefits from the cooling effect of the Indian Ocean breeze, so the temperatures always stay a few degrees below Perth.

On Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, the average temperatures in [summer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) are:

* December: 25.1°C – 17.7°C
* January: 26.5°C – 19.1°C
* February: 27.2°C – 19.5°C

### Sun safety and staying cool

Southern hemisphere locations actually receive about 15% more UV radiation than the equivalent place in the northern hemisphere — meaning you’re much more likely to feel damage from the sun.
There are a few simple preventative measures to stay sun safe:

#### Clothing

When you're outside, cover up with breathable, lightweight clothing. Choose light-coloured items, with plenty of coverage, like long-sleeved shirts and full-length pants — and always wear a hat.

#### Sunscreen

Cover any exposed skin with sunscreen that has an SPF rating of at least 50, being sure to reapply every two hours and again after swimming. A tip: always opt for a reef-safe sunscreen and help us to protect the island’s unique marine environment.

#### Hydration

Everyone needs to consume at least two litres of water each day, but this amount grows when you’re active and out in the sun. When you leave the settlement, bring as much water as you can comfortably carry (a litre or more is recommended), as there are limited refilling stations once you venture out.

#### Take a dip

An easy way to feel refreshed is to go for a swim in one of the [island’s bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches). This will lower your core body temperature and is especially effective if you submerge your entire body, including your head.

Although Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is an invigorating destination all year, visiting the island during summer is an experience baked into the Perth lifestyle. And when you stay safe from the heat and sun, there’s nothing limiting you from building lifelong memories on these shores.

### Tips for a time well spent

Make your visit even more meaningful with helpful advice from those in the know.
