### Frequently Asked Questions

Should I visit Rottnest Island in winter?

Whether you’ve never visited, or you make the journey over every summer, Wadjemup during winter is an experience not to be missed. Most island vendors also remain open, serving up warming meals and providing all the hire services and memorable experiences you need for your stay.

What is there to do on Rottnest Island in winter?

The cooler months of winter present an opportunity for [unique experiences](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/10-unmissable-activities-to-enjoy-this-winter-on-rottnest-island) on Wadjemup. Rug up and cycle or hike your way around the island, stopping along the way to watch for migrating whales and other wildlife. Or don a wetsuit and take to the warmer winter waters for a spot of snorkelling, diving or surfing. For those who want to take it slower, dine at one of the many cosy venues or immerse yourself in culture at Wadjemup Museum. During August, keep an eye out for young quokkas emerging from pouches, one of the island's most remarkable sights. [See more seasonal guides and tips here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips).

Is Rottnest Island cold in winter?

The island is actually a few degrees warmer than the mainland of Perth during winter. From June to August, the average daytime temperature on Wadjemup is 19°C. It does get chilly when the sun slips behind the clouds or during early mornings and evenings, so come prepared with warm clothes.

What can I do on Rottnest Island if it rains?

Don’t let winter rains get in the way of your adventure, there are plenty of indoor activities for visitors of all ages to enjoy. Plus, if you come prepared with waterproof clothing and shoes, you can continue to explore the natural wonders of the island by foot or bike.  If you want to see the island sights while staying dry, you can opt for the Quokka Coaches Island Explorer bus service or one of the bus tours. For more inspiration, [read this guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-wonders-all-the-things-to-do-on-a-rainy-island-day) to everything you can do on a rainy Wadjemup day.

What should I bring and wear during winter on Rottnest Island?

Here are some recommended travel items to make your island experience as comfortable as possible. But if you get caught out or forget something back at home, [The General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store), [Indianic Boutique](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/indianic-boutique) and [Island Gypsy](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/island-gypsy) also have items such as ponchos and jumpers available for purchase.

* Rain jacket
* Enclosed shoes / hiking boots
* Wetsuit (for snorkelling or surfing)
* Camera
* Water bottle (there are water refill stations around the island)
* Reusable coffee cup
* Jumper
* Beanie
* Small umbrella or poncho (best for hands-free exploration and windy days)

What is the average temperature on Rottnest Island in winter?

The average temperature over the winter months on Rottnest Island are:

* June: 13.5 – 18.8°C
* July: 12.5 – 17.9°C
* August: 12.4 – 18°C

These mild winter temperatures make the island perfect for a retreat to explore nature's charms by day and cosying up in the warmth of your accommodation by night.

What is the average monthly rainfall on Rottnest Island during winter?

Winter on Wadjemup brings a refreshing change with its rain showers, averaging:

* June: 103.2 mm
* July: 114.1 mm
* August: 86.6 mm

Rain showers bring a refreshing change to the island landscapes, making for an especially wonderful experience exploring the natural wonders. Don a weather-proof jacket and head for the peaceful rain-kissed trails or opt for a cycle along coastal paths. Alternatively, you can choose to relax indoors with a book or at one of the many cosy dining venues.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

The friendly reservations team at your chosen accommodation will contact you to advise that all ferries have been cancelled for the day of your departure and offer an alternate solution. Please note, the conditions of booking vary for each operator.

**Nestled alongside the stunning lakes of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, The Lodge offers a tranquil retreat where modern comfort meets the island’s rich cultural heritage.**

Whether you’re travelling solo, as a couple, or with family and friends, you can choose from a range of rooms designed to suit every need for a space that feels like home. Surrounded by native landscaping, the property provides a peaceful and natural environment to enjoy, allowing you to immerse yourself in the island's natural rhythm.

The Courtyard Rooms offer a unique stay within the historic reformatory building, blending timeless heritage with modern comfort. For those seeking tranquillity, the Lake Rooms feature picturesque views of Garden Lake, ideal for a peaceful escape. Meanwhile, the Poolhouse Rooms provide a refreshing retreat with direct access to the sparkling, heated pool.

Whether you're here to unwind or seek adventure, the Lodge's onsite dining options cater to all tastes. Head to [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest), the open-air dining space or, for a more casual experience, the [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican) Kiosk serves coffee, soft serve ice cream, and quick bites.

From snorkelling in crystal-clear waters to exploring the island’s trails, activities like cycling, sunset sailing, golf, and even skydiving await you. Book your stay at The Lodge Wadjemup and be one of the first to enjoy this extraordinary retreat.

There are a number of Courtyard and Poolhouse rooms suitable for guests with mobility requirements.

For more information or to make a booking, visit [The Lodge Wadjemup website](https://www.thelodgewadjemup.com/).

#### Where to find The Lodge Wadjemup

Situated behind the main settlement and overlooking Garden Lake, The Lodge is conveniently located at the corner of Digby Drive and Kitson Street. Just off the main settlement of the island, the main entrance is easily accessible via Boreham Street.

### Frequently Asked Questions

When will bookings open?

Bookings are now open for all stays.  
  
Guests can visit [The Lodge Wadjemup website](https://www.thelodgewadjemup.com/) to book.

What types of rooms are available at The Lodge Wadjemup?

The Lodge offers a variety of room types, including:

* **Courtyard:** Queen, King, and bunk options.
* **Lake:** King rooms, some with serene lake views, plus options for connecting rooms ideal for families or groups.
* **Poolhouse:** King rooms featuring pool, heritage, or lake views, with select rooms offering connecting and accessible layouts.

What time is check-in?

Check-in is available from 3 pm.

What time is check-out?

The check-out time is 10 am.

Is there a minimum stay requirement?

Yes, minimum night stays are required and vary according to the season. Please refer to [The Lodge Wadjemup website](https://www.thelodgewadjemup.com/) for further details.

Is The Lodge Wadjemup family-friendly?

Absolutely! The Lodge welcomes families with children of all ages. A range of room configurations are on offer including Queen, King and bunk rooms. They also offer connecting rooms, which can be configured with either king beds or two single beds, providing flexibility and comfort for your family's needs.

What dining options are available?

[Sunsets](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest) is the main bar and dining area offering a Mediterranean-inspired menu.

[Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican) is the kiosk, serving coffee, soft serve ice cream, baguettes, and more.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If ferries are cancelled on your scheduled departure date, the reservations team at The Lodge Wadjemup may be able to assist with extending your stay or rescheduling your arrival date, subject to availability. Please note that additional costs may apply.

If accommodation at The Lodge Wadjemup is not available for an extra night, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire about availability.

# Oliver Hill

### Come face-to-face with an integral part of Western Australia’s military history

Head west from the main settlement, between the salt lakes and through the bristling scrub towards the centre of the island, and you’ll eventually start the steep climb up Oliver Hill. And it’s not just another natural vantage point — Oliver Hill is one of the three locations on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island that showcases its wartime history.

Constructed in 1937 to defend Fremantle Port from potential enemy seaborne attacks, the battery of two 11-metre 9.2-inch naval guns at Oliver Hill is now a significant heritage icon. In fact, it’s the only intact emplacement of its type left in Australia.

Sited to take advantage of panoramic views over the island, the guns were capable of firing an armour-piercing shell up to 28 km away, ensuring Fremantle’s safety from enemy attack. Decommissioned in the 1960s, the guns and infrastructure still remain. And while the threat of seaborne attack is long gone, visitors can explore the site, and appreciate the lingering stories from yesteryear.

After viewing the battery, take a [guided tour underground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) to explore the tunnels that burrow into the sandy hillside, used to house the gun’s engine room and ammunition supply. These tours are run by Rottnest Island’s volunteer guides, and are conducted daily. You can purchase a ticket for your tour at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre), through [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) or on arrival.

An incredible natural lookout, Oliver Hill offers a panoramic view over the entire southern side of the island. It’s particularly stunning at sunset, when the fiery colours in the sky silhouette the iconic Wadjemup Lighthouse in the distance.

Due to the secluded nature of the area, however, the setting sun signals time to return to your accommodation, or make it safely back to the main settlement before nightfall.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

### Where to find Oliver Hill Battery

Oliver Hill is located in the centre of the island, somewhat out of the way. It’s a 4 km, 15 minute [cycle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from the main settlement, through the salt lakes and peaceful bushland.

The [Captain Hussey](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) historical train provides a unique way to get there. Using infrastructure originally built to transport equipment, building materials, and ammunition to the guns, the train runs from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), passing Bickley Point and on to Oliver Hill.

Alternatively, keen hikers can make a stop at Oliver Hill on their way along the [Wardan Nara Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/wardan-nara-bidi) and [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi). This can be a challenging trail in parts, so it’s recommended for experienced hikers only.

Image 

[Oliver Hill](/learn/military-maritime-history)

### Learn more about the role Wadjemup played in the Second World War

The Oliver Hill battery is just one location on Wadjemup that was used for military purposes.

On the nearby Signal Ridge, a 20-minute ride from Oliver Hill, you’ll find the Battery Observation Post and the Signal Station, buildings that helped turn the sandy hill into a secret communications hub. The eastern corner of the island is home to [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery), whose two 6-inch naval guns also played a part in Western Australia’s coastal defence system. The Kingstown Barracks complex, just north of Bickley Point, was built during the late 1930s to accommodate military personnel stationed on Rottnest Island, who helped man the guns.

For those interested in learning more about the island’s military history, the [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) is an engaging place to start. Wander from the main settlement, past Kingstown Barracks, through Bickley Battery, and around the coast, cutting inland to arrive at Oliver Hill.

[Learn more about Military & Maritime History](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history)

### Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best way to get there?

It’s a steep hill in parts, but at just 15 minutes from the main settlement it’s quite an accessible ride. You can also get to Oliver Hill is on the [Captain Hussey](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) historical train.

How much are the guided tours?

The Oliver Hill guided tours are run by trained volunteer guides. They take around an hour, where you get to descend into the tunnels underneath the gun emplacement and learn more about how the battery operated.

At $15 per adult, $7 per child, and $34 for a family (two adults, two children), tours depart daily on the hour from 10 am to 2 pm.

How long is the tour?

The tour takes around 45 minutes. There are no rest stops during the tour, which ensures those who are returning on the [Captain Hussey Historical Train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) will arrive back in time to catch it back to the settlement.

Can children do this tour?

Yes, however please note that children aged 12 and under must be accompanied by an adult. Children also cannot be carried during the tour, so they need to be able to walk the entire distance on their own.

How far do I need to walk during the tour?

The tour covers approximately 700 metres. You will climb up and down about 240 uneven steps, and the return walk includes a section of a bush trail.

Is the tour accessible?

The tour descends several steep stairways through the tunnels, with a bushwalk ascent back to base.  
  
Unfortunately, there is no wheelchair access beyond the landing area where you can view the above-ground gun.

What facilities are nearby Oliver Hill?

There are toilet facilities at Oliver Hill and bins on site but be sure to pack food and water to fuel your adventure. Alternatively, [Kalli’s at Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kalli-s-on-rotto) is nearby at [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse), providing food and drink options for those exploring the centre of the island.

* Family Fun: 9 Rainy Day Island Activities

# Family Fun: 9 Rainy Day Island Activities

Bundle up and bring your most adventurous selves; rainy days on the island are designed to ignite your sense of winter wonder.

5 minutes

Image Stormy clouds over the island landscape

Cloudy island landscape

**When temperatures fall and summer crowds thin, the possibilities for unchartered family adventure awaits on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Winter on the island invokes curiosity, with every puddle a portal; every path providing fresh perspective.**

The weather on Rottnest Island during [winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) is refreshing, but often pleasantly mild. Expect crisp days filtered with subtle sunshine, in-between gunmetal skies that replenish the land. If unexpected showers set in, embrace a different kind of holiday – less bustling, more connected, and filled with space to make memories for seasons to come. The following rainy-day activities are sure to leave eyes wide, cheeks rosy and cups full.

### Explore the wonders of the outdoors

As rainclouds drift dreamily overhead, equip everyone in wet weather gear for an invigorating expedition. Damp Wadjemup days are perfect for path following and puddle-jumping beneath brooding skies. Make your way to the [balyan boodja (wetlands)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/nature-wildlife), where the earth is renewed after seasonal sprinkles. As you follow the short track from the settlement, each splash in the rain’s reflective pools sends up a spray of giggles. Water ripples under feet, big and small, as satisfying stomps land into passing puddles.

Around the wetlands, listen out for bursting sounds of life amongst the patter of raindrops. The call of the kwiya (squelching froglet) and kwooyar (moaning frog) are unmistakeable, as are the rising revs of the kooboolong (motorbike frog). Stand in stillness as you eavesdrop on amphibian chatter, gleefully guessing the source of every sound.

### Spot active quokkas between showers

Winter is a special time on Wadjemup, for both its visitors and the creatures that inhabit the island. During the cooler months the iconic [kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) is most active, presenting ample opportunities for sightings. Join the [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) on a free guided quokka tour that offers insights about these iconic marsupials as you walk short distances to spot them from close, but safe distances. Sightings of joeys in their mothers’ pouches will warm hearts of all ages; a spectacle that occurs from August every year.

Image 

[Quokka spotting in the rain](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

Image 

[Oliver Hill underground tunnels](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour)

Image 

[Oliver Hill from above](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour)

Image Captain Hussey Historical Train

[Captain Hussey Historical Train tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour?tab=see-do)

### Ascend the stairs of Wadjemup Lighthouse

Join the Rottnest Voluntary Guides and [climb this  towering structure](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour) as a group. The lighthouse winds up 155 steps to bring you 38 metres above sea level. Take your time, especially if little legs are joining, and listen to enthralling tales shared by your guide along the way. At the top, gaze out at the glistening green land beneath you. If you pause long enough, you might spot local [birdlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching) soaring through surrounding skies as cool air nips at your cheeks.

### Travel back in time with an Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnel tour

But first, travel there by train on the historic [Captain Hussey](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour). Enjoy window seats and uninterrupted views of the passing scenery as you click-clack along the railway tracks to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). Here, you can slip out of the elements by going underground with the Rottnest Voluntary Guides. [Join an underground tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) and slink around the tunnels that lead to the gun’s ammunition supply and engine room. Examine the 9.2-inch naval gun and observe the newly installed and interactive replica Ghost Engine, which is sure to excite with its loud rumblings.

### Enjoy a warming winter meal

All that exploring is bound to whip up an appetite. Casual dining is readily available around the island, featuring cosy indoor nooks to escape passing showers and outdoor seating to perch at when the winter sun sneaks out.

Swing into [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) in the main settlement for hunger-busting homemade pizzas and other Italian-inspired fare. Over towards the cobalt-tinged waters of Thomson Bay, the familiar aromas of [Dome](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe) waft out to mingle with the salty sea air. Grab a table here and sample the seasonal menu featuring fluffy pancake stacks and crowd-pleasing toasties. At [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) is serving up all-day classic eats, like fish and chips and flavour-bursting burgers. Relish in a moment of calm as the kids unleash extra energy on the outdoor playground. The shade structure overhead can capture drizzles of rain, allowing the fun to continue.

[Cosy desserts at Geordie's Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/geordies-cafe-art-gallery)

### Get cosy and competitive

Tuck yourselves away and chase the thrill of a winning streak. Think: a merry game of ‘Snap’ in between sips of creamy hot chocolates at Dome. Or slip back into the cosy surrounds of your [accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) to bust out everyone’s favourite board game. Rain falls slowly on your roof, blankets are bundled tightly, and laughter fuels an afternoon or evening of game play. Bring games over to the island with you or grab extra games or a new deck of cards from [The General Stores](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store).

### Reflect out of the rain

As rain trickles and the ground glistens, [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum)  presents a journey into stories, traditions and cultural significance. Exhibits carefully tucked within the museum date as far back as 40,000 years and hold deep meaning. Allow the rich history held here offer a contemplative contrast to the grey day beyond the glass.

### Win prizes under the neon arcade lights

Inside the arcade at [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf), there’s a bright kaleidoscope of colour that draws you in when skies are silver. Let your brood loose for hours of full tilt winter fun. There are retro pinball machines to take you back in time and teach the young ones a few tricks, claw machines to grab prizes, and racing games to get everyone buzzing. Here, warmth comes from the joy of playful chaos and the making of shared memories.

### Curl up and catch a film

As an intermission to island explorations or to wind up an adventurous day, slip into the cotton deckchairs inside [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf). Family-friendly flicks are showing daily at the historic Picture Hall. Unfurl your blankets like sails and settle in for a few hours of blissful escapism – complete with handfuls of warm buttered popcorn and sweet treats from the candy bar.

* Where to Snorkel at Rottnest Island: Six of the Best Spots

# Where to Snorkel at Rottnest Island: Six of the Best Spots

Dive into the world beneath the waves for a snorkelling adventure at these lesser-known wonders.

3 minutes

Image Schools of fish

Schools of fish

**Dive in and find yourself amongst some of the world’s most unique marine gardens.**

The waters surrounding Wadjemup / Rottnest Island are home to numerous snorkelling spots featuring tropical fish, [coral gardens](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/5-coral-species-you-can-spot-at-rottnest-island), and even shipwrecks that are sure to fascinate.

While you may have heard of popular spots like [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), why not wander beyond the well-travelled path? Grab your snorkel and head to these spots to submerge yourself in a world of vibrant marine life and dazzling underwater landscapes. These lesser-explored spots promise not only unforgettable adventures but also a deeper connection with the ocean’s wonders.

[Take Care When Snorkelling and Diving

Take care when snorkelling and diving and note that spearguns and handspears are not permitted in the Marine Reserve.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### Henrietta Rocks

If you like a touch of mystery with your underwater explorations, grab your mask and snorkel and head to [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks). Here, just 50 metres from the shore, lies an intriguing shipwreck which hosts a whole range of fascinating sea creatures. With shallow waters all around, it's the perfect spot for snorkelling fun, whether you're a first-timer or a seasoned explorer.

**How to get there:** Henrietta Rocks is located on the south-east corner of Wadjemup, about 3 km from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay). Hop off at Stop 3 if you’re taking the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus. Or it’s an easy [cycle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from Thomson Bay along the coast, which will take you approximately 10 minutes, depending on how fast you pedal.

Image Henrietta Rocks

[Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks)

### Parker Point

You might be familiar with the panoramic views from [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point)’s iconic stairs and the picturesque sight of boats gently swaying on the water here. Yet, beneath the surface you’ll also find an underwater playground teeming with a variety of djildjit (fish) and a [vibrant pink coral reef](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/5-coral-species-you-can-spot-at-rottnest-island). This striking aquatic landscape owes its allure to its protected status as a designated [marine sanctuary zone](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones).

Parker Point also features its own [snorkel trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail), a series of information panels carefully installed on the seabed that will tell you all about the sea life you may meet in the waters here.

**How to get there:** Easily accessible by bicycle, Parker Point is approximately 5 km from the main settlement or a 17-minute cycle. Or simply hop on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and get off at Stop 5. For the more nautically inclined, you can even get there [by boat](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-private-boat), as it provides ideal anchorage conditions.

Image The wooden staircase down to the glossy clear waters of Parker Point Bay.

[Snorkel at Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point)

### Rocky Bay

Venture towards the western end of the island where you’ll find a narrow stretch of land connecting the two halves of Rottnest Island. It’s here that you’ll find [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay) - the perfect place to get away from the crowds for a peaceful snorkel. This coastal haven is home to an undulating rocky expanse that gives way to crystal clear blue lagoons. Dive under and you’ll find yourself surrounded by a vibrant community of marine life, from schools of colourful fish to gardens of coral reef formations. If luck is on your side, you might just run into an elusive booyi (sea turtle), stingray, or octopus.

**How to get there:** Depending on the route you take, Rocky Bay is 10-14 kms away from the main settlement and a 30–45-minute [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) ride, depending on how fast you ride, and how often you stop to take in the views on your journey. Alternatively, you can take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off at Stop 13 and take the short walk down to Rocky Bay.

Image Boats on the crystal blue waters with visitors sunbathing on the sands of Rocky Bay Beach at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

[Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay)

### Little Armstrong Bay

Picture a peaceful bay with gently lapping waves and inviting shallows – perfect for little ones or those new to the underwater world. As you wade further out, the bay’s depths increase, offering greater adventure for experienced swimmers. For an added hint of wonder, you’ll also have an opportunity at [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay) to encounter unique species that call the surrounding marine sanctuary home.

**How to get there:** Jump on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and get off at Stop 17. Alternatively, hop on a [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) and take the 4 km, 13-minute ride from the main settlement – although we suggest being prepared for a longer journey, depending on how often you stop to admire the iconic beaches and bays along the way.

Image -130_lr.tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=308a72a2_1)

[Swim and snorkel at Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay)

### Little Parakeet Bay

A great option for younger children with its shallow water and calm conditions, this serene bay is home to a wealth of marine life, including charming little, blue-scaled fish, graceful starfish and the occasional stingray.

**How to get there:** [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay) is not far from the main settlement, about 3 km away and a 12-minute cycle depending on how fast you pedal. It’s also on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus route — just hop off at Stop 18 and walk the last few hundred metres. Or travel on the [accommodation shuttle bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) to [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) and walk the rest of the way from there.

Image Little Parakeet Bay

[Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay)

Reef Care

Please avoid walking on any reef as this can damage the fragile environment and the marine species that inhabit these areas.

### Fay’s Bay

[Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay) boasts lush green maambakoort djooraly (seagrass meadows), which are able to flourish within the safety of a shallow limestone reef. This reef is also riddled with caves and channels, providing a twisting, turning playground for schools of colourful fish and sea life. With calm waters, it makes it an ideal spot for beginner snorkellers to explore and enjoy.

**How to get there:** Fay’s Bay sits between [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) and is located about 2 km away from the main settlement. It’s an easy 30-minute stroll or an 8-minute cycle, depending on how energetic you feel. Alternatively, you can jump aboard the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off at Stop 19 (Geordie Bay) and walk the short distance to the bay from there.

Image Fay's Bay

[Fay's Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay)

# Discover the Perfect Gift for the Island Lover in Your Life

Give the gift of experience with a voucher to redeem on overnight stays, oceanside dining, memorable tours and activities, and ferry transfers.

5 minutes

Image 

Aerial of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

**Treat someone special to an experience gift on Rottnest Island.**

Gift your loved ones an adventure on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, where every moment is a treasure. Choose from a range of gift vouchers that open the door to a world of unforgettable experiences, tailored to every taste and interest. Whether your special someone seeks thrilling escapades, serene relaxation, or a deep dive into natural wonders, these vouchers promise memories that will last a lifetime.

### TOURS

For adventure seekers, ocean lovers, and nature enthusiasts who crave an unforgettable experience that will last a lifetime.

[**Charter 1**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1)**:** Treat a special someone to a day soaking up the sun onboard the sunshine yellow catamaran, Capella.
Choose from a full day sail to Rottnest Island from Fremantle for $269, a Rottnest Island snorkel and sail for $175, or an amount from $50 to $500 to use on any Charter 1 tour and receive your voucher directly via email.

[**Rottnest Air-Taxi**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi)**:** Experience breathtaking aerial views of the island with scenic joy flights or transfers between Perth and Rottnest Island.
Choose from a private round trip for up to three passengers for $600 and $750 for 4-6 passengers, a 10-minute scenic flight for $110, $199 for 20-minutes and $299 for 35-minutes, or an amount from $100 to $600 to use on any Rottnest Air-Taxi flight. Your voucher will be sent via email and is valid for three years from date of purchase.

[**Rottnest Cruises**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises)**:** For a truly indulgent gift, spoil a loved one with an experience onboard a premium charter boat where they’ll enjoy a decadent sea-to-plate 7-course meal experience.
Choose anywhere from $50 to $300 and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Rottnest Snorkel**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-snorkel)**:** Surprise the ocean-lover in your life with a snorkel adventure. Guided by marine experts, they’ll explore the island’s underwater playground, which is home to hundreds of fish and stunning coral reefs.
Choose a custom amount up to $10,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Segway Tours WA**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa)**:** Give the gift of a fun-filled and effortless tour around the island with scenic and educational off-road segway tours for ages 12 and above. Choose from a $98, $139, or $175 voucher to use on any of the Rottnest Island Segway tours. Your voucher will be emailed free of charge, or printed and posted to you for a small additional fee.

[**Skydive Geronimo**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/skydive-geronimo)**:** For the ultimate adrenaline seeker. Tandem freefall before gliding over the island giving you a moment to take it all in before landing on the soft sand.
There are a variety of voucher options available, from all-inclusive options with video and photos included and ferry transfers from $439 to $826, or custom amounts from $100 to $300 all delivered straight to your email.

[**The Hike Collective**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective)**:** Give the gift of nature with a guided hiking tour around the island traversing unique landscapes and engaging all fitness levels with stories of the island’s history and nature.
Choose anywhere from $25 to $200 and receive your voucher directly by email. Valid for three years from date of purchase.

[**Rotto Rickshaws**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rotto-rickshaws)**:** Treat someone to an effortless and breathtaking adventure tour around the island with a 90-minute rickshaw ride. Sit back and relax as you take in stunning coastal views, encounter local wildlife, discover the island's history and visit historical landmarks. Choose an amount from $59.50, $74.50, or $219 and receive your voucher directly by email.

**[**Eco Express Boat Tours**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours):** Experience the island's wild side with a scenic boat tour around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Choose the Adventure Boat Tour from $79 where you'll get expert commentary and opportunities to spot wildlife in the warm morning sunlight or a custom amount from $20 to $4,999 and receive directly by email.

### 

### ACCOMMODATION

For those who want to extend their visit and enjoy the island for longer.

[**Discovery Resorts – Rottnest Island**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island)**:** Treat someone special to the ultimate escape with eco-luxury glamping nestled behind the iconic Pinky Beach. Simply choose your desired amount, from $50 to $500, and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Samphire Rottnest**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest)**:** Gift a stay at this boutique accommodation that seamlessly blends nature and luxury, offering a tranquil escape with stunning island views.
Choose anywhere from $25 to $2,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

**[**The Lodge Wadjemup**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup):** Surprise your loved ones with an escape that blends modern comfort and timeless heritage with picturesque views of the island. Choose anywhere from $50 to $2,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

### EAT & DRINK

For the foodie in your life.

[**Hotel Rottnest**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest)**:** Delight someone with views across Thomson Bay and pub classics at Hotel Rottnest - the perfect spot to relax, sip and socialise.
Choose anywhere from $25 to $2,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Isola Bar e Cibo**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest)**:** Give a delicious gift of a dining experience at this fresh take on a classic Italian beachside bar, complete with beautiful views of Thomson Bay.
Choose anywhere from $50 to $300 and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Lontara**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara)**:** Immerse a loved one in a sensory culinary journey at Lontara, where South East Asian-inspired dishes and world-class wines await.
Choose anywhere from $25 to $2,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

[**Dome Café**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe)**:** Perfect for families, a voucher to Dome offers crowd-pleasing classic meals, just a short stroll from the main jetty.
Choose anywhere from $10 to $150 and receive your voucher via the post for an additional fee.

[**Boost Mobeel**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/boost-mobeel-rottnest)**:** The perfect treat to cool down and refuel on your favourite juices, crushes, and smoothies all summer long.
Choose from a $20 or $50 voucher and receive it via the post.

[**Frankie’s on Rotto**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto)**:** A laidback family-friendly spot serving up handmade sourdough pizzas and Italian-inspired fare in the heart of the settlement.
Choose anywhere from $25 to $200 and receive your voucher directly by email.

**[**Sunsets Bar & Dining**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest):** Gift a relaxed dining experience that has something for everyone, with Mediterranean flavours and a handpicked menu of signature drinks. Choose anywhere from $50 to $2,000 and receive your voucher directly by email.

**[**Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery):** A delightful family-friendly cafe and art gallery, offering breakfast classics to milkshakes and burgers. Choose anywhere from $25 to $200 and receive your voucher directly by email.

**[**HAVZA**](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza):** For those who love Mediterranean-inspired dishes with an ocean view of The Basin. Choose anywhere from $50 to $300 and receive your voucher directly by email.

### FERRIES

Travelling to Rottnest Island by ferry is the most popular way to reach this beautiful destination. With three ferry operators to choose from, you can treat your loved ones to a ferry transfer. Gift vouchers are available for departures from Fremantle, Perth City, and Hillarys with [Rottnest Express](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-express), [SeaLink Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sealink-rottnest), and [Rottnest Fast Ferries](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-fast-ferries).

### Tips for a time well spent

# Your Guide to Geordie Bay

Immerse yourself in the wonders of Geordie Bay for a visit filled with adventure and relaxation.

6 minutes

Image 

Geordie Bay

**Just beyond the main settlement, Geordie Bay awaits, offering a unique and serene escape from the hustle and bustle of Thomson Bay.**

This special spot is perfect for spending a memorable visit to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, with its stunning beaches, scenic [cycling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-rotto-mini-loop--4-km-of-easy--scenic-cycling) and [hiking trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi), options to satisfy your hunger, and [accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained). There’s a unique kind of peace here that makes Geordie Bay truly special.

### Discover Geordie Bay

[Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) is more than just a convenient stop; it’s a place where you can truly unwind and savour the unique experience it offers.

As one of the largest beaches on the island, Geordie Bay boasts a stunning curve of white sand and bright blue water, ideal for a day at the beach. Wade into the bay for excellent snorkelling opportunities, where you can come face to face with schools of fish and the occasional passing stingray.

When it’s time to refuel, visit [Geordie Bay Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) to enjoy delicious food surrounded by local art that captures the island’s natural beauty. Snacks and other supplies are easily accessible from the [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store), and, in the warmer months, don’t miss out on a refreshing scoop of ice cream from [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery).

For those staying longer than a day, [Stay Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained) offers a variety of recently refurbished self-contained accommodation to become your home away from home. A great choice for groups and families, each unit is just steps away from the bay, with balconies that offer breathtaking views of the vast northern Indian Ocean.

Image 

[Cycle through salt lakes towards Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes)

[Stay Rottnest Accommodation at Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained)

Image 

[Geordie Bay at sunset](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay)

Image A long metal pier extends over shallow turquoise water towards the deeper blue ocean. The sky is clear and bright blue. Boats are anchored in the distance, and a small rocky island is visible on the horizon.

[Geordie Bay jetty](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay)

Image 

[Spot quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

### 

### Where to eat

Whether you’re in the mood for a meal, a quick snack, or a refreshing treat, you’ll find plenty of options to satisfy your cravings. Enjoy a variety of tasty bites and beverages that perfectly complement a day spent by the beach.

#### Geordie Bay Cafe & Art Gallery

There’s lots to love about [Geordie’s Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery). Amongst the work of talented local artists, Geordie’s serve up everything from fresh juices and salads to old school shakes and burgers in their art gallery restaurant. Open for breakfast and lunch daily, and dinner on select days, Geordie’s is also fully licensed, making it a top spot to indulge in a feast for both the eyes and the taste buds.

#### Geordie Bay General Store

Stock up for a delightful DIY feast with a visit to the charming [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store). This one-stop shop offers a selection of fresh fruit and vegetables, succulent meats made for a post-swim barbecue, and an array of seafood. You’ll also find tempting snacks, and other pantry staples you might need for an extended stay in the area. Plus, if you're an [avid fisherman](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing), you’re set with a selection of bait and tackle for a spot of fishing off the Geordie Bay jetty.

Whether you're swinging by for a few items, forgotten essentials or prefer the convenience of a pre-ordered grocery delivery, Geordie Bay General Store ensures you’re well stocked for your visit.

#### Kuld Creamery

The perfect complement to your day of sun, sand, and sea, is a cool scoop of ice cream from [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery). Indulge in their unique and unexpected ice cream flavours, each crafted to impress and sure to leave your taste buds wanting more.

#### HAVZA

If you’re visiting over the warmer months, take a short trip from Geordie Bay to discover [HAVZA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza), where Mediterranean vibes meet the beautiful shores of [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin).

During the day, this pop-up gem serves up beloved Simmo’s ice cream and aromatic coffee. As evening falls, HAVZA transforms, offering a mouthwatering selection of tapas that blend the rich flavours of the Aegean Sea with the best local produce from Western Australia. These dishes are made to be enjoyed by hand and shared, all while soaking in the ocean views. Whether you’re cooling off with ice cream or diving into a Mediterranean feast, HAVZA promises a delicious adventure with a view.

Image Couple eating at Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery with art prints on wall behind them of Rottnest Island beaches

[Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/geordies-cafe-art-gallery)

[Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/kuld-creamery)

[Shopping at Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/geordie-bay-general-store)

Image 

[HAVZA at The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/havza)

### 

### HOW TO GET TO GEORDIE BAY

#### Cycle to Geordie Bay

You have two picturesque options to choose from to reach Geordie Bay [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) — the coastal route and the path through the [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). If you choose the coastal pedal, you’ll be treated to some of the island’s most iconic views, passing by [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) and [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) before arriving at your destination.

Alternatively, follow Digby Drive and Geordie Bay Road through the salt lakes, where you can witness serene stillness and [birdlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching) before reaching Geordie Bay. Both routes are about the same distance at just over 2 km, which will take you approximately seven minutes (depending on how fast you pedal!). Choose your path based on your preference for scenery and enjoy the ride.

#### Bus to Geordie Bay

Alternatively, the [accommodation shuttle bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) offers a swift and convenient journey between [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), Geordie Bay, Kingstown, and the airport. This service offers a hassle-free way to travel the island, ensuring you can soak in the scenery without a worry.

For those with a sense of adventure, explore the further reaches of the island on the [Island Explorer bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour). This hop-on-hop-off service travels around the entire island, stopping at 19 different locations, with Geordie Bay being the final stop on the loop.

### 

### More beaches nearby

While spending the day at [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), you can also venture out to explore and experience more bays nearby, adding extra beauty to your island adventure.

#### Fay’s Bay

Just east of Geordie Bay lies [Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay), a small cove tucked between high limestone rock outcrops providing shelter against wind and rougher waters. Wade into the water with your snorkel and mask to discover the caves and channels teeming with colourful fish and intriguing sea life. With its calm waters, Fay's Bay is an ideal spot for kids and beginner snorkellers to explore.

#### Longreach Bay

Just next to Fay’s Bay is [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay), renowned as one of Rottnest Island’s most beloved family beach destinations. Its expansive shoreline adorned with soft white sand, while the calm turquoise water glistens under the sun’s rays. Here, you'll find shelter from prevailing winds, allowing for a peaceful beach experience. As you explore the crystal-clear waters, you’ll encounter a diverse array of fish species and the occasional stingray gracefully gliding above the seabed, often visible from the shoreline.

#### Little Parakeet Bay

West of Geordie Bay, nestled over the rising dunes and tucked behind a rocky outcrop, is [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay). Protected by a submerged coral reef, Little Parakeet Bay boasts shallow waters and calmer conditions, making it a great choice for families with smaller children. As you dip into the bay's clear blue waters, you'll encounter a vibrant underwater world teeming with life. Dive beneath the surface and you may encounter small blue-scaled fish, such as the Miller’s damsel fish, along with sea stars and the odd stingray.

* Your Guide to Snorkelling the Warm Waters of Wadjemup

# Your Guide to Snorkelling the Warm Waters of Wadjemup

As you snorkel through the diversity of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s waters, you find yourself amongst the world’s most unique marine gardens.

5 minutes

Image Snorkelling

Snorkelling

**When you dive into the warm waters of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, you meet the most unique marine gardens. Tropical fish, stingrays, octopus, and even the occasional dolphin pod; for a moment in time you become immersed in their world.**

> “Snorkelling around an island is full of opportunities that you just can’t find on the mainland,” says Annabelle, marine biologist and [Rottnest Snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-snorkel) guide. “It’s all about the diversity of the underwater ecosystems and the range of coral and fish species that dwell in each region.”

### Warm currents and limestone homes

The Leeuwin Current flows down from Indonesia, stimulating the growth of tropical coral around the island's marine gardens. This current also increases the water temperature by four degrees compared to the coast of Western Australia, expanding your experiences underwater.

Wadjemup was once connected to this mainland and, since sea levels rose and created a new land mass, the limestone ridges have eroded over time. These foundational changes have created intriguing caves and a thriving home base for algae, seagrass, and [coral species](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/5-coral-species-you-can-spot-at-rottnest-island); landscapes unique to Rottnest Island that offer endless opportunities for discovery.

Image Colourful Corals Found in the Waters of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Pink coral

### The diversity of island snorkelling

Snorkelling beneath the surface of island waters is unique. There are the [tropical corals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/5-coral-species-you-can-spot-at-rottnest-island) and [fish species](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see) on the south side, and the deeper waters of the north attract bigger fish and stingrays. Embarking on a snorkelling adventure around an island like Wadjemup also means that there is always somewhere sheltered to go.

“When the wind and swell are high on one side, we can find calm waters on the other side of the island. There are always protected spots and ideal snorkelling conditions to be found,” says Jesse Pesch, Rottnest Snorkel. “Island snorkelling means that we can travel just 20 minutes by boat and be in a whole new marine environment.”

###### Snorkelling amongst tropical fish and coral on the south side

The popular snorkelling spots in the south — Salmon Bay and [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) — are where you will find yourself in an underwater world reminiscent of Hawaii or the Caribbean Sea. Swimming amongst the vast seagrass and kelp beds, which carpet the homes of 135 species of tropical fish, will begin to feel as common as passing suburban grassed ovals.

Wrasse, dusky morwong, and big schools of black bream are common sightings, swimming past as you admire each new species of coral. There’s lilac-coloured cauliflower or brain coral, turquoise and pale pink branching coral, and plate coral — these flat discs may not burst through the colour palette, but they have the unique ability to swell their flesh and move autonomously around the ocean floor.

###### Observing larger fish and stingrays in deeper, northern waters

When you venture to the island's north side, you will swim in deeper waters that attract bigger fish and even stingrays. [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) and [Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay) are built on limestone caves that tempt deeper sea snorkellers and divers. Closer to the shore, those skimming the surface will spot emerging crayfish, burrowing stingrays, and even a gloomy octopus (Octopus tetricus) or two.

“Octopuses are territorial so they will always return to the same rock or crevasse, making them easy to find around the island,” explains Anabel. “We often get to see the octopus changing the colour, and even texture, of their skin within a matter of seconds. From maroon brown to kelp green, rough limestone to silken seagrass. It’s magic.”

Image A beach with white sand, turquoise water, and three anchored sailboats. The horizon shows a distant green landmass under a clear blue sky.

Parker Point

Image Fish

Schools of fish

### Unforgettable moments with underwater wildlife

While a gloomy octopus encounter is high on the experience list for snorkellers, stingrays, dolphins, and even a passing [whale migration](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) are all possible sightings.

“When you venture out on the Rottnest Snorkel boat from Thomson Bay, you get access to underwater areas that you just can’t reach from the shore. We will often have dolphins playing at the bow as we slowly make our way around the island and, when in season, we spot whales migrating in the distance.”

“There was one occasion in the waters of Parker Point where we got to witness up to eight stingrays cruising along the ocean floor. They would whip up the sand, burrow in, and then peacefully keep swimming,” says Jesse. “They’re actually quite curious and will come close if they feel safe.”

### Playing your part in marine conservation

Like the land, the waters of Wadjemup are protected. There are five [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones) that require strict conservation efforts to keep them thriving; it’s vital that everyone plays their part.

* Look but don’t touch (or take) – Rottnest Island’s reef and coral systems are delicate so it’s important that you don’t touch, break, or stand on the reef at any time. And as the saying goes, take only memories.
* Reduce high traffic – Small group tours are necessary to help reduce the human impact on sanctuary zones. Joining an organised snorkelling tour will ensure that the correct numbers are counted.
* Safe waste disposal – No rubbish should ever go into the sea, and you should also wear reef-safe sunscreen if you plan to swim, snorkel, or dive.
* Take time to get educated – With a guided snorkelling tour, you learn about the underwater environment you’re about to enter. This knowledge will include the right techniques to snorkel within a marine sanctuary zone.

"With a marine biologist guiding your snorkelling adventure, you really learn how to avoid putting unnecessary stress on the coral. Because, without a healthy coral ecosystem, smaller fish won’t have the habitats, food, and protection they need. And without small fish species, the larger fish won’t venture into the reef looking for food,” says Annabelle. “It’s all working in a delicate balance.”

Image Rottnest Snorkel

Rottnest Snorkel boat

Image Rottnest Snorkel

Swimming with Rottnest Snorkel

### Going deeper

For those with a penchant for diving, you’ll find limestone ledges and drop-offs that grow fascinating coral formations. And caves that were once part of the earth connected to the mainland. These underwater valleys are sanctuaries for marine life and rival some of the best diving spots in Western Australia and around the world.

> Snorkelling is a call to silence. A chance to witness the incredible workings of an entire ecosystem that you can’t experience unless you merge with it. Calm, still, and slow. Underwater, you’re part of it all.

### Tips for a time well spent

Make your visit even more meaningful with helpful advice from those in the know.

# Parakeet Bay

## A secluded sandy stretch

A secluded stretch of beach on the northern tip of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, Parakeet Bay is the bigger sister to Little Parakeet Bay. Just around the rocky outcrop, past the teeming dunes, pristine white sand gives way to sparkling azure water.

It’s a calm, tranquil beach and ideal for families. Shallow, well-protected waters provide safe conditions for newer swimmers. Or lay down a towel for a long, lazy afternoon in the sun.

The sandy-bottomed beach gives way to large swathes of underwater rocks, making it a safe haven for a variety of curious sea life. You might even spot a friendly stingray here or there as you drift underneath the waves.

### You might also see

Image 

Stunning blue water

Image 

Serene swimming conditions

Image 

Spot the friendly stingrays

Image 

Hike the Gabbi Karniny Bidi

### Where to find Parakeet Bay

One of Wadjemup’s northernmost beaches, Parakeet Bay accessible by bus. Take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off at Stop 18, then walk the 400 metres to the beach. Close to the main townsite, it’s just 12 minutes [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from the Thomson Bay settlement, and only five minutes from Geordie Bay.

Hikers can access Parakeet Bay via the [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi).

Image Boats, Parakeet Bay

[Boating](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/boating)

### For land-dwellers and seafarers alike

Parakeet Bay is a favourite for boating enthusiasts. Much calmer and quieter than the more popular beaches, the bay offers a gentle, sheltered spot to pull up at a mooring or lower the anchor. Lounge on the side of the boat and watch the fish swim by, or throw on the snorkel, slip into the calming blue swell, and explore a glittering undersea world.

[Learn more about boating](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Boating)

[Beware of Coastal Hazards

It’s important to note the coastal environment of Rottnest Island is fragile. Keep clear of the limestone cliffs here as they can be unstable and may collapse. To avoid dune erosion, please remain on designated tracks. See here for more Practical Tips.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

Image Parakeet Bay, Rottnest Island

Parakeet Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are available at Parakeet Bay?

There are no facilities available at Parakeet Bay, but it’s just a five-minute cycle (or 20-minute walk) away from the Geordie Bay facilities.

Are there any shaded areas at Parakeet Bay?

Parakeet Bay is entirely in the sun, until the later afternoon when the rocky outcrop on the western side of the beach starts to throw shadows down onto the beach. So be sure to bring an umbrella and sunscreen!

Can I fish at Parakeet Bay?

Shore-based fishing is permitted by means of a rod and line, or hand-held line, but no spear fishing or net fishing is allowed.

# Quokkas

## Home of the iconic quokka

Native to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, the quokka, or kwoka in Noongar, is an icon of the island.

Their story is literally written in the land. The name ‘Rottnest’ comes from 17th-century Dutch explorers who considered the animals to be large rats and bestowed the island, ‘Rat’s Nest’.

These curious and cheerful marsupials are recognised around the world, and it’s worth the journey across just to see them in their natural habitat.

### Some facts about these curious critters

Image 

Native to the island

Image 

A type of small wallaby

Image 

Mainly nocturnal

Image 

They can climb trees

### Quokka spotting for all seasons

On Wadjemup, you’re amongst the world’s largest quokka population with family groups found right across the island.

The quokkas have plenty of natural resources and no natural predators, so you’ll never be short of opportunities to experience them regardless of the time of year.

Nocturnal by nature, they spend most of the day sleeping and resting under shady bushes, but can easily be seen lazing around the island. Early mornings and late afternoons see most quokkas out and about, in various spots across the island.

During August, you can experience the childlike joy of seeing little joeys poking their heads out of their mothers’ pouches; come September, you can watch them take their first hops out into the world.

For an informative quokka experience with an educational focus, take one of the  [free guided quokka tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) and see them up close while learning some interesting facts about this iconic animal.

For the best opportunity to experience a quokka in its natural environment, read our [guide on quokka spotting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) in any season.

Image Quokka joey

Quokka joey

### Welcoming new life in spring

Like other marsupials, such as kangaroos, wallabies, wallaroos, bettongs, and potoroos, female quokkas carry their young in pouches.

During the cooler months on the island, the quokkas seem to take on a new personality. They are no longer in pursuit of shelter from the hot Australian sun and are more easily spotted throughout the day, particularly early in the morning and late in the afternoon. This is because the mornings stay cooler longer and the afternoons cool down earlier, meaning you don’t have to get up as early or stay out as late as you would in summer.

Quokkas give birth in late summer and their young remain in the pouch until August or September. From June, the mother quokka’s pouch becomes heavier and by September, you could catch a glimpse of a baby quokka (known as a joey) taking its first hops into the world. After about one-and-a-half to two years of age, the quokka reaches maturity, reaching a size similar to a house cat and living to about ten years of age.

Image Mother quokka and baby quokka joey

Quokka and baby joey

### Preserving and protecting the world’s largest quokka population

Despite quokka populations continuing to thrive on the island, due to the abundant resources and lack of predators, they are still a vulnerable species.

To ensure we protect the quokka from becoming endangered, continued monitoring from the island’s rangers helps keep the population thriving.

You can do your part to help protect the island’s iconic marsupial by following some key guidelines:

* Observe the quokkas from a safe distance
* Don’t touch them
* Let them forage for their own food instead of feeding them
* Stick to the paths

[Read more about how to play your part in quokka conservation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

Image Quokka

[A quokka in its natural environment](/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

### Become a quokka conservation hero

You can show your support for Rottnest Island’s famous furry inhabitants by purchasing one of [Rottnest Foundation’s](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/) adoption kits that fund conservation initiatives on the island.

Your kit comes with a cuddly, life-sized soft quokka toy, tote bag, quokka fact sheet and an official adoption certificate.

[Learn more about the Adopt-a-Quokka Kits](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/shop/p/adopt-a-quokka)

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I find quokkas?

On Rottnest Island, you’re amongst the world’s largest quokka population with family groups found right across the island. Check out [our guide to spotting quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) on the island – from the main settlement to further afield.

What do quokkas eat?

Quokkas are herbivores so they eat a variety of plants such as leaves, seeds, and shrub buds, which is available in abundance on Rottnest Island. As a vulnerable species, it is illegal to feed the quokka (or any animal on the island) as any food and water that they haven’t collected themselves can be harmful to their health and wellbeing.

Why do quokkas smile?

Quokkas have earned a global reputation for themselves as “the happiest animal in the world”. But it’s not just their perpetually smiling appearance that makes them seem cheerful - a result of the shape of their face and panting habit - but also their idyllic island home. With abundant resources and a lack of natural predators on the island, Rottnest Island is home to the world’s largest population of quokkas. Learn more about these incredible creatures and how to have your own memorable encounter with them in the wild in our [Guide to Quokka Spotting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island).

Do quokkas only live on Rottnest Island?

Rottnest Island has the world’s largest wild quokka population, but you can also find quokkas in some zoos across Australia. A very small population also lives in the south-west of mainland Western Australia.

Can quokkas swim?

No, quokkas can’t swim but they are known to climb trees to find food.

What time do quokkas come out?

Quokkas are nocturnal and will spend most of the day sleeping and resting under shady bushes. Early mornings and late afternoons are the best times to see quokkas out and about.

Are quokkas endangered?

Quokkas are a vulnerable species. To ensure we protect the quokka from becoming endangered, continued monitoring from the island’s rangers helps keep the population thriving. You can do your part too:

* Observe the quokkas from a safe distance
* Don't touch them
* Let them forage for their own food instead of feeding them
* Stick to the paths

Anyone who deliberately interferes with (including feeding) wildlife on Rottnest Island will be fined on the spot under the *Rottnest Island Regulations 1988* and potentially prosecuted under the *Wildlife Conservation Act 1950* with fines up to $10,000. Acts of animal cruelty may result in fines up to $50,000 and five years imprisonment under the *Animal Welfare Act 2002*.

What other wildlife can be found on Rottnest Island?

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is full of [wildlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/nature-wildlife) you won’t find on the mainland. There are six distinct habitats that are abundant with animal, bird, and sea life, from lively scrub heath to the serene woodlands, the vibrant wetlands and expansive ocean.

Amongst the scrub you can spot countless bush birds including the golden whistler, red-capped robin, silvereye, and singing honeyeaters. On the lakes and in the skies, there are Australian shelducks, bridled and crested terns, waders, red-necked phalaropes, wedge-tailed shearwaters, and magnificent ospreys.

Dive under the sparkling water to find over 135 species of tropical fish. Plus, the wider ocean is home to migrating humpback whales, long-nosed fur seals, bottlenose dolphins, and Australian sea lions.

Lakeside, listen for amphibians like the moaning frog, motorbike frog, and squelching froglets. On the trails, keep an eye out for reptiles like bobtails and the king skink. And of course, watch the world-famous quokkas as they roam the natural landscape.

What are common misspellings of "Quokka," and how do you pronounce it?

The word "quokka" is often misspelled due to its unique pronunciation. Pronounced *“kwok-uh”*, the name can sometimes be tricky to spell. Common misspellings of "quokka" include:

* Qokka
* Qoukka
* Quaka
* Quakka
* Quikka
* Qukka
* Quoakka
* Quocka
* Quoka
* Quakkas
* Quokas

# Your Guide to Wetting a Line on Rottnest Island

Your guide to fishing on Rottnest Island. For kids, amateurs, and experts, there’s a perfect spot waiting for your cast.

5 minutes

Image Fishing at Rottnest Island

Fishing at Rottnest Island

**No matter the season, it’s hard to beat the quiet stillness and easy patience that goes with a spot of fishing. As the weather begins to cool on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, meaty squid, hungry pink snapper, and the annual salmon run offer ample opportunity for all anglers.**

And with numerous headlands, beaches, and reefs to choose from, you’ll have no trouble finding your patch — especially in winter.

Wherever you choose, remember this: leave nothing behind, never take more than you need, respect the space of other visitors, and always give due respect to the [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones). Stopping at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) to familiarise yourself with the guidelines of each zone will ensure the island’s vibrant underwater world continues to flourish and that there’ll be plenty of bounty left for future expeditions.

> You can bring all your fishing gear from home and buy any extras you need (including bait) from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) in Thomson Bay and Geordie Bay.

### Family (and beginner) friendly bays

For those with small fries in tow, banking on beginner’s luck, or who are in it for the serenity as much as anything else, pull up a deck chair – the jetty life is for you.

**Thomson Bay jetties**

The jetties in [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) are some of the most popular fishing spots for families. Schools of herring present just the right amount of challenge to young arms and if beginner’s luck fails you, you’re just a short stroll from the main settlement and an easy-won (but just as enjoyable) plate of [fish and chips](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink).

[Staying overnight](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay)? Park yourselves on the jetty and try your luck at a spot of squidding. The lights of Hotel Jetty attract squid in large numbers and if nothing else, they’re amazing to watch.

> When fishing on the island’s jetties, stay aware of who you’re sharing the space with. Other jetty users will be pulling boats alongside or swimming nearby, and it’s important to respect their space. Also, keep your gear tidy, as birds like pelicans often try to steal bait or catches and this can lead to dangerous entanglements in fishing lines.

**Geordie Bay**

One of the great advantages of fishing on an island? It’s never too difficult to find a shoreline sheltered from the wind. Just a short bike from the main settlement you’ll find [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), one of the island’s most beautiful spots.

You’ll find plenty of herring here but there’s plenty of table fish on offer too — think skippy, tailor, silver bream, whiting, and even the occasional founder or flathead foraging on the bottom.

**Ricey Beach**

Once you’ve got all the gear and some idea, then you’re ready to get your feet wet on a more remote beach. Ride out towards [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) and you’ll find [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach), where those with their eyes on a bigger prize set up camp. This stretch of beach offers all the spoils of Thomson and Geordie Bays as well as the elusive and highly sought-after mulloway.

Image A person stands on a wooden pier holding a fishing rod over the water. Two others sit on the edge of the pier. The background shows a sandy beach with vegetation and structures under a partly cloudy sky.

[Jetty fishing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing)

Image Rottnest Island Jetty

[Fishing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing)

Staying Safe When You’re Fishing

It’s important to be prepared for changes in the weather and ocean conditions while you’re fishing, and wearing a lifejacket if required. Also, if you have children joining you, ensure they are always supervised.

**Casting out from afar**

Taking your fishing to the depths of the ocean? You can bring your own boat to the island and enjoy the freedom to head out into open waters. You'll have the chance to haul in impressive catches, including maran (western rock lobster).

**West End**

Some of Western Australia’s most revered species abound in the prolific [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). Keen anglers here can take on breaksea cod, dhufish, pink snapper, samson fish, and world-class sport fish such as Spanish mackerel, yellowtail kingfish, and dolphin fish (mahi-mahi).

Just a few kilometres off West End, the continental shelf drops away and apex predators including several species of shark can be found… this adventure is not for the faint-hearted or inexperienced.

> While here, be aware of the sanctuary zone that encompasses Radar Reef, Cape Vlamingh, and Cathedral Rocks. Shore-based fishing, with a rod, line, or hand-held line, is permitted along the platform of Radar Reef and you’re allowed to fish for pelagic fish (those found near the middle or surface of the ocean) from your boat.

**Phillip Rock**

Seafarers don’t need to drift beyond the continental shelf in search of a challenge – plenty of action can be found closer to the island. Schools of herring, squid and even salmon can be found in all of the bays, while sitting between Thomson Bay and Kingston Reef at Phillip Rock can be a particularly good hideout for King George whiting.

### Places to explore without your fishing rod

There’s no fishing permitted at [Little Salmon Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-salmon-bay), so leave your rod behind when enjoying these waters.

Daylight fishing is prohibited at [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). Reserve casting out for the quiet evening and visit these spots for a swim instead during the day.

Whatever your style or level of luck on the day, few activities are as rewarding as a day’s fishing. For many it’s more than a bit of fun, it’s like a tonic for the soul; a rare chance to remember you are part of this delicate – but beautiful – ecosystem.

Find out more about the island’s [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones) and [boating permits](https://ria.wa.gov.au/boating) before you arrive for your fishing vacation.

For more information visit the Department of Fisheries and familiarise yourself with the [recreational fishing rules](http://rules.fish.wa.gov.au/).

# Ferry Transfer FAQ

Schools planning a visit to Rottnest Island can choose to travel with any ferry operator. All operators offer discounted fares for school groups, with terms and conditions varying by provider. Schools should contact their preferred ferry operator directly to discuss fares, schedules, and travel arrangements.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What ferry discounts are available to schools?

All schools can request discounted group fares from ferry operators, subject to each operator’s terms and conditions. Discounts and eligibility requirements vary between providers, so schools should contact their preferred ferry operator directly for details.

Which ferry operators can schools use?

Schools may book with any ferry operator servicing Rottnest Island. All operators offer discounted fares for school groups.

For information on ferry services, timetables and departure locations, visit [the By Ferry page](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry).

How do schools access ferry discounts?

Schools should contact their preferred ferry operator directly to request discounted school group fares and assistance with travel arrangements such as departure schedules and luggage transfers. Please note, terms and conditions vary by operator.
