# Accessibility

With wide pathways and ramps to most facilities, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is an accessible holiday destination.

Image Geordie Bay jetty

Geordie Bay jetty

## An accessible holiday destination

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is committed to ensuring everyone in the community can access, use, and enjoy the island and its facilities. Our goal is to create an inclusive holiday destination by focusing on key areas such as mobility equipment hire, transport, accommodation, accessible facilities, and on-island assistance.

### Accessibility of Ferry Services

What accessibility services does Rottnest Express offer?

Rottnest Express provides access and inclusion for people with all types of disability. Facilities to accommodate passengers with disabilities are available on Rottnest Express vessels, but not on all services.

If you require special assistance when travelling with Rottnest Express, call the reservations team on (+61) 1300 467 688, prior to booking ferry travel.

**Wheelchair Access**

* Certain voyages from the terminal at North Fremantle (Rous Head) are wheelchair accessible, including standard and motorised wheelchairs.
* Voyages from Perth CBD are not accessible for wheelchairs due to restrictions caused by a bend in the gangway.
* Due to the need to change levels within the vessel between embarkation and disembarkation, voyages from B Shed in Fremantle (Victoria Quay) are not wheelchair accessible.
* Please note that in the event of bad weather, high tides may cause slight difficulty during boarding or disembarking the ferry.

**Mobility Scooter Access**

* Due to space constraints, mobility scooters cannot be taken inside the vessels.
* They will be loaded onto the vessel in a designated crate with crew on hand to provide assistance during boarding and disembarkation.
* Wheelchairs will be available for any guests with mobility issues who require assistance boarding the vessel.

For more information visit the [Rottnest Express website](https://rottnestexpress.com.au/about/special-assistance/).

What accessibility services does Rottnest Fast Ferries offer?

For Rottnest Fast Ferries, exploring the island is something that everyone should be able to enjoy. The fleet’s newest vessel, Harbour Master, is wheelchair accessible with special assistance toilets available on board.

If you require special assistance when travelling with Rottnest Fast Ferries, contact the reservations team on (+61 8) 9246 1039 prior to booking your travel. This ensures you can receive the necessary service and departure information.

For more information, visit the [Rottnest Fast Ferries website](https://www.rottnestfastferries.com.au/special-assistance).

What accessibility services does SeaLink Rottnest Island offer?

All SeaLink Rottnest Island vessels are built to accommodate people with accessibility requirements, though options depend on the departure location.

To assist with passenger comfort and safety, all passengers travelling in a wheelchair will be given priority boarding. Please contact the reservations team on (+61) 1300 786 552 prior to booking your travel as there are limited wheelchair spaces on board.

If you have any questions, or want more information, [contact the SeaLink team.](https://www.sealink.com.au/about-us/contact-us/)

### Air Services

A number of operators provide flights between the mainland and Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. For details on aircraft facilities available for people of all ages and abilities, please contact the operators individually.

* [Air Charters West](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/air-charters-west)
* [Corsaire Aviation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/corsaire-aviation)
* [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi)
* [Swan River Seaplanes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/swan-river-seaplanes)

Image Ferry arriving in Thomson Bay

Ferry arriving in Thomson Bay

### Getting Around

###### Bus Services

The [Discover Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour) tour bus, and [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) shuttle and tour buses are accessible; however, please call ahead to allow seats within the bus to be removed to accommodate your mobility equipment if required. 

###### Mobility Equipment Hire

A range of mobility equipment is available to hire from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire). Electric scooters (gophers) can be delivered to the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) for collection. All other equipment can be collected from Pedal & Flipper Hire.

A limited number of wheelchairs are available for loan from the Visitor Centre for single-day use (please note a deposit is required). Wheelchairs cannot be pre-booked so it is recommended that visitors bring their own wheelchair if the requirement is known in advance.

See below for equipment options and applicable hire fees, deposits and booking conditions. 

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Equipment** | **Hire Cost** | **Deposit** | **Booking Conditions** |
| Adult Tricycles | $41 for a single day  $25 per additional day  $23 per afternoon | $100 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email) . Available for extended hire. |
| Beach Wheelchair | No Charge | $100 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email). Single day hire only. |
| Electric Scooters (Gophers) | $54 for a single day  $33 per additional day  $30 per afternoon | $200 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email). Available for extended hire. |
| Handcycle | $32 for a single day  $20 per additional day  $18 per afternoon | $100 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email). Available for extended hire. |
| X-Rover Trailers | $27 for a single day  $17 per additional day  $15 per afternoon | $200 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email) . Available for extended hire. |
| Tandem Bike | $70 for a single day  $42 per additional day  $39 per afternoon | $100 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email) . Available for extended hire. |
| Golf Buggy | No charge | $200 | Permit to drive on Rottnest Island is required. Must be returned to Pedal & Flipper Hire daily (cannot be hired overnight).  Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email). Single day hire only. |
| Rear Steered Tricycles | $20 for a single day  $10 per additional day | $100 | Needs to be pre-booked (phone or email). Available for extended hire. |

Contact [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/pedal-flipper-hire) for further information.

Image Bus on the coast road

Bus on the coast road

### Toilet & Shower Facilities

###### Changing Places Facility – Closed for works until mid-December 2026

Rottnest Island has a fully accredited Changing Places facility for visitors with accessibility requirements. It is located at the Henderson Avenue ablution block – near the Holy Trinity Catholic Church. MLAK users are already able to access the facility. Keys can also be requested from the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre).

For more information, please visit the [Changing Places](https://changingplaces.org.au/) website.

###### Accessible Toilets

A number of accessible toilet and shower facilities are available across Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. These include the following locations:

* Visitor Centre, Thomson Bay
* Digby Drive - accessible toilet and separate parenting room. The parenting room has a fixed baby changing table, parent and child toilets next to each other and a place to feed in private.
* Henderson Ave, Thomson Bay - this unisex facility includes male and female changing rooms.
* Bedford Ave, Thomson Bay - this facility includes a push button operated, level access shower.
* Stay Rottnest Campground
* The Basin
* Geordie Bay
* Parker Point
* Stark Bay
* West End

[View accessible facilities on the Island Map](https://www.rottnestisland.com/island-map)

Image Toilets at the Basin

Toilets at the Basin

### INFORMATION SERVICES

The [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) is located within a wide open pedestrian space that connects the main ferry jetty to the Thomson Bay settlement. The knowledgeable team here are able to assist with wheelchair hire (free to hire, deposit required). Mobility equipment can also be delivered to the Visitor Centre from  [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) , ready for customer collection.

The team can also assist with accessible transport enquiries and tour bookings, including bookings using the Companion Card.

### SERVICE DOG ASSISTANCE

Service dogs are permitted on Rottnest Island but due to it being a Class A Reserve, you should contact the rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788 prior to your visit to advise them of the service dog prior to travelling.

### ACCOMMODATION

###### Stay Rottnest

Stay Rottnest offers accessible accommodation options. If you require wheelchair accessible accommodation, please send your request to [stay@rottnestisland.com](mailto:stay@rottnestisland.com) during business hours Monday - Friday and don’t forget to attach a copy of your ACROD card (front and back).

For more information regarding bookings, visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/).

###### Discovery Resorts – Rottnest Island

Superior Accessible Tents have been designed with more space to accommodate those with physical limitations and disabilities, with a fit out that complies with Australian Standard 1428. These are available with an added bunk annex to accommodate families and carers and are bookable via the [Discovery Resorts website.](https://www.discoveryholidayparks.com.au/resorts/rottnest-island) For more information, call reception on (+61 8) 6350 6170.

###### Samphire Rottnest

Accessible rooms are available at Samphire Rottnest and are bookable via [their website](https://samphirerottnest.com.au/). Alternatively, you can contact Samphire Rottnest for more information by phone on (+61 8) 9292 5011 or by email [hello@samphirerottnest.com.au](mailto:hello@samphirerottnest.com.au).

###### The Lodge Wadjemup

Accessible poolside rooms are available at The Lodge Wadjemup. These generous rooms are newly built and thoughtfully combine contemporary, laidback design with high-end amenity, incorporating accessibility as a key priority. Rooms are bookable via the [Lodge Wadjemup website](https://www.thelodgewadjemup.com/). Or, for more information you can contact The Lodge Wadjemup via email [stay@thelodgewadjemup.com](mailto:stay@thelodgewadjemup.com).

# Minimise Your Impact

In a delicate and precious ecosystem like Rottnest Island, the mark you leave behind becomes your legacy.

Image Hiking the Gabbi Karniny Bidi

Hiking the Gabbi Karniny Bidi

### Play your part to reduce the ecological footprint of the island

All of the conservation efforts on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island don’t mean much without the help of everyone who sets foot on the island. With just a few mindful actions, we can all help to protect the island's natural beauty and ensure its sustainability for generations to come.

Here's how you can minimise your impact:

#### Save water and electricity

If you’re staying overnight, save energy by turning off all lights and appliances when you head out of your accommodation. Take quick showers and be mindful of water use in the kitchen and the bathroom.

#### Reuse and recycle

Help reduce plastic waste on the island by taking a reusable water bottle with you and a reusable coffee cup. Put your rubbish in the right bin and recycle what you can. You can also take part in the [Containers for Change](https://www.containersforchange.com.au/wa/) program on the island.

#### Respect the flora and fauna

When you experience the island by foot, bike or bus, there are ways you can respect the island and its unique natural environment. Don’t touch or feed the quokkas (or other wildlife), leave the island’s flora where you found it, get approval from the Rottnest Island Authority if you want to bring any flora over from the mainland, and contact the rangers prior to arrival should you need to bring a guide, assistance, or companion animal for medical reasons.

Make a Conscious Choice to Leave No Trace

Spending time on Rottnest Island means being aware of the land that was here before you and the place that will be here after you depart. Taking some time to pause and think about the trace you leave behind can make all the difference.

Image Quokka Drinking

Quokka

Image 

[Eating in the settlement mall](/see-do/eat-drink)

### What happens to your waste on Rottnest?

With a lot of visitors comes a lot of rubbish. To manage this responsibly, it's important to sort general waste and recyclables correctly, so it can be processed the right way. This starts with the right bin: red lid for general waste and yellow lid for recyclables.

Waste from across the island is collected daily, kept separate, compacted and sent to the mainland. General waste goes to landfill, while recyclables are processed at a Recycling Materials Recovery Facility.

Image Aerial of Boats at Rottnest Island

Boats in Longreach Bay

### Reducing the island's waste footprint

Waste management is vital to sustainability. And in a delicate and precious ecosystem like Rottnest Island, every action you take contributes to reducing the island’s overall waste footprint.

Here’s how you can help:

* Take your waste home with you when possible.
* If you do throw rubbish in the bins on the island, check the signs and use the correct bin.
* Don’t add rubbish to overflowing bins.
* If you’re coming to the island in your own boat, make sure that the contents of your boat are secure from wind and local birds.
* When at sea, ensure items like used boat batteries, appliances, and furniture are taken back with you.

Image 

### Containers for Change

Rottnest Island has multiple container collection points on the island in support of this important initiative to reduce litter and improve container recovery rates.

Here’s how you can be involved, and find out more about where the change from your containers goes:

* Drop off your loose containers at our public donation point, located at the [R.I.G.C Clubhouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/ricg-clubhouse) and we’ll do the rest. Your change will go to the [Rottnest Foundation](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/).
* Or, bag your containers, label the bag with your own Containers for Change ID, and take it to one of our Drop & Go refund points located at [Geordie Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) and [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire). The change from your containers will then go back to you.

[Learn more about Containers for Change](https://www.containersforchange.com.au/wa/)

# Snorkelling & Diving

### Explore a world beneath the surface

Immerse yourself beneath the surface and experience Wadjemup / Rottnest Island from a different perspective. Among the water's wonders is a rare and remarkable mix of temperate, subtropical, and tropical species of marine life.

With the mild Indian Ocean, warming Leeuwin Current and natural reef barrier, the clear turquoise waters reveal an underwater paradise home to a mesmerising mix of tropical fish, friendly stingrays, coral, and shipwrecks.

With so many sheltered and protected bays, you can interact with over 400 different species of fish, green turtles, and colourful western rock lobsters. The rich marine reserves are home to a chorus of corals, meadows of seagrass, and more - all ready for you to explore.

[Take Care When Snorkelling and Diving

Take care when snorkelling and diving and note that spearguns and handspears are not permitted in the Marine Reserve.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### Spots for all ages and abilities

With a number of sheltered and protected bays, and breathtaking sights just metres from the shore, Wadjemup offers snorkelling and diving adventures for a range of ages and abilities.

Take your pick from the popular snorkelling spots of [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin)
, [Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parakeet-bay)
and the shipwreck at [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks)
, or simply cycle from beach to bay to find a new favourite.

For a story-filled swim, explore the snorkel trail at [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail)  and be guided by the series of information panels attached to the seabed below.

Thanks to its diversity of marine life, clear water, reef caves and swim-throughs, Wadjemup is a spectacular diving destination. Although there are countless reef dive spots, Crystal Palace is one on the south east side that showcases the island’s intricate network of underwater caves, with an expanse of flowing submarine flora visible from the surface and dark blue openings in the reef teasing at hidden pathways below.

The waters around Rottnest Island also disguise the sunken remains of [multiple historic ships](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history) dotted around the bays. Many of these are impressive dive sites, with *Maced**on* and *Denton Holme* lying close enough for one dive visit.

*Macedon* still sits upright, the ribs and gunwales of the hull splayed open, merging with reef, while *Denton Holme*’s bow stretches upward, almost breaching the surface.

[Diving Safety

For your safety, always log your dives with the metropolitan sea rescue groups.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### What you’ll need to snorkel or dive

It doesn't matter if you have all the gear or no idea, you can still enjoy an unforgettable snorkelling or diving experience on Wadjemup. Bring your own gear over or hire snorkel sets, dive tanks and refills on the island from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire).

You can travel to your chosen snorkel or dive spot [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike), or simply take the [Island Explorer Bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off whenever you see somewhere that takes your fancy!

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where are the best places to snorkel on Rottnest Island?

Rottnest Island has amazing snorkelling spots all around its many [beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches), with clear turquoise waters, stunning coral and vibrant [marine life](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see) waiting just beneath the surface. Some of the most popular snorkelling spots include [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point), [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay), [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), [Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay) and [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks), where you can explore everything from shallow protected waters to coral gardens, seagrass meadows and nearby shipwrecks.

For more inspiration, discover [six of the best snorkelling spots on Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/where-to-snorkel-at-rottnest-island--six-of-the-best-spots) before planning your underwater adventure.

Can you snorkel at the Rottnest Island shipwrecks?

Yes, you can [snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) some of the [shipwrecks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/shipwrecks) around Rottnest Island. The wrecks of *Shark* and *Uribes* are easily accessible for snorkellers of all levels. These can be found just off the beach in reasonably shallow water. The rest of the wrecks are only visible underneath the water, so the best way to view them is by going on a scuba dive down to the vessels.

Do I need to bring my own snorkelling gear?

You are welcome to bring your own snorkelling gear, and there are also plenty of options on the island if you would rather travel light. To help plan your day, explore the island’s [beautiful beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) and [beach and water activities](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities), then hire snorkel gear from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) or [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals). You can also buy snorkel masks, flippers and other essentials from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) in Thomson Bay or the [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store) if you need extra gear once you arrive.

Can beginners snorkel at Rottnest Island?

Yes. Rottnest Island has a number of calm, sheltered bays that are well suited to beginners and families when conditions are suitable. [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) is a popular choice, with protected water close to shore, while other [beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) offer easy places to start before exploring deeper [snorkelling spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/where-to-snorkel-at-rottnest-island--six-of-the-best-spots).

What can you see while snorkelling or diving at Rottnest Island?

Snorkelling and diving around Rottnest Island can reveal colourful fish, coral, stingrays, seagrass meadows and even [shipwrecks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/shipwrecks). For a closer look beneath the surface, explore the island’s [marine life](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see) and discover the [coral species](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/5-coral-species-you-can-spot-at-rottnest-island) you can spot around Wadjemup.

# A Perfect Three-Day Escape to Rottnest Island

A three‑day island escape offers endless ways to explore, unwind, and make the most of your time on Wadjemup, with nature, adventure, and discovery around every corner.

6 minutes

Image Parker Point

Parker Point

**After a few days on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, you are sure to leave with a fresh perspective and a renewed sense of energy that only comes from time well spent in nature.**

From peaceful mornings to afternoons exploring secluded bays and evenings soaking up the island atmosphere, here is our ultimate guide for a three day escape that invites adventure, inspires connection, and helps you make the most of your island time.

### Day 1: Beach and bay hopping

Wadjemup is less than an hour from Fremantle and Hillarys [by ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry), but once you arrive, you’ll feel a world away from the mainland. As your ferry pulls into [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), you’re welcomed by the picturesque coastline, dotted with boats bobbing on the blue water.

Today you’re going to see the whole island, but there’s no need to rush. Take a moment to pause at the commanding sculpture, Koora-Yeye-Boordawan-Kalyakoorl (Past-Present-Future-Forever), and reflect on the [significance of the island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history) to the Whadjuk Noongar people before continuing your journey.

With a deeper understanding of the island’s history, move into the settlement, where you’ll find restaurants, shops and transport options. Grab some takeaway lunch from [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican), the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) or [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane) and pop it in your bag for later so you can enjoy a picnic on route.

There are two ways to explore the island if not [by foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) — [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or [by bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus). If you feel like cycling, head to [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) to hire your bike or collect your pre-booked equipment. They have a huge selection of bikes, plus trailers, and mobility assistance options as well as e-bikes if you want an extra boost.

If you’d prefer to tour the island from the comfort of a bus, take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus service. This service circumnavigates the island giving you the freedom to hop on and off as you please. You can book tickets online or visit the ticket booth at the main bus stop to purchase a day pass.

Start your day of exploration by heading south towards Kingstown Barracks and enjoy those first amazing glimpses of turquoise ocean, bright green bush and white sandy beaches. Take your pick between [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point), Green Island, and Mary Cove — all perfect options to admire the gorgeous views, take a walk on the sand or hop in the water for a swim and a snorkel.

Next, you’ll visit [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) in the centre of the island. Constructed in 1896 and standing at approximately 38 metres, this island landmark is the fourth tallest lighthouse in Australia. [Take a tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour) to the top and soak up the panoramic views across the island and out to sea; on a clear day, you’ll be able to spot the Perth skyline or the Fremantle ports.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

Now it's time to head down the hill and back towards the coast, continuing to the westernmost part of the island. The [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) is a special place on Wadjemup, where you can feel the expanse of ocean that stretches out to Madagascar.

Enjoy the views at Cathedral Rocks where you can spot resident marine life including long-nosed fur seals, Australian sea lions, bottlenose dolphins and, from August to December, [migrating whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching).

Next, venture to the northern side of the island - a feast for the eyes. Along this spectacular stretch you’ll pass Stark Bay, Catherine Bay, [Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parakeet-bay), and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay). Take your pick of these expansive beaches and find an idyllic spot for the afternoon.

The bus will head back to [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), but those on bikes can round the corner to The Basin. With its shallow clear waters and protective reef, it's an ideal spot for a final swim or ice cream from the Simmo's window at [Havza](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza).

After a full day of exploring, it's time to head to your accommodation to freshen up. Once you’ve unpacked, it’s time to relax over a [culinary feast](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink) and refreshing drink. Enjoy classic fish and chips or some locally caught seafood at one of the nearby restaurants, paired with a craft beer or renowned Western Australian wine.

### Day 2: Relax and recharge

We covered some distance yesterday, so today it's time to slow down, recharge and connect to all that is here.

Treat yourself to a lazy breakfast, reading a book or just enjoying the incredible views out to the ocean. There are plenty of places to choose from, so you can enjoy a sit-down breakfast or grab a takeaway pastry and a coffee from the [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery).

There are bound to be spots you didn't explore yesterday, or ones you'd love to head back to. Enjoy a few hours of [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving), swimming, playing games, or just snoozing in the sunshine. Level up your beach day with a cool cabana, sun lounger, or inflatable water chair from [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals).

If you feel like exploring without the effort, let [Rotto Rickshaws](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rotto-rickshaws) take you on a guided ride around the island, where live storytelling and beautiful views showcase the island in a relaxing new way.

In the afternoon, explore more of the history of Rottnest Island at [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), a significant World War II heritage site, built to defend Fremantle port from warships. Enjoy the panoramic island views from the site then [take a tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) to discover the military remnants hidden within, including a maze of underground tunnels.

As the day draws to a close, settle in for an iconic Rottnest Island sunset. [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) offers an unbeatable view where you can see the sky-show over iconic [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse). Enjoy a sundowner and a bite to eat at [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island). For a different sunset experience, dine at [Sunsets](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest) within [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup), offering stunning views over Garden Lake.

### Day 3: Get cultural

So far, you’ve soaked up the island scenery and touched on the history of Wadjemup. But there is still so much more to immerse yourself in, and these tours and activities will give you the full experience.

Wander around Wadjemup Museum which houses a number of fascinating exhibits that tell the island's story from its beginnings more than 40,000 years ago, right up to its role in the 2020's global pandemic.

Explore Rottnest Island’s natural scenery and historic stories on your own revolutionary set of wheels. [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa) will lead you on a journey of discovery and exploration, taking you to parts of the island you’ve never been before. Riding a segway is easy to learn and you’ll quickly be on your way to experiencing the previously hard-to-reach corners of Wadjemup.

Heighten your appreciation for Wadjemup from an Aboriginal perspective. [Go Cultural Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) offers unique walking tours where your Noongar guide explains the [historical significance](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) of the island to the Traditional Owners, the Whadjuk Noongar people.

Have little ones with you? [Koorda's Crew](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda) offers hands-on cultural experiences where kids can wander through nature, learn about native plants and their traditional uses, and create a Lego landscape inspired by the current Noongar season.

Deepen your cultural understanding with [Dooga Waalitj Healing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences), where you can visit significant sites on a guided walk, listen to stories passed down through generations, and take part in creative art workshops. Or, join [Mirliny](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mirliny-cultural-yarning-experience) for an intimate yarning experience, where you can learn Noongar language, try rope-making, and explore traditional tools.

As your time on Wadjemup draws to a close, spend some time spotting the island’s famous residents - [the quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)
Just remember that quokkas are wild animals, and you are visiting their home, so rather than approach, simply observe them from a respectable distance. On your journey back to the mainland, reflect on your newfound connection and appreciation of the island, to be renewed on your next visit.

# Hire

## All the right gear to enhance your experience of the island

Visiting Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is an all-terrain escape. Where the right equipment opens doors for deeper, more invigorating experiences. A snorkel set to see the thriving sea life in vivid detail. Or a wetsuit to surf and dive in cool waters without a thought for the season.

There are multiple vendors where you can hire the gear you need for any island activity. Snorkelling, boating, diving, cycling … they are all open to you. There’s no need to bring anything with you, simply show up and have the adventure that calls you on the day.

[Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) is the main vendor, where you can find equipment for snorkelling, diving, sports, and cycling — they also offer a range of mobility assistance equipment. Whereas the clubhouse at the [Rottnest Island Golf Course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) carries the items you need for a day on the green and [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals) has everything you need for the perfect beach day.

# Getting Around

Whether it be by bike, bus or on foot, there’s no shortage of easy ways to get around and explore everything the island has to offer.

Image Salmon Bay

Salmon Bay

### Journey your way

Renowned for its natural beauty and active outdoor lifestyle, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is equally well known for what it doesn’t have - traffic.

With few cars permitted on the island, there is a unique kind of tranquillity as you explore everything the island has to offer.

Explore the island's numerous ways of options for navigation.

Image 

[Cycling](/visit/getting-around/by-bike)

### Cycling

A healthy, efficient way to explore the island, cycling lets you stop wherever (and whenever) you please. Bikes can be hired from three of the ferry providers or from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) who offer a range of bike options including e-bikes, accessories, and one-day or multi-day hire.

[Getting around by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike)

Image Cathedral Rocks, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

[Hiking trails](/visit/getting-around/by-foot)

### Walking

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island offers plenty of island experiences just a short walk from the main settlement, so you're never far from the action.

For those looking to venture further afield, you can discover a wealth of natural wonders on foot. From guided walking experiences to exploring the Wadjemup Bidi trail network, every step tells a story.

[Getting around on foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot)

Image 

[Bus on the island road](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus)

### Buses

See the island by shuttle with daily buses seamlessly transporting you between Thomson Bay, Geordie Bay, and Kingstown.

You can take the [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) Island Explorer hop-on-hop-off bus, with 19 stops around the island.

There are also bus tours that offer a relaxing way to explore the island in the comfort of an air-conditioned coach with insightful commentary along the way.

[Getting around by bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus)

Image Quokka Hopper running along the coast with passengers on board

[Quokka Hopper passing the salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/quokka-hopper)

### Private transfer

Getting around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island by private transfer offers a convenient and flexible way to explore this beautiful destination.

On land, [Quokka Hopper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/quokka-hopper) provides a convenient on-demand private transfer vehicle around Thomson Bay settlement, and between Kingstown and Geordie Bay.

For those looking to explore by water, the [Rottnest Water Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-water-taxi) effortlessly connects you to all corners of Rottnest Island with pick up and drop off points around the entire island. Providing a convenient, flexible and on-demand transport option.

Image Quokka Hopper travelling along a coastal road on Wadjemup/Rottnest Island

[Quokka Hopper Private Transfers](/see-do/hire/quokka-hopper)

### Accessibility

Rottnest Island provides an accessible and facility-friendly holiday destination for all visitors.

With wide pathways, easy to read signage and ramps to most facilities, it’s all about making your experience as easy and accessible as possible. Even the buses are wheelchair accessible so everyone can enjoy the same convenience.

For those requiring extra assistance, a range of mobility equipment is also available for hire from Pedal & Flipper Hire.

[More about accessibility on the island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/accessibility)

# Trade & Media

## Experience a fresh perspective and energy from time well spent

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is an iconic destination in Western Australia, and offers a unique opportunity for visitors to connect with the land, history, and culture through unique experiences.

Visitors come to Wadjemup for different reasons: invigorating adventures in nature, mindful interactions with history, or seaside getaways spent submerged in tranquil waters. Whatever you’re looking for, every journey creates moments for grounding into appreciation and peace.

## Trade Resources

Explore a range of resources designed to support trade partners, including marketing materials and product updates. Everything you need to promote Rottnest Island and its affiliated businesses is available in one place.

### Holiday Planner

Keen to learn more about the island but don't know where to start? Start with our holiday planner below.

#### How to Order a Hard Copy of the Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Holiday Planner

1. Click the link to visit our print partner, [Vanguard Distribution](https://www.vanguarddistribution.com.au/Login.aspx?utm_source=website&utm_medium=online&utm_campaign=orderplanner).
2. Sign in if you already have an account.
3. If you’re new, click “**Sign up**” to create an account, then sign in.
4. Select "Order Brochures".
5. In the Name field, search “Rottnest Island.”
6. Tick the checkbox next to the brochure.
7. Choose the quantity you need (bundles, cartons **or** individual units).
8. Click "**Proceed to Shopping Cart and Order**".
9. Review and confirm your order details.
10. Click "**Order**".  *Note: This will complete your order*
11. Vanguard Distribution will email you to finalise payment and delivery details.

### Trade Guide

The  [Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Trade Guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/wadjemup-rottnest-island-trade-guide-2025-edition.pdf?sfvrsn=cbfa8854_7) is your go-to resource for all things related to the diverse experiences and activities available. Whether you're a travel agent, event planner, or tourism professional, we are here to provide you with the essential information and tools to help you curate extraordinary experiences for your clients.

* [Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Trade Guide 2026 Edition](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/wadjemup-rottnest-island-trade-guide-2025-edition.pdf?sfvrsn=cbfa8854_7)
* [Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Trade Guide 2025 Edition Chinese](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/wadjemup-rottnest-island-trade-guide-2025-edition-chinese.pdf?sfvrsn=27e664b8_6)
* [Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Trade Guide 2025 Edition Japanese](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/wadjemup-rottnest-island-trade-guide-2025-edition-japanese.pdf?sfvrsn=32f11eac_4)

### Corporate Groups Guide

Wadjemup is an ideal destination for group travel, inspiring connection and reflection. Access our [Corporate Groups Guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/ria3928---a4-corporate-groups-guide.pdf?sfvrsn=6cfa40b9_13) for a detailed breakdown of the itinerary options and experiences suitable for groups.

* [Corporate Groups Guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/ria3928---a4-corporate-groups-guide.pdf?sfvrsn=6cfa40b9_13)

### Island Map

Download the [Rottnest Island map here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/rottnest-island-map_dec-2022.pdf?sfvrsn=f8508b18_6).

* [Rottnest Island Map](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/trade-groups/rottnest-island-map_dec-2022.pdf?sfvrsn=f8508b18_6)

### Image Library

You can register to the [Rottnest Island image library](https://rottnestisland.imagegallery.me/site/welcome.me) and find the perfect visual assets to suit your needs. With content that captures the full breadth and depth of the island experience, it’s the best place to see all Wadjemup has to offer.

# Explore West End on the Ngank Wen Bidi

### Chase the sun towards the western corner of Wadjemup

The Ngank Wen Bidi allows hikers to explore the rugged and stunning West End of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

As the westernmost point of the island, there’s nothing else between you and the vast Indian Ocean here. At the right time of day you can watch the sun set over the horizon, bathing the entire ocean in warm hues. Visit some of the island’s most secluded beaches as the 7.8 km trail loops around from Narrow Neck to Cape Vlamingh and back.

Hikers are treated to a trek along the coastline of Marjorie Bay, a curve in the island that creates a natural lagoon, playing host to an array of sea life. At Cathedral Rocks, a purpose-built platform allows you to see some of the island’s elusive long-nosed fur seals frolicking on the rocks. Plus, spot dolphins playing in the waters out to sea.

The [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) boardwalk allows hikers to access Cape Vlamingh where you can spot osprey nests perched high above the murmuring sea. Between late August and December, you may be lucky to witness the seasonal migration of humpback whales off the coast too.

Looping eastward past Radar Reef, hikers can take in the stunning views of the island’s southern coast, and the rolling surf break. The trail continues on, back to Narrow Neck, providing an exceptional, self-contained hike for those looking to discover the island’s more secluded beaches and spaces.

### Where to start the Ngank Wen Bidi

The Ngank Wen Bidi is its own self-contained loop, so it starts and ends at the same place, whichever way you walk it. You can catch the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), and get off at Stop 12 at Narrow Neck. From there, simply follow the trail markers to discover the island’s [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end).

### Frequently Asked Questions

What do I need to bring on this hike?

The Ngank Wen Bidi provides a hike around the dramatic southern coast of Wadjemup. It’s quite rugged in parts, so be sure to wear strong hiking boots. Bring at least two litres of water with you, and always wear a hat and sunscreen.

How difficult is the Ngank Wen Bidi?

The Ngank Wen Bidi takes you all around the western end of Wadjemup. Some of the terrain can be challenging, and you’ll face beach walking, rough surfaces, and some sections of steep climbing. Hikers should have some degree of bushwalking experience first before attempting the Ngank Wen Bidi.

Are there any toilets or facilities on the trail?

You can find public toilets at the starting point, Narrow Neck, and again at Cape Vlamingh. There’s no water available on the trail, so fill your bottles up at Thomson Bay before you leave.

Wheelchair access is available at some of the island’s West End experiences, including the Cathedral Rocks Viewing Platform, and along the West End boardwalk.

There are rubbish bins available at West End and Narrow Neck.

# Pinky Beach

## Wadjemup’s iconic beach has space for everyone

Taking its title as one of the widest and longest stretches of beach on the island, Pinky Beach is known for its gorgeous swimming conditions. The safe, calm waters are shielded from south, southwest, and west winds, and being only a few [minutes’ walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) away from the main settlement, it's the ideal place for families.

A sheltered bay and undulating coral reef make it the perfect start for beginner [snorkellers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) to discover Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s underwater stories.

Views of the historic [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) provide a scenic backdrop to a long, lazy afternoon. But it’s the vibrant sunsets that really bring the crowds. Pinky Beach has built a reputation as being the best place on the island to watch the sun dip slowly over the ocean. So come for the day — and stay for the sunsets.

Just up the stairs and over the dunes you’ll find [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) (previously Pinky’s Beach Club), a place to refresh and revive with top class food and drinks. Expansive views of the ocean offer stunning sunset scenes — and, at the right time of the year, you might even see some whales frolicking further out to sea.

### Where to find Pinky Beach

Located on the northern side of the island, Pinky Beach can be found within close proximity to [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), just a short 10-minute [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) from the main settlement—and even quicker [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike).

Image Pinky Beach

Bathurst Lighthouse overlooking Pinky Beach

Image Bathurst Lighthouse

[Bathurst Lighthouse](/learn)

### Shining a light out to sea

Bathurst Lighthouse is one of the most iconic Rottnest Island views. Built in 1900 to support the established Wadjemup Lighthouse, the structure itself began in sad circumstances.

In 1899, *City of York* hit a reef off the western coast of Wadjemup and sank with 11 lives lost. An inquiry into the incident determined that the guiding light wasn’t enough — and so the Bathurst Lighthouse was established.

20 metres high, the stark white brick structure works with Wadjemup Lighthouse and the Fremantle Lighthouse to form a navigation triangle to help avoid future maritime disasters.

While the lighthouse runs automatically and is closed to visitors, it’s one of the highest points on the island. Its scenic outlook provides an opportunity for some iconic Wadjemup photos, including the famous sunsets of Pinky Beach.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby Pinky Beach?

The closest public toilet facilities to Pinky Beach are at the [Stay Rottnest Campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-campground) or at [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin).

Can I stay at Pinky Beach?

While you can’t stay precisely at Pinky Beach (in fact camping on any beach on the island is illegal), there is accommodation close by. Glamping accommodation is available just over the dunes at [Discovery Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island). [Stay Rottnest Campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-campground) is also just a stone’s throw away.

Is fishing allowed?

While hand line and reel fishing is allowed at Pinky Beach, there’s better fishing to be had elsewhere on the island.

# Bike Hire FAQ

### Frequently Asked Questions

Are helmets and locks included?

Yes, they are included with your pedal bike hire. Helmets must be worn at all times when riding and bikes should be locked when not in use.

Are e-bikes included in this offer?

No; however, they can be booked for the booking period at standard rates.

Can I choose from all bike sizes?

Yes, if students require adult size bikes there is no extra charge (subject to availability).

Can I hire a bike if I can’t ride?

No, there is no safe option for non-riders.  There is a [hop-on hop-off bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) that circumnavigates the island. However, there is a charge for this service.

Are there any special rules around the use of bikes?

Yes, bikes should be treated with care. Only one person should ride a bike at any time. Bikes should not be ridden off-road or down steps.  Charges will apply for any damage or theft to hire equipment.

Are there any special rules relating to riding bikes on Rottnest Island?

Normal road rules apply on Rottnest Island and riders should watch out for service vehicles. Riders should keep to the left-hand side of the road and helmets must be worn in compliance with WA road laws.

What if my bike breaks down?

Pedal & Flipper Hire offer a free callout service during opening hours if you experience any mechanical difficulty with your bike. The number to call is (+61 8) 9292 5105 and is marked on all hire equipment.

I have a student with a disability, do you cater for them?

Yes. Please contact [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/pedal-flipper-hire) direct for more information.

Where do I collect the bikes from?

[Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/pedal-flipper-hire) is located on Bedford Avenue, just behind Hotel Rottnest and a short walk from the main jetty.

What if I injure myself while riding a bike?

The [Rottnest Island Nursing Post](https://ria-prod.equ.com.au/see-do/shopping-services/nursing-post?tab=see-do) is open daily between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm with an on-call nurse available after hours. In the case of an emergency, please call 000.

# Salmon Bay

## A breathtaking southern shoreline

Located on the southern coast of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, Salmon Bay is a wide, beautiful stretch of coastline where soft white sand meets calm, clear water. With its sweeping views across the Indian Ocean and open sense of space, it’s the kind of place that invites you to slow down, take a breath and settle into the island’s natural rhythm.

The bay’s sparkling turquoise water and sandy shoreline make it a rewarding stop for swimming, [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) or simply stretching out on the beach for a lazy afternoon. Beneath the surface, limestone and seagrass habitats create opportunities to spot [marine life](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see), making Salmon Bay just as memorable below the water as it is from the shore.

For walkers travelling the [Wardan Nara Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/wardan-nara-bidi), Salmon Bay offers a refreshing place to pause along the southern coast. The trail curves around the coastline here before turning inland towards [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), making the bay an ideal spot to pause, breathe in the sea air and take in the sweeping views across Wadjemup’s southern shoreline.

### Keep an eye out for

Image 

Sparkling turquoise water and soft white sand

Image 

Seagrass, reef and limestone habitats beneath the surface

Image 

Eastern ospreys nesting and hunting around Salmon Bay

Image 

The nearby Wardan Nara Bidi

### Where to find Salmon Bay

Salmon Bay sits on the south side of the island, around five kilometres from the main settlement. It’s a bit long to [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot), but the [ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) there takes you along the Parker Point loop and past some of Wadjemup’s most striking southern coastline. Alternatively, take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and hop off at stop 7 for Salmon Bay.

Image 

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Beneath the surface of Salmon Bay

Salmon Bay’s clear water and open sandy shoreline make it a beautiful place to swim, snorkel and slow down along Wadjemup’s southern coast. On calm days, the bay offers plenty of space to wade in, float above the sand or venture further out to explore the underwater landscape at your own pace.

Beneath the surface, limestone and seagrass areas create habitat for a variety of marine life, giving snorkellers and divers plenty to look for as they move through the water. Schools of fish, shifting seagrass and reef pockets make Salmon Bay just as memorable below the water as it is from the shore.

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

Image Aerial view of Salmon Bay on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, showing white sand, clear turquoise water, reef patches, beachgoers and coastal vegetation.

Aerial view of Salmon Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby?

There are no facilities at Salmon Bay, so be sure to bring what you need with you. The closest facilities are available at nearby stops along the southern coastline, including Parker Point.

Can I fish at Salmon Bay?

Fishing is permitted in parts of Salmon Bay, but not within marine sanctuary zones. The Parker Point Sanctuary Zone has been expanded to include part of Salmon Bay, where fishing is prohibited to help protect marine life. Before casting a line, check the latest marine maps to see where [marine sanctuary zone boundaries apply](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/boating/plan-your-boat-trip/marine-maps---resources).

How do I get to Salmon Bay?

Salmon Bay is around a 25-minute bike ride from the main settlement via the Parker Point loop. Alternatively, take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and get off at Stop 7.

Is Salmon Bay family-friendly?

Salmon Bay can be a lovely spot for families, especially on calm days. There is plenty of beach space to relax, but visitors should come prepared as there are no facilities directly at the bay.

# The Rotto Mini Loop: 4 km of Easy, Scenic Cycling

Cycle this family-friendly trail for the perfect island snapshot. The Rotto Mini Loop covers 4 km of beautiful bays and striking salt lake scenery.

4 minutes

Image 

Cycle along the coast

**Idyllic bayside views, lookout points and roaming kwoka (quokka) sightings. This mini loop cycle trail offers the perfect snapshot of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island by bike.**

Short in distance but large in adventure, this loop can be completed in as little as 30-minutes (depending on your level of pedal power). Or spend hours hopping between beloved bays and revelling in the rich biodiversity of the island’s inland areas. Along the way, there are opportunities for a bite to eat to satisfy appetites of all sizes. Don’t forget to keep your senses switched on to the sounds and sightings of local fauna.

### THE ROTTO MINI LOOP

**Distance:** 4 km

**Time:** 30 minutes

With just four kilometres of winding roads and pathways, this loop is ideal for little legs or those looking to ease into the lengthier trails that encircle the island. The average time to complete the loop depends on your pedalling speed, pit-stops you make and how energised you and your travel companions feel.

The adventure begins from your choice of starting location. Take to the trail from your [accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay), if you’re staying in any of the options north of the settlement. For those on a day trip, set off from the main settlement.

[Take Care when Cycling

Take care when cycling on Wadjemup. Even though there aren’t many vehicles, the hills can get steep and the roads are winding. Make sure to always wear a helmet when riding a bike—it’s mandatory as per Western Australian law.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### GLIDE YOUR WAY TO BEAUTIFUL BAYS

[The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) beckons as a welcome first point to disembark. Here, the pristine, protected waters entice all to wade in and share the sea with an abundance of fish species that dart beneath the surface. Slip on a mask and snorkel to spot them amongst the pink, purple and brown-hued coral.

Conveniently close to The Basin, [Havza](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza) is open daily (seasonal). Treat yourselves to your favourite frothy drink to fuel the rest of the journey. Or grab a sweet scoop of Simmo’s ice cream to savour as you perch on the soft sand. If you arrive later in the afternoon, you can enjoy tapas overlooking the iconic shores of The Basin.

If you continue the route along the coast, the sapphire waters of [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) will soon appear. This bay is a popular swimming spot for families, with its calm conditions and soft sands that foster the perfect place for play. A few extra minutes of pedalling will take you up to [Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay). This little cove is nestled within the northernmost tip of the island, offering a sheltered spot to swim and snorkel. The environment here sets a striking scene, with limestone crops on the shore and green seagrass softly swaying in the sea.

Image 

[The Basin, Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin)

Image 

[HAVZA at The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/havza)

Image Fay's Bay

[Fay's Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay)

### MAKE A PIT-STOP FOR FUEL AND FUN

Back on your bikes? Make tracks towards [Geordie’s Cafe and Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery). This charming cafe is open daily from the early morning until evening, serving up breakfast, lunch and dinner. Take an extended pause from your pedalling adventures here with a delicious meal or snack and refreshing drink. There’s also a playground out the front, just waiting for any extra energy to be released. For additional takeaway snacks or supplies, swing by [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store).

Before the trail veers away from the coast, take the opportunity to swim, snorkel or just enjoy the dazzling surrounds of [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay). Gaze out at the serene sight of boats bobbing in the bay, while casting your eyes towards the dunes, too. Curious quokkas have been known to make an appearance here, so keep a look out.

Image 

[Views of Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay)

Image Couple eating at Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery with art prints on wall behind them of Rottnest Island beaches

[Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/geordies-cafe-art-gallery)

Image A couple enjoying ice-cream at Geordie Bay | Rottnest Island

[Ice cream from the Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/geordie-bay-general-store)

### HEAD INLAND TO THE SALT LAKES

Follow the loop inland for a change of scenery. You’ll pass by the outskirts of the local [golf course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) and weave around the [kabikarning (salt lake) systems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), which are home to local wildlife. These wetlands are a favourite area for birdwatchers, with different species flourishing throughout the year.

Your journey reaches its peak at Vlamingh Lookout: one of the most [scenic vantage points](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-top-five-lookouts-on-wadjemup-rottnest-island) on Wadjemup. Leave your bikes at the base of the hill and enjoy the short walk to the summit. Spend a moment or two marvelling in 360-degree views of the island, including the scenery you’ve cycled past on your travels.

Descend from the lookout and head to the Garden Lake boardwalk nearby. Enjoy a purposeful moment of quiet, respectful observation as the [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) hop about in fields of grass and samphire. From here, it’s just a short cycle back to the main settlement, where your day of island exploration can wind down, or begin its second wind.

### BIKE AND SNORKEL HIRE

For everything you need to enjoy the Rotto Mini Loop or other [island cycling trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island), the team at [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) can assist. Planning ahead ensures a hassle-free start to any adventure. Plus, there are a range of family-friendly options, including baby seats and child trailer hire.

# Privacy

Rottnest Island Authority respects your privacy and is committed to protecting all personal information provided to it in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

This statement explains how and when your personal information and other data is collected, used, disclosed, and otherwise handled by the Rottnest Island Authority.

By using our websites and/or providing your personal information to us by any other means, you consent to us handling your personal information in accordance with this statement.

### How your information is collected and used

Collection of personal information

We may collect personal information about you during your dealings with us (e.g. when you make an accommodation or tour booking, or when you make and enquiry).

We only collect personal information necessary for our business function, which may include:

* Providing you with island access, accommodation, or tourism services,
* Answering your queries,
* Arranging and paying for activities or services on your behalf (e.g. Island tours),
* Providing, administering, improving, and personalising our products and services,
* Data analysis, business consulting, auditing, archiving, printing, delivery, and mailing services,
* Administering a promotion or survey, and
* Fraud prevention and credit checks.

We collect most personal information directly from you by way of written forms, our website, by phone, in person, by our representatives, and other correspondence (such as emails and messaging services).

We may also collect personal information about you from third parties, including booking agents and tourist information centres.

If we are unable to collect the personal information we require, or the information provided is incorrect or incomplete, this may affect our ability to provide products or services to you.

* Personal information collected by RIA will only be:
* Collected by lawful and fair means,
* Used for lawful purposes, and
* Collected with your consent.

If you provide us with personal information about a third party you represent, we collect it on the basis that you have that person’s consent for us to collect and handle their personal information in accordance with this privacy statement.

Types of personal information

The specific types of personal information collected and used by Rottnest Island Authority varies according to the purpose for collection, in general this information includes, but is not limited to:

* Name
* Residential address / Postal address
* Email address
* Telephone number(s)
* Boat registration
* Credit card details\*

Please note: Credit card details are NOT stored on the Rottnest Island Authority website servers.  Transactions are processed through our merchant gateway.

Email and feedback information

If you subscribe to any services on the Rottnest Island Authority website or provide any comments or feedback via email, then your email address and other personal information you may provide will be maintained on our mailing lists.

Your email address is confidential. When you email us:

* We will record your email address,
* We will only use your email address for the purpose for which you provided it,
* We will not use your email address for any other purpose, and
* We will not disclose it to another party without your consent (though from time to time we may disclose your personal information to a party acting on behalf of Rottnest Island Authority).

Any email correspondence sent to us will be treated as a public record and will be retained as required by the Western Australian State Records Act 2000 and other relevant regulations.

Use and disclosure of personal information

We will use and disclose your personal information for the purposes for which we collected it, and/or for other related purposes that you would reasonably expect. Generally, these purposes include, but are not limited to:

* Processing accommodation, products and services, and activity bookings, and to facilitate other transactions relating to those arrangements,
* Providing you with marketing information about the goods and services offered by Rottnest Island Authority and third parties, such as Island businesses,
* Maintaining a relationship with you as a customer or subscriber to our mailing lists,
* Surveys and other market research to assist us in assessing and improving our services, and
* Where required for administrative purposes and all other purposes reasonably associated with our business.

By providing us with your personal information, you consent to us using your personal information for the above purposes. You agree that we may send you such information by post or by electronic means (including email and SMS). You can opt-out of marketing and promotional communications at any time using an opt-out mechanism in one of our communications, or by contacting us directly.

Apart from the above instances, we may also use and disclose your personal information with your consent and as otherwise required at law.

We may disclose your personal information to third-party contractors and service providers, including third parties that are located outside of Australia, for the purposes outlined above.

The Rottnest Island Authority will take reasonable steps to ensure that the overseas recipient does not breach the Australian Privacy Principles.

Accuracy and security

The Rottnest Island Authority will take reasonable steps to:

* Ensure that the personal information we collect, use, hold, and disclose is accurate, complete, up-to-date, and relevant for the purpose of its use or disclosure,
* Protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorised access, modification, or disclosure, and
* Destroy or permanently de-identify personal information, which is no longer required, unless the information is contained in a Commonwealth or State record or the Rottnest Island Authority is legally required to retain the information.

How we protect the information we collect

Personal information is held in both electronic and hard copy records, which are stored securely at our facilities or by contracted partners. We take reasonable steps to securely store your personal information to ensure it is protected from unauthorised access, modification, and disclosure, and from other types of misuse, interference, and loss.

We will take reasonable steps to destroy or permanently de-identify your personal information when we no longer require it for any purpose for which it was collected.  We may retain your personal information for as long as necessary to comply with any applicable law, for insurance and corporate governance purposes, for the prevention of fraud and to resolve disputes.  Your personal information may also be retained in our IT system back-up records.

Online transactions are supported by secure server technology. The technology we use encrypts your personal financial information before it is transmitted over the Internet. You can only transact on our website using a browser that supports secure server technology.

Access and correction

You have the right to both ask:

* For access to personal information that we hold about you,
* That we correct personal information we hold about you.

If you ask, we must give you access to your personal information, and take reasonable steps to correct it if we consider it is incorrect, unless there is a law that allows or requires us not to.

Any such requests must be made in writing to Rottnest Island Authority to our Privacy Officer via the email address [privacy@ria.wa.gov.au](mailto:privacy@ria.wa.gov.au).

The Rottnest Island Authority will respond to written requests within twenty-eight (28) days of the receipt of the request at our offices.

Data breaches

Following the commencement of the Privacy Amendment (Notifiable Data Breaches) Act 2017, the Rottnest Island Authority will take reasonable steps to notify individuals impacted by eligible data breaches (as defined under the Privacy Act), as soon as possible after it becomes aware of the breach.

External links

Some websites accessed via links from the Rottnest Island website may collect personally identifiable information about you when you access or utilise those links.  When you leave Rottnest Island Authority’s website you are no longer protected by its privacy provisions.

Collection of statistical information

Browsing any website generates a trail of the pages that are visited (usage data). When you visit our websites or use our mobile apps, a record of your visit is kept for statistical and research purposes.  Our servers may record the following information:

* Your computer's IP address and top-level domain name (eg. au);
* Pages accessed and documents downloaded;
* Date and time of the visit;
* Time spent on the pages;
* Previous site visited (ie. how you arrived at our website);
* Type of browser used and browser version;
* Unique device identifiers; and
* Selected statistical and diagnostic information (operating system, transfer speed, etc.).

Analysis of this usage data enables Rottnest Island Authority to make its sites more useful to visitors.

Usage data is not itself personally identifiable information. If it is linked to personal information about an individual, it may become personally identifiable and in those circumstances we will treat that usage data as personal information and only use it in accordance with our Privacy Statement, the Privacy Act and other applicable data protection legislation.

No attempt will be made to identify visitors or their browsing activities except in the unlikely event of an investigation, or the need to determine details related to a security breach or other inappropriate activity.

Analytics & cookies

Rottnest Island Authority uses cookies, image analytics and similar technology when you visit our websites or use our mobile apps.

A cookie is a piece of data sent from a website and stored in a user’s web browser while a user is browsing a website. When the user browses the same website in the future, the data stored in the cookie can be retrieved by the website to notify the website of the user’s previous activity. We use this data to monitor the effectiveness of our websites and to help improve site functionality and the quality of our content. We collect information from audiences on our website, on social media and through other advertising channels for the purpose of remarketing.

If you do not wish your computer or mobile device to receive cookies, you can set your browser so that your computer or device does not accept them. You can also clear stored cookies from that browser or device at any time. Please note however that blocking cookies may affect your browsing experience and result in our services not operating as efficiently or effectively as they could.

Cookies have no way of disclosing your name or any personal information. Most browsers can be set to accept or reject cookies. You can choose to adjust your browser to reject cookies or to notify you when they are being used.

Rottnest Island Authority also uses image analytics and location data to refine content served through some marketing campaigns. Image and location data is not itself personally identifiable information. In the event it is linked to personally identifiable information, it will be treated as personal information in accordance with our Privacy Statement, the Privacy Act and any other applicable data protection legislation.

Location services may be disabled in your browser however you may not be able to use some portions of some of our apps.

### Complaints

If you consider that Rottnest Island Authority has not adhered to the provisions of this Privacy Statement, you may lodge a complaint by email at [enquiries@rottnestisland.com](mailto:enquiries@rottnestisland.com).

We undertake to investigate and respond to any such complaint within 28 days of its receipt at our offices.

### Further information

If you require further details about the Rottnest Island Authority’s Privacy Statement, or wish to comment on the statement, please contact us by email at [enquiries@rottnestisland.com](mailto:enquiries@rottnestisland.com) or telephone (+61 8) 9432 9300.

### References

[Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)](https://www.legislation.gov.au/Series/C2004A03712)

[Australian Privacy Principles](https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/australian-privacy-principles/read-the-australian-privacy-principles/)
