# Military & Maritime History

## Wadjemup is an island steeped in cultural, maritime, and historical significance

Outside of the stunning beaches, away from the turquoise water and idyllic setting, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island has a different set of stories to tell.

The island itself has long been used as a key point of Western Australia’s nautical navigation, from providing foundational support for the burgeoning Swan River Colony, to helping cargo and cruise ships safely reach port at Fremantle. It’s even played an important part in Western Australia’s efforts in securing its shores during the First and Second World Wars.

So for those with an enquiring mind, eager to discover a different side of the island, there’s more to explore. Discover the range of stories, names, places, and events that are woven into the island’s fabric, shaping its place in Western Australia’s history.

### Exploration

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island has a long, rich history, spanning generations and cultures. Once used by the [Whadjuk Noongar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) people for important ceremonies and meetings, rising sea levels around 6,000 or 7,000 years ago cut the island off from the mainland. It effectively remained undisturbed by human hands for thousands of years, with no current evidence — either cultural or scientific — suggesting that Whadjuk people inhabited or journeyed to the island during this time.

But it still played a prominent role in [the culture](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-culture), and became known through the Dreaming stories (Nytting) as the place where the spirits go to rest — the Noongar version of heaven.

Without any human disturbance during this time, the animal and bird population thrived.

The earliest known discovery of Rottnest Island by European explorers is credited to Dutch navigators during the 17th century, during their search for a shorter route from the Cape of Good Hope to Batavia. However, it wasn’t until 1658 that anyone actually set foot on the island, believed to have been Samuel Volkerson and his crew of the Dutch ship Waeckende Boey.

In 1696, the next recorded European visitors made landfall. Dutch sea captain Willem de Vlamingh landed on the island, giving it the famous name of Rottnest Island. This means ‘rat’s nest’ in Dutch, as he mistook the island’s abundant quokka population for giant rats.

Despite its prominence, it took until 1831 before any large presence was established on Wadjemup. As part of the Swan River Colony, Robert Thomson moved his family to the island and began building up the main settlement, now known as Thomson Bay.

1838 saw Wadjemup enter a sorrowful chapter of its history, with the construction of the Rottnest Island Aboriginal Establishment — a prison and forced labour camp that incarcerated over 4,000 Aboriginal boys and men over its 93-year lifespan.

Image Wadjemup Museum

Wadjemup Museum

### Over sea, under surf

As nautical travel became more prevalent around the island, the first noted maritime disaster occurred in 1842. The vessel *Transit* ran aground on a reef just off the coast. The same year, the first Wadjemup Lighthouse began construction. This was the first stone lighthouse built, and lit, in Western Australia.

Construction was completed in 1849, and it became active in 1851, providing two important functions to the island. The first, to identify Wadjemup’s presence to nearby vessels and highlight the dangerous reefs surrounding it. The second, to deliver a critical method of communication between seafaring vessels and the island’s pilot service.

The first [Rottnest Island Pilot Station](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pilot-boathouse) was built in 1846, and the service operated from 1848 until 1903. The pilots were experienced sailors whose job was to guide ships around the dangerous reefs surrounding Wadjemup, and into Fremantle harbour.

But even with the pilot service, and newly-built Wadjemup Lighthouse, maritime disasters still occurred — notably, the wooden cutter *Gem*, which was lost in 1876 leaving no survivors. The ship was sighted by the Wadjemup lighthouse keeper sailing three kilometres east of the island, at which point it abruptly sank. What happened to it remains a mystery to this day.

### The dawning of a new age

Despite the safeguards put in place to protect ships and their crews, seven more ships ran aground on reefs surrounding the island between 1878 and 1891. To help combat this, a second, larger lighthouse was built on the same site as [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse).

Designed to replace the existing structure, this newer, more modern lighthouse was built at the highest point on the island. Standing at 38 metres tall, it is the fourth tallest lighthouse of its kind in Australia.

The newer building provided a clearer beacon for seafaring vessels. Where the original lighthouse used a revolving catoptric light, that used a series of mirrors to reflect the light of a lantern, it only shone for five seconds every minute. The new lighthouse featured a more advanced holophotal dioptric revolving light that flashed every 20 seconds, providing much better navigation for any vessels passing by Wadjemup.

But in 1899 tragedy struck again, with the vessel *City of York* running aground on the island’s reefs, with 12 lives lost.

This spurred the construction of a [second lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) at Bathurst Point. This new lighthouse would enable navigators to pinpoint their location by triangulation, greatly increasing safety over the seas.

Image Bathurst Lighthouse

Bathurst Lighthouse

### Wadjemup during the Great War

While the beaches of Gallipoli and the muddy fields of France and Belgium were far, far away, Wadjemup still played a part in Western Australia’s efforts during World War I. Australia’s Department of Defence commandeered the island as an internment camp from 1914 to the end of 1915.

In September 1915, the camp held 989 people on its shores. While most of those within the camp were there purely due to German and Austrian heritage, there were some legitimate prisoners of war.

Despite the initial fervour in the war effort, however, the internment camp was abolished, and recreation and holiday pursuits returned to Wadjemup in December 1915.

Image Oliver Hill Battery

[Oliver Hill Battery](/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill)

### Between the wars

As Wadjemup returned to its peacetime trappings, the world moved on, and the technology on the island progressed. Buildings were improved, [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) was upgraded to an automatic flashing light in 1920, visible up to 14 nautical miles across the waves. This helped further improve the safe passage for ships over the ocean.

During this time, however, political upheaval was rearing itself again in Europe.

In 1933, with rumblings of international conflict on the horizon, Rottnest Island was identified as a critical point in Western Australia’s coastal defence. It was agreed that the installation of a system of guns on the island could provide vital defence of Fremantle Port against any hostile ships.

In 1936, [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) was connected to electrical power. At the same time, preparations began at Bickley Point to make way for the island’s naval defences.

Two gun batteries were constructed on the island: [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery), featuring one set of two 6-inch guns, and [Oliver Hill Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), with two 9.2-inch guns. The military also constructed six searchlight emplacements, magazine shell stores, a powerhouse, a directing station, and a railway from the jetty to the 9.2-inch guns.

This became known as the Rottnest Island Fortress.

### Inside the Fortress

September 1937 saw Rottnest Island declared a permanent station for Australian troops, with personnel from the Army, Navy, Airforce, and the Australian Women’s Army Service (AWAS) and Women’s Royal Australian Navy Service (WRANS). And to perform their vital defence duties, a number of other buildings were constructed to support Bickley Battery and [Oliver Hill Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill).

As well as construction of a barracks at Kingstown, in 1938 a four-storey Battery Observation Post was constructed at Signal Ridge, and another at [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery). The upper floor housed instruments to observe and direct gunfire from the [Oliver Hill Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). The floors below were used by Fire Command, or Fortress Command, as it was known, a station that coordinated gunfire of all the batteries in the Fremantle Fortress area. They shared the space with important roles such as the searchlight control engineer, a signal group, and other personnel.

Signal Ridge, the ridge just next to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), was chosen as the site of strategic signalling and military installations. A Signal Station was originally sited at Bathurst Point in 1904, but was dismantled and moved to this more practical location in 1939. The new site allowed the signallers to see ships approaching in any direction, allowing better communication with incoming ships, and ensuring faster response times should the guns be required. Staffed by WRANS personnel, the two-storey building afforded a full 360-degree view over the island.

Image Bickley Battery

Bickley Battery

### World War II comes to Australia

After war broke out in 1939, Wadjemup was declared a prohibited area in June 1940. All recreational activity ended. A declaration that was intended to last three months, this continued for a further five years until June 1945. The island was occupied by military and naval personnel only during this time, with the two gun batteries manned 24 hours a day.

Accommodation was needed for further personnel on the island, so WRANS House was established for the signallers operating the Signal Station. They worked in shifts of four hours on, and eight hours off, and rotated duties between Rottnest Island and Fremantle. The first signallers arrived on the island in 1943, and stayed until the Signal Station closed in 1945.

And yet, despite the impending threat to Western Australia’s shores, the guns were never fired at an enemy vessel.

As the country’s military focus moved north, the fixed defences at Rottnest Island were reduced. Peace came once again to the island — but the guns, the gun emplacements, the tunnels, and the buildings and infrastructure required for war still remained.

Image Signal Station

Signal Station

### After the wars

By April 1945, all buildings at the main settlement had been vacated by the military, except for the bakehouse and garage. Approximately 200 Italian prison camp internees were sent to the island for four months to carry out repairs and renovations.

In June 1945, the prohibition order on Rottnest Island was lifted, and civilians were again allowed back to its shores.

[Oliver Hill Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) was put into maintenance mode and decommissioned in 1960. Despite its use long since gone, it was never dismantled, and the entire emplacement remains intact, ready to explore. This was part as testament to the role they played in Western Australia’s defence—but also due to the high cost of dismantling them and shipping the scrap back to Perth.

[Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery) remained in operation until 1968. At this point the guns were decommissioned and dismantled. One can be found installed out the front of Kingstown Barracks, as a reminder of the area’s significance. The other was transported back across the channel, and can now be found at the Leighton Battery on Buckland Hill, Mosman Park, almost directly opposite Bickley Point across the waves.

The Kingstown Barracks themselves were still used for military purposes up until 1984. But with just 43 days’ use out of the entire year, it was decided to close these too. Following this, it began its new life hosting hundreds of school children and groups in Barrack-style accommodation, before becoming the [accommodation location](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-hostel) it is today.

### Today you can experience history for yourself

These stories from Rottnest Island’s past are still there to be explored.

Start your historical expedition at [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum). Newly renovated, it provides a gateway into the stories, with exhibits, artefacts, and audio experiences that tell the rich and complex history of the island.

The [Pilot Boathouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pilot-boathouse) still remains for visitors to explore, complete with a replica pilot boat, providing a better understanding of what life was like for these brave seafarers.

Wadjemup Lighthouse provides a unique chance for a guided tour all the way to the top, a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see the inner workings of a fully-functioning lighthouse. It has changed a little from its original lantern fixture, however. The beacon was made fully automatic in 1990, and a newer, brighter lantern was installed, which can shine up to 26 nautical miles out to sea.

While closed to the public, [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) remains a popular tourist spot, providing iconic photos and gorgeous views looking out across Pinky Beach.

Take a guided tour of the [Oliver Hill Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), and descend into the tunnels underneath the guns. Here you’ll learn more about what life was like for the men working the battery, and what went on underneath the earth during its operation.

Signal Ridge, the Battery Observation Post, and WRANS House are all still standing, and provide insight into life during wartime on the island.

Maritime enthusiasts can explore the shipwrecks surrounding the island. Hike around the island to find the landbound plaques that point you out to sea, towards the final resting place of these vessels, and learn more about each ship.

Or, for more intrepid adventurers, you can dive below the waves and explore them yourself. The wrecks of *Uribes*, wrecked in 1942, and the barge *Shark*, sunk in 1939, lie just metres from Wadjemup’s shores, providing an excellent snorkelling experience for those looking to experience history under the waves.

Other wrecks can be found further out to sea, where you can visit them by boat or by scuba diving offshore. The [Western Australian Museum](https://museum.wa.gov.au/maritime-archaeology-db/wrecks/map) has created a map for experienced divers, marking out the GPS coordinates of each wreck.

* An Unforgettable Group Getaway to Rottnest Island

# An Unforgettable Group Getaway to Rottnest Island

Make the most of your time on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island with mates for a visit to remember.

4 minutes

Image 

**There's something especially restorative about a getaway with friends.**

At Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, you’ll have a chance to truly unwind and connect with those around you. From fishing and swimming to barbecue by the beach, or sundowners overlooking some of the best views in Western Australia, Rottnest Island has it all.

Here are a few suggestions for how to make the most of your time on the island and ensure your next group getaway is one to remember.

### Cycling

Cycling is the best way to explore the island at your own pace. Cruise the wide-open roads, amongst vibrant green bushland with birdlife soaring overhead. Every corner you turn reveals a new, sparkling blue ocean vista – guaranteed to put a smile on your face. You can bring your own bikes to Wadjemup or hire them from [Pedal & Flipper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire)  on the island. Saddle up and be prepared to race your friends from beach to bay or tackle one of these cycle routes as a team.

### Snorkelling and swimming

Rottnest Island has 63 beaches and 20 bays, with fine, white sand and inviting blue waters. Surrounded by coral reefs, the island is perfect for snorkelling and swimming. Choose your destination from our [favourite snorkelling spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/where-to-snorkel-at-rottnest-island--six-of-the-best-spots), stop by Pedal & Flipper Hire for a beach cricket set and a paddleboard or two, then prepare yourself for a day of beach fun with your friends.

### Eat and drink

There’s nothing quite like connecting with friends over a feast. And there are countless options to do just that on Rottnest Island, from delicious [bakery treats](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) for a beachside picnic or barbecue to handmade sourdough pizzas from [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) and shared tapas at [The Mezz on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-mezz-on-rotto). Whether you’re looking for a quick bite to eat, a pub feed or an afternoon of drinks, there’s an [option to suit](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink) every group.

### 

### Golf

[Rottnest Island Golf Course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) is one of the island’s hidden gems. Boasting nine holes, which can double to a full 18-hole round, plus a barefoot bowling green and clubhouse, it’s one of Western Australia’s most unique golfing experiences.

### Segway tour

Explore Rottnest Island’s breathtaking scenery and natural beauty on your own revolutionary set of wheels on a tour with [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa). You and your mates will love this exciting, eco-friendly and safe experience. Riding a Segway is easy to learn and you’ll quickly be on your way to experiencing the more off-road corners of the island.

### Skydive

More of an adrenaline-seeking group? A skydive over Rottnest Island is an unforgettable experience that you’ll talk about for years to come. With [Skydive Geronimo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/skydive-geronimo) you can do a tandem skydive from up to 15,000 feet over the island, enjoying a panoramic parachute ride and landing on the beach. The more down-to-earth friends can even watch from the comfort of the sand.

### Hiking

Lace up your boots and explore the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi). This 45-km network of trails, made up of five sections, takes you across spectacular coastal headlands, past stunning lakes, and man-made attractions. Choose your trail, pack a lunch and enjoy a day further afield on the island.

### Diving

If you’re a group of diving fans, you’re in luck too. The diversity of fish, coral species and shipwrecks in the waters around the island make it one of the most [fascinating dive sites](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) to be found in such close proximity to a capital city. Bring your own gear over or head to the team at [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) when you arrive on the island for dive tanks and refills.

### Fishing

Wadjemup is a [recreational fishing dream](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing), with a bounty to offer. The seagrass meadows around Rottnest Island serve as a nursery for many fish species, such as cobbler and flathead. Bring your rod and settle in for a day of fishing with your friends - you might even catch your dinner!

[Sustainable Fishing

To maintain a sustainable supply of fish for the future, please only take what you need. Read more about fishing on Rottnest Island.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones)

# Whale Watching

### WITNESS WHALES IN THE WILD FROM LAND, SEA AND SKY

Sightings of majestic species of whale, or maamoong in Noongar, make a visit to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island an especially memorable experience. During [winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) and [spring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/spring), between the months of August and December – but sometimes as early as June and July – migratory species such as the humpback whale and southern right whale can be spotted as they glide through the expansive Indian Ocean surrounding the island.

Look out for distinctive blowhole spray or barnacled bodies while on board the ferry, with whale sightings possible on the journey to and from the mainland. Upon your arrival, make your way to one (or all) of the land-based island lookouts for glimpses of these gentle giants in the surrounding marine reserve waters. Boat and plane tours that take you on or above the ocean also offer a unique vantage point for your whale watching experience.

### WHERE TO SEE WHALES ON ROTTNEST ISLAND

Whale watching season sees approximately 35,000 migrating whales linger in the calm ocean around the island between August and December. During this time, newborn calves also play in the protected waters and make for a uniquely seasonal spectacle.

[Keep Your Distance

If visiting on a private boat, ensure you keep your distance from whales, especially calves and nursing mothers, and collect floating debris if safe to do so. If you see a marine animal in distress, contact the rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us)

Whale sightings can occur as soon as your [ferry ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry) over to the island. Arrive early to secure yourself a window seat or spot on the open-air deck to relish the refreshing sea air and increase your chances of spotting a whale.

On the island, make for the [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) by [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling) or [bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) where two viewing platforms beckon at [Cape Vlamingh and Cathedral Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-top-five-lookouts-on-wadjemup-rottnest-island). Both are equipped with binoculars for the best views of any maamoong (whale) movement and other wildlife such as frolicking dolphins, lounging long-nosed fur seals and the iconic yoorndoordoo (osprey). This end of the island welcomes hours of exploration with amenities close by.

Closer to the main settlement, [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) is a popular place to spot whales during whale watching season. Ascend the stairs up to [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) and cast your gaze far across the horizon. [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay) also provides a reliable lookout point.

To get the ultimate view, take to the skies. [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi) operates daily scenic flights that allow you to appreciate the entirety of the island below, including any whales that may be dancing above and beneath the waves.

Image Eco Express

### Eco Express Boat Tours with Rottnest Express

**Operating September to April**

If your visit occurs before January, your boat tour could include glimpses of the ocean’s graceful acrobats. Pods of humpback whales commonly breach and offer a breathtaking sideshow to this tour. Earlier in the season, you’ll still be able to spot the whales from various coastal lookouts on the island.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/eco-express-boat-tours)

Image A whale mid-breach, rising from the sea off Rottnest Island-36.tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=98b5f69_2)

Whale watching from Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

### SPECTACULAR SIGHTINGS

#### Southern Right Whale

These creatures cruise at a relaxed pace while showing off their acrobatic side. Delight in a rare sighting of a “head stand”, which involves the whales tipping themselves vertical and waving their flukes in the air. Occasionally these whales will breach (jump out of the water) up to ten times in a row.

When it comes to travelling through the sea, southern right whales tend to be solitary or move only in small groups. The exception is when they are in breeding areas, during which time they swim in larger pods.

#### Humpback Whale

This species of whale is larger and more commonly spotted near the island. Humpbacks are powerful swimmers and will sometimes throw themselves out of the water and roll in the air before crashing down. This behaviour is a beautiful sight to behold but remains a mystery to scientists. These whales migrate in groups, so if you catch a glimpse of a distinctive hump or dorsal fin, there’s bound to be more nearby.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I spot whales from the island?

[Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach), [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay) and [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) are popular locations to whale watch on Rottnest Island at any time of day. Travel around to these locations during your visit to enjoy all that the island offers and increase your whale sighting chances along the way. You might also spot whales on your ferry journey as you approach or leave the island.

Are there any whale watching tours from the island?

There are no specific whale watching tours on Rottnest Island, however there are tours that often see whales on their travels during the migratory season including [Eco Express Boat Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/eco-express-boat-tours?tab=see-do), and scenic flights with [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi).

When is the best time of year to spot whales from the island?

The best seasons for whale watching from the vantage points on Rottnest Island is during [winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) and [spring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/spring). Whales can be seen as early as June and July. The migratory period officially takes place from August to December, further increasing your chances of sightings on the ferry, on boat tours, and from the island.

What other wildlife will I see at Rottnest Island?

You can expect to see [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas), birdlife, [long-nosed fur seals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/seals-and-sea-lions), bottlenose dolphins and [Australian sea lions](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/seals-and-sea-lions) throughout the year. Warmer months increase sightings of reptiles, then during winter various frog species repopulate around the wetlands. From August until December, you may even spot [whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) migrating through the waters around the island.

When is the best time of day for whale watching?

Whales are migrating through the waters surrounding Wadjemup / Rottnest Island at all times of the day during whale watching season, so there is no particular time of day that is best to spot them.

* [Overview](#c9498647-c0a6-42ea-99ec-8028542a1a3b-0 "Overview")

**Discover the Wonders of Rottnest Island with Laura the Explorer Bike Tours.**

Laura the Explorer Bike Tours offer an unparalleled adventure on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Led by Laura, a passionate Perth local, these full-day cycling tours blend excitement and education for a truly unique experience. Participants will embark on a scenic 10 km bike ride, exploring the island’s stunning beaches and bays. Along the way, you’ll delve into the island’s significant history, enjoy a one-hour break for swimming and snorkelling, and unwind with a delicious lunch.

As the only full-day bike tour on the island, you’ll have the opportunity to explore the island’s famous beaches before the crowds and enjoy a personalised and exclusive experience.

Most fitness levels are catered for, making this tour the perfect choice for seasoned cyclists and casual riders alike. With all details handled for you on this all-inclusive tour, simply settle in to enjoy the ride and your breathtaking surroundings.

Whether you’re exploring solo, with a partner, or with friends, Laura the Explorer Bike Tours ensures a memorable day filled with fun and exploration.

### Tours on offer

Image 

All-inclusive package

**Duration:** 7 hours, with 1.5 - 3 hours of cycling time   
**Departs:** Monday to Sunday at 7 am from Hillarys Boat Harbour   
**Ages:** 12+

Includes:

* Complimentary shuttle service from Perth City or Scarborough to Hillarys Boat Harbour
* Return ferry travel from Hillarys Boat Harbour and island admission
* Bike hire
* Snorkel and mask
* Lunch
* Full day tour with commentary from your guide Laura (1.5 - 3 hours of cycling time)
* A 1-hour break for swimming and snorkelling
* A special memento to remember your adventure

[Check Availability](https://lauratheexplorer.com.au/)

Image 

BYO Bike Package

**Duration:** 7 hours, with 1.5 - 3 hours of cycling time   
**Departs:** Monday to Sunday at 8:45 am from Rottnest Island   
**Ages:** 12+

Includes:

* Full day tour with commentary from your guide Laura (1.5 - 3 hours of cycling time)
* A 1-hour break for swimming and snorkelling
* Lunch
* A special memento to remember your adventure

 Please note that you’ll need to arrange your own transport to and from the island, as well as your own bike and snorkel gear.

[Check Availability](https://lauratheexplorer.com.au/)

#### Where to find Laura the Explorer

If you have booked the BYO bike package, tours depart from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), please check your booking confirmation for the specific meeting point. If you have booked the all-inclusive package, tours depart from Hillarys Boat Harbour.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What do I need to bring?

Please wear comfortable shoes for cycling and dress suitably for the weather conditions. Bring a water bottle, sunscreen and a towel if you’d like to swim during the tour.

How old do you need to be?

People aged 12 years and over are welcome to join Laura’s tours. Children under 18 years must be accompanied by an adult.

Can I bring my own bike?

While you're welcome to bring your own bike, please note that you'll need to arrange your own transport to and from the island, as well as your own snorkel gear if you wish to snorkel.

Is wearing a bicycle helmet required?

Yes, bicycle helmets are required by Western Australian law. A helmet will be supplied with the all-inclusive package, if you’re booking the BYO bike package, you must bring your own helmet.

Is it hard to cycle around Rottnest Island?

The route is moderate in difficulty and covers 10 km, suitable for those with some cycling experience. Actual cycling time is between 1.5 to 3 hours.

* 4 Ways to Slow Down and Reconnect in Winter

# 4 Ways to Slow Down and Reconnect in Winter

Whether you're seeking quiet solitude, time with loved ones, or a reconnection with nature, winter invites you to slow down.

4 minutes

Image 

Watch an island sunset

**Winter on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is more than an off-season escape, it’s a time to realign, rest, and recharge. Whether you’re seeking quiet solitude, meaningful time with loved ones, or a deeper connection with nature, winter invites you to slow down and rediscover what matters.**

From the thriving native landscape to the comfort of warming local meals, and the stillness required to reconnect to yourself and all that surrounds you, here’s our guide to the restoration that awaits you at Wadjemup.

### Solo Winter Getaways: Find Stillness, Move Mindfully, Reconnect Deeply

For solo travellers, [winter on Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) is an opportunity to embrace spaciousness. With fewer crowds and time entirely your own, the island becomes your personal sanctuary.

Wander one of the [Wadjemup Bid](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi)i trails, wrapped up against the chill, warming as your heart rate rises. The [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/explore-west-end-on-the-ngank-wen-bidi) traces 10 km of the southeast corner of the island, following the coastline then turning inward to [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) and [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) — it’s the trail where history and nature converge. The natural landscapes of Wadjemup are rich with wonder, so take the time to pause on the journey and take in the humbling vastness of the Indian Ocean and the lush beauty of the bushland.

On your own, you can recharge at your own pace. Perhaps follow your wander in nature with an [indulgent massage](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mobile-massage-on-rottnest-island-by-golden-bees) then settle in for a quiet afternoon curled up with a glass of wine or hot beverage, and a book that holds your attention as gently as the island's hush. Whatever replenishment looks like for you, it's yours to choose.

To deepen the experience, visit [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) and spend time immersing yourself in the island’s layered history. As you wander the 17 exhibits and outside Sculpture Garden, allow space to quietly reflect on what you have seen, and on the stories that have shaped Wadjemup over time.

### Romantic Winter Escapes: Slow Down and Reconnect with Each Other

Couples seeking cosy solitude will find just what they need on the island. Rottnest Island’s isolation from the mainland makes it even more suited for disconnecting... So, you can reconnect to each other.

Winter is a romantic time on the island. Soft rain disturbing the smooth surface of the [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), windy seas bordered by moody violet skies, and a beachside firepit keeping the chill at bay. And when you stay overnight or for a few days, you can sink into the experience, slowly exploring at your leisure.

Crafting the perfect couples’ escape on Wadjemup begins with your [accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay), with options including secluded glamping under the stars at [Discovery Resorts – Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island), a coastal boutique suite at [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest), or a lakeside room with a view at [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup). Share simple pleasures like a homemade dinner or indulge in a sumptuous multi-course feast at one of the [island’s eateries](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink).

Let nature shape your rhythm by heading out to explore the island by foot or by bike. The [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) trails crisscross the island for 45 km, so you can wander at leisure amongst the unique flora and fauna, your time together only interrupted by birdsong. Then finish up with a dinner of satisfying Italian fare at [Isola Bar e Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest), South East Asian eats at the intimate [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara) restaurant, or Mediterranean dishes at [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest), all enclosed to stay toasty and warm this winter.

### Winter Wanders with Friends: Connect Through Nature, Movement & Laughter

Sometimes it’s hard to stay motivated over winter and these seasonal blues can keep us from connecting with others. Gathering your friends and loved ones for a winter getaway is just as important as following the sunshine in summer.

Start the day with a brisk [bike ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island) around the island or test your limits [with a surf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-surfing-rottnest-islands-surf-breaks) at Strickland Bay — the chill in the air only heightens the thrill. Later, enjoy a quiet picnic with sweeping coastal views, or gather for a casual game of [pickleball](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rotto-rackets-sports), adding a playful moment to the day.

But it’s also about slowing down. Evenings invite storytelling, board games, shared cooking, and plenty of laughter. With fewer distractions and more time, you’ll find new ways to connect and appreciate each other without the rush of everyday life.

### Family Reconnection: Nature-Filled Days, Screen-Free Moments

Winter can bring different discoveries for the family. Quiet, misty mornings on your balcony, gumboot-clad escapades, sharing a moment of wonder as an osprey takes flight.

Leave the screens behind and allow the kids to fully connect with nature and the meaningful history of the island.

As vehicles are limited on the island, children can roam safely [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike), exploring trails that wind past inland salt lakes, lush green bushland, and coastal expanses. Treat the kids to a hot chocolate and a bowl of chips at [Geordie’s Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery), then let them explore Wadjemup’s rich Aboriginal culture with an activity or workshop with [Koorda’s Crew](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda) or [Dooga Waalitj Healing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences). Through hands-on storytelling and creative experiences, young minds can connect with the culture of the Noongar people in a meaningful and memorable way. Or visit [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) for a journey of understanding where stories of the island’s past are told through 40,000-year-old artefacts and immersive audio experiences.

Then, bring this knowledge with you, appreciating the past as you engage in light-hearted family activities like an evening at the [Picture Hall](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) for the latest release movies and classic blockbusters.

This winter, give yourself permission to pause. Whether you’re coming alone, as a couple, with friends or family, the island offers space to rest, paths to wander, and mindful moments that will stay with you long after you leave. Let Wadjemup be the place you reconnect with nature, with others, and most importantly, with yourself.

# Lakes & Salt Lakes

### Venture into the centre of Wadjemup

While surrounded by water, the centre of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is home to even more bodies of water. An array of 12 salt lakes occupy 10% of Wadjemup’s inland space, taking up more than 200 hectares.

Interestingly, while being surrounded by the Indian Ocean, the water in these salt lakes is four times saltier than that in the sea.

Despite this, the island’s clever plant life has evolved to cope with these high salt levels. Plants like beaded samphire, coastal bonefruit, grey saltbush, and coastal pigface all exist close to the lakes’ edges. Be sure to stay on the marked trails, though, to make sure you don’t trample the delicate, thousand-year-old microbialites that grow on the shores.

It creates a unique wetland habitat, crisscrossed with walking trails, that’s ripe for quiet exploration and reflection.

The [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi) section of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) winds its way through the lake systems. A 9.5 km loop hike, it takes you up hills, through the patchwork Wadjemup bushland. The star of the trail is the lakes’ boardwalk section, installed over the salty surface to make it feel as though you’re walking—perhaps floating—on water.

### Where to find Wadjemup’s salt lakes

The salt lakes can be found all across the northeastern corner of the island. The first, Garden Lake, is located just a three-minute walk along Digby Drive from the main settlement.

Image Lakes, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

[Sunset over the salt lakes](/see-do/wildlife-nature)

### Watch the salt pans come alive

Many of Rottnest Island’s salt lakes, including Lake Baghdad, Lake Vincent, Herschel Lake, Garden Lake, Government House Lake, and Serpentine Lake, are permanent wetland fixtures of the island. They feature water all year round—and even have their own surrounding beaches.

Other lakes such as Pink Lake, Lake Sirius, Lake Negri, and the twin Pearse Lakes, have a tendency to dry out over summer, leaving large swathes of white—or pink—salt pans.

Standing in stark contrast to Wadjemup’s radiant blue summer skies, the real magic happens when the sun sets. As it starts to dip over the horizon, and the light begins to dim, the dry salt lake beds reflect back the burning sunset colours, creating a brilliant canvas for a unique Wadjemup experience.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Can I swim in the salt lakes?

No, no swimming is allowed in the salt lakes. It wouldn’t be very pleasant, anyway, given how salty the water is. Instead, why not try one of the many beautiful beaches dotted around the island.

Where can I start the Gabbi Karniny Bidi?

You can start the Gabbi Karniny Bidi from the main settlement. Step out from the Wadjemup Visitor Centre, head west out Digby Drive towards Vlamingh Lookout, and follow the yellow trail markers as you make the 9.5 km loop around the lakes.

Are there guided tours of the salt lakes?

While it’s very well signposted, [The Hike Collective](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective) provides a Lakes & Bays Guided Hike, which takes intrepid visitors along the Gabbi Karniny Bidi.

Head to the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) to find out more about guided walking tours.

* The Best Sunset Locations on Rottnest Island

# The best sunset locations on Rottnest Island

Settle in for a beautiful sky show at one of our top sunset spots.

4 minutes

Image Rottnest Island sunsets

Rottnest Island sunsets

**It doesn’t get much better than a sun-soaked day on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. But for something special, you need to hang around until the sun goes down.**

Reflect on a day of discovery with one of the most spectacular natural attractions on the island - a golden sunset over the Indian Ocean. The sky turns cotton-candy pink, the ocean glitters and the breeze cools your sun-warmed skin.

Whether you’re staying on the island or just taking advantage of the [9 pm late night ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals/9-pm-return-ferry-travel), settle in for a beautiful sky show at one of these top Rottnest Island sunset locations.

### Pinky Beach

Nestled to the north of Thomson Bay, you’ll find the breathtaking [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). If you’ve spent any time scrolling through Rottnest Island location tags on Instagram, you’re bound to have come across a Pinky’s sunset. With [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) providing a scenic backdrop, Pinky Beach will impress even the most seasoned sunset-enthusiast. Plus, you can head on over to [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) for delicious cocktail or craft beer, and in summer, enjoy live music on weekends. Be sure to check out [what’s on](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/whats-on).

### Bathurst Lighthouse

If you’re looking to level up your sunset views, visit [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse). Here you’ll experience a huge sunset vista with uninterrupted views across Pinky Beach, the Indian Ocean, and back towards the Perth coastline. While the lighthouse is closed to visitors, you can still watch the glow from the base.

Image Sunset at Bathurst Lighthouse

[Sunset at Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island)

### Garden Lake

Only a short walk from the settlement, Garden Lake offers unique sunset views of both the [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) and Wadjemup Lighthouse in one picture-perfect composition. The calm lakes reflect the vibrant colours of the sky, making it a must-see for sunset lovers. Garden Lake is also a renowned location for [quokka spotting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island), so keep your eyes peeled at dusk.

Remember that [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) are wild animals, so please keep a respectful distance and never touch or feed them. If one approaches you, step back slowly to give them plenty of space.

### On-board a sunset cruise

Why not try a beautiful sunset sail with [Charter 1](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1) to finish off your day? Enjoy a stunning perspective of golden hour on their luxury catamaran tour. From the sound of the breeze in the sails to the complimentary bubbles and antipasto, it is a blissful experience to add to your Rottnest Island itinerary.

### Vlamingh Lookout

Located just beyond the main settlement, Vlamingh Lookout offers sunset hunters an alternate view as the sun dips over the shimmering [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). You can easily walk or ride over to the lookout, experience the sunset and make it back in time for your [dinner plans](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/sip--eat-and-indulge-a-little-longer-until-9-pm).

Image Sunset at Rottnest Island

[Sunset on Charter 1](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/charter-1?tab=see-do)

Image Sunset at Rottnest Island

[Sunset over the salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island)

### Geordie Bay

Home to one of Rottnest Island’s largest and most popular beaches, [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) provides stunning sunset views in an idyllic setting. As an alternative to cycling, [bus services](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) offer convenient access to the bay and its attractions. Before making any plans, be sure to check operating hours as late services are seasonal and are subject to change throughout the year. Plus, visitors can enjoy a bite to eat from [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) and a sweet treat from [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery) after basking in the evening’s lightshow.

### Oliver Hill

As well as a hub of history, [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) offers a spectacular sunset spot. The hill provides an incredible lookout, offering a panoramic view over the southern side of the island. You can watch the sun fall behind the distinguished profile of [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse), making for an impressive photo opportunity as the colours of the sky silhouette the iconic landmark. Due to the secluded nature of the location, it is best to cycle back to the main settlement soon after, before it gets too dark.

Image Sunset at Rottnest Island

Sunset

### Tips for taking the best sunset snaps

* **Ensure your camera lens is clean.** Whether you’re using a smartphone or digital camera, a fingerprint on your lens can wreak havoc on any photograph! Give your lens a quick wipe before taking photos with a soft cloth.
* **Consider composition as you frame up your shot.** What elements are in the foreground? This could be the sandy beach, the ocean, a beachside venue, or a natural landmark. Now shift your focus to the background. Is the skyline clear or cloudy, and where is our hero, the sun?
* **Move around.** Don’t be afraid to change positions and capture your Rottnest Island sunset from different angles. Get creative!
* **Shoot wide and then zoom in.** The more you capture in your image, the more you have to work with. Then you can zoom in and simply crop away anything unwanted.

Got the shot? Share it with us on social media! Simply tag us with **#RottnestIsland**

Welcome to Wadjemup

## 'The place across the water where the spirits are’

Once connected to the mainland, Wadjemup was known as an important meeting place and ceremonial site for the Whadjuk people — a place of transition between the physical and spiritual world. Every visit to Wadjemup should be one of reciprocity and respect. Visitors are encouraged to acknowledge and pay respects to the Whadjuk people’s ancestors and their Elders past, present and future.

[Learn the Story of Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history)

# Overnight Camp Subsidy

### Connecting students with the wonders of Wadjemup

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a popular [school camp destination](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/groups-functions/education-groups), offering a wealth of nature-based and cultural experiences to ignite curiosity among students of all ages. And now even more students can access the educational experiences on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, with the Rottnest Island Authority Overnight Camp Subsidy.

Western Australian government schools can apply for the program which includes from 75% to 100% subsidised fees for Rottnest Island Authority accommodation, bike hire and educational tours for schools which meet the criteria of an [Index of Community Socio-Educational Advantage](https://myschool.edu.au/) (ICSEA) percentile between 0 to 60 based on the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (ACARA) 2025 database.

Applications are Now Closed for 2026

Applications to receive a subsidised school camp have now closed.

# Little Salmon Bay

## Wadjemup’s coral coast

Located at one of the southern-most tips of the island, Little Salmon Bay is one of the more popular bays on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Its naturally-sheltered location makes for calm, clear waters, perfect for families looking for a relaxing swimming experience.

It’s an excellent spot for snorkelling and exploring under the waves. Follow the [Little Salmon Bay snorkel trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-salmon-bay-snorkel-trail) to discover more about the plethora of Wadjemup sea life.

Some lucky beachgoers might even have the fortune to spot the rare Australian sea lion lounging on the beach, soaking up the sun. But if you do see one, be sure to watch it from a distance rather than getting up close, and let it enjoy its time on the beach, too.

### Take a look around and find…

Image 

Stunning snorkel trail under the water

Image 

Beautiful coral reefs

Image 

The rare Australian sea lion

Image 

The nearby Wardan Nara Bidi

### Where to find Little Salmon Bay

Located on the south side of the island, Little Salmon Bay is over five kilometres away from the main settlement. It’s a bit long to walk, but makes for a nice 25-minute bike ride. Alternatively, you can simply take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and get off at stop 6.

Image 

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Learn more about Wadjemup’s underwater magic

Little Salmon Bay doesn’t just sparkle on the surface—there’s a whole world under the waves to explore. Strap on your snorkel and tighten your fins, wade into the water and get ready to learn. Little Salmon Bay features its own snorkel trail, a series of information panels installed on the seabed that tells you all about the sea life and its surrounds.

Explore the limestone reef on the left hand side of the bay, and follow the trail right around to the other side. Marked by information panels and marker buoys, the trail guides intrepid snorkellers out into the bay. The water never gets too deep, so it’s perfect for beginners and families—and be on the lookout for glimpses of starfish, crayfish, and other tropical fish.

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

Image Little Salmon Bay, Rottnest Island

Little Salmon Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby?

There are no facilities at Little Salmon Bay. But don’t worry, the Parker Point facilities are an easy five-minute walk away—or one minute on the bike.

Can I fish at Little Salmon Bay?

No. Little Salmon Bay is part of the Parker Point Marine Sanctuary Zone, so no fishing is permitted.

How do I get there?

Little Salmon Bay is a leisurely 25-minute bike ride from the Thomson Bay settlement. Alternatively, get off at Stop 6 on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus.

# Boating

## Explore the waters around Wadjemup unhindered by land

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is often defined by the ocean surrounding it — a collection of sand dunes and salty lakes bordered by clear turquoise bays that merge into the expanse of dark blue. And the best way to connect with these waters is to get up close on a boat.

Travelling around the island on a boat is a deeply nostalgic experience. It’s steeped in childhood memories of wavy voyages from the mainland, cannonball jumps from the deck, and relaxed barbecue dinners by the beach. And for those who don’t have these memories, they are waiting.

Whether join a tour or journey over on your own vessel, endless opportunities awaken with the freedom of a boat.

Image A yellow catamaran sails in clear turquoise waters with people swimming behind it. The sea is calm, and the sky is clear blue. Other boats and a rocky coastline are in the background.

[Charter 1 Sailing Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/charter-1)

Parker Point

### A new perspective of the island

### Trace the island’s coastline with a boat tour

Boat tours are an opportunity to sit back and absorb the views, letting someone else steer your journey — whether that’s with [Charter 1](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1), [Rottnest Cruises](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises), [Eco Express tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours), or [Rottnest Snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-snorkel).

The Charter 1 sailing catamaran has several options, including private charters, a snorkelling trip to the island’s thriving tropical shallows, and a sunset sail that’s pure decompression. Or for the most unique dining experience the island has to offer, join Rottnest Cruises for a decadent sea-to-plate seafood cruise on a voyage over the island’s lush marine gardens. You can also step aboard Rottnest Snorkel for a guided exploration of the island's vibrant underwater world, rich with colourful fish and bright coral. For another perspective, join an Eco Express Adventure Boat tour for a full lap around Wadjemup, stopping to spot wildlife along the way.

### Boating and mooring regulations

With the freedom of your own boat, comes the need to follow regulations that keep the island running smoothly and protect the unique flora and fauna.

Check out important boating and mooring information on the [Rottnest Island Authority website](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/boating) to learn everything you need to know about using your boat in the waters of the island.

# Contact Us

Have a query or comments about your visit? Get in touch.

### Rottnest Island Visitor Centre

For information about visiting Rottnest Island, the friendly team at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) offer a wealth of knowledge and services.

* **Phone:** (+61 8) 9372 9730
* **Address:** 1 Henderson Ave, Rottnest Island WA 6161
* View the [Visitor Centre opening hours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre)

To register any lost and found personal items, please fill in the [Lost Property Form here](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=ZEaTe8_NKE6j7hpbzKChtgxz9dUC4c1Dsj0pQqwhVG1URVpWQldYU1RXV0NQMkZJTEJOTVFCMlVPUCQlQCN0PWcu).

### Stay Rottnest Reservations

For queries about Stay Rottnest accommodation or bookings, get in touch with the Stay Rottnest Reservations team.

* **Phone:** 1800 111 111
* **Email:**  [stay@rottnestisland.com](mailto:stay@rottnestisland.com)
* Visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/)

### Rottnest Island Authority Administration

For general enquiries about the management of Rottnest Island, please visit the [Rottnest Island Authority website](https://ria.wa.gov.au/) or get in touch via the details below.

* **Phone:** (+61 8) 9432 9300
* **Email:** [enquiries@rottnestisland.com](mailto:enquiries@rottnestisland.com)
* **Address:** 1 Mews Road, Fremantle WA 6160
* **Postal Address:** PO Box 693, Fremantle WA 6959
* **Opening Hours:** Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm (excluding public holidays)

### For Sick or Injured Wildlife

If you see sick or injured wildlife, or wildlife being mistreated, please report it immediately to the Rottnest Island Rangers.

* **Phone:**(+61 8) 9372 9788
* **Email:**  [enquiries@rottnestisland.com](mailto:enquiries@rottnestisland.com)

# Accommodation FAQ

### Frequently Asked Questions

Can I stay in the campground?

The subsidy only applies for bookings within the Kingstown Barracks Dormitories, Hostel and Governor Circle accommodation.  Campground bookings will be charged at normal rates.

How many adults do I need to organise for the camp?

We require at least one adult per 10 students when staying in the dormitories and hostel, and a minimum of one adult per Governor Circle cottage.

Is bed linen included as a part of the booking?

A blanket and a pillow are provided for each bed. Bed linen and towels are available to be hired and are not a part of the booking. Download the [Stay Rottnest Hire Form](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/accommodation_hire_items_2026.pdf) for more information.

Is there a room that can be used for night activities?

A complementary activity room hire (for up to one day maximum) can be added to the booking; however, they are subject to availability.

What if I need to cancel my booking?

Your booking can be cancelled without fees up until three months prior to arrival (refer to full  [terms and conditions](https://www.rottnestisland.com/overnight-camp-subsidy/terms-and-conditions)).

When will I need to pay the security deposit and/or the discounted rate?

Security deposits and balance payments are required three months prior to arrival.  Failure to pay deposits and balance by the due date may result in cancellation of booking.

Can we self-cater?

The catering options vary for each accommodation.

Whilst Governor Circle cottages have fully equipped kitchens and a BBQ, the dormitories at Kingstown Barracks have no catering facilities available. The hostel has a shared kitchen and lounge facilities.

There are a range of island businesses that provide catering services for island guests.

Do you have wheelchair-accessible accommodation?

Yes, there is limited wheelchair-accessible accommodation and this is subject to availability.

Where and how do we get down to Kingstown Barracks?

Kingstown Barracks is located 1.8 km south of the Thomson Bay settlement. This is a leisurely 20-minute walk or 5-minute bike ride. There is also a shuttle service to Kingstown at a cost of $5 per person per day or $15 per week.

When and where can I check in?

Check-in time is from 2 pm for Governor Circle and 12 noon for dormitories and hostel accommodation.  Check-in is at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/visitor-centre) at the end of the main jetty prior to going to your accommodation.

When do I check out?

Check-out time is 10 am for the dormitories and hostel accommodation and 9 am for Governor Circle cottages.

How do I book my luggage transfer?

Your chosen ferry operator will provide your luggage labels or book your luggage crates. If you have your luggage delivered in crates, please pre-book your crate pick-up date and time at the  [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre)  while checking in.

Are there quiet times we need to know about?

The quiet times for Kingstown Barracks Dormitories, Hostel and Governor Circle are between 9 pm and 9 am.

What if a student or teacher gets sick on the island during our camp?

The [Rottnest Island Nursing Post](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/nursing-post) is open daily between 8:30 am and 4:30 pm with an on-call nurse available after hours. In the case of an emergency, please call 000.

# Autumn school holiday inspiration for all the family

With cool evenings and clear days, Rottnest Island in autumn is a haven for school holiday excitement, bringing the whole family closer to nature and each other.

6 minutes

Image Family enjoying the beach on a cool Autumn evening at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Geordie Bay

**Turn the April school holidays into golden memories. This is a time for togetherness amongst the rich natural beauty of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.**

With summer’s residual warmth and fewer crowds, [autumn](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/autumn) invites shared family adventure here on the island. The autumn school holidays take place in WA during April, falling over the [Noongar season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup) of Djeran: a time when warmer days can linger but a cool change starts to settle in. This time of year also marks the celebration of Easter, a popular period for family getaways, including to Wadjemup. The season’s pleasant conditions create comfortable active experiences for everyone, from hikes to ocean dips. This is a season for endless exploration.

Looking for the top family adventures to enjoy during autumn? Here’s your all-in-one guide to making the most of the island over the Easter school holidays.

### 

### AUTUMN ISLAND ADVENTURES FOR THE WHOLE FAMILY

#### EXPLORE BY BIKE

[Cycling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling) is a convenient way to get around the island any time of year, but come autumn, the cooler air compels you to go further. Pick up everyone’s gear from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire), including baby seats, child trailers, and kids' bikes. Then, take to the trails. Cruise along coastal paths without the strong summer heat, stopping to [spot wildlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature) and keep an eye out for the [resident quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas), wander hidden coves, or simply breathe in the crisp air.

The [Beaches, Lighthouses, and Lakes trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycling-trail-adventure--beaches--a-lighthouse-and-lakes) is a 10 km journey that takes you to some of Wadjemup’s most beautiful beaches and bays in just a few hours. With more time to spare and extra energy to burn, families with older kids could also take on the [Island Ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-island-ride--cycle-the-entire-island). This trail covers 22 km of stunning scenery all the way around Wadjemup, including the [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). Park up here to refuel at [Lexi’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lexi-s-on-rotto), where you’ll find warming coffee, sweet ice creams, and plenty of other snacks to keep you going. Sip, sit and stay awhile as you look out for the much-loved manyil (long-nosed fur seals) lazing around at [Cathedral Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-top-five-lookouts-on-wadjemup-rottnest-island) nearby.

Quokka Safety

To help keep the unique wildlife safe and healthy, please do not touch, feed or give water to the quokkas and always observe from a respectful distance.

#### BEACH AND BAY HOP

During the Easter school holidays, mild daytime temperatures are common on land. In the sea, the Leeuwin Current makes the island’s surrounding waters warm and inviting, even after summer has ended. Come and discover (or rediscover) your family’s favourite [beach or bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) and [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or [bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) your way to popular swimming and [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-snorkelling-the-warm-waters-of-wadjemup) spots such as [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay), [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), or [Fay’s Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay).

Strolling by foot? [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) is easily walkable from the main settlement and features sheltered, jewel-toned seas. Even on cooler autumn days, little ones will love spending hours crafting sandcastles and searching for shells along the shore.

#### PACK A PICNIC

Pick up some tasty takeaway bites from [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane), like a cray dog: an island classic with grilled crayfish and zesty mayo placed inside a pillowy bun. [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican) is also the perfect spot to stock up on crowd-pleasing sandwiches and rolls (plus a soft serve for sweet tooths!). For deliciously warm pastries, fill up goodie bags at [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) with fresh doughnuts, pies, and sausage rolls to share. Or stop by the Chook Shack window and grab a hunger-busting hot roast chicken to fill fluffy bread rolls. Just a short walk away, find a shady spot under a gently swaying boorn (tree) at [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay). Stretched out here, simple food has never tasted so good.

#### GET CLOSER TO CULTURE

Embrace Wadjemup’s [Aboriginal culture](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-culture) together through hands-on fun and imagination. [Koorda's Crew](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda) offer guided walking tours for kids that share culture and stories. Their craft workshops are also a great way to combine creativity and culture, with kids encouraged to build a Legoscape inspired by the Noongar season of [Djeran](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup).

[Dooga Waalitj Healing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences) also offer family-friendly guided walking tours and custom cultural experiences on Country in a relaxed setting.

#### WHEEL PAST ISLAND WONDERS

Why not see the sights from a new set of wheels? [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa) offers the perfect blend of freedom, novelty, and adventure, with April sunshine gently illuminating the ocean as you glide around. After a safety briefing, cruise together along winding paths, and even off-road. Kids aged 12 and older will appreciate the sense of independence, while parents will love the easy pace.

[Rotto Rickshaws](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rotto-rickshaws) stick to the paths, but the experience is just as entertaining. Sit back, relax and embark on a guided journey that combines immersive audio, live storytelling, and breathtaking scenery. With gentle autumn breezes keeping you comfortable, it’s an experience that lets you explore the island in playful ease.

#### GO ON A GUIDED WALK

Autumn’s pleasant weather sets the perfect stage for guided walking tours. It’s a chance to delve deeper and discover more thanks to [experienced guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours). Visit the [Rottnest Volunteer Guides Information Booth](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-volunteer-guides-information-booth) to see what free tours you can take part in during your family visit. Learn about local wildlife, unique flora, and the island’s cultural history in comfortable autumn conditions.

#### TAKE A FAMILY HIKE

With pleasant cool breezes in the air, the walking trails of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) present hours of free family entertainment. Spanning 45 km and made up of five distinct sections, you can go great distances or simply take a short stroll together as far as you like. Download the handy [Smartreka app](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/smartreka-digital-maps) before you arrive to plan and navigate the trails with ease.

For an option close to the main settlement, head for the [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi): a 9.5 km loop that’ll bring a gentle flush to your cheeks. Wind your way together up hills and around the [salt lake systems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) during the 3-4-hour journey. Alternatively, the [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) takes you on a 10 km one-way trail that blends military history and natural wonders.

#### CLIMB WADJEMUP LIGHTHOUSE

Enjoy just the right amount of thrill with a guided climb of [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse). Led by the [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour), this tour suits those five years and older and brings the island’s maritime stories to life with every step up the spiral staircase. When you reach the top together, the reward is unforgettable. Sweeping 360-degree views will steal your breath in a moment of shared joy.

#### APPRECIATE HISTORY AT OLIVER HILL

Jump aboard the [Captain Hussey train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour): it’s full steam ahead to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). Watch as grins grow across little faces on this ride that mixes education with open-air enjoyment. After a short but scenic journey, arrive at the significant surrounds of Oliver Hill. Here, panoramic views meet [military history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history), providing a place for everyone to reflect ahead of [Anzac Day](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/2026/04/24/rottnest-events/anzac-services-2026). After viewing the battery, you can even take a guided family tour underground [through the tunnels](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) beneath your feet.

#### SHARE A BITE TO EAT

Any time of day, make a beeline for the comforting scents of [Dome Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe). Warm mugs and comforting bites provide fuel for a family day out, or a welcome break from busy activities. Or stroll up to [R.I.G.C. Clubhouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/ricg-clubhouse) for steaming [Chippies](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/chippies) fish and chips, served with a side of barefoot lawn bowls. Unwrap crunchy delicacies as you cheer each other on; good vibes drifting across the green.

Later in the evening, local wines and barbecued meats might entice the grown-ups to [Pinky’s Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island), while classic kids’ meals appeal to the younger members of the family. Over near the main settlement, tasty sourdough pizzas from [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) are always a hit. Share slices and smiles; this family time is meant to be savoured.

* The Top Five Lookouts on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

# The Top Five Lookouts on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

When you journey to the peak of a destination, the landscape unfolds below (and beyond) you. Experience the views of a lifetime from these five island lookouts.

5 minutes

Image Long-nosed Fur Seals at Cathedral Rocks

Long-nosed Fur Seals at Cathedral Rocks

**Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a collection of beautiful vistas. Find out which views will enhance your journey the most.**

This island sits in wonderful opposition to most destinations. Like most of us, you have likely driven at a crawling pace across multiple kilometres of slippery gravel road to reach a mainland lookout. These breathtaking viewpoints are few and far between, so those seeking that quiet moment of awe must travel to find it. Here, you are surrounded by them. And they call you to view the landscape, and your connection to it, from new heights.

Even better is that with its rich natural beauty and without the availability of private vehicles, most choose to travel this unique destination under their own steam, by either walking, cycling, or hiking from one inspiring vista to the next.

[Getting There

You can access each lookout by bus, bike, or foot. Before you set out on your discovery, make sure to get a map and some advice from the Visitor Centre in Thomson Bay.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/visitor-centre?tab=see-do)

### 1. Vlamingh Lookout

**What you’ll see:** Inland vistas, 360-degree views, a network of salt lakes. 

**How to get there:** 10-minute walk or a five-minute cycle from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), through the main settlement and up a small hill.

As a Class A Reserve, Wadjemup’s inland landscapes are thriving with unique wildlife and native flora. Once you step away from the coast, multiple ecosystems await you, from wetlands to lush bush and wind-blown shrubland. Vlamingh Lookout is the perfect vantage point to gaze out over Wadjemup’s internal vistas. Named after the navigator, Willem de Vlamingh, who landed on Wadjemup in the 1600s, the lookout features a monument with a central sundial and inscription. You’ll have panoramic views of the island’s rocky headlands transforming into bush dotted with pink-tinted salt lakes.

### 2. Cathedral Rocks & Cape Vlamingh viewing platforms

**What you’ll see:** Open ocean views, long-nosed fur seals, migrating humpback whales (from August to December).

**How to get there:** 35-minute bike ride from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) to Cape Vlamingh, then two minutes from there to Cathedral Rocks. You can also take a 30-minute [bus ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) from the main settlement.

Wadjemup’s [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) is more remote, with the wind blowing ocean spray and seaweed scents, and the scrubland growing rugged beside the path. Cathedral Rocks and Cape Vlamingh are impressive lookout spots in this part of the island, where you can become a voyeur to the natural world.

Cape Vlamingh is the most exposed part of Wadjemup, at the western point of the island. Stand at the lookout and watch the writhing sea, with the knowledge that there’s only ocean in front of you — until Madagascar. Wildlife encounters are the highlight at Cathedral Rocks, as a colony of long-nosed fur seals live just below the lookout and often flip and play in the water. In late winter to early spring, this is also where you can best see the impressive humpback whale on its annual migration.
