### 3. Jeannie’s Lookout

**What you’ll see:** Remote bays, rocky coastline, and tropical reef visible from shore.

**How to get there:** 20-minute bike ride or an hour’s hike from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

A clear, cool day is the time for a revitalising bike ride along the coast of Wadjemup. Follow one of the many sealed roads which criss-cross the island and pause at each stunning beach that’s laid out before you. Jeannie’s Lookout is a beautiful stop on your short afternoon ride and the ideal destination for a decent hike. The viewpoint looks out over Jeannie’s Pool, a small cove of rocky shores where the turquoise water reveals an intricate reef system below the surface.

### 4. Mushroom Rock Lookout

**What you’ll see:** The ocean impacting the coastline, uniquely shaped rocks, a bay of boats.

**How to get there:** 10-minute walk or five-minute cycle from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

Staying at Wadjemup encourages you to slow down and take in the quiet moments. Like a refreshing early morning walk to a beachside lookout, thermos of tea in hand. Or a sunset wander on the way back to your accommodation. Mushroom Rock Lookout is conveniently nearby accommodation in Bathurst, with a platform that protrudes out into the sea. On sunny days, the mirrored blue ocean stretches out calmly, while cool weather fronts bring frothy dark waves and impressive ocean displays. To one side of the lookout, you can also see boats moored in the shelter of Thomson Bay.

### 5. Wadjemup Lighthouse

**What you’ll see:** The Perth skyline across the ocean, panoramic views, bird’s eye perspective of the island.

**How to get there:** 20-minute bike ride or an hour’s hike from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

Although not technically a lookout, the view from the top of [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) is the most spectacular on the island. Take the tour and, as you ascend the stairs 38 metres to the top, hear about the engineer who imagined everything from desert pipelines to island lighthouses, and learn how the strange prisms and pendulums create light for lost sailors. Out on the windblown platform, Wadjemup is laid out beneath you, all the way from green shrubland to the weaving line of the coast. In the distance you can see the outline of Perth over the Indian Ocean.

### Where to find the lookouts

From around the main settlement to the island's furthest point, there are so many places to pause and take it all in. Wander to these incredible lookouts during your next visit. Use the map below to find these lookout spots.

# Sustainability

## Passionately protecting the island’s beauty and biodiversity

Conserving and sustaining our environment has never been more important and the steps taken today will ensure the same unforgettable experience for the visitors of tomorrow.

A number of strategic initiatives are in place to secure the future of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. From marine sanctuaries to sustainable energy production, efforts are focused on continuing to provide a unique and special place for people to experience, enjoy and appreciate.

Every visit to Wadjemup should be one of reciprocity and respect. It’s about minimising your impact and respecting the unique natural environment so the only footprints you leave behind are washed away by the waves.

Image A School of Fish Found in the Waters of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

[School of fish](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Marine sanctuary zones

When you dive beneath the surface on Wadjemup, a whole new world is revealed with some of the most biodiverse marine gardens you’ll find anywhere. Approximately 400 species of fish and 20 species of coral call Rottnest Island home, and snorkelers, divers, and swimmers all have access to these underwater living sanctuaries.

We all play a role in preserving marine life, so take the time to familiarise yourself with the marine sanctuary zones and guidelines for snorkelling, fishing and boating.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones)

Image 

Diverse plant life

### Rottnest Island Nursery

The natural and unique landscape of Rottnest Island is as delicate as it is beautiful, and needs a plan for revegetation.

Find out how the Rottnest Island Nursery is helping to keep the native landscape alive, and how you can volunteer to help keep the island thriving with plant life.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/rottnest-island-nursery)

Image Salt Lakes, Gabbi Karniny Bidi

[Hiking the Gabbi Karniny Bidi](/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi)

### Minimise your impact

All of the conservation efforts on Rottnest Island don’t mean much without the help of everyone who sets foot on the island. With just a few mindful actions, we can all help to maintain the beauty and sustainability of the land and sea.

Find out how you can reduce your ecological footprint and leave no trace on during your time on Wadjemup.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/minimise-your-impact)

Image Salt Lakes, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

[Aerial view of the salt lakes](/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes)

### Hydrating the island

Water is a precious resource on Wadjemup, but essential for life.

Find out how desalination is used to hydrate the whole island in a self-sustaining system, powered by renewable energy.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/hydrating-the-island)

Image Paul's Eco E-Bike Tours, Geordie Bay

Cycling by wind turbine

### Powering the island

Rottnest has two amazing natural resources — the strong Western Australian sun and the wind of the Indian Ocean — that help keep the island running.

Find out about the island's local sustainable energy network, from the solar farm to your light switch.

[Learn more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/powering-the-island)

# Culture & History

## Pause and reflect on the stories from those who came before you

This small island holds a rich history. From ancient artefacts deep in the earth to military defence structures that watch over the sea and bunker into the ground. This is no ordinary island.

Dating back to tens of thousands of years ago when Noongar people occupied the land, the island’s stories are all imbued with deep meaning. The name itself - Wadjemup - tells the story of its cultural significance to the island’s Traditional Owners, referring to a place across the water where the spirits go.

As you begin to learn the history of the island, you will hear (and read) it told with truth and deep reflection. Used as a prison for Aboriginal men and boys — many of whose bodies still lay beneath the sands — the structures they built while held as prisoners still stand on the island today. The Old Mill & Hay Store, now housing the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum), is one of these heritage structures, now considered an essential gateway to the island.

When you take the time to walk through the museum displays — weaving through military, maritime, and Aboriginal history — you take the knowledge to each place you visit. Oliver Hill, with its maze of underground military tunnels and powerful gun battery. Wadjemup Lighthouse, first constructed in 1849 to keep sailors safe in the surrounding seas. Lomas Cottage, Bickley Battery, and beyond. These places hold the stories that are calling to be remembered.

### Stories from the past

Spend time with the history of the island, discovering the stories from those who came before you. From sunken ships that rest on the ocean floor, to the military structures that were built in defence of Fremantle port; the island's history as a prison for Aboriginal men and boys, and the bodies that lay to rest in the Burial Ground.

The history of this small island is one that every visitor should spend time getting to know. With a deeper understanding of the land you’re visiting, you can walk with respect and care.

# Bathurst Lighthouse

### This lighthouse has played one of the most important roles in the island’s story

The iconic white brick structure of Bathurst Lighthouse is found at Bathurst Point, overlooking Pinky Beach.

Constructed after the fateful voyage of the City of York, an iron ship that sank off the western coast of Rottnest Island in 1899 with the loss of 12 lives, it first shone its light on the seas in 1900.

The lighthouse lantern originally featured a fixed white light, but in 1920 this was changed to an automatic flashing light. With a range of 14 nautical miles, it provides a beacon of hope and safety far out into the ocean around it, and helps to create safer waters around the rocky coast.

While you can’t access the lighthouse itself, Bathurst Point provides gorgeous views of Pinky Beach—and an exceptional spot to watch the sun set uninterrupted over the vast Indian Ocean.

### Where to find Bathurst Lighthouse

Find the Bathurst Lighthouse at Bathurst Point, next door to [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). It’s close to [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), and just a short 10-minute [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) settlement — or even quicker [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike).

### Frequently Asked Questions

Are the lighthouses on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island operational?

Yes, both lighthouses are operational, and serve an important purpose helping ships safely navigate the waters around Wadjemup. When the sun goes down, you can watch as the lights flash out from each location.

Can I climb the lighthouses?

Bathurst Lighthouse isn’t open to visitors, but visitors can explore Wadjemup Lighthouse on a [guided tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour). Here you can discover what goes on within the walls of a real working lighthouse. Climb the stairs, making your way to the top to experience breathtaking 360-degree views.

Are there accessible facilities at the lighthouses?

Disabled access is available to get up close to both lighthouses, however no accessible facilities are available inside.

# Rottnest Island Summer Bucket List: 50 Things to Do

The long-awaited summer warmth is here, bringing abundant daylight to explore. Let these ideas guide your upcoming Rottnest Island adventure.

8 minutes

Image 

Aerial summer island views

**Whether you wish to while away an island day on land, by the ocean, or in air-conditioned comfort, here’s all that you can experience over the summer season.** 

### Ocean adventures

**1. Beach and bay hop:** Find your haven at over [80 locations](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) around the island, where the sea is almost always calm. This summer, choose to travel light and hire everything you need for the ultimate beach day from [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals) when you arrive.

**2. Swimming:** Take a refreshing dip in Wadjemup's tranquil waters and find relief from the sun’s radiating warmth.

**3. Snorkelling:** Spot an array of [underwater attractions](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving), including shipwrecks and flashes of vibrant fish and coral. You can even follow the popular self-guided trail at [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail).

**4. Rottnest Snorkel tours:** Visit the island's top [sheltered snorkel spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-snorkel) with experienced guides, gliding above vibrant coral and marine life. Designed for all skill levels with flotation aids available for those who need a little extra support.

**5. Charter 1 Snorkel & Sailing tours:** Spend the day sailing, swimming, and snorkelling aboard this iconic yellow [sailing catamaran](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1). Or choose the sunset sail and watch the sky turn a golden hue as you explore the coastline with a drink in hand.

**6. Paddleboarding:** Glide across glassy waters in still conditions. Hourly and daily [hire options](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) are available to chart your own path.

**7. Surfing:** Hire a surfboard rack for your bike (BYO board) and explore sheltered [surf spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-surfing-rottnest-islands-surf-breaks) or more challenging waves. Surf conditions here are reliable for groms and experts alike.

**8. Play a round of beach cricket:** [Hire a cricket set](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) and enjoy some friendly competition on the sand.

**9. Bring your own boat:** Spend the day cruising from beach to bay, with plenty of opportunities to snorkel, swim or cast a line straight from your vessel.

**10. Deluxe dining on the water:** Embark on a lavish all-inclusive adventure with [Rottnest Cruises](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises), featuring seven courses of sea-to-plate sensations. Have a go at hauling in western rock lobster pots before your private onboard chef transforms them into a buttery masterpiece.

**11. Eco Express Boat Tours:** Add some excitement to your day with a [boat ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours) around the island to spot wildlife from the water.

**12. Plunge into the pool:** Calling [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup), [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island), or [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) home for the night? Make the most of the on-site pools reserved exclusively for guests.

### Activities on land

**13. Cycling:** Coast between bays all day on your choice of [bicycle or e-bike.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling) Be sure to [make a booking](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) before your arrival for a seamless summer experience.

**14. Lakes:** Head inland to experience the [kabikarning (salt lake) systems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). Marvel in these natural mirrors which reflect varying shades of pink during seasonal dry spells.

**15. West End:** There is an abundance of wildlife to [spot here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). [Mammoong (whale) sightings](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) are common until December, in addition to long-nosed fur seals and birdlife such as the yoondoordoo (osprey).

**16. Yoga:** Find your zen with [Evolve in You](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/evolve-in-you-yoga) classes at [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) and [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin). Bookings are essential.

**17. Quokka spotting:** Like us, the [native kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) likes to escape the heat of the day, so sightings are more frequent early in the morning and from early evening. If you’re taking the [late-night ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals/9-pm-return-ferry-travel) this summer, you’ll have plenty of time to spot them as they come out at dusk.

**18. Wildflowers:** Appreciate the bold blue-purple hues that blanket the island while the iconic [Dek-koordiny-mart (Wadjemup daisy)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup) is in bloom.

**19. Picnic and BBQs:** Stock up on supplies from the [Rottnest General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and park up underneath a shady canopy. Barbecue facilities are available around the island to cook up a flavoursome feast. Or pick up some fresh rolls and a hot roast chicken from [Rottnest Bakery’s](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) Chook Shack.

**20. Mini golf:** Challenge your friends to a round of mini golf under the dappled light of this [18-hole course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf).

**21. Pickleball:** Try something new and serve up some fun with [Rotto Rackets Sports](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rotto-rackets-sports). Pickleball is the island's newest social sport set against stunning views of Bathurst Lighthouse, perfect for all ages and abilities.

**22. Volleyball and Tennis:**Swing by [Pedal & Flipper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire "https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire") to rent a volleyball and net or tennis racket and balls. Compete in your tournament on the beach or visit the tennis courts at Kingstown, Bathurst or Geordie Bay.

**23. Lawn bowls and games:** Spark some good-natured rivalry at [R.I.G.C Clubhouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/ricg-clubhouse), with barefoot bowls and free lawn games. Best enjoyed alongside a fresh serve of fish and chips from the [Chippies food truck](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/chippies).

### Tour the island

**24. Rickshaw tours:** Sit back and soak up the scenery with [Rotto Rickshaws](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rotto-rickshaws), an e-rickshaw tour that blends comfort, storytelling, and stunning island views - no pedalling required!

**25. Segway tours:** For a unique summer experience filled with scenic beauty, opt for a [guided tour by segway](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa).

**26. Wadjemup Lighthouse:** With [360-degree island views](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse), you can witness how the land and sea change during summer.

**27. Cultural tours:** Soak in the sights of the island in summer as you reflect and learn of its significance to the [Traditional Owners](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences), the Whadjuk Noongar people.

**28. Cultural experiences:** Connect with Noongar culture through immersive experiences. Join a guided walk with [Dooga Waalitj Healing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences), share stories in a cultural yarn with [Mirliny](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mirliny-cultural-yarning-experience), or let the kids learn and create with [Koorda's Crew](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda).

**29. Scenic flights:** Board a joy flight with [Rottnest Air Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi) for breathtaking views of the island below.

**30. Skydive:** Get a dose of adrenaline with [Skydive Geronimo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/skydive-geronimo) as you freefall at up to 200 km per hour before a beach landing.

**31. Walking tours:** Embark on a free, short tour with the enthusiastic [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours), complete with fun trivia and fascinating stories of the island’s history and native wildlife.

**32****. Hiking tours:** For those eager to wander further, [The Hike Collective](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective) offer guided hikes that make it easy for you to explore all that’s here. Enjoy the island’s [beautiful trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) and refreshing ocean dips along the way.

**33. Bike tours:** Cruise along with ease on an electric bike with guided commentary as part of [Paul’s Eco E-Bike tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours). Want to unleash your own pedal power? [Laura the Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/laura-the-explorer-bike-tours) offers a day tour filled with bike riding, swimming and snorkelling, paired with island insights and lunch.

**34. Bus tours:** See more of the island without breaking a sweat. [Discover Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour) and [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) provide air-conditioned comfort while you visit iconic island locations. Booking in advance is essential to secure your seats.

**35. Historical train tour:** All aboard the [Captain Hussey train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) for a fun-filled journey! Enjoy scenic views and insightful commentary along the way. This delightful ride to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) also offers respite from the summer heat, with shady seats and a sea breeze that rolls in through the open windows.

### Slip out of the sun

**36. Arcade games:** Follow your sense of fun to the [arcade](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf), where games and great prizes await out of the sun.

**37. Cool treats:** Swing by the Simmo’s window at [HAVZA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza) or the retro [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery) caravan in [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) for icy delights by the beach. Cool down with a zingy juice or smoothie from the [Boost Mobeel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/boost-mobeel-rottnest), or a fruity acai bowl from [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane). [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican) are also serving up energy-boosting iced lattes, matcha, and creamy soft serves with all the toppings.

**38. Must-try island bites:** A visit to Rottnest Island wouldn't be the same without enjoying [Rottnest Bakery's](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) famous jam or Nutella doughnuts. These sweet treats have delighted visitors for generations.

**39. Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnels tour:** Find respite from the sun’s rays [underground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) as you weave your way to the gun’s ammunition supply and engine room, guided by the Rottnest Voluntary Guides.

**40. Wadjemup Museum:** Immerse yourself in the history of the island, shared via compelling stories and [immersive exhibits](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum).

**41. Pilot Boathouse:** Expand your knowledge of the island’s [maritime history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pilot-boathouse) at this insightful site.

**42. Shopping:** Pop in and browse unique souvenirs and bespoke wares at [Indianic Boutique](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/indianic-boutique) and [Island Gypsy](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/island-gypsy). You’ll also find handy items such as bathers and hats, should you find yourself short of any ocean-side essentials.

### Seasonal events

**43. Live music:** Relax with your favourite cold beverage and the sounds of local talent at [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest), [The Mezz on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-mezz-on-rotto), and [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island).

**44. Christmas Day dining:** Book in your nearest and dearest for an indulgent festive feast.

**45. NYE Family Fireworks:** Ring in a joyful new year with fun family entertainment and a dazzling fireworks display over Thomson Bay.

**46. NYE celebrations:** Share the anticipation for the new year in your choice of lively island location.

### Stay a little longer

**47. Tee off:**Experience the charm of a twilight round of golf or lawn bowls at [Rottnest Island Golf Course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/rottnest-island-golf-course). The setting sun creates a stunning backdrop as you work your way through the course, racing daylight to complete your game.

**48. Catch a movie:** Unwind at the historic [Picture Hall](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) and enjoy a classic cinema experience, complete with buttery popcorn and creamy choc tops from the candy bar.

**49. See a sunset:** Witness the daily display of [shifting colours over the horizon](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island). No two days are the same, leaving a lasting memory to take back to the mainland.

**50. Drink and dine:** Those catching the [late-night ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals/stay-a-little-longer-campaign) can indulge in a variety of [seasonal offers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals) from the [bars and restaurants](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/sip--eat-and-indulge-a-little-longer-until-9-pm) you know and love.

# Spring

**The season of spring sees a kaleidoscope of colours appear across Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Warmer weather brings bursts of wildflowers, copious wildlife and a renewed landscape to explore and appreciate.**

#### Rottnest Island in spring

Spring encompasses the months of September, October and November in Australia. September also marks the final month of the [Noongar season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup), Djilba, when the rains start to ease, and quokka joeys start to peek their heads from their mother's pouch. This season is also marked by an abundance of seeds, berries, honey and fish as well as other mammals and birds.  October sees the emergence of the Noongar season of Kambarang, which continues until November. This time is a visual feast, welcoming [wildflower season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup) as the native Wadjemup Daisy and maro (Wadjemup tea tree) burst into bloom over the island. With warmer days returning, signs of new life and summer crowds yet to appear, this is a stunning time to visit Wadjemup.

#### Weather to expect during spring on Rottnest Island

The season of spring sees temperatures that are slightly cooler than the mainland of Perth, averaging around 18-23°C daily. As the spring months progress, the cool air clears away quicker in the mornings and evenings, giving way to pleasant days. This makes water-based activities such as swimming, [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) and relaxing on the sand popular amongst travellers. It’s also a great time to explore after winter rains have refreshed the island, leaving [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) and wetlands full and teeming with native flora and fauna.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What is there to do on Rottnest Island in spring?

The return of warmer weather and the rejuvenated natural environment create an inviting experience that can be enjoyed on the hiking or cycling trails, or in the waters that surround the island. Better still, the few businesses that close during the winter season begin to reopen for summer, offering many places to [dine and drink](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink?tab=eat-drink) and new ways to explore during your visit.

It’s advised that you pre-book your travel to the island, including meals and activities where possible, as school holidays fall during the spring period.

Is Rottnest Island cold in spring?

Wadjemup is slightly cooler than Perth during the spring months, however daytime average temperatures hover around 18-23°C. Due to Australia’s proximity to the equator, the sun provides a lot of warmth, so even lower forecasted temperatures can feel a lot warmer when the sun is out.

Can you swim in spring?

Swimming can be enjoyed all year round on Rottnest Island. As the weather warms up during spring, the waters become more inviting and can be entered with or without a wetsuit. Take the opportunity to beat the summer travellers and enjoy the serenity of the striking [bays and beaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities?tab=see-do) that surround the island.

What should I bring and wear during spring on Rottnest Island?

Here are some recommended travel items to make your island experience as comfortable as possible.

* Enclosed shoes / hiking boots
* Sunscreen
* Hat
* Sunglasses
* Camera
* Water bottle  (there are water refill stations around the island)
* Reusable coffee cup
* Light jumper or jacket
* Bathers (wetsuit if diving)
* Towel

What is the average temperature on Rottnest Island in spring?

The average temperature over the spring months on Rottnest Island are as follows:

* September: 13 – 19°C
* October: 14.1 – 20.6°C
* November: 15.9 – 23.1°C

As the island awakens from winter, the mild and pleasant temperatures make it perfect for outdoor adventures. Wander through blooming wildflowers, enjoy the gentle sea breeze, and soak in the sunshine.

What is the average monthly rainfall on Rottnest Island during spring?

Spring on Rottnest Island brings a gentle touch of rain, with average monthly rainfall as follows:

* September: 51.2 mm
* October: 27.9 mm
* November: 18.2 mm

Enjoy the balance of sunny days and occasional light showers, creating a perfect backdrop for your spring adventures along scenic trails to discover blooming wildflowers.

When is the best time in spring to see the Wadjemup Daisy?

The Wadjemup Daisy, native to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, begins to bloom from late October, especially along the coastal areas around Parker Point. The ideal time to witness these daisies in full bloom is during late spring.

# Six Rottnest Island Experiences for Your Wish List

From segway tours to cultural experiences or a round of golf, there’s so much more of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island to discover.

3 minutes

Image Segway tour

Segway tour

**There’s more to discover on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island — from segway tours to cultural experiences or even a round of golf.**

Here are six experiences to add to your island wish list:

### 1. Segway Tour

Explore the breathtaking natural scenery and history of Wadjemup on your own revolutionary set of wheels. [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa) will lead you on a journey of exploration into Rottnest Island’s hidden treasures, taking you places you’ve never been before. Riding a segway is easy to learn and you’ll quickly be on your way to experiencing the previously hard-to-reach corners of the island.

### 2. Go Cultural Aboriginal Walking Tour

[Go Cultural Aboriginal Tours & Experiences](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) offer unique walking tours from an Aboriginal perspective, guaranteed to heighten your appreciation of Wadjemup. Your Noongar guide will explain the [historical significance](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) of the island to the Traditional Owners, the Whadjuk Noongar people, and its continued importance in culture and storytelling. The tours include a traditional Aboriginal sand ceremony, Dreamtime stories and a traditional song in the Noongar language. Or choose the extended cultural immersion, just for adults, including a traditional Smoking Ceremony and extended information about the historic buildings and infrastructure that tell of the island’s shadowed past.

Image Fortress Adventure Tour riding along the Bickley trails

[Walter McGuire from Go Cultural Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences?tab=see-do)

### 3. Skydive Geronimo

Fancy getting the adrenaline pumping and seeing the island from a new perspective? Push yourself out of your comfort zone and skydive over Rottnest Island.  Experience incredible views of the island’s majestic coastline as you take a scenic flight over the turquoise waters before an exhilarating freefall and parachute ride down to the beach. With [Skydive Geronimo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/skydive-geronimo), you can do a tandem skydive from 10,000 or 15,000 feet, landing on the sands of Wadjemup.

### 4. Rottnest Island Golf Course

[Rottnest Island Golf Course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) is one of the island’s best kept secrets. Boasting nine quality golf holes, the grass greens, tees and fairways pave the way for one of Western Australia’s most unique golfing experiences. Whether you’re playing nine holes or doubling up to 18 rounds, this course is a unique way to experience the island in all seasons.

Image Golfer taking a swing at Rottnest Island Golf Course

### 5. Rottnest from the air

Treat a loved one to a breathtaking, scenic joy flight over the island. You’ll be treated to stunning aerial views of the Western Australian coastline and the colourful patchwork of hills, lakes and bays across Wadjemup. [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi) offer joy flights from 10 to 35 minutes.

### 6. Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf

Challenge your friends or family to a round of mini golf or enjoy the nostalgia of some classic arcade games at [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf). Indulge your inner child with retro pinball machines, Pac‑Man, Space Invaders and air hockey. In the evenings, head to the heritage deck chair cinema for a unique movie experience. There’s even a candy bar serving fresh popcorn, homemade choc bombs and drinks.

# Rocky Bay

## Explore Wadjemup’s western beaches

Towards the western end of the island, you’ll find a narrow stretch of land connecting the two halves of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. It’s here that you’ll find Rocky Bay. It’s something of a different style of beach to what’s usually found around. The sweeping sand dunes give it a unique feeling, while the north-facing position protects it from high winds, making it a peaceful spot to stop and relax.

It’s a place to get away from the crowds, to explore the dunes and rocks, and take in the Wadjemup coastline.

The starting and end point for the [Karlinyah Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/karlinyah-bidi) section of the Wadjemup Bidi trail, it’s an excellent spot for a bracing coastal walk, or a cooling swim to break up a day of cycling.

### Be sure to look out for…

Image 

Sweeping sand dunes

Image 

Underwater adventures

Image 

Vibrant sea life

Image 

The Karlinyah Bidi trailhead

### Where to find Rocky Bay

Depending on the route you take, Rocky Bay is a half-hour [bike ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from Thomson Bay settlement. Alternatively, you can take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off at Stop 13 (Narrow Neck) and take the short walk down to Rocky Bay.

Image Snorkelling, Rocky Bay

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### A special snorkelling experience

Rocky Bay is so-called for a reason, and its undulating rocky expanse gives way to crystal clear blue lagoons. Dive under the water and explore the coral reef hidden away below the surface — you’ll come face-to-face with schools of colourful fish, and if you’re lucky, you might even spot a sea turtle, stingray, or octopus.

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

Image Rocky Bay Beach, Rottnest Island

Rocky Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby Rocky Bay?

The closest facilities are the public toilets located at Narrow Neck.

Are there accessible facilities at Rocky Bay?

Accessible toilets aren’t available at Rocky Beach. The closest accessible facilities can be found at Stark Bay and West End.

Can I fish at Rocky Bay?

All fishing is allowed at Rocky Bay except for spear fishing and net fishing.

Is Rocky Bay a quiet or less crowded beach on Rottnest Island?

Rocky Bay is likely to appeal to visitors who want a quieter bay and a more relaxed beach experience away from the island’s busiest coastal spots. The [Rottnest Island beaches guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) can help compare hidden and more popular beaches before you decide where to visit.

# By Foot

Slow down, enjoy the moment and open up to the spaces that welcome you.

Image Hike Collective

By foot

### Step through a world of stories

When you take a moment to slow down and reconnect with nature, a whole new world of wonder presents itself. When you travel the island by foot, you’ll discover stories in every step as you immerse yourself in everything that is around you.

You never have to venture far with an abundance of island experiences available within a 15-minute walk from the main settlement. For those looking to awaken their appetite for adventure, view the island’s abundant natural wonders on a guided walking tour or a self-guided hike along the Wadjemup Bidi trail network.

[Tips for Safe Travel

Always be mindful of your own fitness level, carry sufficient supplies of water and stick to the marked trails.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

Image 

[Hiking the Wadjemup Bidi](/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi)

### Wadjemup Bidi

Spanning 45 km and threading its way through the island, the Bidi - which means "trail" or "track" in Noongar - is made up of five incredible walk trails.

Each unique stretch displays culturally and environmentally significant landmarks, providing balanced opportunity for historical reflection and celebration of the island’s natural beauty.

[More about the Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Hiking-the-Wadjemup-Bidi)

Image RVGA Walking Tour

[Walking tours](/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours)

### Free Guided Walking Tours

Be intrigued by stories of the past and discover more about our unique island on a guided walking tour led by the Rottnest Voluntary Guides Association (RVGA).

Each unique tour blends environmental awareness and historical education, covering everything from the island’s sustainability initiatives to its famous historic sites.

[View walking tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours)

Image Wilson Bay, Wadjemup Bidi

[The Hike Collective](/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective)

### The Hike Collective

Get a new perspective on adventure with The Hike Collective's unique range of guided hikes of the Wadjemup Bidi.

Wander through the lush inland bush or, if the rugged coastline speaks to you, stay close enough to feel the spray.

[View Hike Collective tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective)

Image Smartreka | hiking group in winter

### LET THE SMARTREKA MAP BE YOUR GUIDE

Embark on your adventure with confidence using the WA Parks Foundation's Smartreka digital maps, your guide to exploring stunning trails and scenery.

With your smartphone's built-in GPS, Smartreka maps display your real-time location, making it easy to navigate the island's diverse landscapes. These interactive maps also highlight key features along the way, including trail access points, scenic lookouts, cultural landmarks, and essential amenities.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/smartreka-digital-maps)

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

Image Hiking the Wadjemup Bidi

Hiking the Wadjemup Bidi

### More ways to get around

  By Bike

  Discover Rottnest Island via a network of roads and bike paths.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike)

# One Day Itinerary For the Spirited Adventurer

Rottnest Island adventure guide to surfing, skydiving, and cycling.

4 minutes

Image Plane flying above the island

Plane flying above the island

**To the ones who leap out of bed (and out of planes), whose hair is in a perennial state of mess, and who always choose dare over truth; this Rottnest Island adventure itinerary is yours.**

### 9 am surf or skydive

The island is home to some of the best [surfing conditions](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) and most consistent breaks in Western Australia. A Rottnest Island surf begins early, so take the 9 am start as a suggestion — those with salt-bleached hair and eternally bare feet may start hours before this. Surfboard in tow, you’re heading straight to [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay). You might even catch some pros in action.

> The best way to get around the island with a surfboard is by bike — with a surfboard rack attachment. Both can be hired from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire).

Image Surfing at Rottnest Island

Surf at Rottnest Island

Image A surfer in a black wetsuit riding a cresting wave in the ocean. The surfer is leaning forward on the surfboard with arms extended for balance. The water around the surfer is choppy with white foam from the breaking wave..tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=9ba9e564_1)

Off the lip

Image Cycling near Little Salmon Bay

[Cycle the coast](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island)

Surfing skills leave a little to be desired? There’s more than one way to interact with the water. The shipwreck at [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) is the place to challenge your snorkelling skills. Four metres below the surface lies the skeleton of *Shark* — a sunken hopper barge from 1939, now brimming with sea life and waiting to be discovered.

> If you’ve tasted the encompassing depths of Wadjemup, cooler temps won’t keep you from the water… Once you’re clad in a thick wetsuit, any season is fair game.

A dive out of a plane is another adventure that’s sure to get the adrenaline coursing through your body. You’ll see the island as a strip of sand and treetops moulding into the expansive, turquoise-tinged waters, as you glide towards a seaside touchdown. Check out [Skydive Geronimo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/skydive-geronimo) for more information on their Rottnest Island skydiving experiences.

Image Skydive Geronimo

[Skydive Geronimo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/skydive-geronimo)

Image Skydive Geronimo, Bickley Bay

Landing on the beach

Image Henrietta Rocks

[Shipwreck at Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks)

Image A person snorkeling near a partially submerged, rusted shipwreck in clear blue water under a bright blue sky.

Shark wreck at Henrietta Rocks

### 11 am refuel

Now that you’re awake and those muscles need a little respite, it’s time to refuel. We recommend a stop at [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) for some of the island’s iconic pastries or some freshly baked bread. You’ll need the carbs for what’s next…

### 12 pm cycle or fly

You’re up for a challenge, so we’ve chosen the island’s [22 km cycle loop](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling). [Head to Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) for a bike of your choosing — either electric or solely pedal-powered — and off you go. This route will take you around the entire island, passing the most spectacular stretches of beach and deep into the [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end)’s rugged ecosystem.

Depending on your speed (and how often you stop to sigh in awe), the entire route should take you approximately 3-5 hours. You’ll be back to the main settlement just in time to grab a restorative ale from [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest) before jumping on your ferry home.

Image 

[Rottnest Bakery doughnuts](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink/rottnest-bakery?tab=see-do)

Image Longreach Bay

[Cycle along Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling)

Image Couple lunching at Hotel Rottnest

View from Hotel Rottnest

Prefer a guided Rottnest Island cycling tour (to relax into the ride and observe the views unhindered by map-checking)? Join one of [Paul’s Eco E-Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours) instead. This electric bike tour will take you through the island’s picturesque and changing landscapes, from coastal and woodland scenes to the salt lakes, and it often includes a bay swim and a BYO lunch stop with stunning island views.

Or swap your ferry ticket for your own private helicopter or fixed-wing aircraft home and take in soaring birds-eye views of the island. The perfect end to an already action-packed day. Check out [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi), [Corsaire Aviation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/corsaire-aviation) and [Swan River Seaplanes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/swan-river-seaplanes) for more information.

Image See the island sights with ease on an electric bike tour at Geordie Bay.

[Paul's Eco E-Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours?tab=see-do)

Image Aerial of Rottnest Island Salt Lakes

[Salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes)

Image Rottnest Air Taxi

[Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/rottnest-air-taxi?tab=see-do)

### Staying overnight?

What’s more exhilarating than reeling in the catch of the day? After a well-earned night’s sleep, a spot of early-morning [fishing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing) is sure to deliver the thrills (and lunch).

The island’s numerous headlands and beautiful beaches offer excellent year-round opportunities for every aspiring angler. Many are just a short bike ride from [Thomson](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) and [Geordie Bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), while the bays themselves offer ample opportunity from their jetties.

> As an island with a focus on sustainability, fishing is only permitted in certain areas in order to conserve marine biodiversity. The five [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability) are located at [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point), Kingston Reef, Green Island, Armstrong Bay, and [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end).

For the more adventurous (and experienced), head to Radar Reef or [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach) and try your luck at some of the island’s sought-after fish species including salmon, tailor, and mulloway.

Remember, this adventure itinerary is simply a guide, because, as any spontaneous traveller will know, true adventure is found with spur-of-the-moment inspiration.

# Cycling

### Experience Wadjemup on two wheels

Experience the wind on your face, the sun at your back, and discover more corners of the island than you can in one day on foot. Fast, fun, and environmentally friendly, cycling is one of the most popular ways to get around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Wadjemup has very few vehicles, making it a haven for cyclists at every level. You can cycle the network of roads and hills in peace — a rare opportunity to feel the abundance of space and take in the scenery around you, riding from beach to bay.

You can bring your own wheels with you, speak with your ferry company about organising bike hire during your time on the island, or alternatively, join a bike tour.

Once you set foot on Rottnest Island, Pedal & Flipper provides a large range of bikes to choose from, available for one-day or multi-day hire. They also provide all the gear you need to ensure a safe, enjoyable ride, including helmets, locks, attachments to carry the kids—even electric bikes and e-scooters.

Cycling around Wadjemup is an uninterrupted experience that you won’t get anywhere else.

[Take Care when Cycling

Take care when cycling on Wadjemup. Even though there aren’t many vehicles, the hills can get steep and the roads are winding. Make sure to always wear a helmet when riding a bike—it’s mandatory as per Western Australian law.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### Explore Wadjemup at your own pace

Over 22 km of cycle paths weave in and out across the island, with plenty of track for every ability.

The [Rotto Mini Loop](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-rotto-mini-loop--4-km-of-easy--scenic-cycling) is a four kilometre round trip that winds its way past some of the island’s favourite locations. Starting at Thomson Bay, cyclists of all ages can ride through the unique Wadjemup bushland to The Basin, past Longreach and Geordie Bay, and out to Vlamingh Lookout. At around 30 minutes to complete, it’s perfect for families looking to explore more of the island.

The [Beaches, Lighthouses, and Lakes trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycling-trail-adventure--beaches--a-lighthouse-and-lakes) takes you further into the unique island terrain, without being too arduous. At 10 km, it makes for a relaxed 1.5- to 3-hour ride around the coast and inland, taking in some of Wadjemup’s most beautiful beaches and bays.

The 22 km [Island Ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-island-ride--cycle-the-entire-island) takes you around the entirety of Wadjemup’s stunning coastline. You’ll cycle the entire island, taking in some of its most popular beaches and stunning scenery. But at anywhere from three to five hours (return trip), this is better suited to experienced riders.

Image Paul's Eco Bikes

[Paul's Eco E-Bike Tours](/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours)

### Join a Bike Tour

Coast your way around the island on an electric bike with [Paul's Eco E-Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours). Join a 4-hour day tour or 2-hour sunset tour to learn about Wadjemup from an entertaining and educational guide. Suitable for a range of fitness levels. Enjoy the ride with ease while discovering the island's unique charm.

[Laura the Explorer Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/laura-the-explorer-bike-tours) offer an unparalleled adventure on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Led by Laura, a passionate Perth local, these full-day cycling tours blend excitement and education for a truly unique experience. Embark on a scenic 10 km bike ride, exploring the island’s stunning beaches and bays. Uncover lesser known spots and hear fascinating local stories along the way.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I hire a bike on Rottnest Island?

You can organise bike hire with your ferry company or hire on the island from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire). Located just behind Hotel Rottnest, it’s open every day of the year for your cycling needs.

Are there guided tours?

[Paul’s Eco Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours) offers a 4-hour or 2-hour electric bike tour to learn about Wadjemup from an entertaining and educational guide.

[Laura the Explorer Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/laura-the-explorer-bike-tours) embark on a scenic 10 km bike ride, exploring the island’s stunning beaches and bays. These full-day cycling tours blend excitement and education for a truly unique experience.

For something a bit different, [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa) provides a two-wheeled experience that takes you off-road—no peddling required.

Are electric scooters allowed on Rottnest Island?

Yes, electric scooters are allowed on the island. The use of electric rideables (e-skateboards, e-scooters, e-wheels, hoverboards, e-unicycles or e-skates) is regulated under the *[Road Traffic Code 2000](https://www.legislation.wa.gov.au/legislation/statutes.nsf/main_mrtitle_2007_homepage.html)*. So be sure to wear a helmet and obey all the same road rules as you would on a bike.

# Your Guide to Spotting Quokkas on Rottnest Island

A short journey across the Indian Ocean lands you amongst the world’s largest quokka population. This is your guide to experiencing this iconic marsupial in its natural habitat.

6 minutes

Image Quokka

Quokka

**There’s something special about the population of quokkas, or kwoka in Noongar, who live on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Their story is literally written in the land. The name ‘Rottnest’ comes from 17th-century Dutch explorers who considered the animals to be large rats and bestowed the island, ‘Rat’s Nest’.**

These small marsupials bring childlike joy to those who make the journey to see them in the wild. They are the sole reason many people visit the island. Protagonists in children’s books. Iconic emblems on holiday souvenirs. Their infamy is undeniable; however, the quokka is a vulnerable species, protected, adored, and respected.

> Rottnest Island is where you can be amongst the world’s largest quokka population. They are related to kangaroos and wallabies, and to see them in the heat of summer is one thing, but it’s quite another to witness these incredible creatures in the cooler months — just like kangaroos, little joey quokkas take their first hops into the world as protective mothers watch on. It’s unforgettable.

### Best Places to Spot Quokkas on Rottnest Island

Many people come to Wadjemup in pursuit of a quokka sighting. And you won’t have to try too hard. They are found all across the island, sleeping, eating, and hopping around their natural habitats.

These five specific areas are ideal vantage points to witness quokkas in their natural state — stay quiet and give them plenty of space. The best time of day to spot them are early in the morning or late afternoon as [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) are nocturnal animals and often spend their days sleeping.

#### Garden Lake

***5-minute walk from the main bus stop***

In a few minutes, you move from the high energy of the settlement and arrive in silence. [Garden Lake](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) is still. Surrounded by trees and ramped by a field of grass and samphire; you will see a family of quokkas sleeping under the trees or venturing out in the early morning and late afternoon. While there are plenty of incidental quokka sightings on the island, with its boardwalk that offers the perfect view at a respectful distance, Garden Lake is an ideal place to go for a purposeful quokka experience.

#### On the way to The Basin

***Where the Gabbi Karniny Bidi meets Kingsway Road***

When you walk the trail between Wadjemup Oval and the [golf course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course), you will come in contact with a line of native tea trees just opposite [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) (the eco-tent village). These tall gums and low-lying tea trees are knitted together to form the ideal woodland habitat for a thriving quokka population. Stand back and take in the marsupial group going about their natural movements.

Image 

[Quokka at Garden Lake](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Quokkas)

Image 

[Quokka spotting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

#### On the Ngank Yira Bidi trail to Bickley Bay

As you walk the [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) to get to Bickley Bay (just south of Kingstown Barracks), you won’t be able to miss a collection of low scrub trees that freckle the path leading to the bay. There is a quokka population here that dwell in the shelter of the native fauna; sleeping, foraging, and making a home among the trees.

#### Just before the ascent to Wadjemup Lighthouse

***Digby Drive***

Positioned at the intersection of trails, cyclists and walkers arrive to make the same ascent as you are, at that moment, contemplating. In this intersection of paths and willpower, you will see a cluster of tea trees that is home to a community of quokkas. They live here at the base of Wadjemup Hill, offering the perfect respite. Pause. Take in this iconic wildlife moment before making the climb up to the highest point of the island.

#### As you cycle to Stark Bay

***Bovell Way***

Take your quokka tour west. As you cycle to Stark Bay, you will encounter tall fig trees and date palms leaning into one another and creating the perfect reserve for island marsupials. If you’re doing a full tour of the island by bike, you can travel the southern track back to the settlement, cycling past [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) (approximately six km from Stark Bay). Here, there’s a natural dip in the road where you’ll see a shrub forest of native tea trees; for those with a keen eye for spotting wildlife, you may get a glimpse of the quokka population here too.

> It's important to move back if a quokka hops within two metres of you and remember not to touch or feed them.

Image Quokka stand9ing on back feet and looking at the camera

[Kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Quokkas)

Image Quokkas

[Quokka joey](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Quokkas)

### Playing your part in quokka conservation

Finding yourself close to a quokka is captivating, an experience that has the power to make you reach for your phone to capture the moment. And, as part of their world in that moment, you, like everyone who steps foot on the island, play a part in their wellbeing.

As a vulnerable species, it’s vital that we protect the quokka so that they don’t become endangered; that comes down to four key guidelines:

#### Simply observe the quokkas as they go about their natural movements

These marsupials are wild. They are not trained or confined in any way. This means that, when you travel to Wadjemup, you are moving through their environment. Not the other way around. So, ensure you simply observe them from a respectable distance.

#### This means that you cannot touch them

It’s important for their safety and yours, that you don’t touch the quokkas. Touching quokkas can make them sick, spread disease, and even cause mothers to abandon their young if they carry an unfamiliar scent. Like any animal, they can be protective of themselves and their young so please keep your distance.

#### Let them forage for their own food

As a vulnerable species, it is illegal to feed the quokkas (or any animal on the island) as any food that they haven’t foraged for themselves can be harmful to their bodies. The only viable nutrition is the food on the island that they collect themselves.

#### Keep foot (and cycle) traffic on the paths

The network of hiking and cycling paths around the island are there to protect the native flora and fauna. By keeping your movements to established paths, you are protecting the natural habitats of Wadjemup wildlife.

> Wadjemup is a Class A reserve, made up of [six unique ecosystems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/wildlife-encounters-at-wadjemup), each one with the perfect conditions for thriving animal, bird, and sea life. The quokka population is a big part of that, but not the only part. When you commit to protecting the quokka, you are protecting the greater island wilderness.

### Tips for a time well spent

Make your visit even more meaningful with helpful advice from those in the know.

# Chilled Bliss: Discover the Best Spots for Cool Scoops and Icy Treats

Recharge after a day of exploration with a frosty delight from one of the island's assortment of refreshment spots, from ice creams and smoothies to fresh acai bowls.

3 minutes

Image Ice cream at Thomson Bay

Ice cream at Thomson Bay

**Beat the heat and cool down with a cold scoop or icy treat while you explore the island.**

With its pristine beaches and crystal-clear waters, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is renowned as the ultimate summer escape. For the young, and the young-at-heart, it’s the place where you pedal around in your swim gear, letting the sea breeze dry salty skin, as the drips of the melting ice cream in your hand mark a perfect, sun-soaked day.

Whether it’s the simple joy of an ice cream cone, the nostalgia of a frosty milkshake, or the wholesome sweetness of an acai bowl, here's where to find refreshingly cold treats on Rottnest Island.

### Simmo’s Rottnest

**Settlement Mall and The Basin**

The perfect complement to any day by the sea is a sweet scoop of the much-loved [Simmo’s ice cream](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/simmo-s-rottnest). Boasting over 60 flavours to choose from, you’ve got a truly delicious dilemma.

### Kuld Creamery

**Geordie Bay**

Head to this [retro caravan](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery) overlooking the iconic [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) to enjoy sensational ice cream with a serious flavour twist. Be sure to try their exclusive Rottnest Island creation, Quokka Traxx, featuring a delectable blend of peanut butter cups, chocolate fudge swirl, and vanilla bean ice cream.

### Pelican

**Thomson Bay Settlement**

Discover the taste of nostalgia at [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican), the charming kiosk at [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup). Overlooking Heritage Common, enjoy a creamy soft serve with a variety of your favourite topping options like sprinkles, wafers, and the classic crunchy shell of a chocolate dip.

### The Lane Cafe

**Settlement Mall**

Ease into the day with a trip to [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane) where you will find a selection of cold treats like juices and smoothies. For a fresh and fruity start to your day, grab a healthy and delicious acai bowl to go and savour it while soaking in the panoramic views of [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), located just behind the cafe.

[Ice cream from the Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/geordie-bay-general-store)

### Lexi’s on Rotto

**West End**

A welcome rest stop and the perfect addition to enjoying the views out at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). Whether you’ve made the trip by bus or pedal power, refuel with an assortment of ice creams as well as other refreshments at [Lexi's on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lexi-s-on-rotto). Take a moment to soak in the stunning views before heading back to the settlement, ensuring your island adventure is both delicious and rejuvenating.

### Kalli’s on Rotto

**Wadjemup Lighthouse**

If you’re exploring further or visiting [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse), reward yourself with a well-deserved pit stop at [Kalli’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kalli-s-on-rotto). Sit back, relax and relish the stunning 360-degree views of the island while you take a minute to recharge with a selection of ice creams or cold drinks.

### General Stores

**Settlement Mall and Geordie Bay**

Whether you're passing through the [main settlement](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) or exploring the picturesque setting of [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store), make a pit stop at the conveniently positioned General Stores. Each store boasts a range of ice creams and refreshing cold drinks to indulge in, all while also grabbing your grocery essentials.

### Rottnest Movies and Mini Golf

**Thomson Bay Settlement**

Wrap up your day by settling into a deckchair for a unique cinematic experience at [Rottnest Movies and Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf). For a sweet fix, make a bee line for the candy bar for a homemade choc bomb and more classic favourites. If the day’s schedule of adventures doesn’t allow for some time at the movies, never fear. You can still swing by to indulge in the tasty treats on offer, perhaps with a side of mini golf or a few games at the arcade on site.

### Boost Mobeel

**Heritage Common**

If a nourishing juice or smoothie is what you crave, stop by the [Boost Mobeel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/boost-mobeel-rottnest). The pop-up location at Heritage Common has your summer thirst covered, serving up the delicious cold juices, crushes, and smoothies you know and love, all summer long.

Seasonal Closure

Boost Mobeel Rottnest is now closed for the season.

### Your on-demand private island transport

Discover convenience in connection as you enjoy the comfort that comes from travelling via the [Quokka Hopper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/quokka-hopper) — your on-demand private transfer operating between [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay).

As you move between restaurants, accommodations, and facilities as you please, you can enjoy a stress-free island experience with 12 convenient pick-up and drop-off locations.

Each journey holds a maximum of seven passengers without luggage, or five passengers with luggage.

* 8 Must-See Exhibits at the Wadjemup Museum

# 8 Must-See Exhibits at the Wadjemup Museum

Wadjemup Museum is the essential starting point for your island experience. Take your time to explore and understand the culture and history you stand amongst.

4 minutes

Image Wadjemup Museum

Wadjemup Museum

**The Wadjemup Museum is a place for visitors to gather and learn about the rich, complex history of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.**

Home to a range of exhibits, ancient artefacts, and incredible sculptures, the museum encourages visitors to reflect on everything that has come before. Enter the Old Mill and Hay Store building and let the meaningful stories and interactive displays create a deeper understanding that you can take with you on your island journey.

> Walking through Wadjemup Museum on Rottnest Island gives you the gift of perspective. You see the island through the lenses of those who came before you, beginning the journey of awareness, understanding, and deeper respect.

### Nine museum experiences to broaden your perspective

**Zephyr Scroll**

One of the first objects you will see when entering the museum is the bow scroll of the S.S. Zephyr, which ferried passengers between Wadjemup and the mainland between 1907 and 1952. Hand carved from solid timber, the scroll contains images of the Western Australian black swan nestled amongst river reeds.

**Mill Stone**

The Wadjemup Museum has been built in the Old Mill and Hay Store, a place where the events of the past feel close. The remnants of the mill stone in particular create a visceral experience, as the Aboriginal men and boys who were held as prisoners on the island used it to grind wheat into flour. It sits in its original location, where up to eight Aboriginal prisoners would perform the arduous task of rotating the stones by pushing long wooden handles. It is the only known mill in Western Australia built to be powered by human hands.

**Aboriginal stone flake tools**

Explore one small part of the expansive local Aboriginal history through a selection of ancient spearheads that have been found on the island. These fascinating artefacts date back to between c. 8,000 and 40,000 BCE, and offer insight into the important connection the Noongar people have always had with Wadjemup.

Image 

Zephyr Scroll

Image 

Mill Stone

Image 

Aboriginal stone flake tools

**Memorial Stone**

At the beginning of World War I, Wadjemup was commandeered by the Department of Defence as an internment camp for enemy aliens, who were then at war with Australia. The Memorial Stone remnant is a unique relic created by the internees to signify their period of confinement on the island. Alongside the display sits a photograph taken by one of the internees, Karl Lehman, who captured moments from their time on the island. The picture shows the original Memorial Stone, and the translated German inscription reads:

*‘c.1914-1915/in memory of our captivity/we brothers Austrian-Hungarian Slavs.’*  
  
**Lighthouse Keeper’s jacket**

The Wadjemup museum exhibits are full of artefacts that help ground historical facts and stories in reality, like the jacket of lighthouse keeper, Lionel Clarence Jacobs. Born in 1895 in Victoria, Jacobs was a permanent staff member at the Rottnest Island Station on a salary of 241 pounds per year.

**Seaweed collages**

The museum’s seaweed collages were created by Charlotte Duffield, a girl who lived on Wadjemup in the 1800s and gathered seaweed from around the island to make her artwork. She was the eldest daughter of Samuel Duffield, the lighthouse keeper on Wadjemup from 1854-1879. Charlotte and her six siblings spent most of their time down by the beach and reef, and her collages are a window into what their daily life was like.

**Hallie’s Hat**

Hallie’s Hat is another seaweed creation, this one made in the 1940s by Hallie Margaret Stow (1876 - 1972), from seaweed she collected around the island. Hallie is quoted in The West Australian newspaper saying, “The weed is soft to wear and durable in sun and rain, and it makes good garden hats…ideal also for sun basking swimmers.” (Hallie Margaret Stow, The West Australian, 1972). This beautiful object is on loan from the Western Australian Museum.

* Aboriginal Culture

# Aboriginal Culture

Wadjemup is a place of cultural significance for the Whadjuk Noongar people.

Image Traditional smoking ceremony

Traditional smoking ceremony

### Place across the water where the spirits are

Thousands of years ago, before sea levels rose following the last glacial maximum, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island was part of the mainland. Accessible by foot at the time, its elevated position on the coastal plain made it an important place for the local Noongar peoples and a site for hunting, gathering and trade.

Archaeological evidence proves that Wadjemup was occupied by Whadjuk people for tens of thousands of years before the rising Wardan (Indian Ocean) cut off land access, making it an island.

### Whadjuk Noongar Boodja / Land

In traditional Aboriginal culture, a person’s identity and sense of belonging is intrinsically connected to the land on which they live. Great importance was placed on maintaining and monitoring the health of the land (and water surrounding and within it) due to the essential role it played in their ancestors’ cultural practices. It was believed it not only sustained life physically, but also socially and spiritually. This still continues to this day.

Whadjuk Noongar Elders are the keepers of kaartidjin (knowledge) about the complexities of boodja (land) – its management, seasons, and creation. Kaartidjin was passed down, unwritten, for thousands of years on Wadjemup before sea levels rose.

As Traditional Owners of the land, the Whadjuk Noongar people lived in a way that ensured the sustainability of the world around them. This was governed by the patterns observed in the six seasons that indicated when and how to move – taking advantage of varying resources according to weather, ecology and fertility.

They brought up their children to know their lore and customs where they could and could not go, where to find water and food, and how to understand the habits of animals, fish and birds. This kaartidjin was passed down through thousands of generations.

Image Birds, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island

Flock of birds

Image Salt Lakes at Rottnest Island

Salt lakes and sand dunes

Image Plants at Rottnest Island

Plants

Image A School of Fish Found in the Waters of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

School of fish

### Cultural tool-making

The remains of tools have been found at a number of sites on Wadjemup embedded in paleosols dating between 10,000 and 49,000 years ago. The artefacts provide evidence of Whadjuk Noongar people’s activity on Wadjemup when it was still part of the mainland.

Fossiliferous chert was the preferred tool-making stone for the Whadjuk people due to its ability to be quickly flaked into a very sharp edge to assist with hunting and gathering.

Wadjemup has no known chert quarries today. As sea levels rose, it is likely that the island's quarries disappeared underwater. Evidence of chert remains on the mainland today.

### Welcome to Country

Visitors who attend an event or join a tour on Wadjemup will hear a Welcome to Country. A recorded audio Welcome to Country is available to all at the Koora-Yeye-Boordawan-Kalyakoorl (Past-Present-Future-Forever) sculpture at the end of the main jetty.

This Aboriginal ritual recognises the area of land where Whadjuk Noongar people traditionally lived, hunted and gathered (Moort Boodja). A “Welcome to Country” also reinforces spiritually being one with the land. Aboriginal peoples’ connection with Wadjemup today remains strong, with community members paying respect to Elders, past and present and future.

Image Chert in Wadjemup Museum collection

Chert in Wadjemup Museum collection

### European settlement

When the Noongar people first saw the seafaring explorers (and eventual colonisers) off the coast and along the Swan River, they believed them to be their ancestors who had returned in life-form as djanga (white spirits). However, the subsequent colonisation of Western Australia resulted in Wadjemup acquiring a different significance, one which still impacts Aboriginal people today.

For nearly a century, the island served first as a prison and then a forced labour camp for Aboriginal people. Almost 4,000 Aboriginal men and boys from all over Western Australia were exiled at the Rottnest Island Aboriginal Establishment from 1838 to 1931. These men and boys came from many different Aboriginal tribes across Western Australia, including Whadjuk Country.

The prisoners were occasionally permitted to hunt and fish on Sundays and artefacts have been found around the shady hills of Wadjemup, suggesting a regular practice of their knowledge and culture. Glass points that are distinctive to the Kimberley have been found, particularly on the outskirts of the Settlement where the prisoners would have been able to work on them away from the guards’ eyes. These artefacts are available to view in the Wadjemup Museum.

Culturally significant sites are registered as culturally significant places on Wadjemup and are protected under the *Aboriginal Heritage Act 1972*.

[Learn more about Aboriginal history on Wadjemup here.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history)

## Steps towards reconciliation

Together with the Government of Western Australia, the [Rottnest Island Authority](https://ria.wa.gov.au/) has adopted the Innovate  Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP) 2021-2023.

The RAP aims to ensure all people can move forward together in an environment of cooperation and understanding, built upon acknowledging the past and focused on the future.  The RIA work with and consult various stakeholders to progress reconciliation.

* The Wadjemup Aboriginal Reference Group (WARG) is a Cabinet-appointed advisory group to the Rottnest Island Authority (RIA).  It was established in 2017 and their role is to advise RIA on all Aboriginal cultural matters in relation to the day-to-day functioning of the island.

* In 2020, the Government of Western Australia announced support for a new process of reconciliation and healing with Aboriginal communities across the State, led by Whadjuk Noongar people as the Traditional Owners of Wadjemup. The Wadjemup Whadjuk Cultural Authority Reference Group was established in 2021 to lead the State-wide consultation regarding the future of the Burial Ground and the Quod. The Wadjemup Project will focus on how to commemorate the Aboriginal boys and men buried on the island and the future use of the old prison building (the Quod).

* Rottnest Island Deaths Group Aboriginal Corporation (RIDGAC) formed in 1993 has raised awareness of the history of the Aboriginal prisoners, the Quod and burial ground.

* The South West Native Title Settlement is the largest native title settlement in Australian history.  The Settlement is made up of six Individual Land Use Agreements, including the Whadjuk People (Perth Metropolitan area).  The Whadjuk Regional Corporation has a Cultural Advice Committee (CAC) which is made up of Elders who consider matters relevant to culture and make decisions to promote and protect cultural interests.
