* Your Guide to the Wildflowers of Wadjemup

# Your Guide to the Wildflowers of Wadjemup

Wildflower season on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a striking annual event. Visit between September and December to witness this natural spectacle at its best.

5 minutes

Image 

Wadjemup Daisy

**The sun is shining, bees are pollinating, and flowers are blooming: it must be wildflower season on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.**

September marks the arrival of [spring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/spring) on the island and the second month of the [Noongar season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup) of Djilba. This period is defined by warmer, sunnier days and sprinklings of rain, creating a transitional period for seeds to burst and plants to flower. Wildflower season on Wadjemup officially starts around September although some will begin blooming as early as July until the early [summer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) months, creating a sweeping eruption of colour over the island.

### The wildflowers of Wadjemup

#### Wadjemup Daisy

**When: late October to December**  
**Where: Parker Point, Henrietta Rocks, Oliver Hill**

The island’s iconic native daisy stands tall and proud between the months of October and December. The distinctive blue-purple petals unfurl from domed flower heads, creating clusters that mimic starry explosions across the dunes behind [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) and [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point). A little further west at [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill), another large constellation sways beneath the dappled light of the tuart trees.

Keep to the Island Paths

The roads and cycle paths are designed to give you a full experience of the island with minimal impact on the native environment. You can help by staying on the roads and admiring the flora and fauna from a distance.

#### 

#### Tar Bush

**When: July to October**  
**Where: Vlamingh Lookout**

Glimpses of the warm orange florals on this small shrub offer a sense of warmth when the temperatures are still on the cooler side. Flowering as early as July, this plant features unique, tubular flowers and can be found commonly around coastal heaths and the path up to Vlamingh Lookout.

#### Old man’s beard

**When: July to September** **Where: Island wide**

Another early bloomer includes this widespread climbing plant. It’s white, outstretched flowers can be witnessed sporadically around Wadjemup. Curiously, these florals feature a design that loosely mirrors the large wind turbine spinning on Mt Herschel.

#### Cockies tongues

**When: July to September**  
**Where: Western end of Geordie Bay**

You can’t miss this colourful shrub when its flame-like florals are on display. These rich red flowers feature curled back petals, mimicking the shape of its common namesake. This species blooms from July to September around the western end of [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay).

#### Grey cottonhead

**When: August to September**  
**Where: Island wide**

Don’t let the name deceive you, this plant produces bright, bell-shaped flowers when in bloom. Grey cottonhead commonly flowers beside island trails, so you won’t miss the sunshine-yellow hues as you walk or cycle around the island.

Image Samphire at Rottnest Island

[Red Samphire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup)

#### 

#### Samphire

**When: August to December**  
**Where: Around Garden Lake**

This unique plant, also known as sea asparagus, features bead-like leaves and glassy shoots that adorn the shorelines of the salt lakes in stunning shades of red and pink. Perfectly adapted to the coastal environment, it adds vibrant splashes of colour to the island's natural landscape.

#### Coastal groundsel

**When: August to October** **Where: Below Vlamingh Lookout and West End**

This delicate daisy is abundant on the island, with pleasant yellow petals that gently bob in the spring breeze. Naturally bountiful on the island, this makes for a welcome sight to those exploring the [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) or Vlamingh Lookout.

#### Shark’s tooth wattle

**When: August to October** **Where: In sand in southern and western parts of the island, also planted in the main settlement**

Throughout the year the angular leaves might catch your eye, but it’s during wildflower season that this wattle truly comes to life. When flowering, it bursts with masses of soft yellow spheres and thrives in heathland and coastal areas.

#### Nitre bush

**When: September** **Where: Cape Vlamingh**

This sprawling shrub is commonly found where seabirds roost, such as the exposed heaths and cliffs of Cape Vlamingh. It’s a vivid illustration of the symbiotic relationship between the island’s flora and fauna, with white flowers unfurling in the presence of guano-enriched soil from the large colony of wedge-tailed shearwater birds that live on the island.

#### Fan flower

**When: November to February** **Where: Island wide throughout coastal heaths**

The pale blue colouring of this petite flower pairs perfectly with the Wadjemup sky. Found on sprawling shrubs, each flower features fan-shaped petals that stretch away from fleshy green leaves. Find them around the settlement, and the island’s coastal heaths.

#### Rottnest Island tea tree

**When: Year-round with the flowers blooming during summer** **Where: Main settlement, Vlamingh Lookout, Parker Point**

Cast your gaze upwards to appreciate this large native tree. The moonah features bottlebrush-like white flowers that burst out amongst dense branches.

#### Coastal pigface

**When: September** **Where: Cape Vlamingh**

This creeping perennial lays low, with stems that trail lazily in the surrounding sand. Found amongst the exposed beauty of Cape Vlamingh, it boasts bright pink florals that demand the attention of all those who pass by.

Appreciate at Arm's Length

The wildflowers on the island are for all to observe. Please leave plants as you find them to ensure that every island visitor can enjoy their beauty.

Image Underwater plant

[Rottnest Island tea tree](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup)

### 

### TOP SPOTS TO ENJOY WILDFLOWERS

#### Main settlement

Even if your visit to the island during wildflower season is brief, one thing’s certain: you don’t have to wander far to view a variety of blooms. Stroll around the settlement and marvel at the different hues that surround you.

See: Coastal groundsel, shark’s tooth wattle, Rottnest Island tea tree, fan flower

#### Southern side

No visit during wildflower season is complete without casting your eyes upon the purple daisies that illuminate the land. The [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) travels through [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) and [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) allowing ample opportunities to pause and observe. Sections of the stunning [Wardan Nara Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/wardan-nara-bidi) also cover Oliver Hill and [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point), where the Wadjemup daisy is a decorative highlight. Embrace these hikes under the guidance of [The Hike Collective](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective), or take to the trails at your own pace.

See: Wadjemup daisy, Rottnest Island tea tree

#### Northern coastline

Colour combinations around [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) include baby blues and brilliant reds. Come here for celebrated floral finds that complement the diverse seascape. The [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi) winds around these beautiful bays, offering a welcome opportunity to appreciate the surrounding seasonal blooms.

See: Cockies tongues, fan flower

#### West End

The rugged coastline and rolling swell of this remote area of the island is a stark contrast to the delicate florals that flourish here. Wander the [Ngank Wen Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/explore-west-end-on-the-ngank-wen-bidi) section of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) and the boardwalk around Cape Vlamingh for kaleidoscopic display.

See: Tar bush, coastal groundsel, nitre bush, coastal pigface.

[Beware of Snakes

Be aware there are venomous snakes on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. The dugite is a timid creature, but may bite if harassed. If bitten, seek immediate medical assistance.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

# West End

### Explore the island’s rugged West End

Away from the beaches and lively buzz of the main settlement, around the sandy coast and rolling swell, you’ll find Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s West End.

Connected to the main part of the island by a narrow neck of land (aptly named Narrow Neck), West End is Wadjemup’s westernmost point, with nothing beyond it but the vast Indian Ocean.

A place of contrasts, West End is alternately whipped by strong winds coming in off the ocean, and embraced by calming breezes as the swell goes down. Its ancient rocky coastline has little protection from the elements, leaving it feeling more rugged than the rest of the island.

### Where to find West End

West End feels like a world away from the main settlement. At over two hours to walk, it’s not recommended to get there by foot unless you’re [hiking](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi). Alternatively, you can jump on a bike and do the 10 km [ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) in around 30 minutes, right through the centre of the island.

But the easiest way is to get there [by bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus). Just catch the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), and get off at Stop 11 at Eagle Bay.

### Immerse yourself in the natural landscape

There’s plenty to explore at West End.

The [Ngank Wen Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/explore-west-end-on-the-ngank-wen-bidi) section of the Wadjemup Bidi threads around the coast, allowing you to visit some of the island’s most secluded places. The 7.8 km trail loops around from Narrow Neck to Cape Vlamingh and back. One particular section of the trail leads down to Cathedral Rocks, and tells Nyitting (Dreamtime) stories through interpretive artwork and audio yarns.

At Cape Vlamingh, 120 metres of elevated boardwalk brings you closer to nature, weaving carefully around the natural habitat. Constructed from environmentally friendly materials, including recycled plastics, the suspended path helps protect the fragile limestone cliffs.

While you can’t set foot on these rocky cliffs, they’re home to an abundance of animals, many not seen elsewhere around the island. There’s an important breeding ground and nesting site for wedge-tailed shearwaters. The iconic yoorndoordoo, or osprey, soars over the West End’s coastal ridges, nesting in large stacks at Fish Hook Bay.

Down in the water you can watch pods of dolphins frolicking in the waves off Cape Vlamingh. Cathedral Rocks plays home to a colony of long-nosed fur seals, who enjoy sunning themselves on the rocks. And from August to December, when you look further out to sea, you might spot the telltale spray of water from migrating humpback whales.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are available at West End?

While secluded, West End has a number of facilities available for visitors, with public toilet facilities at Narrow Neck and Cape Vlamingh. Wheelchair access is available at some of West End’s key locations, including the Cathedral Rocks Viewing Platform, and along the West End boardwalk. There’s even a coffee caravan, [Lexi’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lexi-s-on-rotto), located at the Island Explorer bus stop, for those in need of a caffeine fix or restorative bite to eat.

What is the best way to get there?

The fastest and easiest way to get to West End is on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and getting off at Stop 11 at Eagle Bay.

Is fishing allowed at West End?

The marine area surrounding the West End headland is protected under fisheries legislation as a Demersal Sanctuary Zone. This means that all bottom-dwelling marine species are protected in this sanctuary; however, fishing for pelagic species is permitted.

# Cycle Your Way Around the Island

From coastal landscapes to pink-stained salt lakes, iconic lookouts, and everything in between, this is your guide to experiencing Wadjemup on two wheels.

5 minutes

Image Salmon Bay

Salmon Bay

**There is a limited number of vehicles on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Traffic noise is replaced by the sounds of birdlife, travellers’ voices lowered in awe, and distant waves crashing along the coastline. [Cycling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling) has become the main form of transport on the island, allowing visitors to slow down and properly take in the unique landscape.**

A 22 km road network weaves across Wadjemup, providing access to most of the beautiful Class A Reserve. Both paved and dirt tracks wind past grassy headlands, incredible ocean vistas, and colourful [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), all vibrant with an array of [native wildlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature).

Stick to the Island Paths

The roads and cycle paths are designed to give you a full experience of the island with minimal impact on the native environment. You can help by staying on the roads and watching wildlife go about their natural movements.

### Getting started — hire everything you need

Bring your own bikes across on the ferry, hire some from the ferry operator, or book your bikes (and any other gear you need) in advance from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) so that when you arrive, they will be waiting for you. Pedal & Flipper Hire is located on the island and has step-through and cross-bar bikes, electric bikes, and a large selection of children’s bikes. You can also hire bikes with baby seats and child trailers for transporting smaller travellers around the island.

Pedal & Flipper Hire also offers a bike and bus package, designed for those looking to experience more of the island while taking a break when needed. You can cycle out to one of the many beaches and then simply leave your bike on the racks and take the bus back to the settlement.

Bike hire

Image 

Safety first

Image 

Choose your ride

### Choose your adventure — island cycle routes

#### The Rotto Mini Loop

Distance: 4 km

Time: 30 minutes

[This 4 km loop](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-rotto-mini-loop--4-km-of-easy--scenic-cycling) gives the perfect snapshot of Wadjemup. It winds past some of the island’s most impressive locations and is easy to complete in less than an hour.

Setting off from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), you’ll ride through the peaceful bushland towards [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin). The clear, shallow waters and protective reef wait invitingly for your refreshing mid-cycle dip. 

The route continues along the coast, past the quiet accommodation hideaway of [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) towards [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay). [Geordie's Cafe and Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) is another place you can stop on this leisurely cycle; pick up a fresh juice, sit at the beach, and watch the boats tack across the water. Back on the road, the trail runs inland, traversing between the [golf course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) and still waters of the [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). 

The peak of the journey is Vlamingh Lookout, where you can take in expansive views over the island before you arrive back at the settlement.

#### Beaches, Lighthouses, and Lakes

Distance: 10 km

Time: 1.5-3 hours

[This 10 km loop](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycling-trail-adventure--beaches--a-lighthouse-and-lakes) explores more of the island without being too arduous. If you take your time, pausing at every stunning vista and dipping your toe at all the beaches, then you can while away an entire afternoon.

Begin by heading south past Kingstown Barracks, gliding along vibrant green headlands, and watching as a new beach unfurls around every corner. The route passes by some of the most picturesque spots on the island, including [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks), Porpoise Bay, [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point).

After Salmon Bay, ride inland towards [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse). Then pause your journey and ascend 38 metres of stairs to the top of the lighthouse, where you can admire 360-degree views and spot the Perth skyline in the distance across the ocean.

On the way back to the settlement, you will cycle through the island’s network of mirrored [lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) and wetlands. Stop to take a stroll along the lakes boardwalk and discover how the lakes were formed from the interpretative signage. These wetlands are a haven for birdlife, so look out for banded stilts, crested terns, and Red-necked Phalarope on Lake Herschel and Lake Baghdad.

Image Henrietta Rocks

[Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks)

Lakes boardwalk

Parker Point

#### The Island Ride

Distance: 22 km

Time: 3-5 hours

This is the ultimate adventurer’s route, where you [cycle the entire island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-island-ride--cycle-the-entire-island) — all the way to [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). If you’re willing to go the distance, then you will discover abundant rewards. As you travel the southern side of the island, you will pass along the same string of popular beaches visited in the 10 km ride, providing ample opportunities for a cooling swim.

After this, the landscape becomes more rugged as you enter the narrow western end of the island. For the chance to witness local marine life in their natural habitat, stop at the Cathedral Rocks and Cape Vlamingh viewing platforms. From there you can see long-nosed fur seals resting in their colony, Australian sea lions basking on the beach, and out in the sea, bottlenose dolphins and [migrating humpback whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) (from August to December).

The coastal return path is a collection of beautiful, expansive beaches, as you travel past places like [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) and [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) on your way to the main settlement. Watch the headlands transform into bushland dotted with thriving [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), before arriving in the bustle of [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) once again.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

# Geordie Bay

## Explore the northern coast of Rottnest Island

A curve of white sand gives way to brilliant blue water, dotted with boats. The large, curved beach provides space for roving groups of families and friends.

One of the largest beaches on the island, Geordie Bay offers enough space for everyone to set down a towel, open up the picnic blanket, and spend their day by the water. Swimming further out into the bay, you’ll find [excellent snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) opportunities. Dive below the gentle waves to come face to face with schools of fish, and even the occasional stingray passing by. Stay until sunset for one of the best views of the island’s daily sky shows in an idyllic setting.

While home to bands of curious [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas), make sure you look without getting too close, and give them the distance they need to enjoy their island home.

### You'll also find...

Image 

Vibrant blue water

Image 

Friendly quokkas

Image 

Holiday accommodation

Image 

Boat moorings

### Where to find Geordie Bay

One of Wadjemup’s northern beaches, Geordie Bay is situated just an easy 7-minute [bike ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) from the Thomson Bay settlement. A key stop on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus route, you can take the bus around the island and get off at Stop 19. There’s also [boat mooring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/boating) available, but be sure to book in advance, as the bay gets busy.

Image 

[Stay Rottnest](/stay/stay-rottnest-self-contained)

### Make your Wadjemup stay something special

Geordie Bay features everything you need to make the most of your Wadjemup holiday.

One of the busier accommodation locations, visitors will find a range of lodging options suitable for groups and families. Each one is located conveniently close to the beach, with a view out to the vast, northern Indian Ocean. Simply step outside your front door and it’s a quick walk to the crisp white sand.

The nearby [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) provides mouth-watering cafe meals, available to eat in or take away, while the [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store) has a selection of the provisions you’ll need to ensure you make the most of your island holiday.

[Learn more about accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained)

Image Geordie Bay

Geordie Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are available at Geordie Bay?

Geordie Bay is one of the more populous beaches, so it has plenty of close amenities available, including public toilets, showers, accommodation options, as well as a cafe and general store.

Can I fish at Geordie Bay?

Yes, rod and hand line fishing is permitted at Geordie Bay, both on the shore and by boat.

Is Geordie Bay good for snorkelling?

A large portion of Geordie Bay is sandy-bottomed and shallow, making it ideal for swimming and splashing around. If you head further out into the bay, you’ll traverse green seagrass, which eventually gives way to colourful coral. Here you’ll find some excellent snorkelling conditions, with plenty of inquisitive reef fish — and if you look hard enough, you may even see the occasional octopus or stingray.

# Value-packed Rottnest Island Adventures Guaranteed to Become Priceless Memories

The value of time spent on Wadjemup can’t be measured. From a snorkel in marine gardens to a picnic with incomparable views or a free walking tour — here’s how to experience maximum fun on the island with minimum spend.

3 minutes

Image 

Explore the many beaches and bays

**A journey to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island promises a world of adventure. And the best part? The most memorable experiences that will stay with you for a lifetime won’t cost you a cent.**

From the moment you arrive to when you settle into your seat on the ferry home, this island offers endless opportunities to disconnect from the day-to-day and immerse yourself into its unique wonders. And as you watch the island shrink into the distance behind you on your journey back to the mainland, you’ll find the value of your time spent here lingers long after.

Here is our guide to a wealth of free and low-cost experiences waiting to be embraced, guaranteed to become lifelong, priceless memories.

#### Nature’s wonders: free for all to explore

As you journey away from the mainland, the ocean unfolds in front of you, and it begins. Surrounded by the expanse of ocean on your short journey towards the island, you’ll find yourself drawn to its natural beauty as it appears on the horizon. Whether you’re walking the [Wadjemup Bidi trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi), taking a refreshing [dip in the bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches), [spotting quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) hopping around, or stopping for a picnic at a [lookout point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-top-five-lookouts-on-wadjemup-rottnest-island) that makes Perth city seem so small, yet so close— nature’s charms are yours to explore here.

#### Oceanside fun for free

The island’s sun-drenched coastline beckons its visitors to explore the wonders along the water’s edge. Even if you’re exploring Rottnest Island with a budget in mind, there are plenty of free seaside activities available from swimming through the [underwater sanctuaries](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) to venturing out to [shipwrecks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks), just a short paddle from the shore.

#### Stay dry with activities on land

Beyond the island’s beaches and bays, there’s a collection of wallet-friendly land-based activities that nurture a deeper understanding of the island you’re visiting. Join a [free walking tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) with the Rottnest Voluntary Guides to seek out the native flora and fauna freckled around the island or to gain insight into the significant history of Wadjemup. Plan your visit based on the exhibitions at [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) (entry by contribution) and the [calendar of free events](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/whats-on) that add even more vibrancy to the island’s atmosphere throughout the year.

#### 

#### The freedom of a picnic

There are plenty of affordable venues on the island for a delicious feast with your friends and family, but some of the best dining experiences are the ones you create for yourself. With public barbeques at [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), and [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), you can set up a midday or sundowner feast with unbeatable views, surrounded by nature. Thomson Bay makes for an idyllic spot for a shared meal with your loved ones, with its shady trees and protected waters.

#### Explore for less by foot or bus

Wadjemup invites you to slow down the pace, and it’s [easy to do that on foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/a-guide-to-walkable-delights-near-the-main-settlement) allowing you to soak up the island surrounds. Within a 10-minute walk of the main settlement, you can find [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) nestled in lush landscapes, panoramic views of the island, and the crystal-clear waters of The Basin and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). For those wanting to travel further afield, the [accommodation shuttle bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) is an affordable way to travel between Kingstown Barracks in the south and Geordie Bay to the north, at just $5 for a day pass.

#### Plan smart, save more

When you put spontaneity aside and plan your visit to Rottnest Island in advance, you can often find a range of [discounts and special offers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals). Everything from discounted ferry tickets to tours and activity deals are available so that you can connect to all that is here while staying within your budget.

#### Value-packed stays for the thrifty traveller

Travelling to Rottnest Island on a budget doesn’t mean that you’re restricted to a day trip. There’s a range of [accommodation options](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on Rottnest Island that allow you to extend your visit and witness the quiet and stillness of the evenings and early mornings.

Sleep under the stars at the [campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/stay-rottnest-camping) and wake up to the natural sounds of the island or stay in a [shared hostel or private family dorm](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/stay-rottnest-hostel), just ten minutes from the main settlement. Choosing to travel in the low season (even mid-week vs the weekend) can also make a big difference.

# Emergency Services

Important emergency contacts should you need assistance while at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Image Fuel jetty

Fuel jetty

### Emergency contacts

When travelling to Rottnest Island, please take note of the following emergency contacts should you need assistance during your visit.

Call 000 in an Emergency

If at any point during your stay at the island there is a life-threatening emergency, contact emergency services on 000 first, or Channel 16 on VHF radio.

[If You See Sick or Injured Wildlife

If you see sick or injured wildlife, or wildlife being mistreated, please report it immediately to the Rottnest Island Rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us)

### For non-emergencies

**Police:** 131 444

**Rottnest Island Nursing Post:** +61 8 9292 5030

Vessel breakdowns or mechanical assistance should be directed to your [local Sea Rescue group](https://www.searescue.com.au/).

If you notice a fuel or oil spill, immediately contact the Department of Transport on (+61 8) 9480 9924 or by email on [marine.pollution@transport.wa.gov.au](mailto:marine.pollution@transport.wa.gov.au).

### Other useful contacts

**Rottnest Island Visitor Centre:** (+61 8) 9372 9730 or (+61 8) 9372 9728 after hours

**Rottnest Island Rangers:** (+61 8) 9372 9788 or Channel 16 call sign ‘Rottnest Rangers’

Image Rottnest ranger boat

Rottnest ranger boat

### Automated External Defibrillators (AED)

Automated external defibrillators (AED) are located in specific areas on the island.

* Kingstown Barracks
* The Mall
* The Basin
* Geordie Bay shopping complex
* Rottnest Island Fire Station
* West End Ablution Block
* Oliver Hill
* Wadjemup Lighthouse

The defibrillators were purchased with the assistance of the [Rottnest Island Foundation](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/) and a St John Lotterywest Heart Grant.

Please note that in the event of an emergency on the island, dial 000 and follow the prompts. If the incident is a cardiac-related medical emergency, the 000 operator will provide a code to unlock and use the AED.

The AEDs are registered with [St John Ambulance WA](https://stjohnwa.com.au/) and their locations are listed on their [First Responder mobile app](https://stjohnwa.com.au/working-together/app). Everyone who has received first aid training is encouraged to download it to their mobile phone or tablet.

We also encourage everyone to download the [Emergency+ app](https://www.emergencyplus.com.au/). This app uses the GPS functionality built into smartphones to provide location information including GPS coordinates and street address, which assists in an emergency. For more information visit [Emergency+ website.](https://www.emergencyplus.com.au/)

Bushfire Safety

Hot and dry conditions in Western Australia mean there is a risk of bushfire on Rottnest Island, and care should be taken at all times. As a Class A Reserve, the lighting of fires (including campfires) is prohibited.

**Every visit to Rottnest Island offers you the chance to slow down, take a breath and open up to the spaces that welcome you.**

With accommodation options ranging from cottages to cabins, beachfront units to bungalows, you’ll find the perfect place to connect back to yourself as you explore an island that is unlike anywhere else you’ve ventured.

**Open Days**

Stay Rottnest is a popular choice of accommodation on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. With a large range of accommodation at affordable prices, Stay Rottnest often books out regularly. Lock in key dates for Open Days to book reservations nine (9) months ahead. Open Days occur the first Wednesday of each month.

It is recommended to review the [booking guide](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf) ahead of the open day to review available booking periods, room types and booking terms and conditions.

Visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf) for more information about open days.

**Managing your booking**

Book, manage and pay for your accommodation on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/retrieve?_gl=1*lvhfdr*_ga*MTIzMTI1MjY0OC4xNzQ5MDAxNjQ2*_ga_LBX2JC94NF*czE3NTM3Njc4ODEkbzMkZzAkdDE3NTM3Njc4ODEkajYwJGwwJGgw).

**Arrival and Luggage Information**

The check-in time is from 2 pm, with keys available from the Visitor Centre, found at the Island end of the main jetty. If you arrive at the Visitor Centre before 2 pm, you can provide your mobile phone number and staff will send you an SMS if your unit is ready for an early check-in.

For more information regarding arrivals and luggage visit the [Stay Rottnest Website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_arrival_information.pdf).

**Frequently Asked Questions**

For more information and frequently asked questions, visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_faqs_2024.pdf).

If you require further assistance, please contact Stay Rottnest directly.

Your accommodation number will be emailed to you approximately three weeks prior to your arrival date. If you book within three weeks of your arrival, your accommodation number will be emailed to you with your booking confirmation.

The accommodation map can be viewed on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_accommodation_maps.pdf), simply click the relevant accommodation icon to open a more detailed map.

### Frequently Asked Questions

How do I book accommodation?

Stay Rottnest accommodation is available to book online via [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) or via phone on (+61) 1800 111 111 (Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm, excluding public holidays). Bookings can be made up to nine months in advance of your stay.

**Booking online**

[Booking online](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) is the quickest and easiest way to secure Stay Rottnest accommodation and receive instant confirmation.

Special requests and notes are also able to be placed in the booking.

How do Open Days work?

Availability for bookings opens on the first working Wednesday of each calendar month, for accommodation nine months in advance.

While you can book by calling Stay Rottnest on (+61) 1800 111 111, online is the simplest and most successful way to book accommodation. As demand for bookings is high, a virtual queuing system is used to ensure a smooth experience for everyone on busy Open Days.  

**Booking for Accessibility**

If you need wheelchair accessible accommodation, please send your request after 8:30 am to [stay@rottnestisland.com](mailto:stay@rottnestisland.com) and ensure you attach a copy of your ACROD Card (front and back). These requests are processed in the order they’re received from 8:30 am onwards on Open Day, so hold your email until then. There is a limit of one booking per ACROD Card.

For more information, visit [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates)

When are Open Days scheduled?

Open Days are held on the first Wednesday of each month, to release availability for the next booking period, nine months in advance.

Visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/files/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf) to see all current scheduled Open Day dates.

How much will it cost?

The prices of Stay Rottnest accommodation vary based on the type of accommodation chosen, the time of year and availability. To check prices for available accommodation, select your preferred dates, location and accommodation type on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates).

Is there a minimum stay requirement?

Yes, minimum night stays are required and vary according to the season. Please refer to the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) for further details.

Can I alter or cancel my booking?

Yes, however cancellations and modifications may incur a cancellation fee.

Further details on how to cancel or alter your booking, and applicable fees, can be found in the [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

Can I transfer my booking to someone else?

You may nominate another person as authorised to check in to the accommodation, however you will remain as the owner of the booking as the original guest. As the owner of the booking, you will be liable for any costs related to the accommodation for the duration of the booking.

You can view the full [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

Are there booking blocks?

Specific booking blocks for different types of accommodation can be found in the Stay Rottnest [Open Day Booking Guide](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf?instrck=eyJhIjoiZGFhNjMxNmYtM2E4YS0yYTk2LWEzZmEtMWRiZWI3ZjE1Y2Y1IiwicyI6Ijk4NDc2NTg3LWRmMjctNDg0OC04ZjlhLTk1ZGVkYWQ0ODVhYyIsImQiOiJXZWJzaXRlIiwidCI6MTc1NDAzNDQ0NDk0OSwic2kiOiIxNzU0MDM0MTk3NzA0LTUxMDExMDMwLTM3YzMtNDg3Ni05OTFhLTZhMDFjNTcyNmI1YiJ9) which is released the month before the corresponding open day.

When do I find out my unit number?

Your accommodation number will be emailed to you approximately three weeks prior to your arrival date. If you book within three weeks of your arrival, your accommodation number will be emailed to you with your booking confirmation.

Where can I find an accommodation map?

You can find a accommodation map of all accommodation types on the [Stay Rottnest website here](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_accommodation_maps.pdf).

What time is check-in?

Check-in is from 2 pm. You can leave your mobile number at the Visitor Centre, who will text you if your accommodation is ready early.

What time is check-out?

The check-out time is 9 am.

What’s included in my accommodation?

The inclusions vary by accommodation. You can see what is included for each type at [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates).

Do I need to bring linen and towels?

No, linen and towels are provided.

How do I hire extra items like cots, high chairs and heaters?

If you require additional items, please complete a [Hire Items Booking Form](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/accommodation_hire_items_2026.pdf).

Please contact Stay Rottnest at least 48 hours prior to arrival for hire items. 

Note the default setup is one king size bed per unit, with remaining rooms configured as twins. Requests for alternative configurations must be received at least seven days prior to arrival.

When is luggage collection?

For Stay Rottnest Self-Contained accommodation, luggage must be out for collection by 8 am for ferries departing at 10 am or later. For ferries departing before 10 am, luggage must be out for collection by 7 am and must be pre-booked by notifying the Visitor Centre 24 hours before departure.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If ferries are cancelled for the day of your departure, guests of Stay Rottnest accommodation will be contacted by reservations and given the option to:

* Leave the day prior and receive a refund for your unused night of accommodation, or
* If your accommodation is available for an extra day, you will be invited to stay for 50% of the rack rate.

If you do not wish to leave early, and your accommodation is not available for an extra night, nor is any alternate Stay Rottnest accommodation available, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire if they have availabilities.

# Weather

A destination for all seasons

## Inviting weather year-round offers unique seasonal experiences, from spectacular flora and fauna to rich history and aquatic adventures

The best time of year to visit Wadjemup / Rottnest Island varies for everyone, as the weather in each season brings its own charm. Discover seasonal weather forecasts that highlight typical temperatures, wind and waves, helping you plan the escape that suits you.

Whether you’re seeking a relaxed family holiday making memories with local wildlife, a weekend of aquatic and outdoor adventures, or a reflective retreat to soak in serenity and cultural insights, Rottnest Island offers something special in every season.

On sun-drenched [summer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) days, you can expect light mornings and an afternoon sea breeze, with gentle waves ideal for swimming and snorkelling among the thriving marine life. In [autumn](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/autumn) and [winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter), mild weather, shifting winds and lively swells set the scene for coastal walks on the Wadjemup Bidi hiking trails. Alternatively, you can choose to settle in for cosy and peaceful seclusion with loved ones in these cooler months. Come [spring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/spring), wildflowers burst into colour and quokka joeys begin to appear along with the warmer weather.

Whatever season you choose, Rottnest Island promises unforgettable adventures.

### Frequently asked questions

What is the weather like on Rottnest Island?

Rottnest Island has a mild climate with warm, dry summers and cool winters. Summer temperatures average around 26°C, while winter averages about 18°C. Rainfall is mostly in winter, and sea breezes keep conditions pleasant year-round. Expect plenty of sunshine and inviting weather across all seasons.

What is the best time to visit Rottnest Island?

Rottnest Island is an incredible destination all year round, with each season offering its own unique experiences.   
While [summer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) (December – February) is the most popular time to explore the beautiful beaches, you can still enjoy warmer weather for water-based activities between September and April. The [winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) months (June – August) are a great time for a range of land-based experiences from hiking to wildlife encounters.

Learn more about how the incredible flora and fauna change throughout the year with our [guide to the Noongar seasons](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup) on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

Can you swim at Rottnest Island year-round?

Yes, you can swim at Rottnest Island year-round. Summer brings the warmest weather and ideal conditions, while autumn and spring remain pleasantly warm. Winter is cooler, but swimming is still possible with many visitors opting for a wetsuit during this time. Thanks to the Leeuwin Current flowing from Indonesia, water temperatures are about 4°C warmer than the WA coast.

# Eat & Drink

## Choose your food adventure: fueling nature explorations or indulging beachside?

On Rottnest Island, you’ll have a dining option for every craving. Hunger-taming hot chips while you’re still dripping from the sea. A jam doughnut oozing with sweetness at the halfway point of your hike. Or a generous plate of fresh pasta, paired with a glass of wine and Thomson Bay views.

For those travelling with family, [Dome Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe), [Geordie’s Café](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) or [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) are some crowd-pleasing favourites, with dishes like homemade sourdough pizzas and hearty burgers to satisfy tired explorers. And when you’re heading out to discover the natural surroundings, spots like [The Lane Café](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane), [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery), [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and the vintage caravan [Lexi’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lexi-s-on-rotto) have takeaway options for refuelling on the go. The island even has several fine dining restaurants like [Isola Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest) and [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara), where you can while away an evening with some local seafood and refreshing cocktails.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Can you take food and drink to Rottnest Island?

Yes, you can bring your own food and drinks to Rottnest Island. Just ensure you are within your weight limit if you are catching the ferry or plane. As with the rest of Western Australia, street drinking is strictly prohibited.

Can you drink alcohol on Rottnest Island?

Yes, there are a number of licensed venues on Rottnest Island where you can purchase and drink alcohol. As with the rest of Western Australia, street drinking is strictly prohibited.

If you’re staying overnight, you may be allowed to bring drinks with you to consume in your accommodation. [Check with your accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) providers about bringing your own alcohol.

How many bars are on Rottnest Island?

There are a number of bars, restaurants and places to get a drink on Rottnest Island. From casual settings like [Geordie Bay Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery), [Dome Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe), [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) and [The Mezz on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-mezz-on-rotto), to seaside options including [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island), and more fine dining choices like [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar), [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara), and [Isola Bar E Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest).

# Little Salmon Bay Snorkel Trail

## A bucket-list snorkelling experience

Little Salmon Bay provides a sheltered spot for families, and snorkelling enthusiasts, to get acquainted with one of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s most popular aquatic experiences.

A series of ten buoys mark out information plaques installed on the seabed, which allow divers and snorkellers to learn more about the unique plants and sea life that surround them under the gentle waves.

Starting and ending on the white sandy beach, the trail winds its way around Little Salmon Bay in a loop, around 700 metres long in total. Bright, colourful, tropical fish dart in and out of seagrass and limestone rocks. Pink-hued coral dots the seabed here and there. There’s a lot to see when you glide along the trail, so despite the calm waters, allow for around an hour to complete the trail.

### Where to find the Little Salmon Bay Snorkel Trail

Located on the south side of the island, Little Salmon Bay is over five kilometres away from the main settlement. It’s a bit long to walk, but makes for a nice 25-minute [bike ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike). Alternatively, you can take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus and get off at Stop 6.

Image 

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](/learn)

### Creating a future for Wadjemup flora and fauna

The Little Salmon Bay Snorkel Trail is part of the Parker Point Marine Sanctuary. One of five Marine Sanctuary Zones located at different points on Wadjemup’s coast, these are specific areas of the island set aside for conservation. All plant and animal life within this area is protected, which means that no collection of flowers or plant life, or fishing of any kind, is permitted.

These Sanctuary Zones have been put in place to build a thriving underwater ecosystem, and foster a healthy, sustainable undersea environment for generations to come. And it’s already working. Under the waves, you’ll find a diversity of fish and sea life among one of Wadjemup’s most extensive coral reef systems.

So duck beneath the waves, enjoy the calming tides, and do your part to ensure the future of Wadjemup’s natural beauty.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby?

There are no facilities at Little Salmon Bay. But don’t worry, the Parker Point facilities are an easy five-minute walk away — or one minute on the bike.

Can I fish at Little Salmon Bay?

Little Salmon Bay is part of the Parker Point Marine Sanctuary Zone, so no fishing is permitted.

How do I get there?

Little Salmon Bay is an easy bike ride  from Thomson Bay settlement, just a few kilometres. Alternatively, get off at Stop 6 on the Quokka Coaches Island Explorer bus.

# Amenities

From barbecue blocks to toilet stops, discover where to rest and refresh on the island.

Image The Basin

The Basin

### All the essentials

While Wadjemup / Rottnest Island feels a world away from the mainland, rest assured that you can find all the important amenities for a convenient and comfortable stay.

You'll find accessible bathroom facilities, showers and drinking water across the main settlement, with additional toilets across the island and water refill points at the Army Jetty, Kingstown Barracks, The Basin, Vlamingh Lookout and Geordie Bay.

For those with little wanderers in tow, there are baby change facilities and playgrounds in central locations at Thomson Bay and Geordie Bay.

Check the island map for bus stops, rest areas and barbeques around the island to plan your day, as well as boat fuel and water access points for those travelling on the water.

# See & Do

## Things to do on Rottnest Island

There is so much to see and do on Rottnest Island, with experiences for everyone from snorkelling and swimming to wildlife encounters, dining and relaxing by the coast. Discover the best things to do and start planning your island getaway.

## Rich history, incredible coastal scenes and thriving native wildlife

Awaken your appetite for curiosity and adventure; discover amazing experiences that will reconnect you to the energy of life. While shoes are optional, a desire to wonder (and wander) is highly recommended.

Tick off your bucket list by spotting a [world-famous quokka](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) or travel the network of [bike paths](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling) and [walking trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) under your own steam. Explore underwater marine sanctuaries [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) at iconic [beaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) and during the [whale watching](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) season from August to December, get up close with migrating humpback and southern right whales as they linger in the calm waters around the island. Whether you are here for a [day trip](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/a-day-trip-to-rottnest-island) or a longer stay, find the best things to do, seasonal highlights and practical tips to help plan your visit.

Enjoy a variety of places to eat and drink, including relaxed cafes, restaurants, pubs and quick bites suited to every taste while exploring what to do across the island.

**Disconnect from the world and discover what really matters, with a low-impact glamping experience on Rottnest Island.**

Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island values enrichment, connection and minimal impact. Featuring 83 eco-tents, this accommodation delights in the natural setting, with all the luxurious comforts of a hotel or resort.

Wake up to a soft sea breeze and unparalleled ocean views. Then in the evenings, drift serenely to sleep under the stars. During the day, explore boardwalks through the sand dunes to [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) and laze by the resort pool. Even in the cooler months, the eco-tents are a great way to escape mainland reality; the thick canvas will keep you cosy as you enjoy the peaceful seaside surroundings.

Options range from deluxe hideaways to simpler set-ups, so there’s an accommodation level for every preference.

There are a number of tents designed specifically for accessibility.

For more information or to make a booking, visit the [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island website](https://www.discoveryholidayparks.com.au/caravan-parks/western-australia/greater-perth/rottnest-island?propertyCode=WROT&arrive=2024-09-02&depart=2024-09-03&adults=2&kids=0&infants=0&sort=price-desc&maxSearchResults=30&children=0).

#### Where to find Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island

Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island is a scenic 1 km walk or cycle from the ferry jetty through the main settlement.
Transfers are available upon request.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to carry my own bag to Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island?

Take it easy with Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island’s luggage delivery service. Luggage tags will be sent to you upon booking, or can be collected at the ferry terminals.

On boarding the ferry, your luggage will be stored and delivered to your accommodation for you.

What time is check-in?

Check-in is available from 2 pm.

What time is check-out?

The check-out time is 10 am.

Where can I find an accommodation map?

You can view an accommodation map showing all tent types on the [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island website](https://www.discoveryholidayparks.com.au/getmetafile/c3568ed7-1e93-48de-ab16-87aa0cfd5550/discovery-resorts-rottnest-island-park-map-sep-2024).

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If ferries are cancelled on your scheduled departure date, the reservations team at Discovery Resorts – Rottnest Island may be able to assist with extending your stay or rescheduling your booking dates, subject to availability. Please note that additional costs may apply. 

If accommodation at Discovery Resorts – Rottnest Island is not available for an additional night, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire about availability.

# Winter School Holiday Fun for All

Ignite adventure with a visit to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. An action-packed itinerary awaits with winter school holiday activities and wonder for all to appreciate.

5 minutes

Image 

Spot wildlife around the lakes

**Bundle up and make your way to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island this July school holidays.****Here, families of all ages will be delighted** **by the island’s natural wonders, active wildlife, and seasonal activities.**

### Winter on Rottnest Island

If your family has only experienced Rottnest Island in summer, it’s time to discover the [wonder of winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter). Daily temperatures are mild, while trails and beaches are blissfully quiet. [Accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) is also more readily available, often with [seasonal deals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals). It’s a time when the quieter side of the island’s natural beauty beckons, whether you're spotting native wildlife, enjoying a scenic cycle, or observing your surroundings with warm drinks in hand. With cosy delights around every corner, including free school holiday activities, this just might become your favourite season to visit.

### Outdoor winter fun for families

#### Wildlife spotting

Whether you wander near or far, there are endless opportunities to spot winter wildlife. Stroll a few minutes away from the main settlement to Garden Lake and amble along the boardwalk surrounded by the fascinating happenings of the [kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) from a respectful distance.

While you wander near the [kabikarning (salt lakes)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), listen out for unique species of (kooboolong) frogs that repopulate with the winter rains, then take to the ngobar (coastal) trails for sightings of the island’s many [djerap (birds)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching).

Further afield at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), keep little eyes fixed on the waves for possible glimpses of [maamoong (whales)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) on their annual migration.

Quokka Safety

To help keep the unique wildlife safe and healthy, please do not touch, feed or give water to the quokkas and always observe from a respectful distance.

#### 

#### Explore on two wheels

Let outdoor exploring be fuelled by the revitalising energy cooler weather offers. Glide around as a group thanks to the large selection of children’s bikes, baby seats and trailers at [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire). The [4 km Rotto Mini Loop](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-rotto-mini-loop--4-km-of-easy--scenic-cycling) trail is a popular pick for families, starting from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) and passing through bushland and striking coastland. When you’re rosy-cheeked and ready to refuel, [Geordie’s Café & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) offers a selection of kids’ meals and moreish mains, plus outdoor seating and a playground nearby.

For families with kids aged 12 and older, [Segway Tours WA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa) provides a few hours of guided exploration. Teens will love the independence that comes with these two-wheeled tours, which can either take you off-road to hidden reaches or around popular attractions.

Image 

[Quokka spotting in the rain](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

#### Hiking

Take to the trails of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-wonders-along-the-wadjemup-bidi) together, powered by cool salty air. It’s a dreamy season to trek along winding beachside trails, towards hidden coves, panoramic salt lakes or the wild West End. Each shared step invites new discovery. Spot passing marine life, splash in fresh puddles, and breathe in surrounding earthy scents. There are trails spanning across the island, to suit all abilities and ages.

#### Take a historical tour

Bring young explorers to learn more about the legacy of [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). Better still, arrive via rail on the historical [Captain Hussey train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) that departs from the main settlement. The [Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnels Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) details the history of the battery before taking you below ground to navigate the tunnels. Watch for excited faces when the Ghost Engine elicits a mighty roar.

Above ground, share a sense of family accomplishment by ascending 155 stairs on a [Wadjemup Lighthouse Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour). Your guide will share tales of engineering feats, before you marvel in the 360-degree views, including the Perth city skyline (on clear days). Nearby, [Kalli’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kalli-s-on-rotto) provides a welcome place to park up and enjoy panoramic views with a warming drink before or after your climb.

*Please note children aged 12 years and under must be accompanied by an adult on both tours. For the Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnels Tour, children cannot be carried and must be able to walk the full distance. The Wadjemup Lighthouse Tour is suitable for participants aged five years and over.*

#### 

### Cosy indoor island activities

#### Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf

Tee off for a round of [family mini golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) and enjoy a light-hearted game. If rain clouds gather overhead, the bright lights of the arcade offer a thrilling way to spend a few hours. Then, once everyone’s worked up an appetite, stroll over to [Dome](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/dome-cafe) for crowd-pleasing meals, plus creamy hot chocolates for good measure.

Staying overnight? Head to the [historic Picture Hall](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) for family-friendly flicks and the latest blockbusters paired with warm, buttery popcorn from the candy bar.

#### Fireside dining

Throughout the day and into the evenings, settle in at these family-friendly spots for drinks and food beside dancing flames. The fireplace is roaring inside at [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest) and [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest), where you can savour seasonal menus featuring hearty comfort food all day.

Later in the day, enjoy quality time together beside the outdoor firepits at [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island). Enjoy tasty, shared bites alongside cheek-flushing red wine, while the little ones are entertained by the gooey goodness of complimentary marshmallows.

### School holiday activities and events

#### Rottnest Voluntary Guides winter school holiday program

The Rottnest Voluntary Guides Association (RVGA) run a program of [free activities and tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/2027/07/03/rottnest-events/rottnest-voluntary-guides-july-school-holiday-program) to get kids of all ages to learn more about the island during the winter school holidays. 

#### Rottnest Voluntary Guides Free Walking Tours

The guides also offer [free daily walking tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) year-round. Environmental awareness and historical education are a primary focus during tours, which can include wildlife sightings, stories of shipwrecks, sailors and past settlement workers, plus information detailing the agriculture, industry, geology, and marine reserves of the island.

# Terms and Conditions

All applicants will be subject to the terms of Rottnest Island Authority (RIA) and the booking conditions of the Rottnest Island Authority.

All applications are records of the Rottnest Island Authority. RIA is subject to the *Freedom of Information Act 1992 (WA)*, which provides a general right of access to records held by the State Government agencies and local governments.

Any modification, amendment or other variation of the assessed application will be made in writing to applicants. Variations may include changes to the program, purpose, the timeframe of delivery, or the subsidy amount.

## Stay Rottnest Accommodation Booking Conditions

Maximum stay of three consecutive nights;

Monday to Thursday nights inclusive;

Kingstown Barracks Dormitories, Hostel and Governor Circle only, and,

Stay period of  **Monday 20 July 2026 to Thursday 24 September 2026 inclusive**.

**Stay Rottnest Accommodation Payment Terms**

* For bookings made greater than 90 days from arrival: no payment required at the time of booking.
* A $500 security deposit is required three months prior to arrival and applies to all group bookings made. This deposit is refundable for schools on the 100% off program after departure less any applicable costs.
* For schools on the 75% off program, full payment plus the $500 security deposit is due three months prior to arrival. The security deposit is refundable after the group have departed less any applicable costs.

**Stay Rottnest Accommodation Cancellation / Change Fees**

If a school changes or cancels a group booking within 90 days of arrival and:

* more than 48 hours' notice is provided prior to 2 pm check-in time: $55 fixed charge will be retained for each booking (each Dorm / House).
* less than 48 hours' notice is provided prior to the 2 pm check-in time: full payment / security deposit retained, whichever is the lesser amount.

RIA reserves the right to retain some or all of the security deposit for damages, cancellation fees or any other applicable accommodation costs.

**Occupancy limits:**a maximum of one person per bed for all accommodation; no additional bedding is provided.

**Adult / student ratio:** a ratio of one adult per house is required for school bookings at Governor Circle; and one adult per 10 students is required for school bookings at Kingstown Barracks and Hostel.

**Quiet times:** all visitors are required to respect the rights of others to enjoy the island at all times and to observe a quiet time of 9 pm to 9 am for Kingstown Barracks Dormitories, Hostel and Governor Circle.

Any breach of the applicable booking and stay terms and conditions by any individual of the group may result in immediate cancellation of tenancy without refund. This includes additional terms and conditions provided by email and those located on the reverse of the registration card which must be signed on check-in.

Please note that linen is not provided within the cost of accommodation and can be hired on a per person basis, or guests are welcome to bring their own. Linen costs can be found on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://www.stayrottnest.com/).

Where bulk luggage delivery is required, schools must contact the ferry company to book and pay for dedicated crates. Note that supporting ferry providers (Rottnest Express and Rottnest Fast Ferries) are offering discounts on luggage crates.

## Rottnest Voluntary Guides Association Educational Tours Booking Conditions

Tours must be booked a minimum of six weeks prior to arrival on the island.

All tours are subject to guide availability.

The subsidy is valid for educational tours in Term 3 of the WA school year in 2026 -  **Monday 20 July 2026 to Thursday 24 September 2026 inclusive**.

A choice of one educational tour:

* **Pioneers and Prisoners:** A 50-minute guided walking tour in the settlement of stories of Wadjemup in the 1800s. Tours run daily at 10:15 am, 11:15 am, 12:15 pm, 1:15 pm and 2:15 pm.
* **Reefs, Wrecks and Daring Sailors:**A 50-minute guided walking tour in the settlement to discover the coastline-forming events and the exploration of early European vessels. Tours run daily at 11:10 am, 12:10 pm and 2:10 pm.
* **Wadjemup Museum:**Located behind the bakery in the settlement, experience a 30-minute guided tour through mixed media displays that tell the rich history of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Tours run daily every half an hour from 10 am to 2:30 pm.

**Number of participants:**the maximum number of participants for each group is 25. Additional bookings for the same tour can be made if the school group is larger than 25.

**Duty of care:**the school is responsible for all duty of care in respect of persons attending those tours.

**Adult / student ratio:**schools must ensure every 10 students are accompanied by a responsible adult (based on Year 3 and up; a ratio of 1:5 applies for younger groups). The students are to always remain with the responsible adult whilst on a tour.

**Responsible adult:**schools must ensure responsible adults in charge of a minor are aware that they are responsible for ensuring the minor is bound by, and complies with, these terms and conditions.

**Indemnity:**the school shall indemnify Rottnest Island Authority for any loss, damage, and liability (including claims) incurred by it on account of any breach of these conditions, or any other wrongful act or omission, by any participant or responsible adult.

**No liability:**Rottnest Island Authority accepts no liability (in negligence or howsoever) for any loss, damage, or injury (including death) arising from a tour or any of the sites visited.

**Fitness:**on some of the tours (particularly in the heritage buildings) there may be uneven surfaces and stairs which require a reasonable level of fitness and mobility.

**No food / drinks in heritage locations:**food and drink cannot be taken into or consumed at any heritage venues.

**No smoking and no alcohol:**smoking and alcohol consumption are prohibited on all tours.

**Emergency:**in the case of an emergency, all tour participants must follow the instructions of Rottnest Island Authority staff or representatives (including volunteer guides).

**Behave lawfully:**all tour participants must not, whilst at, or in relation to their visit to or stay at the island, infringe any rule or requirement of any statute, subsidiary legislation, the common law or equity.

**Safety briefing:**people attending the tours will be provided with a safety briefing at the beginning of a tour.

Tours operated by the **Rottnest Voluntary Guides Association (RVGA)** - the tours are operated by volunteers. All volunteers have current Working with Children checks.

## Pedal & Flipper Hire Booking Conditions

To qualify for an Overnight School Camp Subsidy, the school must have a confirmed overnight accommodation booking in Kingstown Barracks Dormitories, Hostel or Governor Circle which matches the dates of hire equipment.

The subsidy applies for standard pedal bikes (adult and child sizes) and accessible fleet only.

Accessories other than helmets and locks will incur additional fees (example: baskets, gel seats etc). A full list of hire items and costs can be [found here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/docs/default-source/vendors/pedal-flipper/pricelist2025.pdf?sfvrsn=1ffdfd06_25).

**Payment Terms**

A $500 security deposit is required for all school group bike bookings.

RIA reserves the right to retain some or all of the security deposit for damage to bikes as assessed at the time:

* $50 for skidded tyre (through to the canvas)
* $27 for lost lock and / or key
* $27 for a lost helmet
* Up to $200 depending on level of damage for accessible trailers.

**Cancellation / change fees:** there are no fees to change or cancel a bike hire booking for school groups up until the day of hire collection.

## Cultural Safety Services Terms and Conditions

Cultural safety involves creating a safe, nurturing, and positive environment for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People. Schools participating in the subsidy and requiring cultural safety services for children and students must book all services six weeks prior to arrival on the island.

The subsidy is valid for the following cultural safety services in Term 3 of the WA school year in 2026 - **Monday 20 July 2026 to Thursday 24 September 2026** **inclusive**:

* **Cultural Ceremony:** A traditional smoking ritual used to cleanse and purify a specific area, as well as to cleanse the spirit, body, and soul while on Noongar Country.
* **Cultural Tour:** Aims to educate school students about Aboriginal cultural heritage and the island's history, particularly significant cultural sites such as the Quod (Aboriginal Prison) and the Wadjemup Aboriginal Burial Ground.
* **Cultural Care Personal Support:** An Aboriginal cultural health carer available to Aboriginal students who require cultural healing.

The following terms and conditions are subject to the availability of the service provider:

* Booking dates and times.
* Number of participants per cultural safety service.

**Duty of care:**the school is responsible for all duty of care in respect of persons attending cultural safety services.

**Adult / student ratio:**schools must ensure every 10 students are accompanied by a responsible adult (based on Year 3 and up; a ratio of 1:5 applies for younger groups). The students are to always remain with the responsible adult whilst taking part in a cultural safety service.

**Responsible adult:**schools must ensure responsible adults in charge of a minor are aware that they are responsible for ensuring the minor is bound by, and complies with, these terms and conditions.

**Indemnity:**the school shall indemnify Rottnest Island Authority for any loss, damage, and liability (including claims) incurred by it on account of any breach of these conditions, or any other wrongful act or omission, by any participant or responsible adult.

**No liability:**Rottnest Island Authority accepts no liability (in negligence or howsoever) for any loss, damage, or injury (including death) arising participation in a service or at any of the sites visited.

**Fitness:**on some of the tours (particularly in the heritage buildings) there may be uneven surfaces and stairs which require a reasonable level of fitness and mobility.

**No food / drinks in heritage locations:**food and drink cannot be taken into or consumed at any heritage venues.

**No smoking and no alcohol:**smoking and alcohol consumption are prohibited on all tours.

**Emergency:**in the case of an emergency, all participants must follow the instructions of Rottnest Island Authority staff or representatives.

**Behave lawfully:**all participants must not, whilst at, or in relation to their visit to or stay at the island, infringe any rule or requirement of any statute, subsidiary legislation, the common law or equity.

Rottnest Island Authority has engaged a service provider to deliver cultural safety services who have current **Working with Children checks**.
