# Practical Tips

Practical tips and advice to ensure your experience of the Class A Reserve is a safe and enjoyable one.

Image Couple overlooking the ocean

Couple overlooking the ocean

### For Helpful Advice

The [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) can help you with important information you should know about the island. Drop in for personalised advice, maps and assistance with booking tours and experiences.

### Staying On The Island

Unaccompanied Minors

Minors should be supervised while on Rottnest Island and are not permitted to stay overnight if unaccompanied by a responsible adult. Unaccompanied minors may be issued with caution notes or infringements for non-compliance with the *Rottnest Island Regulations 1988* or their accommodation booking conditions. This will result in the cancellation of their accommodation booking, and they will be made to return to the mainland on the next available ferry. Fees may apply for any cancellation of accommodation bookings as a result and refunds may not be given. Refer to your accommodation booking conditions for further details.

Camping

Camping on the island is only permitted in designated campsites in the settlement. Sites can be booked through [Stay Rottnest Campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-campground).

Personal property

All personal property must be taken each time you leave the island. Any personal property left in the Class A Reserve will be treated as abandoned property and disposed of by the Rottnest Island Authority accordingly.

Acceptable behaviour, noise and alcohol consumption

For the enjoyment of all visitors, guests are asked to be considerate of others and keep noise to a minimum. This is especially important after 11 pm. This includes music and generator noise. Guests wanting to quietly enjoy alcohol are welcome to do so, however as is the case throughout Western Australia, street drinking is not permitted. Infringements and evictions from the island are applicable.

### Nature and Wildlife Safety

Reef care

Please avoid walking on any reef as this can damage the fragile environment and the marine species that inhabit these areas.

Sandboarding

Sandboards or similar devices used to slide down dunes or sandy areas are prohibited and penalties apply. Dune blowout is an ever-present threat on Rottnest Island.

Can I swim with the seals?

Swimming with the long-nosed fur seals at Cathedral Rocks is not permitted. Visitors may use the purpose-built viewing platform at Cathedral Rocks to see wildlife from a safe distance.

Blue bottle jellyfish

Keep in mind that blue bottle jellyfish can be present in the water and wash up on the beach, as is common on Perth metropolitan beaches at different times of the year. While not life-threatening, stings can be painful and these creatures shouldn’t be touched – either in the water or if washed ashore.

Beware of snakes

Be aware there are venomous snakes on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. The dugite is a timid creature, but may bite if harassed. If bitten, seek immediate medical assistance.

Do not touch or feed wildlife

Never feed or touch wildlife on Rottnest Island and always observe from a reasonable distance, for your own personal safety and theirs. In some cases, feeding wildlife can result in the death of the animal and lead to unnatural behaviours.

Anyone who deliberately interferes with (including feeding) wildlife on Rottnest Island can be fined on the spot under the *Rottnest Island Regulations 1988* and potentially prosecuted under the *Wildlife Conservation Act 1950* with fines up to $10,000. Acts of animal cruelty may result in fines up to $50,000 and 5 years imprisonment under the *Animal Welfare Act 2002*.

If you see sick or injured wildlife

If you see a sick or injured animal or animals being mistreated, please report it immediately to the rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.

### Health and Safety

In case of emergency, dial 000 for assistance.

Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) are located on the island and at the Nursing Post; however, in a life-threatening emergency, call 000 immediately.

Reporting anti-social behaviour

If you witness or experience any incidents of anti-social behaviour during your stay, please report them to the [WA Police](https://www.police.wa.gov.au/), [Rottnest Island Authority Rangers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us) or the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre).

Wear adequate shoes and clothing

With a rich offering of active pursuits on the island, ensure you wear shoes adequate for hiking and cycling. As weather conditions can change rapidly, be prepared by checking local conditions before your visit and bring suitable clothing.

Prescriptions and scripts

There is no pharmacy available on Rottnest Island. Visitors are reminded to bring adequate supplies of essential prescription medications.

Non-prescription medicines are available at the [General Stores](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store). For injuries, please visit the [Nursing Post](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/nursing-post) in Thomson Bay.

Bushfire safety

The hot and dry conditions in Western Australia mean there is a risk of bushfires on Rottnest Island. As a Class A Reserve, the lighting of fires is prohibited and can be extremely dangerous. Care should be taken at all times and campfires are prohibited on the island. Please help protect our natural environment and follow the fire warnings. Safety information is available from the [Department of Fire and Emergency Services](https://www.dfes.wa.gov.au/)  (DFES).

Coastal hazards

The coastal environment of Rottnest Island is extremely fragile. Beware of unstable rock slopes, cliffs and overhangs. Stay clear of limestone cliff edges, caves and overhanging rocks. These areas can be unstable and may collapse. To avoid damage to dune vegetation, please remain on designated tracks when accessing coastal areas. This will help to reduce the risk of dune erosion.

Carry adequate water supplies

Always carry adequate supplies of water (minimum of two litres per person or three litres in hot weather). Once outside of the main settlement, there is limited access to drinking water. Drinking water refill points can be found within the Thomson Bay settlement and at the Army Jetty, Kingstown Barracks, The Basin, Vlamingh Lookout and Geordie Bay.

Sun safety

Travellers should always wear a wide-brimmed hat, long-sleeved shirt, sunglasses and sunscreen when outdoors. It is also recommended that you drink at least two litres of water each day. Take extra care and seek shade when outdoors in the middle of the day, when the UV radiation is intense.

Helmets, electric bicycles and e-rideables

Helmets must be worn by all visitors riding a bicycle. Electric bicycles and electric rideables (e-rideables) are also permitted on Rottnest Island in accordance with the requirements of the *Road Traffic Code 2000*. If you wish to bring an electric bicycle or e-rideable to the island, please ensure that it is compliant.

Safety at the Beach

* Always swim under supervision, or with a friend
* Read and obey the signs
* If you are unsure of conditions, don't swim
* Don't swim directly after a meal
* Don't swim under the influence of alcohol or drugs
* Don't run and dive in the water
* Conditions change regularly; check before you enter the water
* If you get into trouble in the water, don't panic - signal for help, float with a rip current or undertow, and wait for assistance

Snorkelling and diving

All divers and snorkellers should be aware of high boat traffic around the island. All divers using underwater breathing equipment (SCUBA) must fly or tow the international ‘A’ flag. Visitors in boats should keep at least 50 metres clear of vessels flying this flag, or divers towing the flag. Dive contractors may be working within the moorings areas and dive flag regulations should be observed. For your safety, always log your dives with the metropolitan [Sea Rescue](https://www.searescue.com.au/) groups.

Swimming

Swimming between the main ferry jetty and the Fuel Jetty is prohibited at all times. Swimming is not permitted from the ‘T’ Jetty or from the end of the main ferry jetty. Boating-prohibited areas have been designated in certain bays around the island to provide areas for swimming. These are identified by either signs or float lines. Please keep vessels clear of these areas. For your safety, swimming near moorings and jetties or designated anchorage areas is not recommended.

### Fishing

Sanctuary zones

As part of Rottnest Island Authority’s Marine Conservation Action Plan, five marine sanctuary zones have been established to help conserve the pristine marine environments surrounding the island. Fishing and/or collecting is prohibited in these areas. For more information see [Marine Sanctuaries](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability).

Ensure you have the appropriate licence if taking restricted species and note that spear fishing is prohibited within the specified boundaries of the Rottnest Island Marine Reserve. For more information, visit the [Department of Fisheries](http://rules.fish.wa.gov.au/).

Fishing line bins

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island has a number of fishing line bins located on its jetties. Please use bins to dispose of any fishing line and tackle.

### Boating

Boating emergencies

In the event of a life-threatening boating emergency, please contact the Police on 000 first or Channel 16 on VHF radio.

If your vessel breaks down or requires mechanical assistance, please contact your local [Sea Rescue](https://www.searescue.com.au/) group.

In the case of an oil or fuel spill, please contact the Department of Transport on (+61 8) 9480 9924 or [marine.pollution@transport.wa.gov.au](mailto:marine.pollution@transport.wa.gov.au).

If you need assistance from the rangers at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, they can be contacted on (+61 8) 9372 9788 or Channel 16, call sign “Rottnest Rangers”.

Liquid waste

All the waters within the Rottnest Island Marine Reserve are protected. No liquid waste can be discharged anywhere in these waters, including waste from marine sanitation devices (MSDs). Ensure you store your liquid waste appropriately and discharge to a suitable mainland facility or outside the marine reserve.

Solid waste

If possible, help to reduce carbon emissions and carry your own waste and recycling off the island. All waste placed in bins on the island is picked up by a truck, compacted and shipped by barge off the island. It is then processed in the same manner as mainland waste.

Loading zones

These are located in Thomson Bay on the Fuel Jetty, Hotel Jetty and ‘T’ Jetty on the main ferry jetty, as well as on the Geordie Bay Jetty. All loading zones have a 20-minute limit. Please observe the maximum time limit when loading or unloading passengers or equipment.

Personal watercraft and jet skis

There are no designated water ski areas within the Rottnest Island Marine Reserve and a 5 knot speed limit applies in most bays around the island. For further information please contact the [Department of Transport](https://www.transport.wa.gov.au/imarine/personal-watercraft.asp).

Rafting of vessels

Rafting of approved vessels up to 6.75 metres on swing moorings is permitted only where a mooring has been certified with “+ 6.75m” rating. Rafting is also permitted when vessels are on anchor. Appropriate admission fees apply.

### Island Facilities

Barbecues & Fires

The lighting of fires is not permitted on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. For your convenience, barbecues are located in Thomson and Geordie Bays.

Drinking water

As there is limited access to drinking water outside of the Thomson Bay main settlement, ensure you carry sufficient supplies with you. Refill points can be found within the Thomson Bay settlement and at the Army Jetty, Kingstown Barracks, The Basin, Vlamingh Lookout and Geordie Bay. Visitors travelling by boat are recommended to fill their water tanks from the mainland prior to departure. Water is desalinated on the island and restrictions apply.

Fuel and gas supplies

Unleaded, premium unleaded and diesel fuel is available from the Fuel Jetty in Thomson Bay by electronic self-service 24 hours per day, seven days per week. Mastercard, Visa and EFTPOS is accepted. For operator assistance (during office hours) please call the number displayed on the fuel bowser. Instruction and safety compliance for the operation of the fuel bowsers is displayed onsite. Fuel and gas supplies cannot be transported by bus.

Waste disposal and recycling

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a Class A Reserve and as such, all flora, fauna and landforms are protected. Please help care for the island’s fragile marine and terrestrial environment by observing the following:

**What goes in the recycling bins**

* Glass bottles and jars (clean and empty)
* Aluminium and steel (clean and empty)
* Plastic containers and bottles (clean and empty)
* Paper (not shredded)
* Cardboard (please flatten)

**What goes in waste bins**

* Food scraps or other green organic matter
* Coffee cups and take away containers
* Soft plastics
* Medical waste
* Nappies
* Clothing or textiles

Public Wi-Fi

Free Wi-Fi is available in the main settlement area. To access, select “RottnestWiFi” from your available Wi-Fi networks on your device and follow the prompts to connect. Wi-Fi may also be provided by accommodation providers.

Laundry Facilities

Laundry facilities, including Washers and dryers are available at three locations on the island: Geordie Bay, Kingstown Barracks, and behind [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire).

* Geordie Bay: Three washing machines (card or coin payments) and two dryers (card payments only).
* Kingstown Barracks: Two washing machines (card or coin payments) and one dryer (coin payments only).
* Behind Pedal & Flipper Hire: Four washing machines and two dryers (coin payments only).

Washing powder dispensers are available at the machines in Geordie Bay and behind Pedal & Flipper Hire. Additionally, you can purchase washing powder from the General Stores located in the [Settlement Mall](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store).

ATMs

An ATM is available inside the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) and can be accessed during opening hours. Please note that transaction fees may apply depending on your bank.

### Animals on the island

Pet restrictions and assistance dogs

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a Class A Reserve and domestic pets (including dogs) are not permitted on the island or in its waters. Persons in contravention of this regulation will be penalised and required to remove the pet immediately, at their own expense.

If there is a genuine medical requirement to bring an animal with you such as a guide, assistance or companion dog this is acceptable, however please contact the rangers prior to arrival on (+61 8) 9372 9788.

Domestic pets

Domestic pets are not permitted within the boundaries of the Rottnest Island Marine Reserve. Persons in contravention of this regulation will be penalised and required to remove the pet immediately at their own expense.

### Drone Use

Can I use a drone on the island for recreational use?

Drones for recreational use are currently not permitted on Rottnest Island.

General, ground-based photography and videography for personal use is always welcomed and encouraged.

Can I use a drone on the island for commercial use?

A permit is required for all commercial filming and photography on Rottnest Island, including for commercial drone use. You can find more information on the  [Rottnest Island Authority Website](https://www.ria.wa.gov.au/permits-and-fees/commercial-filming).

# Wildlife & Nature

## A biodiverse sanctuary of unique native wildlife and blooming flora

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island sits peacefully in the Indian Ocean, blooming just above the water’s surface. A protected sanctuary for native wildlife, the island is a flourishing oasis for flora and fauna.

Their homes are found in [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones), [salt lake shores](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), dense tea tree woodland, and undulating sand dunes. These habitats are part of six unique ecosystems, each with its own character. And, when you travel through this biological diversity, it can feel like you are crossing continents.

One unmistakable part of the Rottnest Island experience is a [quokka sighting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas). Spending time in proximity with these iconic marsupials is a memory that stays with you long after you leave the island.

As a Class A Reserve, the quokka population, as well as all native flora and fauna on Wadjemup, is protected for both recreation and conservation. So, when you travel the network of paths and roads around the island, you play an important part in maintaining the unique natural environment that surrounds you.

Image Birds over the lake

[Bird habitat](/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes)

### Help us protect island wildlife

Wadjemup is a Class A Reserve, home to an abundance of protected flora and fauna—with some species not found anywhere else on the planet. Trails and paths allow you to safely wander the precious ecosystem, while underwater, marine sanctuaries protect the unique sea gardens. This island is a vital wilderness and, as short-time spectators, it’s our work to protect the land and sea we’re privileged to experience.

 [Learn how to help protect our wildlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability)

[If You See Sick or Injured Wildlife

If you see sick or injured wildlife, or wildlife being mistreated, please report it immediately to the Rottnest Island Rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us)

# Educational Tours FAQ

### Frequently Asked Questions

What educational tours can be booked?

There are three educational tours to choose from:

* **Pioneers and Prisoners:** A 50-minute guided walking tour in the settlement featuring stories of Wadjemup in the 1800s. Tours run daily at 10:15 am, 11:15 am, 12:15 pm, 1:15 pm and 2:15 pm.
* **Reefs, Wrecks and Daring Sailors:** A 50-minute guided walking tour in the settlement to discover the coastline-forming events and the exploration of early European vessels. Tours run daily at 11:10 am, 12:10 pm and 2:10 pm.
* **Wadjemup Museum:** Located behind the bakery in the settlement, experience a 30-minute guided tour through mixed media displays that tell the rich history of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. Tours run daily every half an hour from 10 am to 2:30 pm.

How many educational tours can be booked?

Each school is entitled to one educational tour. If the school group exceeds the maximum number of participants per tour (25), subsequent tour bookings of the same tour can be booked so that each child in the school group visiting Rottnest Island receives an educational tour experience.

Do teachers count as part of the maximum number of participants per educational tour?

Yes. The maximum number of participants per tour (25) includes teachers and students.

What happens if our visit is cancelled, or I need to amend my educational tour?

Schools can re-book or amend tours for a new date within Term 3 2026, subject to availability. To cancel or amend and re-book, the school will need to email [groups@rottnestisland.com](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/pedal-flipper-hire)

Where do I go to start my educational tour?

Your tour booking confirmation email will include a meeting location of either the [RVGA Information Booth](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) or the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum). These areas are highlighted on [the Island Map here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/island-map).

# The Perfect Romantic Escape on Rottnest Island

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s natural beauty makes it a haven for couples seeking a romantic escape.

4 minutes

Image Couple looking at each other smiling sitting under an umbrella in the evening having a drink with views of Thomson Bay

**With stunning vistas around every corner and secluded beaches perfect for two, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is the ideal getaway for the romantic at heart.**

Whether you want to relax and recharge, indulge in a gourmet feast or explore together, the perfect romantic escape on Rottnest Island is only a short ferry ride away. Here are our favourite ways to impress someone on the island.

### Cruise the ocean

Set sail with a romantic day on the water, exploring the sparkling waters and white, sandy beaches.

Share a love of good food? Get ready for a day on a luxurious seafood cruise with [Rottnest Cruises](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises). As a bonus, you can even impress your significant other by pulling your own lobster pot from the ocean before tucking into your indulgent seven-course lunch.

If you're staying overnight, experience the romance of a sunset like never before with [Charter 1's Sunset Sail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/charter-1). Settle in and enjoy golden hour as it transforms the sky into a radiant spectacle, painting the horizon with hues of warmth and wonder. Savour the intimacy of the moment as you indulge in refreshing drinks and a charcuterie platter, all while cruising the waters of Wadjemup.

### Picturesque picnics

Sometimes simple romance is the way to go. Think: a picnic, a secluded bay, and a priceless view. Pack a basket and blanket and head to the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) to stock up on goodies for your very own grazing style lunch (there’s a store in Thomson Bay and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store)). If you prefer something ready-made, you can always stop off at the [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery), [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican), or [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane) for savoury and sweet treats to go. Once you’re loaded up with your gourmet feast, head off on bikes or catch the Quokka Coaches [Island Explorer Bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour). With 63 beaches and 20 bays to choose from, you’re guaranteed to find a dreamy spot for just the two of you.

### Sunset cocktails

Nothing says romance like a delicious cocktail or mocktail paired with a stunning view. If you're around during sunset, head to [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) at [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) for one of their creative concoctions and enjoy with your toes dipped in the sand as you overlook [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay). [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) is also an iconic [sunset spot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island). Simply, order a drink and settle in on the deck to toast the sun as it melts into the ocean. Or, visit [The Mezz on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-mezz-on-rotto), where you can savour your drink under the festoon lights as you look out across the Indian Ocean, seeing the distant glow of the mainland on the horizon.

### Delicious dining

The island offers plenty of dining options to make your day unforgettable. For a truly special experience, three standout picks are [Isola Bar e Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest), [HAVZA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza), and [Sunsets](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest).

At Isola, indulge in an Italian feast of fresh pasta and Western Australian seafood cooked over a charcoal-fired grill, perfectly paired with views over Thomson Bay. For a more intimate setting, head to HAVZA and share tapas while overlooking the turquoise waters of The Basin. Or, choose Sunsets, where you can savour vibrant Mediterranean dishes while taking in views across the island's salt lakes.

### Long walks

When it comes to long romantic walks, you’re spoilt for choice on Rottnest Island. Amidst the beauty and nature, the island offers the perfect backdrop for connecting with your special someone. Choose a stretch of pristine sand to wander hand in hand. Or immerse yourself in the island’s lush landscapes while you wander the paths of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi), where you’ll be taken from [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) and wetlands to rugged coastline.

### Relax with yoga

For a unique and serene date idea, practice yoga and meditation by the ocean, enjoying the soothing sounds of the waves around you. Connect with nature and each other as your stretch, relax, and learn breathing techniques together. Whether you're beginners or seasoned yogis, [Evolve in You](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/evolve-in-you-yoga) caters to all levels, ensuring a welcoming and enriching experience for everyone.

### Scenic flights

Want to make your visit even more exceptional with a touch of adventure? Treat yourself and your loved one to a scenic joy flight and experience breathtaking aerial vistas of the island. Soar above the island with [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi) and experience views that will make your romantic getaway even more memorable.

### Secluded accommodation

If you’re turning your romantic adventure into an overnighter, there are lots of [accommodation options](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) to help elevate your day into a loved-up mini break. From the island's newest accommodation, where you can stay lakeside at [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup), to [glamping under the stars](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) and [luxurious](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest)[hotel stays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest), there’s somewhere special waiting for you. Or, check out the [ocean view self-contained units](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained) at Stay Rottnest; these fully equipped beachfront units are the perfect setting for a romantic getaway, overlooking the tranquil Wadjemup waters.

### Relaxing massage

If your visit includes an overnight stay, choose to indulge in a world of relaxation from the comfort of your accommodation with a massage. [Mobile Massage on Rottnest Island by Golden Bees](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mobile-massage-on-rottnest-island-by-golden-bees) offers a decadent menu of treatments that allow you to unwind without leaving the comfort of your accommodation. Whether you’re after a relaxing massage or a restorative deep tissue massage, relax with a tranquil treatment together.

# The Perfect family Escape on Rottnest Island

Just a short ferry journey away, relax and reconnect with your family on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

3 minutes

Image Rottnest Island Beach

Rottnest Island Beach

**Whether you’re travelling with young children or teens, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is the perfect place to relax and reconnect with your family.**

Here are our top tips for making treasured memories on a perfect family holiday on Wadjemup.

### Ferry to the island

There are three operators running ferries to and from the island – [Rottnest Express](https://rottnestexpress.com.au/), [Rottnest Fast Ferries](https://www.rottnestfastferries.com.au/) and [SeaLink](https://www.sealinkrottnest.com.au/) – so find the departure point and timetable that suits you best. The ferry companies also offer free travel for children, so you can visit the island for less (conditions apply - check with your preferred ferry operator for details).

### Where to stay

There are so many places to stay on the island, from [budget-friendly cabins to self-catered holiday homes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained). Or enjoy an elegant stay at [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) and glamping at [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) eco-tents on the doorstep of Pinky Beach.

Image Stay Rottnest

Stay Rottnest Self-Contained Accommodation

Image 

[Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest?tab=see-do)

Image 

[Glamping at Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island?tab=see-do)

### Cycling

[Cycling is the best way to explore](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island) the island at your own pace. Cruise through open spaces, surrounded by vibrant green bush and panoramic coastal views, with birdlife soaring overhead.

Every corner reveals a new, sparkling blue ocean vista – guaranteed to put a smile on every family member’s face. You can bring your own bikes or hire them from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) on the island. You’ll also find bike trailers, e-bikes, mobility assistance options, infant bike seats and children’s bikes, so the whole family can head off on adventures together.

### Island Explorer bus

If you don’t fancy cycling, have a pram, or older family members travelling with you, take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour). This bus service circumnavigates the whole island, allowing you to hop off whenever you see something that takes your fancy and discover the further reaches of the island. Kids will love the journey, marvelling at the amazing scenery along the way.

### Snorkelling and swimming

Rottnest Island has an impressive 63 beaches and 20 bays with sparkling blue water, surrounded by protected coral reefs. [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), [Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parakeet-bay), [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay) and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) are perfect for children, with calm shallow water to play, swim or snorkel in. It’s also a good idea to chat with the team at the [Rottnest Voluntary Guides Information Booth](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-volunteer-guides-information-booth) and the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) to get advice on the best options for the day’s weather conditions.

Image Rottnest Island Beach

Snorkel at sheltered bays

Image Bike riding and quokkas at Rottnest Island

Cycle around the island

Image Quokka Coaches Bus Tour

[Explore by bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus)

### Playgrounds

Let the little ones roam free at one of the playgrounds while you enjoy a coffee. There are playgrounds on the waterfront of [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), in South Thomson Bay behind [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) and at [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery). Alternatively, visit [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) where the kids (and adults) can enjoy a round of putt or play some classic arcade games.

### Rottnest Movies

In the evenings, head to the heritage [Picture Hall](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) to watch the latest family blockbuster. Relax in retro deck chairs and visit the candy bar for fresh popcorn and homemade choc bombs. 

### Quokkas

No visit to Rottnest Island is complete without watching the resident [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) as they roam in the wild. You'll spot them across the island, and can find our [suggested locations here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island).

Quokka Safety

To help keep the unique wildlife safe and healthy, please do not touch, feed or give water to the quokkas and always observe from a respectful distance.

Image Quokka

Observe curious quokkas

Movies at the Picture Hall

Mini Golf

### School holidays

The island offers a range of activities and tours that get kids out exploring and learning about Wadjemup’s [natural environment](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/nature-wildlife) and [important history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history). The [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) holiday activity programs are published online before the start of a new school break, so check out [what’s on](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/whats-on) before planning your trip or [sign up to our newsletter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/subscribe) below to stay up to date.

# Aboriginal History

For Aboriginal people across Western Australia, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a significant place.

Image Sculpture at Wadjemup Museum

Noongar Boodja, who represents all Noongar men

Content Warning

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are advised that this content contains images and names of individuals who have passed away.

Visitors are also advised that this content contains material, including historical names and images, which relate to the island’s prison era and may be confronting and/or challenging.   
  
The Rottnest Island Authority does not endorse the language and views of the past, and sincerely apologises for any distress this content may cause.

### A tale of two histories

For Aboriginal people across Western Australia, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a significant place. Once connected to the mainland some 6,500 years ago, Wadjemup was used by the Whadjuk Noongar people for important ceremonies and meetings. After the sea levels rose Wadjemup was no longer accessible by land and there is no physical evidence that Whadjuk Noongar people visited Wadjemup after the completion of islandisation and European settlement.

Following the colonisation of Western Australia in the early 1800s, Wadjemup played an increasingly sorrowful role in Aboriginal history. European settlers established Wadjemup first as a prison, incarcerating thousands of Aboriginal boys and men from across Western Australia, then as a forced labour camp – known as the Rottnest Island Aboriginal Establishment.

### The dissolution of culture

State records indicate that 3,700 Aboriginal men and boys were imprisoned at Wadjemup between 1838 and 1931. There were children as young as eight and adults as old as 70; many were leaders, lore men and warriors, and the removal from their communities had lasting effects.

With the loss of their leaders, many Aboriginal communities across Western Australia also lost their role models, decision-makers, and cultural historians — the lore men and Elders who gave guidance and passed on important knowledge. As a result, many Aboriginal communities were forced to merge, putting untenable pressure on the remaining leaders due to tribal differences and over-stretched populations.

Many Aboriginal women found themselves as single parents, and without support from their menfolk and leaders, were forced to adopt colonial customs. Consequently, tribal protocols and cultural practices were neglected due to a lack of opportunities, guidance, and support.

Prison was a terrifying punishment for Aboriginal people. In Aboriginal society or lore, there was nothing like it, and the separation from people, land and culture had devastating effects.

### An island prison

#### The Rottnest Island Establishment

Founded in the late 1830s, the Establishment was thought by the colonial authorities to be a more progressive and humanitarian form of incarceration for Aboriginal people compared to the close confinement and cold stone environment of mainland, European-style jails.

The intention was for Aboriginal prisoners to learn ‘useful’ skills, such as farming and building and so they could more easily transition into the new colonial culture upon their release.

Over the Establishment's 93 years, numerous Aboriginal prisoners were sent to Rottnest Island for offences ranging from petty felonies to murder. Not all of these prisoners were guilty however, with many admitting to the charges in order to avoid physical brutality.

The Establishment operated through three distinct periods which were marked by temporary closures and changes in operational procedures.

Image 

Exhibit in the Wadjemup Museum of Aboriginal Prisoners on Wadjemup in 1889

### The early years

The first six Aboriginal prisoners were transferred to the Establishment in 1838, but no preparations had been made for their arrival. Due to the lack of buildings, the prisoners were forced to shelter in a since-eroded coastal cave near Bathurst Point for several nights.

Over the next 11 years, prisoners were sent to the Establishment for mostly petty crimes that included theft, sheep-spearing, threats to settlers, and tribal disputes. During this time, prisoners undertook gardening, building construction and farming on the island.

The island’s original colonial infrastructure was built by the prisoners, including the seawall, the Quod, and the Superintendent’s cottage. In 1842, the prisoners also assisted with the construction of the first lighthouse on the island – the original [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse).

Although the prisoners’ labour ensured that great progress was made in establishing infrastructure on the island, there was some concern for the prisoners’ wellbeing during this early period. 

Henry Trigg, the civil engineer working on the original Wadjemup Lighthouse, recorded in his journals the negative psychological impact of incarceration on the Aboriginal prisoners. However, Mr Trigg’s concerns were relatively insignificant when compared to the physical punishment inflicted on the prisoners at the hands of Superintendent Henry Vincent which led to the death of many prisoners through neglect or mistreatment.

In 1849, Vincent's cruelty led to the first closure of the Establishment, and most of the prisoners were returned to mainland jails.

### 

### The grim years

After reopening the Establishment in 1855, more than 3,000 prisoners were transferred onto the island.

Henry Vincent returned as Superintendent, but his ongoing harsh administration was soon the subject of several official inquiries.

Over the coming years, a fire caused significant damage to the prison which reduced its capacity. This event, along with prisoners being given longer sentences, meant that the facility soon became overcrowded and living conditions steadily worse. When influenza and measles epidemics struck in 1883, it was impossible to isolate the sick and over 60 prisoners lost their lives in one epidemic alone.

As time passed, the Establishment changed from a vision of a training institution to a bleak, unforgiving prison.

In most cases, introduced diseases caused prisoner deaths. However, the transfer of Aboriginal men from the tropical climates of the north to the cold south also contributed to sickness.

Along with the brutal living conditions, the Aboriginal prisoners were forced to undergo strenuous labour, such as turning the mill to grind flour in the building that now houses the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum). They were only fed a meagre diet of gruel that provided little in the way of nutrition or sustenance for such work and could only supplement their diet by hunting when they were permitted.

As the death toll rose, concerns around the conditions on Rottnest Island were raised in Parliament and many investigations were conducted, but the resulting recommendations were continually suppressed. It was even suggested that some prisoners had left the island in better health than when they arrived, which caused them to recommit offences in order to be returned.

Aboriginal prisoners continued living in harsh conditions with inadequate food and shelter, but it wasn’t only the physical environment that had an impact on them.

Long-term prisoners became severely depressed due to the forced displacement from their Country and community and the severed spiritual connection to the land that sustained them psychologically as well as physically.

Finally, in 1883 after more concerns were raised in Parliament, plans were put in place to shut the Establishment again, though it took until 1902 for the facility to be formally closed.

Just prior to this, Wadjemup’s only female prisoner was incarcerated on the island.

In 1894 a motion was raised in Parliament that the island should be opened to the public as a summer resort. While this was rejected, the concept eventually gained more interest in the ensuing years.

### 

### A new identity

Two years after the Establishment was closed, the Government declared Rottnest Island a penal outstation, annexed to Fremantle Prison.

A new area was set down for the prison facility, with the rest of the island opened up to tour groups and holidaymakers.

For several years, the prisoners continued to occupy the old prison (known as the Quod) but plans were soon made to relocate them due to it being allocated as future holiday accommodation.

In 1904, European prisoners arrived and in the following years there were as many as 40 prisoners on the island – about one in ten of whom were Aboriginal. The Aboriginal prisoners were assigned menial tasks such as cutting firewood, washing clothes, cleaning and tending to the livestock. In contrast, the European prisoners were given more responsibility and worked as cooks, kitchen hands, clerks, stablemen, blacksmiths and carters.

In 1917, the Rottnest Island Board of Control was appointed to manage the island. At the same time, the island was declared as a Class A Reserve for public recreation - creating a significant shift from the prison era to one of tourism and increasing general public interest in the island as a holiday destination.

By 1931, the last prisoner on Rottnest Island, an Aboriginal man by the name of Maitland Narrier, was escorted to the mainland. This marked the end of the era of the Rottnest Island Establishment.

### 

### The Burial Ground

A key reason why Wadjemup is painfully significant to Aboriginal communities today is the burial ground that is located in the settlement.

Aboriginal men and boys who died in custody were buried in unmarked graves on Wadjemup during the operation of the Rottnest Island Aboriginal Establishment.

Many of the deaths resulted from epidemics of influenza in 1883, which swept through the Establishment due to overcrowding. The lack of sanitation and nutrition, living and working in extreme weather, and physical and psychological abuse also contributed to the deaths.

After the prison closed, one of Australia's largest Aboriginal burial grounds was largely forgotten about. The island became a holiday resort and the area where the Aboriginal burial ground lay became a budget camping ground known as Tentland. 

During the earthworks for extending the sewerage scheme to the golf club in 1970, human remains were discovered. There was no public announcement of the discovery, and the remains were reburied.

Many people – especially Aboriginal people – felt that the failure to recognise the discovery of the graves was callous and disrespectful. It wasn’t until 1985 that the cemetery was recorded and protected under the *Aboriginal Heritage Act 1972*.

In 1992, the assumed cemetery area was fenced off and signs erected to inform the public of the site’s significance. Then in 1993, more bone fragments were found in the island’s main camping area about 100 metres from the known Aboriginal cemetery site. This discovery instigated a significant acknowledgement by the State Government in 1994 to recognise Wadjemup as the largest site of Aboriginal Deaths in Custody in Australia.

In 2007, Tentland officially closed to protect the graves of the Aboriginal men and boys.

In 2018, after more than a century of operating as tourist accommodation, the Quod closed its doors. This was a significant and welcome step towards recognition, reconciliation and healing for Aboriginal people.

Image 

The Settlement, Quod and Aboriginal Burial Grounds

## Steps towards reconciliation

Together with the Government of Western Australia, the [Rottnest Island Authority](https://ria.wa.gov.au/) has adopted the Innovate  Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP) 2021-2023.

The RAP aims to ensure all people can move forward together in an environment of cooperation and understanding, built upon acknowledging the past and focused on the future.  The RIA work with and consult various stakeholders to progress reconciliation.

* The Wadjemup Aboriginal Reference Group (WARG) is a Cabinet-appointed advisory group to the Rottnest Island Authority (RIA).  It was established in 2017 and their role is to advise RIA on all Aboriginal cultural matters in relation to the day-to-day functioning of the island.

* In 2020, the Government of Western Australia announced support for a new process of reconciliation and healing with Aboriginal communities across the State, led by Whadjuk Noongar people as the Traditional Owners of Wadjemup. The Wadjemup Whadjuk Cultural Authority Reference Group was established in 2021 to lead the State-wide consultation regarding the future of the Burial Ground and the Quod. The Wadjemup Project will focus on how to commemorate the Aboriginal boys and men buried on the island and the future use of the old prison building (the Quod).

* Rottnest Island Deaths Group Aboriginal Corporation (RIDGAC) formed in 1993 has raised awareness of the history of the Aboriginal prisoners, the Quod and burial ground.

* The South West Native Title Settlement is the largest native title settlement in Australian history.  The Settlement is made up of six Individual Land Use Agreements, including the Whadjuk People (Perth Metropolitan area).  The Whadjuk Regional Corporation has a Cultural Advice Committee (CAC) which is made up of Elders who consider matters relevant to culture and make decisions to promote and protect cultural interests.

# Autumn

**The arrival of autumn breathes a welcome sigh of cooling air around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. During these months, the strong summer sun softens, offering bright days that provide the perfect backdrop to all island activities.**

#### Autumn on the island

Autumn encompasses the months of March, April and May in Australia. March is the second and final month of the [Noongar season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup) of Bunuru and the first month of autumn. During this time, the hum of the island’s peak summer season is yet to dim with visitors still revelling in the mild temperatures. Come and discover a beloved bay or beach and enjoy swimming and snorkelling in the waters of Wadjemup before needing a wetsuit in the approaching cooler months. April and May welcome the Noongar season of Djeran, which brings cool nights and clear days to create a comfortable environment for you to explore without the crowds of summer.

#### Weather to expect during autumn

During autumn, the island is slightly cooler than the mainland of Perth, with average daily temperatures hovering around 21-26°C. Early autumn days are often warm with plenty of sunshine, but the mornings and evenings start to cool down and the westerly winds appear. Later in the season, morning dew drops form glistening gems on the ground, the daytime temperatures dip slightly, and the days come to a spectacular end more swiftly. Cooler conditions often make for calmer ferry rides, as well as more comfortable active experiences and increasing the likelihood of island wildlife encounters.

#### Autumn Guide and Itineraries

Looking for more inspiration? Read our guides to exploring the natural surrounds, wildlife sightings and historical experiences that are best appreciated during autumn.

### Frequently Asked Questions

Should I visit Rottnest Island in autumn?

Autumn weather offers an opportunity to comfortably explore the land and enjoy the waters of Wadjemup. The crowds start to thin after the busy summer period, but there’s still a lively energy that lingers with key events such as school holidays, the Easter long weekend and Anzac Day falling during this season. Generally, summer businesses remain open until mid to late April, making it an ideal time to experience all the activities available in summer, with fewer people around.

What is there to do on Rottnest Island in autumn?

The mild temperatures and frequent sunny days during the autumn months create the perfect setting for island adventures. A [Djeran day](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/a-djeran-day-at-rottnest-island) on the island can be spent hiking the trails of the Wadjemup Bidi, cycling to iconic lookout destinations, having a dip in the ocean and savouring delicacies from the many places to dine and drink.

It’s recommended that you pre-book your travel to the island, including meals and activities where possible, as school holidays and the Easter long weekend fall during the autumn period.

Is Rottnest Island cold in autumn?

During the autumn months of March, April and May, the island is slightly cooler than the mainland of Perth. Average maximum temperatures hover around 21–26°C, providing welcome conditions for land and water-based activities.

What is the temperature range of the water around Rottnest Island in autumn?

Coming out of the summer months, the water temperature is relatively warm during autumn, particularly during March and early April. Average water temperatures around Rottnest Island hover around 22°C during autumn, making it an enjoyable time to enjoy water-based activities.

What is the average temperature on Rottnest Island in autumn?

The average temperature over the autumn months on Rottnest Island are as follows:

* March: 18.8 – 26.2°C
* April: 17.3 – 23.8°C
* May: 15.3 – 21.2°C

As summer slips into autumn, explorers can expect the perfect blend of warm days and cooler evenings. The days continue to radiate with the sun's warmth, the waters remain inviting, and you'll find plenty of experiences on offer amidst a lively atmosphere.

What is the average monthly rainfall on Rottnest Island during autumn?

Autumn on Rottnest Island brings a gentle increase in rainfall, with a monthly average as follows:

* March: 18 mm
* April: 32.1 mm
* May: 70 mm

These light to moderate showers create a refreshing atmosphere, perfect for those who enjoy a tranquil and serene getaway in nature.

# Guides & Tips

Tips for a time well spent

## Everything you need to know for an unforgettable island experience

With a world of events, natural phenomena, and historic tales to explore, you’re probably wondering what took you so long… and where to start.

Discover insightful guides and practical tips from island experts to ignite your sense of adventure and curiosity. Or explore itineraries for every season of the year, crafted by those who know it best.

### What's Happening

Image Children and parents at the 2024 Quokka Birthday celebration.

12-13 September

Join the Little Quokka’s Big Birthday Weekend

Celebrate the wonder of nature as quokka joeys emerge on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island with a weekend program of fun workshops, activities and entertainment for the whole family.

[Register now](https://www.eventbrite.com.au/e/little-quokkas-big-birthday-weekend-tickets-1997421517528)

* [On your Doorstep](#629d5cb4-5375-48d0-b526-284154423108-1 "On your Doorstep")

**Located close to the main settlement, just a short stroll from one of the island's most famous beaches, Stay Rottnest Campground invites you back to nature to immerse yourself in the natural beauty of Rottnest Island.**

43 non-powered sand covered campsites are available, accommodating up to a maximum of six people and two tents each, along with wheelchair-accessible ablution blocks. You’ll have access to a communal camp kitchen with cooking facilities including four barbecue plates and troughs, with a further two freestanding barbecues also available.

The Stay Rottnest Campground is just a leisurely stroll from one of the widest and longest stretches of beach on the island, Pinky Beach, known for its gorgeous swimming conditions.

A boat-free bay with undulating coral reef, Pinky Beach offers safe, calm waters that are shielded from the breeze making it the ideal place for families

It’s also just a short wander back to the main settlement to grab a bite to eat and refreshments.

#### Where to find Stay Rottnest Campground

It’s just a 10-minute walk on foot, and easily accessible by bike, or by bus.

### Frequently Asked Questions

How do I book accommodation?

Stay Rottnest accommodation is available to book online via [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) or via phone on (+61) 1800 111 111 (Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm, excluding public holidays). Bookings can be made up to nine months in advance of your stay.

**Booking online**

[Booking online](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates) is the quickest and easiest way to secure Stay Rottnest accommodation and receive instant confirmation.

Special requests and notes are also able to be placed in the booking.

How do Open Days work?

Availability for bookings opens on the first working Wednesday of each calendar month, for accommodation nine months in advance.

While you can book by calling Stay Rottnest on (+61) 1800 111 111, online is the simplest and most successful way to book accommodation. As demand for bookings is high, a virtual queuing system is used to ensure a smooth experience for everyone on busy Open Days.  

**Booking for Accessibility**

If you need wheelchair accessible accommodation, please send your request after 8:30 am to [stay@rottnestisland.com](mailto:stay@rottnestisland.com) and ensure you attach a copy of your ACROD Card (front and back). These requests are processed in the order they’re received from 8:30 am onwards on Open Day, so hold your email until then. There is a limit of one booking per ACROD Card.

For more information, visit [stayrottnest.com](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates)

When are Open Days scheduled?

Open Days are held on the first Wednesday of each month, to release availability for the next booking period, nine months in advance.

Visit the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/files/pdfs/stay_rottnest_booking_guide.pdf) to see all current scheduled Open Day dates.

How many sites can you book?

A maximum of two sites can be booked in one transaction.

Each site accommodates a maximum of six people in up to two tents or four single swags (two single swags equal one tent) and each site must have one registered guest over the age of 18.

How much will it cost?

The prices of Stay Rottnest accommodation vary based on the type of accommodation chosen, the time of year and availability. To check prices for available accommodation, select your preferred dates, location and accommodation type on the [Stay Rottnest website](https://bookings.stayrottnest.com/search-rates).

Can I alter or cancel my booking?

Yes, however cancellations and modifications may incur a cancellation fee.

Further details on how to cancel or alter your booking, and applicable fees, can be found in the [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

Can I transfer my booking to someone else?

You may nominate another person as authorised to check in to the accommodation, however you will remain as the owner of the booking as the original guest. As the owner of the booking, you will be liable for any costs related to the accommodation for the duration of the booking.

You can view the full [Stay Rottnest Terms & Conditions](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_bookings_terms_and_conditions.pdf) on the Stay Rottnest website.

What time is check-in?

Check-in is from 2 pm. You can leave your mobile number at the Visitor Centre, who will text you if your accommodation is ready early.

What time is check-out?

Check-out for the Stay Rottnest Campground is 10 am.

Where can I find an accommodation map?

You can find a accommodation map of all accommodation types on the [Stay Rottnest website here](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/stay_rottnest_accommodation_maps.pdf).

Can I have my luggage delivered to the campground?

Stay Rottnest Campground guests can purchase labels from their ferry operator to have luggage delivered direct to the campground from the ferry. Prior to arrival on the island, please check with your ferry provider to ensure all luggage is labelled correctly. You will also need to ensure individual items of luggage do not exceed the 22 kg weight limit. See further information about [Luggage & Equipment](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/luggage-equipment).

When is luggage collection?

For Stay Rottnest Campground, luggage must be out for collection by 9 am for ferries departing at 10 am or later.

For ferries departing before 10 am, luggage must be out for collection by 7 am and must be pre-booked by notifying the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) 24 hours before departure.

Are fires permitted?

No, open flames are not permitted within the campground.

What happens if I’m staying overnight, and all ferries are cancelled?

If ferries are cancelled for the day of your departure, guests of Stay Rottnest accommodation will be contacted by reservations and given the option to:

* Leave the day prior and receive a refund for your unused night of accommodation, or
* If your accommodation is available for an extra day, you will be invited to stay for 50% of the rack rate.

If you do not wish to leave early, and your accommodation is not available for an extra night, nor is any alternate Stay Rottnest accommodation available, you will need to contact the [other accommodation providers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) on the island to enquire if they have availabilities.

How do I hire extra items?

If you require additional items, please complete a [Hire Items Booking Form](https://www.stayrottnest.com/cms/stayrottnest/pdfs/accommodation_hire_items_2026.pdf).

Please contact Stay Rottnest at least 48 hours prior to arrival for hire items.

### How to check in once you arrive

Once you arrive on the island, make your way to the Visitor Centre to check in.

Photo ID is required for registration by the person who made the booking.

Upon registering, you will receive a sticker to attach to your tent once it has been erected.

All tents must be situated within the area of the site booked.

# Celebrate a Little Longer: Your Ultimate Celebration Is Just a Ferry Ride Away

Whether it’s a special occasion or simply the joy of being here, there’s always a reason to celebrate on a visit to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

4 minutes

Image Friends celebrating with summery drinks at Rottnest Island

Friends celebrating at Rottnest Island

**Just a short ferry ride away, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is the ultimate destination to turn every birthday, catch-up, and date night into an extraordinary celebration.**

Special occasions deserve an escape where time slows, and every detail feels elevated. Where a humble gathering of friends turns into an unforgettable group celebration. And where meals with your other half turn into timeless memories.

Here on Wadjemup, your next island visit doesn’t call for annual leave or overnight bags. Instead, take advantage of the spring and summer [late-night return ferry](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals/stay-a-little-longer-campaign) and slip away for a blissful, unhurried day. Better still, your visit can extend long after the sun has slipped away – revealing an intimate side of the island that feels worlds apart from the everyday. Rottnest Island is closer than you think, and your next celebration is waiting.

## IMPRESS WITH A SOARING SCENIC FLIGHT

Looking for a unique couple’s celebration? Experiences make for the most unforgettable gifts of all. Rise to the occasion of a loved one’s birthday, Valentine’s Day or your anniversary, and arrive in style with [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi). As you ascend, watch as jewel-toned coastline sprawls beneath you. Shifting from sky to shore, the sense of wonder is sure to stay; you’ve set the tone for a memorable day to come.

Prefer to arrive via the ocean? You can take a scenic flight throughout the day instead, with departures also offered from the island. Lock eyes in anticipatory glee as you spend up to 35 minutes together gliding high over shimmering lakes and sparkling bays.

Image Rottnest Air-Taxi flying over the pristine lakes of the island.

Rottnest Air-Taxi over the salt lakes of Rottnest Island

Image Rottnest Air-Taxi flying over the luscious green hills of Rottnest Island.

Rottnest Air-Taxi over the hills of Rottnest Island

## SET SAIL FOR THE DAY

Mark a milestone birthday or long-awaited reunion with unforgettable flair. A luxury seafood cruise with [Rottnest Cruises](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises) holds the promise of something special for groups over four memorable hours. It all begins with a hands-on cray pot collection together; embrace the lively atmosphere that fills the deck as you cheer each other on.

excitement gives way to awe at a secluded bay where the scenery is sure to steal your breath. Here, your onboard chef serves up decadent seafood courses, including the fresh lobster you caught just hours earlier. Between courses, dip in and out of the ocean or relax onboard with free-flowing drinks. It’s an experience close enough to home to be a reality, yet far enough away from ordinary to feel like a dream.

## TOAST TO TOGETHERNESS

Over on dry land, park up with your nearest and dearest to celebrate the greatest gift of all: time together. Step across the soft sand and settle in your seats at [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) for pre-dinner drinks. Order creative cocktails or pick premium wines as crisp as the breeze on salty skin. Toast to the moment, knowing you’ve got time to soak it all in before your 9 pm ferry back home.

## SAVOUR A LAKESIDE SUNSET

You can choose from a range of locations to appreciate [sunset skies](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island) around Wadjemup, but at this restaurant, the experience is enhanced. [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest) is the only restaurant on the island with a [lake](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) view, with tables overlooking the mirrored surface of Garden Lake. So, when sunset casts its daily honeyed haze, it’s a showstopping sight.

Sip on custom cocktails and curated wines, as you watch still waters catch every brilliant hue. Then, stay long into the evening to sample the shared feasting menu in your tranquil surroundings. With the late return ferry, there’s no rush. Linger over dessert and let the evening unfold.

Celebrating at Bayside Bar

Image A couple enjoying drinks at Sunsets Rottnest.

Drinks and Sunsets Rottnest

## DISCOVER DREAMY DATE NIGHT VENUES

Stroll hand-in-hand to your dinner destination, with all that’s familiar a distant mainland memory. This is the place to embrace new flavours and create new traditions as a couple. Across the island, discover different [dining spots](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/sip--eat-and-indulge-a-little-longer-until-9-pm) and celebrate one another under the stars.

For laidback fare and beachfront dining, [HAVZA](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/havza) offers a relaxed tapas experience overlooking [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin). Raise a glass to a refreshing day out as the gentle ocean rhythms set a relaxing tempo for conversation. Stay for another round, soak in the coastal atmosphere, and share vibrant plates that blend flavours of the Aegean Sea with the best of Western Australian produce. And thanks to the 9 pm ferry, your evening doesn’t have to end early – you can celebrate at your own pace.

Alternatively, follow tantalising scents to a table overlooking [Isola Bar e Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest). This Italian beachside bar invites indulgent afternoons that echo the Amalfi Coast experience. Time stretches between the first round of spritzes and antipasti, with the real world feeling far from here. It’s the kind of place where candlelit intimate dinners for two feel inevitable.

Also, near the soft sands of Thomson Bay lies [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara): an expansive restaurant designed to take you on a culinary journey to the islands of South East Asia. While Bali may be just a short flight from Perth, its flavours are even closer at hand here. Settle in for a feast of sizzling seafood, expertly prepared and layered with fragrant spices, in a coastal setting that makes every occasion feel special.

# Protect Our Wildlife

We all play a role in ensuring that the plants and animals on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island are protected.

Image Wadjemup Daisies

Wadjemup Daisies

### Protect Our Local Wildlife

###### Respect the flora and fauna

Rottnest Island is a Class A Reserve, meaning that all the plants and animals are protected.

When you experience the island [by foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot), [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or [bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) there are ways you can respect the land and its unique natural environment. Please don’t touch or feed the wildlife, leave the island’s flora where you found it, and [contact the rangers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us) prior to arrival should you need to bring a guide, assistance, or companion animal for medical reasons.

###### Do not feed the wildlife

It is important to let all animals on the island forage for their own food and water. Feeding wildlife can cause illness and lead to aggressive behaviour, and it’s important they don’t learn to rely on humans.

###### Do not touch the wildlife

For their safety and yours, don’t touch any of the animals on the island. While quokkas are certainly curious, touching and petting them is not permitted. Touching quokkas (or any animal) can make them sick, spread disease, and even cause mothers to abandon their young if they carry an unfamiliar scent.

If you accidentally come into contact with an animal, wash the area of contact with soap and water as soon as possible to minimise the risk of infection.

###### Dispose of your rubbish

Putting your rubbish and food scraps in the bin is important to keep the island beautiful and the wildlife safe. Island animals can become aggressive or sick from eating human food or ingesting plastics and other harmful materials.

###### Ride your bikes with care

To avoid accidents with quokkas, and other wildlife such as lizards, please take care while riding and keep your eyes on the road. Stick to the paths and roads to protect the native flora and fauna. If you see a sick or injured animal or animals being mistreated, please report it immediately to the Rottnest Island rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.

###### Protecting birdlife

Australia confirmed its first case of H5 bird flu on 20 June 2026. The highly contagious strain of H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza (bird flu), has spread globally, affecting more than 560 bird species and over 100 mammalian species. Australia is closely monitoring these outbreaks and carrying out strong surveillance, testing and preparedness measures to ensure any suspected cases are detected early and responded to quickly.

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a critical location for this monitoring, due to the combined factors of:

* Migratory birds;
* Diverse bird populations; and,
* Capacity for active surveillance.

**How you can help**

Bird flu is a notifiable animal disease which means if you suspect it, you must report it even if you’re unsure.

Following these actions can protect birdlife and prevent the spread of the disease:

**Avoid** sick and dead birds;

**Record**by taking photos and recording the location; and,

**Report** signs of sick or dead birds to the **Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888**.

Learn more about how you can assist with surveillance at [wa.gov.au](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/department-of-primary-industries-and-regional-development/avian-influenza).

[How to report](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/department-of-primary-industries-and-regional-development/avian-influenza-signs-and-how-report)

### A note from Rottnest Island Authority

Remember, anyone who deliberately interferes with (including feeding) wildlife on Rottnest Island will be fined on the spot under the *Rottnest Island Regulations* 1988 and potentially prosecuted under the *Biodiversity**Conservation Act* 2016 and the *Biodiversity Conservation Regulations* 2018 with fines up to $10,000. Acts of animal cruelty may result in fines up to $300,000 and 5 years imprisonment under the Animal Welfare Act 2002.

[Quokkas](/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)

### Become a quokka conservation hero

You can show your support for Rottnest Island’s famous furry inhabitants by purchasing one of [Rottnest Foundation](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/)’s adoption kits that fund conservation initiatives on the island.​

Your kit comes with a cuddly, life-sized soft quokka toy, tote bag, quokka fact sheet and an official adoption certificate.

[Learn more about the Adopt-a-Quokka Kits](https://www.rottnestfoundation.org.au/shop/p/adopt-a-quokka)

# Beaches & Water Activities

## The waters that surround the island are often described as glass, crystal… unforgettable

A sea this clear is not just an invitation; it draws you into an aquatic world where life thrives beneath the surface. Curious stingrays move with the rhythm of gentle waves, schools of tropical fish weave through the warm waters, and marine gardens flourish in the shelter of underwater sanctuaries.

With countless [beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches), it is easy to find a secluded spot. Quiet coves invite long swims and moments of stillness, while soft sandy shorelines offer some of the most unforgettable beach and water activities, whether you arrive with friends, family or simply on your own.

The Indian Ocean shapes every experience here. A tropical current carries snorkellers over coral at [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point), plays with swimmers at [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) and stretches endlessly beyond the boardwalk at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). It is this same ocean that defines many of Perth’s coastal experiences, making a visit to Rottnest Island a natural extension of beach and water activities near Perth.

Exploring [by boat](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/boating) or joining a [water based tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/set-sail-with-rottnest-island-s-ultimate-water-adventures), you feel like a small part of something much bigger, carried by the openness of the ocean and the life beneath the surface. Whether you are swimming, [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving), [surfing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) or setting out on the water, these beach and water activities offer unforgettable ways to connect with the island.

## Beach and water activities on Rottnest Island

### Swimming and snorkelling in calm bays

Discover beach and water activities shaped by sheltered bays, warm waters and marine life beneath the surface. From long swims to quiet snorkelling moments, the island offers memorable ways to slow down and experience the ocean.

### Diving, shipwrecks and life beneath the surface

Diving and snorkelling reveal reefs, sea life and historic shipwrecks in the surrounding waters. These underwater experiences invite you to look closer and discover another side of the island.

### Surfing, tours and ocean experiences

From surfing and swimming to exploring by boat or joining a water based tour, there are ocean activities for every pace and perspective. Whether you are seeking stillness or adventure, the coastline opens up new ways to experience the water.

### Whale watching and seasonal water activities

Seasonal experiences add even more to explore, with whale watching offering a memorable way to witness the movement and scale of the ocean. At different times of year, the waters around the island reveal something new.

### Tips for a time well spent

Make your visit even more meaningful with helpful advice from those in the know.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What are the best beach activities to do on Rottnest Island?

Rottnest Island is perfect for beach adventures; you can swim in calm turquoise bays, snorkel vibrant reefs, or simply relax on the sand. Many visitors also enjoy paddleboarding and beach cricket, with equipment available to hire through [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire).

Where to swim at Rottnest Island?

With 63 beaches and 20 bays to discover, there’s always somewhere new to swim on Rottnest Island. Whether you are looking for a popular beach close to the main settlement or a quieter bay to linger a little longer, the island’s [beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) offer plenty of choice. For some of the best snorkelling, head to the [Parker Point Snorkel Trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail).

What should I pack for a beach day?

A beach day on Rottnest Island usually calls for swimmers, a towel, sun protection, water and any snorkel or beach gear you plan to use. If you are heading to a quieter bay, it also helps to pack snacks and anything else you may want for a longer stay by the water.

Is Rottnest Island good for beach fishing?

Western Australia is home to some of the best beach fishing in Australia, and [Rottnest Island beaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) are a standout for visitors looking to combine coastal scenery with great fishing opportunities. Surrounded by reef and rich marine life, the island offers a mix of beach, jetty and boat-based options, with plenty of spots to suit different experience levels. Get all the tips and insights about [fishing on Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing).

# By Air

When you travel by air you experience Wadjemup / Rottnest Island from a whole different perspective.

Image Aerial view over the island

Aerial view over the island

### 

## Soaring high above

Travel to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island by air and you'll enjoy breathtaking views of the island.

Fly return, opt to start your adventure with a scenic flight before catching the ferry back, or cap off your day with a flight over the island before returning to Perth.

Whether you’re travelling by plane, helicopter or seaplane, you can take to the skies for an unforgettable experience as you see Wadjemup / Rottnest Island from a different perspective.

Image Rottnest Air Taxi

[Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/rottnest-air-taxi?tab=see-do)

Image 

[Swan River Seaplanes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/swan-river-seaplanes)

Image 

All aboard

Image A small aircraft landing at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island Airport.

Coming in to land
