[Rottnest Air-Taxi](/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi)

### Rottnest Air-Taxi

Take to the sky with Rottnest Air-Taxi for the thrill and enjoyment people have been experiencing for more than 25 years.

Offering a range of daily departure times for maximum flexibility, you can elevate your experience ever more by adding scenic detours over the Perth beaches to the city centre, Optus Stadium, the Swan River, Fremantle and Rottnest Island itself.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi)

Image 

[Swan River Seaplanes](/see-do/hire/swan-river-seaplanes)

### Swan River Seaplanes

Experience a thrilling water departure followed by spectacular views as you travel to the island in a Swan River Seaplane.

With a journey time of 20 minutes, catching a seaplane to the island is a swift and exhilarating way to get your adventure off to a sensational start. Flights depart on a seasonal schedule from the Perth foreshore.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/swan-river-seaplanes)

Image Corsaire-Aviation-crown

[Corsaire Aviation](/see-do/hire/corsaire-aviation)

### Corsaire Aviation

Corsaire Aviation offers the unique opportunity to observe the magnificence of the island from all angles with an unforgettable helicopter transfer.

Sit back and relax as you take in spectacular scenes of jagged reefs, breathtaking bays and salt lakes that make this island unique. With a short travel time, you can enjoy extended exploration of Wadjemup, including a leisurely lunch at one of the many tantalising restaurants.

Flights are available daily to the island, departing from Jandakot Airport, Crown Towers, Fremantle and Hillarys Boat Harbour.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/corsaire-aviation)

Image Air Charters West

[Air Charters West](/see-do/hire/air-charters-west)

### Air Charters West

Soar over to Rottnest Island in style with a private charter flight from Air Charters West.

Specialising in private charter services to the island from Bunbury Airport, you can turn the drive to Perth into a dazzling panoramic display of the land and waters between Bunbury and Wadjemup. Flights are available for groups.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/air-charters-west)

# City of York Bay

## A place to reflect over the waves

A quiet, secluded bay on the northwest coast of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, City of York bay sits in an embrace between [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach) and Catherine Bay.

The bay is named after the ill-fated *City of York* iron ship, which sank off the coast of Wadjemup in 1899. The ship’s large iron anchor was recovered and now sits in remembrance near the main jetty at [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

Despite the tragedy that unfolded offshore, the beach itself is calm and relaxing. A great picnic spot, there’s a canopy of trees just off the beach providing shade from the Western Australian sun. Families can enjoy lounging by the beach, or watching [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) nearby — but be sure to let them enjoy their fun, without getting too close.

Up through the dunes, the [Karlinyah Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/karlinyah-bidi) winds its way past City of York Bay, making it a beautiful spot to stop and take a breather. And with good reason, as the section of the Karlinyah Bidi between City of York Bay and Ricey Beach is some of the more rugged terrain found on the walk.

### You might see...

Image 

Calm blue water

Image 

Resident quokkas

Image 

Osprey stacks

Image 

Stop by on the Karlinyah Bidi

### Where to find City of York Bay

City of York Bay is accessible  [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike), just a 20-minute ride through the centre of the island, or around the northern coast. You can also get there on the  [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), hopping off at Stop 16.

Image 

[Wildlife](/see-do/wildlife-nature)

### Exploring the skies of Wadjemup

One of the notable sights of City of York Bay is the resident yoondoordoo / eastern osprey population. There are at least six ospreys that call the island home, with anywhere from two to six breeding pairs living on Wadjemup. This number swells to 20 during breeding season, as ospreys from all around the state come home to roost.

City of York Bay is one of the 14 nesting sites around the island. You’ll find the osprey’s home, known as a stack, built up off the ground. Made from sticks and debris, they’re carefully woven together to form high piles - which, for a bird of their size, can get surprisingly large. Some stacks have measured several metres across and more than one metre from bottom to lip.

They’re such a beautiful, graceful bird, so be sure to give them the space and distance they need to enjoy their home in peace. Disturbing the osprey by approaching them or their nest, especially during breeding season, can lead to them abandoning their nest.

Image City of York Bay

Sunset at City of York Bay

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are available at City of York Bay?

Public toilets are available just off the beach.

Is fishing allowed?

Yes, hand line, reel, and rod fishing is allowed off the beach—but no spearfishing or netting.

Are the yoondoordoo/eastern osprey endangered?

While the yoondoordoo aren’t endangered, they are quite sensitive. Getting too close can startle them, causing them to leave the island—and never come back. So please keep your distance, and give them the space and respect to make their homes in peace.

# A Day Trip to Rottnest Island

Stunning turquoise beaches, iconic quokkas, and scenic cycling – this is your perfect one-day itinerary on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

6 minutes

Image Beaches and bays

Beaches and bays

**Just a short ferry ride away from Perth and with an abundance of activities from cycling to snorkelling, and exploring history, there’s something for everyone to experience in as little as a day on Rottnest Island.**

This day trip connects you with the best of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or [by bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus). You’ll visit some of the island’s most picturesque beaches, snorkel or swim in turquoise waters, take in the views from [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) and [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), and spot resident [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) along the way.

### 7 am All aboard the ferry

With just one day to explore, set your alarm early and hop on the first ferry you can. There are [three operators](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry) running ferries to and from the island – [Rottnest Express](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-express), [Rottnest Fast Ferries](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-fast-ferries), and [SeaLink](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sealink-rottnest) – so find the departure point and timetable that suits you best. Be sure to book the latest return too, so you have plenty of time to soak up the Rottnest Island day trip experience. Departing from Hillarys, Perth, or Fremantle, your adventure starts on the ferry. Watch the coastline stretch out behind you and keep your eyes peeled for marine life like dolphins, seals, and even [whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) from August to December.

### 8:30 am Getting ready to adventure

The ferry arrives into [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), where you’ll find cafes, shops and transport options. Take a moment to pause at the commanding sculpture at the island end of the main jetty, Koora-Yeye-Boordawan-Kalyakoorl (Past-Present-Future-Forever), which explains the [significance of the island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history) to the Whadjuk Noongar people.

Head over to [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) to collect your bike and any extra equipment like a snorkel set. Fo even more convenience, [Rottnest Rentals](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-rentals) offers beach essentials such as umbrellas, chairs, and other gear to make your day by the water easy. If you’re not cycling, head to the ticket booth at the main bus stop to get your [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) bus pass. This hop-on-hop-off service circumnavigates the island giving you the freedom to explore as you please.
Alternatively, if you like the idea of cycling but don’t want to commit, try the bike and bus package with [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire). You can cycle as far as you like and once you’ve had enough, just leave your bike in one of the racks and take the bus for the rest of the journey.

If you’re planning on having lunch at one of the beautiful [bays and beaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches) around the island, either get something from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) or grab a takeaway from one of the [many cafes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink) and pop it in your bag for later. Be sure to fill up your water bottle before you leave the settlement as well. There are limited water points once you’ve left [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).

### 10 am Time to explore

Starting out, head south towards Kingstown Barracks and some of the most picturesque beaches on the island. [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) is a perfect location to admire the gorgeous view, take a walk on the sand or hop in the water for a refreshing swim. On route to
Parker Point, [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) is home to a stunning coral reef and an intriguing
[shipwreck](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/shipwrecks), surrounded by seagrass that plays home to an array of diverse sea
life.

After this stop, it’s time to head to [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) in the centre of the island. Constructed in 1896 and standing at approximately 38 metres, this landmark is the fourth tallest lighthouse in Australia. Admire the breathtaking views of sparkling water and Perth City in the distance. On a clear day you can even make out the pine trees that line the coast at Cottesloe. For an even more memorable experience, [join a guided tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour) with the Rottnest Voluntary Guides and climb the spiral staircase to the top for panoramic views across the island.

Take your time to explore the other [buildings in the precinct](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/explore-rottnest-island-s-historical-military-attractions) — the Signal Station, the Battery Observation Post and the Women’s Royal Australian Navy Service House — all linked by self-guided interpretive signage.

Continue along the southern side of the island past Green Island and Mary Cove. As you move to the western most part of the island, you’ll notice the landscape looking more rugged and wild.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

### 1 pm Rest and refuel

Stopping off at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), it’s time for a pause; take a deep breath and soak up the salty atmosphere at this special part of the island. The alluring Indian Ocean shimmers and stretches before you, all the way to Madagascar.

There are viewing platforms at Cathedral Rocks and Cape Vlamingh where you can watch the long-nosed fur seals gently frolicking in the water, or observe the majestic osprey in its nest. You’ve probably built up an appetite by now, so take a break, soak up the views and refuel, in mind and body. [Lexi’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lexi-s-on-rotto) is close to hand, providing extra drinks and snacks to energise you for the afternoon.

### 2:30 pm Beaches and lakes

The northern side of the island is a feast for the eyes, whether seen by bike or bus. This spectacular stretch is dotted with more beautiful beaches and snorkelling spots. Take your pick from [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach), [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay), or [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) for an afternoon on the beach. [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-geordie-bay) is also home to a [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store),  [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery), and [Kuld Creamery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/kuld-creamery), so it’s a great place to stop for afternoon refreshments.

Stop off to visit the unique [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) on the island’s interior, meandering through the colourful lakes and native Wadjemup bush. You can walk part of the [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi) (a 9.5 km loop) from [Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parakeet-bay) or [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay). Or, if you’re on a bicycle, you can ride down Defence Road to the boardwalk at Lake Vincent. These wetlands are a [haven for birdlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching) too, so look out for banded stilts, crested terns, and red-capped plovers on Lake Herschel and Lake Baghdad.

The bus will head back to the main settlement, but those cycling can continue to stay on the coastal track, rounding the corner to see [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin). With its shallow clear waters and protective reef, this is an ideal spot for a final swim or snorkel. Continue towards [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) and then walk up to [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) for some impressive views over the ocean, reflecting on your adventurous day trip.

As the afternoon fades, keep an eye out for quokkas. These creatures are an unmissable sight on the island and are easier to spot when they become more active as the heat of the day fades.

Quokkas

Remember quokkas are wild animals and you are visiting their home, so rather than approach, simply observe them from a respectable distance.

### 5 pm A relaxed evening

Make the most of your Rottnest Island adventure by extending your day into the evening. With seasonal [late-night ferry services](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry), there’s no need to rush. You can linger longer, enjoy a relaxed dinner and watch the sun dip below the horizon.

There’s no better pairing for a day of exploring than a celebratory drink and delicious meal at one of the island’s [bars or restaurants](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink). From pub classics like pizzas and fish and chips to freshly made pasta and shareable tapas, there’s something to suit every taste.

As twilight approaches, let the sunset take over. Watch the sky transform into shades of gold and pink from Thomson Bay, or wander to [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) for a breathtaking view behind the iconic [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse). When it’s time to leave, simply head back to the main jetty 15 minutes before your ferry departs, farewelling Wadjemup with memories that will last a lifetime.

* 10 Unmissable Activities To Enjoy In Winter On Rottnest Island

# 10 Unmissable Activities to Enjoy in Winter on Rottnest Island

This is your guide to experiencing the island when the weather cools down, but your adventurous spirit doesn’t.

5 minutes

Image Take in the views

Take in the views

**When the mercury dips and others escape indoors, embrace an invitation for adventure.**

[Winter on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) sees the island burst into life, with muted summer hues replaced by bright bushland and jewel-toned seas. The land stirs with wildlife and the endless potential for connection.

When you step off the ferry, there’s a familiarity that washes over you. The bold blue hues of Thomson Bay; soft whispers of salt in the air; the anticipation of all that awaits… But in winter, there’s a newfound sense of adventure afoot – no matter how many times you and your fellow companions have visited the island.

Let the following list of unmissable Rottnest Island winter activities help navigate your upcoming visit, but don’t be afraid to craft your own experiences along the way. This is your journey… let curiosity be your guide.

### 1. Cycle around the island

The responsibilities of daily life are left on the mainland, just like your usual mode of transport. With minimal cars around, stretches of quiet open road invite leisurely cycling explorations. During winter, take the opportunity to go further afield. Cooler temperatures increase stamina and allow for longer journeys – like to the wild and unmissable [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). If you'd prefer a less strenuous way to embrace the peaks and valleys, join one of [Paul's Eco E-bike tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours).

Every day presents a picturesque backdrop, whether the sun dazzles overhead or clouds form a blanket above. Coast around on clear, cool days for deep blue ocean views and frequent flashes of the flourishing native bushland around you. When the sun hides away, dappled skies enhance the rich shades of the surrounding Indian Ocean, and bring enjoyable rides scented with freshly dampened vegetation.

### 2. Witness migrating whales

If the question “is Rottnest Island worth visiting in winter?” has ever passed your lips, it’s sure to be silenced upon witnessing the seasonal spectacle of migrating whales. Every winter, majestic [maamoong (whales)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) migrate along the Western Australian coastline, pausing at the sheltering waters of Wadjemup to rest along the journey.

Whale watching can take place as early as June, with migration season in full force from August to December. During this time, a trek out to Cape Vlamingh or Cathedral Rocks viewing platforms may offer more than just an invigorating hike. You and your crew could witness the unforgettable mighty movements of these deep-sea creatures, as flipping bodies outline the horizon.

Image A whale's tail from the side with Rottnest Island in the background-54.tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=5f4fe164_1)

[Whales spotted swimming past Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching)

Image

[Whale sightings](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching)

### 3. Hike the Wadjemup Bidi

Five unique adventures await on the trails of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-wonders-along-the-wadjemup-bidi); each trail section threads a corner of the island, bursting with winter flora and fauna. This special season presents the opportunity to wander as far as you like, without the sun slowing you down.

[The Hike Collective](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective) offers guided tours of each trail, with the Lakes & Bays hike taking you on a trek past pink-tinted [kabikarning (salt lakes)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes), historic landmarks, and windblown coastal headlands – a seasonal delight. Or, gather your own group for a self-guided walk, using [Smartreka](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/smartreka-digital-maps) as your digital navigation companion. Reconnect with one another as you meander mindfully, pausing along the way to take it all in.

### 4. Marvel at historic buildings

When rain clouds loom, look to the heritage buildings of Wadjemup. Here, stories of the past are grounded by tangible pieces of history. Start with a grounding experience at [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum). As you step into the Old Mill and Hay Store building, you can feel the presence of a complex and meaningful history.

Just a short [bus ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) or [cycle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) into the centre of island, [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) stands tall. Feel the warmth build in your muscles with every satisfying step up the 38-metre structure. At the top, let cool air slow your breath and appreciate a new perspective of Perth’s skyline, distorted by distance and the shimmering ocean in between. Closer to sea level, iconic landmarks including Signal Station, Battery Observation Post, and the Women’s Royal Australian Navy Service House lie at the base of Wadjemup Hill. Follow the self-guided interpretive signage that tells stories of the past.

Image Wadjemup Lighthouse

[Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse)

Image

### 5. Sit, sip and eat!

Celebrate your efforts in coordinating a successful group getaway with island dining. Eating hearty meals and toasting with local tipples (preferably by a roaring fireplace) is all part of the winter experience. Wadjemup has plenty of [cosy venues](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-warmers--where-to-eat-and-drink-on-the-island) open during winter to indulge your senses, or to simply pop in for a quick, tasty bite before resuming your adventures. There are also takeaway spots to fuel hiking or cycling journeys on the go.

### 6. Appreciate the native wildlife

During the cooler months, there’s a stillness that is hard to replicate at any other time. You feel it and the wildlife feels it too. Native creatures are often observed nesting, emerging for the first time, and migrating through ocean waters. It’s as if this special time on the island has been purpose-designed for a memorable [wildlife experience](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/uniquely-winter-wildlife-experiences-on-wadjemup). Watch multiple [bird species](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching) glide across the water, encounter bats fly silently overhead, and witness mother [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) carrying their babies in their pouches.

### 7. Catch a winter wave

Become salt-crusted creatures for the weekend with the [surf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) (mostly) all to yourselves. Stay overnight and wake up to an empty beach for your first surf at Wadjemup. Paddle out, turn your faces to the slowly emerging sun and let the sunrise glow distract you from the cool water immersion.

At [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay), swells come from various directions and light up different sections of the reef — so there are good waves guaranteed. Other Wadjemup surf breaks include [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), Stark Bay, and Chicken Reef. You can hire surfboard racks for your bike from [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) and you can transport surfboards over on the ferry.

### 8. Snorkel and dive in pristine waters

With summer crowds long gone, winter unveils a calmer, more intimate underwater experience on Wadjemup. Clear days delivers ideal [snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-snorkelling-the-warm-waters-of-wadjemup) conditions in the island's protected bays where you'll often share the water only with its marine inhabitants.

The Leeuwin Current carries warmer tropical waters south from the Kimberly, making a wetsuit-clad snorkel comfortable and rewarding. Settle into sheltered spots like [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay) or [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), to enjoy excellent visibility and gentle conditions.

For those keen to explore further, Wadjemup is known for its [underwater landscapes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving), from seagrass meadows and colourful corals to schools of tropical fish and historic shipwrecks like Denton Holme, resting just below the surface.

### 9. Take a refreshing plunge

A pleasantly surprising fact for most island visitors: [winter here](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) is actually a few degrees warmer than the mainland of Perth. In fact, average land and sea temperatures are similar during the cooler months. When the sun’s out to play, test the bounds of your comfort zone on a cool-plunge adventure that awakens your winter self. You've carved out time to be here, why not fully immerse yourself in all that the island offers.

For inspiration on how to fit these uniquely winter activities into your island itinerary, [check out this guide](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/embrace-the-unexpected-with-an-ocean-adventure-this-winter) to two action-packed island days. Featuring fresh coastal walks, ideas for hearty fuel and tips for finding the best swell, ensuring every moment brims with adventure.

### 10. Play pickleball by the coast

The cooler days of winter on Wadjemup provide ideal conditions for a social game of pickleball. Located near Bathurst Point with scenic views towards [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse), the courts offer a refreshing mix of coastal air and friendly competition.

Start the day with a morning match or unwind after a round at the nearby Rottnest Island Golf Course. [Rotto Rackets Sports](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rotto-rackets-sports) offers casual court hire, coaching and equipment rental, making it easy to get straight into the game.

# By Bike

Travel under your own steam exploring the island via a network of roads and bike paths. With the ability to stop wherever (and whenever) you please, the cycling experience on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island lets you appreciate every moment.

Image 

Cycling

### A fun, environmentally friendly way to explore the island

Cycling on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is more than a mode of transport, it’s a way of life. As a vehicle-restricted island, people love the switch from petrol to pedal power, enjoying a slowed down pace that’s not only good for their health but also the environment.

Ideal for young children and families, experience that childlike joy and nostalgia as your own memories from your younger days start to return as you explore.

Whether you bring your own wheels or hire a bike once you've arrived, you can pedal to every corner of the island or cruise along on an electric bike, enjoying stunning views and that salty sea air.

Caution: Train in Operation

A train is active on the island. Pedestrians and cyclists, please be cautious, look both ways at railway crossings and keep off the tracks.

Image See the island sights with ease on an electric bike tour at Geordie Bay.

[Paul's Eco E-Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours?tab=see-do)

Image 

Explore by bike

Image 

[Laura the Explorer Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/laura-the-explorer-bike-tours)

Image 

[Pedal & Flipper Hire](/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire)

### Where to hire bikes

[Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) are the island’s hire specialists with an expansive fleet of bikes available including step-through and cross-bar bikes, electric bikes and a large selection of kids’ bikes.

In addition to the large range of bikes and equipment, they provide helmets (which are required by law), locks, island information and cycling advice. The team is trained to personally fit customers to bikes to ensure optimal comfort and safety.

You can also hire a bike from your [ferry provider](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry) or opt for a guided tour on wheels with [Paul’s Eco E Bike Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours).

Image Cycling

Cycling

### Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to bike around Rottnest Island?

There are more than 22 km of cycle paths across the island, with routes for every ability.

The Rotto Mini Loop takes just 30 minutes, weaving through the Wadjemup bushland to The Basin, past Longreach and Geordie Bay. The 10 km Beaches, Lighthouses, and Lakes trail takes between 1.5 to 3 hours, plus however long you want to spend lazing and swimming at the expansive beaches. The full 22 km island loop takes anywhere from three to five hours, varying by how many stops you make along the way.

You can find more information about the trail in our [guide to cycling on Rottnest Island her](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island)e, as well as shorter options if you don’t have enough time – or energy – for the entire loop.

Is it hard to cycle around Rottnest Island?

With few vehicles and many cycle paths that weave throughout Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, cycling is one of the best ways to get around. There are cycling routes for every level on the island, offering uninterrupted views as you ride from lakes to beaches and bays, with the added freedom of being able to stop wherever and whenever you please.

Cycling between the Thomson Bay and Geordie Bay settlements is quick and easy, but the full 22 km island cycle loop is suited for experienced bike riders. There are also some challenging hills in places. If you’d like to make it a little easier, opt for a shorter trail such as the Rotto Mini Loop, or you can always [hire an electric bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) or bring your own.

What should I do if bikes are fully booked?

Pedal & Flipper Hire has one of the largest fleets of hire bikes in the southern hemisphere. Bikes are also available to hire directly through your ferry operator. However, in peak season, there can be occasions where bikes are fully booked. For this reason, we recommend reserving your bikes as early as possible before you arrive.

If you are unable to secure a hire bike, you can choose to bring your own with you on the ferry. Freight charges and conditions may apply so it is best to contact your chosen ferry operator directly for more information.

There are great alternative ways to explore the island too. The [Quokka Coaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) Island Explorer hop-on hop-off bus service is a flexible option allowing you to venture around at your own pace. Or you can opt for one of the guided bus tours from Quokka Coaches or the [Rottnest Express Discovery Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour). An accommodation shuttle is also available to all visitors, allowing easy travel between the Thomson Bay and Geordie Bay settlements. You may also like to book a [private transfer with Quokka Hopper](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-private-transfer), or simply [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) – there are a number of experiences within easy walking distance from the main settlement.

Do I need to wear a bicycle helmet?

Yes, bicycle helmets are required by law; these are supplied with all equipment hired.

Can I bring my own bike over to the island?

Yes, you can certainly bring your own bike to Rottnest Island.

To bring your bike with you by ferry, simply add bike freight to your ticket when booking.

Can I bring my personal bike, electric bicycle or an electric rideable device to the island?

Electric bicycles and electric rideables (e-rideables) are permitted on the island  in accordance with the requirements of the [Road Traffic Code 2000](https://www.legislation.wa.gov.au/legislation/statutes.nsf/main_mrtitle_2007_homepage.html). If you wish to bring an electric bicycle or e-rideable to the island, please ensure that your device is compliant. For more information, please visit the [Road Safety Commission website](https://www.wa.gov.au/organisation/road-safety-commission).

To bring your device with you by ferry, simply add bike freight to your ticket when booking.

How old do I have to be to hire a bike?

The person signing the hire agreement must be 18 years of age or over.

For full terms and conditions of hire, please check with your [ferry provider](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-here/by-ferry) or [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire).

# Henrietta Rocks

## Stunning scenery above and below the waves

Just a short [bus ride](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) away from the main settlement, Henrietta Rocks is a spectacular spot for Wadjemup / Rottnest Island explorers, offering both long, lazy days at the beach and hidden adventures below the waves.

Surrounded by rocky and rugged coastline, the crisp white beach sand gives way to clear blue water. Further up on the hill, beachgoers and [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) trail walkers are treated to expansive views out over Porpoise Bay.

The beautiful water hides an even more stunning coral reef and an intriguing shipwreck, surrounded by seagrass that plays home to an array of diverse sea life.

So grab your snorkel and your fins, and discover one of Wadjemup’s premier underwater playgrounds.

### Where to find Henrietta Rocks

### 

Henrietta Rocks is located on the south-east corner of Wadjemup. While the fastest way to get there is to hop on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer Bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), it’s less than half an hour’s [walk](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) away from the main settlement.

Alternatively, you can hire a [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) and take the easy ride from [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) that wends its way around the island and along the coast.

Image Wreck of Shark

Wreck of Shark

Image Wreck of Shark, Henrietta Rocks

[Snorkelling & Diving](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Discover the wreck of Shark

Henrietta Rocks is one of the more quiet snorkelling spots, and a true hidden treasure of the Wadjemup beaches. And it’s not just what’s above the surface that makes it so special…

Located just 50 metres offshore is the [historic wreck](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/shipwrecks) of Shark. A hopper barge that broke free from its mooring in Fremantle in 1938, it drifted across the channel to its current location, where it ran aground on the reef and slowly sank.

It’s been lying submerged under the tranquil waters ever since, providing an underwater playground for Wadjemup’s famous sea life — and an exciting experience for both new and seasoned snorkellers and divers alike.

[Learn more about Snorkelling & Diving](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

[Safety in the Water

To have the safest experience, always check the weather and tidal conditions before snorkelling and be aware of your abilities in the water.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are near Henrietta Rocks?

Henrietta Rocks is quite secluded, so there are no established facilities nearby. The closest public facilities are at either Army Groyne or Little Salmon Bay.

What is the best way to get there?

Jump on the Quokka Coaches Island Explorer Bus and get off at Stop 3. Alternatively, it’s less than half an hour’s walk or a short cycle away from the main settlement.

Are there accessible facilities at Henrietta Rocks?

There are no facilities at Henrietta Rocks and, at present, no accessible entry to the beach.

# Fall in Love with the Beaches of Rottnest Island

From popular beaches to quiet coves, you are guaranteed to find a favourite spot on Wadjemup.

4 minutes

Image The Basin

The Basin

**Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is home to 63 spectacular beaches and 20 beautiful bays, each one with its own special charm. From wide, stretching expanses of white sand to quiet, private coves, you will find your dream beach on Rottnest Island.**

Here’s just a few of our favourites:

Go Clockwise

We recommend exploring the island in a clockwise direction as usually the southern beaches are the most sheltered from wind in the morning, while the northern coast is preferable in the afternoon. This is also the direction of the Island Explorer bus.

### Thomson Bay

***Access by bike or walking***

[Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) is where your ferry arrives on the island, giving you a first glimpse of a Rottnest Island beach. This long, sandy beach runs along the front of the restaurants and accommodation, so it's the perfect spot to enjoy a coffee or let the kids have a run around before lunch. Keep your eyes on the water - green turtles and friendly stingrays can be spotted in the shallows here thanks to the tropical Leeuwin Current.

### Henrietta Rocks

***Access by bike, the Ngank Yira Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

[Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) is an interesting beach for explorers. The lookout point offers expansive views across the ocean and if you look closely, you can see the wreck of the barge *Shark* under the surface of the water. Head down the steps and enjoy fine white sand and rugged outcrops hugging the coastline, before snorkelling over the wreck just a short distance from the shore.

### Parker Point

***Access by bike, the Wardan Nara Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

With its iconic staircase and clear turquoise waters, [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) is always a favourite with visitors. The moored boats inspire picture-perfect views across the water, and it’s a popular place to take a refreshing dip or swim along the [self-guided snorkel trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail) to see the beauty of the marine sanctuary here up close.

### Strickland Bay

***Access by bike, the Wardan Nara Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

If you’re chasing a [blue water high](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) on Wadjemup, [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay) is a popular spot, even visited by world surf league champions! Strickland Bay curves along the south side of the narrow neck (the isthmus) of Rottnest Island, providing space to stretch out and [enjoy the surf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing). If you’re catching [the bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), disembark at stop 10 and walk ten minutes down the sandy track.

### Rocky Bay

***Access by bike, the Karlinyah Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

This beach is located on the northern side of the narrow isthmus (or neck) that connects the two ends of Rottnest Island. Looking a little different to other beaches on the island, [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay) features sweeping sand dunes. If you’re using the [Island Explorer Bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour), hop off at Narrow Neck (stop 13) and walk down the Rocky Bay beach access path.

### Ricey Beach

***Access by bike, the Karlinyah Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

[Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach) is a secluded gem, with calm, shimmering waters. This beach is normally a little quieter as it’s further from the Thomson Bay settlement, so you’re bound to find a sandy spot just for you.

### Little Armstrong Bay

***Access by bike, the Karlinyah Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

If you want to enjoy some of the island’s best snorkelling, head to [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay). The surrounding [marine sanctuary zone](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones) and rocky outcrops are home to sea life you won’t find anywhere else along the island’s coastline – think large schooling fish and a maze of reefs and seagrasses.

### Little Parakeet Bay

***Access by bike, the Gabbi Karniny Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

[Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay) is easily accessible from Geordie Bay. It’s usually sheltered, with still, glassy water that’s perfect for snorkelling. A popular choice with visitors, this small cove is a firm favourite for the afternoons.

### Geordie Bay

***Access by bike, the Gabbi Karniny Bidi hiking trail, or Island Explorer bus***

[Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) has one of the largest and most popular sandy beaches on the island. A number of holiday units are located here, which have unrivalled views overlooking the ocean. Geordie Bay also has a [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store) and the [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery), so you can grab supplies for a picnic or enjoy a meal.

### The Basin

***Access by bike or walking***

[The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) is close to the main settlement and an iconic location on Rottnest Island. This is a great place for kids or beginners learning to snorkel, with easy access to the natural swimming bowl or “basin”. Seagrass attracts a variety of sea life, so look out for fish and crustaceans.

### Pinky Beach

***Access by bike or walking***

[Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) is a local favourite, offering sheltered sandy stretches and an inviting blue lagoon. Close to the main settlement, it’s usually busy on warm summer days, but it’s easy to see why visitors love this beach. Look up and you’ll also see the iconic [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) towering over you.

# A Traditional Owner's Guide to Wadjemup

Become immersed in the island’s Aboriginal culture and history.

3 minutes

Image Lake view

Lake view

**If you’re looking for a truly insightful journey into Wadjemup’s Aboriginal heritage, a [Go Cultural tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) with Walter McGuire is a must-do during a visit to the island.**

Walter is a respected Noongar man around Whadjuk Country (Perth), and a descendant of several Aboriginal tribal clans of Western Australia’s South West region.

Now a Traditional Owner of Noongar Boodja (Noongar land), Walter’s childhood involved being educated in Noongar culture, language and customs, so he’s passionate about sharing his culture to ensure ongoing understanding and appreciation of [Aboriginal heritage](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history).

“Cultural heritage is in all of us,” says Walter. “So, I often encourage people joining the tour to share their heritage when I conduct the Welcome to Country.”

“It can help make the connection that we all come from somewhere. By tracking back through the generations, you can acknowledge your ancestors which is an important ritual in Aboriginal culture.”

Image Walter McGuire

Walter McGuire

[Go Cultural’s](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) tours began running at Goomup (Elizabeth Quay) in 2016 and from there more were developed including the ones offered on Wadjemup.

Walter offers two tours on the island: a one-hour walking tour exploring the island’s significance to Noongar people and its recent history as an Aboriginal prison; and, another two-hour tour providing a more immersive experience into Noongar culture, including a smoking ceremony.

Each of them offers an unique insight into [Aboriginal culture](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-culture) and [history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) on Wadjemup, and provides a way for visitors to gain a much deeper understanding of Wadjemup’s Whadjuk Noongar people. On the tours, Walter shares both the good and the confronting in relation to Aboriginal heritage on Wadjemup.

“I tell a story that explains the effect of Western Australia’s colonisation on Aboriginal culture,” says Walter. “Especially the impact of the removal of the Aboriginal men of high degree from their lands – the Boordier – or in other terms, the kings and emperors of our Aboriginal nations.”

Image 

Aboriginal flag

Image 

[Smoking ceremony](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences)

Image Lakes

Aerial view of lakes

Image Salt Lakes, Gabbi Karniny Bidi

Aerial view of boardwalk

Walter hopes that by telling these stories visitors will better understand how the incarceration of Boordier men on Wadjemup had such a destructive effect on not only them, but also on the communities they left behind. While the colonial past of Wadjemup is a challenging story to tell and hear, Walter acknowledges that the present time is one for deep listening and acceptance. We can’t move forward without acknowledging the past

“I talk about Wadjemup’s brutal prison history, but this tour is not about blame,” he explains. “It’s about telling a truth from our perspective and sharing the stories that have been told to us by the old people.”

Walter says that joining a [Go Cultural tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) at Wadjemup often proves to be a very spiritual experience for visitors. “As I share my knowledge, I can see people becoming emotionally moved from hearing the truth from our perspective, this shows me that they have become more connected to country.

"Our culture is about sharing and we invite everyone to get to know our culture and be part of this country and this land.”

# Shipwrecks

### Discover the shipwrecks of Wadjemup

Wadjemup / Rottnest Island has a long maritime history. And, over time, the island’s surrounding waters have become the resting place for over 13 unfortunate ships.

Some have sunk in treacherous tides, unable to navigate Wadjemup’s coral reef system. Others have been caught adrift on the Western Australian tides, slowly making their way across from the mainland and coming to rest off Wadjemup’s coast. At least one has sunk due to a drunken skipper setting out on a misguided attempt to reach Bunbury.

While most of the vessels lie off the coast in deep water, plaques have been installed both on land and under the sea, providing details of each one of the wrecks.

Intrepid explorers can hike around the island to find the landbound plaques. Alternatively, you can get up close and dive the shipwrecks.

Two of them, *Uribes* and *Shark*, lie just metres from shore, providing excellent snorkelling for those looking for a different environment to explore. Other wrecks can only be found by boat or by scuba diving offshore — but be aware that some of the locations are only suitable for experienced divers.

Image Two people in straw hats stand on a sandy beach, facing the ocean. A child in blue swimwear walks towards the water. The ocean is clear with some rocks visible, and two more people are swimming near the rocks under a clear blue sky.

### Where to find the Shipwrecks

The individual shipwrecks can be found all along Rottnest Island’s coast. So make sure you get a map of the island from the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre), and then take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) to the corresponding bus stop. If you’re feeling more adventurous, visitors can cycle all over the island and seek out the plaques.

The wreck that’s the easiest to find is *Shark*, which lies in shallow water just off [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks). You can get there by jumping on the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and getting off at Stop 3. Alternatively, the [Ngank Yira Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/ngank-yira-bidi) winds right past Henrietta Rocks, providing excellent views of the wreck.

*Uribes* can be found in shallow waters just metres off shore near Phillip Point, accessible from the Natural Jetty. Take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) to Stop 4, or walk the 20 minutes south from Thomson Bay.

Image Aerial view of a coastal landscape with turquoise waters, rocky outcrops, and a sandy beach under a clear blue sky.

[Henrietta Rocks](/learn/military-maritime-history)

### A colourful history lies under the waves

Dating back to 1842, the first ship to make the Wadjemup coast its final resting place was *Transit*. The 124-ton wooden, two-masted schooner struck Duck Rock and sank off the island’s northern coast. Some, like *City of York* which ran aground in 1899, have taken their place in the naming of Wadjemup.  Two wrecks remain a mystery to this day, with unknown ships discovered in both Salmon Bay and [City of York Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/city-of-york-bay).

And it’s not just ancient history. The Japanese tuna boat *Kiryo Maru* ran aground on its way to Fremantle in 1984, 50 metres offshore at Cathedral Rocks and has remained in place ever since.

To find out more about each of the individual shipwrecks surrounding the island, stop first at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre). Here you’ll find all the information you need to start your maritime trail. Then, take a quick walk to the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) to learn more.

[Learn more about Military & Maritime History](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history)

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I learn more about the shipwrecks?

An information flyer is available at the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre), and the [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) features a wealth of information detailing the wrecks.

Can you snorkel at the Rottnest Island shipwrecks?

Yes, you can [snorkel](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving) some of the [shipwrecks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/shipwrecks) around Rottnest Island. The wrecks of *Shark* and *Uribes* are easily accessible for snorkellers of all levels. These can be found just off the beach in reasonably shallow water. The rest of the wrecks are only visible underneath the water, so the best way to view them is by going on a scuba dive down to the vessels.

How many shipwrecks are around Rottnest Island?

The waters surrounding Wadjemup / Rottnest Island are the final resting place of more than 13 shipwrecks. These wrecks reflect the island’s long maritime history and serve as reminders of the challenges sailors faced navigating the area.

# Embrace the Unexpected With an Ocean Adventure in Winter

Dive deep with this weekend itinerary for adventure-loving friends, from fresh coastal walks to brisk ocean swims and surfing.

3 minutes

Image Aerial of Strickland Bay

Aerial of Strickland Bay

**As the days cool and the island flourishes with a new season, more opportunities arise to connect with your people. Whether it’s those who will pull on their wetsuits to discover an underwater world or the ones who chase the best swell of the season, paddling out alongside you.**

Swell that rivals the southwest of Australia, sunken ships and marine gardens that wrap you in underwater wonder, and local bites that warm you to the core. This itinerary is for the group who usually swags under the stars at Conto’s, Margaret River or who ventures north to dive Muiron Islands, Exmouth. Wadjemup holds your next ocean adventure.

### Day One

As any group of water enthusiasts will know, the best weather for ocean-based sports is in the morning. So, we recommend catching the first ferry so you can arrive as early as possible. Once you’ve landed, it’s time to head for the water.

#### SNORKELLING & DIVING

With the Leeuwin Current flowing down from Indonesia, the water here is usually approximately four degrees warmer than the coast of Perth. This means that on a warmer winter day you’ll find the conditions are perfect for a wetsuit-clad snorkel or dive to fully immerse yourselves in the thriving underwater world of Wadjemup. Spectacular spots are easily accessible from the shore, such as [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), Salmon Bay, and the shipwreck at [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks). Or you can opt for a story-filled swim along the snorkel trail at [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point-snorkel-trail).

#### CHECK-IN & LATE LUNCH

After swimming amongst the underwater world of Wadjemup, it’s time to check into your home away from home for the night, so wander over to the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre) if you’ve booked [Stay Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) accommodation, or make your way to [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup), [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) or [Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) to get settled in.

By the time you’ve warmed up with a hot shower and left your wetsuits out in the winter sun, it’ll be time for a late lunch. And after all that exertion, [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest) will leave even the hungriest satisfied with all your favourite pub classics on offer, such as fish and chips, pizzas, burgers, and more.

#### COASTAL WALK

Take in the expanse of the Indian Ocean from land by following the first section of the [Gabbi Karniny Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/gabbi-karniny-bidi) (a [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) trail) from the main settlement to [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) and continuing onto [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay). Keep an eye out to sea for a glimpse of [migrating whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) from August to December when you’re at Pinky Beach.

#### SUNSET & DINNER

As the sun bids farewell to the day, evenings hold a promise of respite, inviting you to soothe your weary legs, unburden your mind and embrace your island escape. To end your memorable first day of your group’s weekend away, wander back over to Pinky Beach— it’s one of the best spots to witness an island sunset. With the iconic white brick structure of Bathurst Lighthouse as your backdrop, watch the skies transform into hues of gold as you make conversation about your favourite moments of the day over dinner at [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island).

### Day Two

#### TIME FOR A SURF

It’s another early start for the other wintery ocean activity: [surfing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing). The cooler months bring light conditions and big, rolling swells, with the surf paralleling the waves of Margaret River. With your accommodation packed up and your luggage sorted, either for collection to the main jetty or stored in the lockers behind the [Visitor Centre](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/visitor-centre), it is time to hit the waves. The ideal time to head out is right after sunrise, about 7 or 8 am, with Strickland Bay being the spot for experienced surfers and softer waves found at Mary Cove or Chicken Reef near Salmon Bay.

The best way to get to your chosen break for the day is by [bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus), [bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or e-bike. If you need a surfboard rack for your bike, swing by [Pedal & Flipper Hire](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pedal-flipper-hire) to hire one for the day.

#### LUNCH

There’ll be time to visit a spot in the main settlement for lunch before catching the ferry. The iconic [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) is the perfect spot to pick up some hot and hearty food to warm yourselves up after a morning of surfing the waves. Choose from hot meat pies, sausage rolls, pastries and the famous jam and Nutella doughnuts, or some hot chips from the Chook Shack window. Settle in outside of the bakery or find a spot overlooking Thomson Bay before you hop on your afternoon ferry home.

# Spring Into a School Holiday Adventure

Days arrive soft and sunlit during this season of new life, setting the perfect scene for a spring school holiday getaway.

4 minutes

Image Family cycling past Geordie Bay

Family cycles

**As the days brighten up, a visit to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is a welcome way to spend the spring school holidays. Opportunities for adventure beckon at every bay and with each blooming wildflower.**

### Spring on Rottnest Island

[Spring](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/spring) arrives in September, as the second month of [Noongar season](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-six-noongar-seasons-on-wadjemup), Djilba, brings pleasant temperatures and longer days. After recent rains, the land wakes with vibrant [wildflowers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup) and peaceful birdsong. Trails wind and beaches glimmer with the promise of a quiet getaway without summer’s crowds. This special time of year also sees the sweet sight of joeys peeking out of their mother’s pouch; new life is all around.

### Spring school holiday getaway

Western Australia’s spring school holidays run from late September to early October. During this time, daytime temperatures are slightly cooler than the mainland of Perth, hovering around 18-23°C. Warming sun rays make waters dazzle and invite refreshing dips – particularly after active hours spent enjoying the island’s natural beauty.

### SPRING FAMILY ACTIVITIES ON ROTTNEST ISLAND

#### Go on a wildflower walk

At this time of year, salty air mingles with the fresh scent of spring flowers. Clusters of colour are bound to catch your eye, like the purple-blue of the island’s iconic [Wadjemup Daisy](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup). Head to [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks) and [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) where the first petals may be starting to peek through the dunes.

Vibrant pops of orange, red, pink and sunshine yellow can also be found over the island, you just need to know where to look. Hike the trails of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) and see how many different species you can spot along the way.

Image 

[Spot the Wadjemup Daisy](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-the-wildflowers-of-wadjemup)

Image Samphire at Rottnest Island

#### Spot quokka joeys

Delight in one of the island’s most memorable sights: [kwoka (quokka) joeys](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island)! As the mothers hop about, look from a careful distance for curious, tiny faces that peek out of pouches. This once-a-year event is a special treat for families discovering the island together during spring.

####

Quokka Safety

To help keep the unique wildlife safe and healthy, please do not touch, feed or give water to the quokkas and always observe from a respectful distance.

#### Whale watching

Beneath spring skies, the sea offers a show-stopping sight. Let excitement grow as you gather around the island’s edges to spot migrating [maamoong (whales)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching). The WA spring school holidays align perfectly with the movements of these mighty creatures as they migrate between seasons. Cycle or take the bus over to [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end), which features two viewing platforms at Cape Vlamingh and Cathedral Rocks, both equipped with binoculars for the best views for all ages.

#### Take a boat tour

Sprinkle some sea spray in your hair on board the [Eco Express](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours). Ideal for adventurous families, your tour takes you around the island under the warm spring sunshine. Let laughter ring through the air as the tour travels around Wadjemup’s natural wonders. Along the way, spot wildlife like the iconic yoondoordoo (osprey) and manyil (long-nosed fur seals).

Image Quokkas

[Quokka joey](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Quokkas)

Image Eco Express Boat Tour

[Spot wildlife on the Eco Express Boat Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/eco-express-boat-tours)

Image A whale breaching backwards with Rottnest Island in the background-36.tmb-fallback.webp?Culture=en&sfvrsn=98b5f69_2)

[Spot migrating whales](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching)

#### Lawn bowls and games

Spring sunshine calls for some family competition on the green. Make your way to [R.I.G.C Clubhouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/ricg-clubhouse) for barefoot bowls and free lawn games surrounded by softly swaying trees. When all the fun sparks a ferocious appetite, Chippies is serving up crunchy fish and chips fit for champions.

#### Pop into the Pilot Boathouse

Travel back in time to discover the island’s maritime history. Constructed in 1859, the still-standing [Pilot Boathouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pilot-boathouse) houses a replica pilot boat and historical photos, inviting visitors of all ages to come and look. Little ones can also learn how to tie boating knots here.

#### Head to Oliver Hill by train

The [Captain Hussey train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour) departs daily on the journey to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). Climb aboard and gaze out the open windows as the rhythm of the rails transports you all to this historic island site. It’s an adventure filled with fresh air, fascinating sights and imagination-sparking moments.

#### Grab a bite

In between all the exploration, there are plenty of places to stop for a bite. Grab some flaky pastries from [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) or fresh sandwiches from [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane) and park up at a picnic bench to enjoy your goodies. For a sit-down meal, [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) serves up crowd-pleasing sourdough pizza and pasta. To top it all off, [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican) is the perfect pitstop for creamy soft serve ice cream. Looking for more family-friendly eats? [See all dining options on the island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink).

### FREE FAMILY-FRIENDLY EVENTS & ACTIVITIES

#### Rottnest Voluntary Guides spring school holiday program

The Rottnest Voluntary Guides Association (RVGA) run a program of free activities and tours for kids of all ages to learn more about the island during the spring school holidays.

Stay tuned for updates on the program and [subscribe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/subscribe) to be kept updated about [new experiences](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do), [events](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/whats-on), and [specials offers](https://www.rottnestisland.com/deals).

#### Free Walking Tours

The guides also offer [free daily walking tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) year-round. Environmental awareness and historical education are a primary focus during tours, which can include wildlife sightings, stories of shipwrecks, sailors and past settlement workers, plus information detailing the agriculture, industry, geology, and marine reserves of the island.

# Find Your Ideal Winter Escape on Wadjemup

Check out the range of accommodation available and plan your ideal cosy seasonal escape.

5 minutes

Image Geordie Bay Stay Rottnest accommodation aerial 

Geordie Bay

**Gather your loved ones or escape with someone special and let a quieter season set the tone for your stay.**

From indulgent oceanside retreats to tents nestled in nature, laidback self-contained stays to shared rooms, discover the variety of winter accommodation available on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island.

### Luxe Stays Close to Nature

#### The Lodge Wadjemup

Enjoy a central location and contemporary interiors just behind the main settlement, with views across the striking [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). Reserve a romantic lakeside room for two and take in tranquil winter scenes from your verandah or private balcony as violet-toned clouds gather overhead. Courtyard rooms suit small groups and families, with connecting options and bunk bed configurations available. Shared verandahs encourage moments of togetherness within the historic surrounds.

For an added touch of winter indulgence, book one of the Poolhouse rooms. Step outside into gentle winter sunshine and unwind by the pool, with seasonally heated water and plush pink lounge chairs setting the scene for relaxed, slow mornings.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:**Quiet [quokka spotting](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) along the Garden Lake boardwalk.
* **Dine and drink:** Visit [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest) for breakfast, fireside lunch, or dinner and drinks with lake views. The on-site kiosk, [Pelican](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pelican), also offers breakfast bites, takeaway treats and hot drinks.

#### Samphire Rottnest

Overlooking the serene water of Thomson Bay lies [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest). Whether you're a couple looking to indulge for a night or two or want a premium shared spot between pairs of friends, this is an ideal base. Every room offers ample space and elevated amenities to make your stay special. Indulge in a beachfront suite to enjoy relaxed mornings spent wrapped under warm layers, listening to gently lapping waves and crisp sea breezes beyond your private balcony. Later in the day, reserve an in-room massage to soothe and warm tired muscles after a day [hiking the Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi). Best followed by a lengthy soak in your private bathtub while rain softly taps the roof.

The private pool is also heated throughout winter, perfect for a dip after a busy day. Additionally, all guests gain exclusive access to the Samphire Club. Here you'll find a crackling fireplace along with complimentary coffee and baked treats available.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:** Stroll the cool sands of T[homson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) to start your day.
* **Dine and drink:** Enjoy daily breakfast at [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara), lunch and dinner at [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), Lontara or [Isola Bar E Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest), and drinks at [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar).

#### Discovery Resorts - Rottnest Island

Families and couples alike will appreciate the restful location of this eco-sustainable resort with all the comforts of a hotel. Resting behind the sand dunes of Pinky Beach, every eco-tent at [Discovery Resorts](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/discovery-rottnest-island) is designed with connection to your surroundings in mind. Wake up to swaying trees and distant crashing waves on a cool morning, tucked away behind thick canvas. Peaceful afternoons are spent floating in the on-site pool or relaxing on your fully furnished deck, mug of hot tea or a hearty red wine in hand.

Take advantage of flexible tent configurations like the superior duplex tent, which sleeps up to ten guests. Other family-friendly options feature bunks or rollaway beds to sleep everyone comfortably.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:** Witness blazing sunsets and sunrises from [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) or the base of [Bathurst Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse).
* **Dine and drink:** The signature breakfast at [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) is included in all bookings. Convenient on-site dining is also available for lunch and dinner, plus free marshmallows for toasting by the fire in the evenings.

## Self-Contained Serenity

#### Stay Rottnest Self-Contained

Holiday homes on offer via [Stay Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-self-contained) are self-contained for the ongoing ease of a group getaway. Booking everyone's favourite unit, heritage cottage, beachfront bungalow or coastal cabin is made simpler during this peaceful season, with ample options for groups of all sizes, including up to 18-bed configurations at Kingstown's Governor Circle.

With the vibrant winter landscape as your backdrop and a settled seasonal hush surrounding you, there's no need to rush. Each space is equipped to do things your way. Relax indoors with great company as rainclouds roll overhead, wrap up and watch fiery sunsets from your enclosed courtyard, and spend cosy nights cooking shared meals with supplies from the [General Stores](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store). Wherever you decide to call home, connection and comfort come first.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:** Serene coastal surrounds of [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), [Longreach Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/longreach-bay), [Fay's Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fays-bay) or [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay).
* **Dine and drink:** Pop into [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) for breakfast and lunch, plus dinner on select nights or [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) for drinks and all-day dining. In the main settlement, grab casual meals from [Frankie's on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) or [The Lane Cafe](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/the-lane).

## Back to Basics

#### Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms

Calling all solo travellers, friends or families with an eye for low-cost accommodation. Whether you're bunking with new faces or reserving a dorm as a group, there's comfort in simplicity. Think shared spaces full of charm, where mismatched mugs are filled with warming brews and shared over friendly chatter.

[Stay Rottnest Hostel & Dorms](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-hostel) offers an affordable way to spend time on Wadjemup this winter. The hostel sleeps up to 50 like-minded guests, with communal kitchens, barbeques and bathrooms on-site. The dorms feature 17 rooms, varying between two and 18-bed layouts, with some rooms offering a private bathroom. Please note that the dorms do not have kitchen facilities.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:** The historic surrounds of Kingstown Barracks and intriguing walking trails around [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery)**.**
* **Dine and drink:**  Collect fresh groceries from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) or pick up a selection of items from [Rottnest Bakery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-bakery) in the main settlement.

#### Stay Rottnest Campground

Gather your group and embrace the grounding delight of being in nature. Winter weather on Wadjemup is often sunny, inviting campers to pitch up tents on a site that's just a short stroll to [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach). [Stay Rottnest Campground](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/stay-rottnest-campground) is a non-powered campground offering a maximum of six guests and two tents per site for a low-cost, but entirely enriching, island experience.

Wake to pale filtered light as you burrow deeper into sleeping bags, breath hanging in the cool air. The days unfold slowly during winter, filled with invigorating walks and hours of cycling powered by cool temperatures. When evening approaches, wrap up active days around the barbeque sharing simple, hearty meals.

**On your doorstep**

* **Experience:**Cool nights spent rugged up under the dazzling night sky.
* **Dine and drinks:** Pick up barbeque supplies from the [General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) in the main settlement or enjoy easy all-day dining at nearby [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island).
