## Fishing spots on Wadjemup

#### Jetties

For the occasional anglers inspired by the rich waters of the island, the small jetties at [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), Stark Bay, and [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay) are ideal easy wins. Hotel Jetty at Thomson Bay is a haven for families who prefer a short walk home after catching their haul — and the schools that circle the barnacle-clad jetty poles are a lightweight catch for little ones using hand lines. The sheltered Geordie Bay jetty attracts herring and other table fish as well, including tailor, whiting, and silver bream.

#### Beaches

Proper seclusion and peace can be found on some of the island’s remote beaches. [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach) is one of the places you can cast out and simply enjoy the wait. Wade in knee-deep, breathe in the clear, sea-scented air, and let the gentle lap of waves be the rhythm of your day — until the moment you spring into action and reel in one of the sought-after mulloway found in these waters.

#### Boating

If you’re journeying to the island on your own boat, then the open waters around Wadjemup become a possibility. The deeper the water, the more impressive the catch — and the best can be found offshore from [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). There’s a bounty of species like western rock lobster, Spanish mackerel, yellowtail kingfish, and breaksea cod. When you’re fishing here, make sure you respect the sanctuary zone that encompasses Radar Reef, Cape Vlamingh, and Cathedral Rocks. From your boat, you’re only permitted to look for pelagic species of fish.

Staying Safe When You’re Fishing

It’s important to be prepared for changes in the weather and ocean conditions while you’re fishing, and wearing a lifejacket if required. Also, if you have children joining you, ensure they are always supervised.

Image Two people dining outdoors on a boat with an ocean view, enjoying meals served on dark plates along with wine.

[Rottnest Cruises](/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises)

### Local seafood straight from the waves

Whether you stay the night on Rottnest Island or settle in for a picnic with a view, the fresh catch of your day will elevate your dining experience and deepen your appreciation for the land.

For a taste of island seafood without the patience, there are [plenty of restaurants](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink) featuring fresh, local seafood on their menu and even [boat tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/boating) where you can taste the fish minutes after it’s caught.

[Learn more about deluxe dining experiences on the water](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-cruises)

## Respecting the marine sanctuaries

As a Class A Reserve, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is the home of unique wildlife, a place where over 400 species of fish thrive in the warm waters of the Leeuwin Current. The island has five marine sanctuaries dotted around the coastline, protecting this rare tropical sea life from over-fishing and human damage.

It’s vitally important that visiting anglers never take more than they need, don’t leave anything behind, and respect the boundaries of these sanctuaries. Also, spear fishing, spear guns, and gidgees are prohibited within the island waters, and net fishing isn’t permitted within the marine reserve. When you fish on the island, follow these rules to ensure Rottnest Island will always be a place of abundance for future expeditions.

**Places to avoid**

* No fishing is permitted at [Little Salmon Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-salmon-bay)
* Daylight fishing is prohibited at [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin), and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach)

[Fishing Information

Before arriving for your fishing getaway, find out more about the marine sanctuary zones, boating permits, and recreational fishing rules from the Department of Fisheries.](http://rules.fish.wa.gov.au/)

## Where to get fishing equipment

Visitors can bring fishing gear over on the ferry or in their own boat, and you can also buy a range of tackle from the General Store in the [main settlement](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and  [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store).

### Frequently Asked Questions

Can you fish on Rottnest Island beaches?

Yes, you can fish from many of the island's [beaches and bays](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/beaches), as well as from rocks, jetties and boats. However, fishing is prohibited or restricted in a number of [marine sanctuary zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones), so always check the relevant maps and fishing rules before choosing a spot.

No fishing is permitted at [Little Salmon Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-salmon-bay), and daylight fishing is prohibited at [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach).

Before arriving for your fishing getaway, find out more about marine sanctuary zones, boating permits and current recreational fishing rules from the [Department of Fisheries](http://rules.fish.wa.gov.au/).

Can I bring, buy or hire fishing gear on Rottnest Island

Bring your own fishing gear or travel light and purchase bait, tackle, rods and handlines on the island. Fishing supplies are available from the [General Store in Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and the [Geordie Bay General Store](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store).

Where are the best fishing spots on Rottnest Island?

The best fishing spot on the island depends on the [weather](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather), the species you are chasing and whether you want to fish from shore or by boat. The easiest place to start is our [guide to fishing around Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-wetting-a-line-on-rottnest-island).

What makes Western Australia such a good destination for fishing?

Western Australia is an incredible fishing destination thanks to its long coastline, diverse species and the variety of places you can cast a line. On Rottnest Island, that ranges from easy family spots like the [Thomson Bay jetty](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay), to more adventurous sessions around [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). Find more inspiration in our [guide to wetting a line on Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-wetting-a-line-on-rottnest-island).

What fish can you catch around Rottnest Island?

The waters of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island are home to a wide mix of species, with herring, whiting, skipjack, squid and tailor all commonly mentioned by anglers, while larger fish are more often found in deeper water. For more on local species and current recreational rules, see [marine life around Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see) and [WA recreational fishing rules](https://www.dpird.wa.gov.au/individuals/recreational-fishing/recreational-fishing-rules/).

What fishing equipment is prohibited at Rottnest Island?

Spearguns, fishing spears and gidgees are prohibited within Rottnest Island waters, while fishing nets cannot be used within the marine reserve. Following these restrictions helps protect the island’s fish populations and unique marine environment.

# Location

## The island story

Lying just 19 km off the coast of Fremantle, Wadjemup / Rottnest Island sits so tantalisingly close to the mainland that it can be seen on the horizon, glimmering across the water.

And while it’s a favourite holiday destination for both local and international travellers, Wadjemup’s history goes back a lot further than you might think.

### Wadjemup in numbers

The island lies 19 km from Fremantle Port, 33 km from Perth, and 22 km from Hillarys Boat Harbour.

A marine paradise, visitors can explore 63 of the most stunning beaches you’ll find in Western Australia. 20 beautiful bays border the island, brimming with sea life, with over 135 species of tropical fish and numerous species of coral to observe.

A haven for swimming, snorkelling, boating, and cycling, island visitors can explore 45 km of [walking trails](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) and 22 km of [cycling paths and roads](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/sport-recreation/cycling).

Despite its expansive feel, however, it’s not a big island—it measures 11 km long by 4.5 km wide, and 19 km2 in area, with its highest point sitting just 45 m above sea level.

Image Parakeet Bay, Aerial

Parakeet & Little Parakeet Bay

Image Snorkelling

[Underwater world](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-snorkelling-the-warm-waters-of-wadjemup)

Image Cycling near Little Salmon Bay

[Cycle the coast](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island)

Image Wadjemup Lighthouse

Wadjemup Lighthouse in the distance

Image Wilson Bay

[Hiking the trail](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/Hiking-the-Wadjemup-Bidi)

### A story told by the land itself

While seemingly alone in the ocean, the island is actually part of a chain of limestone islands and reefs on the continental shelf off the west coast of Australia.

The largest of the chain, this limestone plays a large part in its current character, and Wadjemup is famous for its limestone headlands and bays, with white sandy beaches. Its coast is fringed with unique shoreline platforms — like at [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) — and offshore reefs, which provide excellent diving opportunities.

The geographic features on Wadjemup tell a story spanning back far beyond human occupation, with much of the rock found on the island playing particular geological significance.

At the hypersaline lakes, fragile microbialites can be found on the shoreline. While they look like reef and rocks, they’re actually living things, made up of millions of tiny microbes. Three different types can be found around the lakes: stromatolites, thrombolites, and leolities, some of which may be up to 1,000 years old. The island’s [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) is dominated by a different kind of rock, Tamala Limestone. It’s a fascinating example of the changing oceans over time, and is dated back approximately 140,000 years — when the sea level was almost 130 m lower than what it is today.

The coral reef at Fairbridge Bluff also hints at evidence of ancient sea levels, and how seas have risen and fallen over time. These fluctuating sea levels have created some of the island’s key features, such as the inland salt lake system.

At one point, these shallow salt lakes were a large series of deep caves. Over time, both rain and groundwater dissolved the roofs of the caves, causing them to collapse. As sea levels rose, the caves were flooded, and this seawater remained trapped in what are now the 12 [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes).

Image Salt lakes on the island

Salt lakes on the island

### How Wadjemup was formed

At one point in time, in fact, Wadjemup wasn’t even an island — it was connected to the mainland by a belt of sand dunes.

It was during a period known as the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), when almost 10% of the earth’s surface was covered in ice. Not Australia, though: sea levels were at their lowest, and Wadjemup formed part of an expansive coastal plain that was divided by the Swan River.

[Aboriginal artefacts](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) found on the island suggest that it was inhabited by the Whadjuk Noongar people up until around 6,500 years ago. At this point, temperatures post-LGM began to increase, causing the sea levels to rise. This disconnected the island from the rest of the mainland.

Cultural and scientific evidence suggests that once this land bridge was submerged, Wadjemup remained completely uninhabited by the Whadjuk Noongar people. Without boats, Noongar people weren’t able to journey back to the island, and it lay dormant across the waves for thousands of years.

The plant and animal population flourished, giving rise to the famous population of [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas), or kwoka in Noongar — the lack of predators has helped them thrive.

Lying just off the shore, the island plays an important part in [Noongar cultural beliefs](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-culture), too. The Whadjuk Noongar people are the Traditional Owners of Wadjemup, and their name for the island is sometimes referred to as a place across the water where spirits go.

Image Sand dunes on Wadjemup/Rottnest Island

Sand dune

Image Quokka on the ground searching for food

Quokka by the lake

Image West End

[West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end)

### Protecting the land

Wadjemup is just far enough from the mainland shores that it feels like a world away. Its flora and fauna help to achieve this, which is why preserving Wadjemup’s animal, plant, and marine life population is so important.

Being mostly car-free helps to keep the animal population safe. The high percentage of cyclists ensures their environmental footprint is kept to a minimum. And the [Marine Sanctuary Zones](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones) around the island ensure there are places for fish and sealife to be protected.

As a [Class A Reserve](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/nature-wildlife), the island works to preserve and protect its natural beauty, and these measures all ensure the stewardship of the island for generations to come.

### Inviting weather, all year round

Wadjemup is lucky to enjoy a Mediterranean-style climate. But it’s not quite like the mainland.

During the hot summer months of December to February, the island is usually a few degrees cooler than Perth, with average temperatures hovering around the mid-to-high 20°C. Interestingly, this means that it’s warmer in winter. From June to August, you can typically expect to find Rottnest Island a few degrees warmer than Perth, with an average daytime temperature of 19°C.

Despite being further out in the ocean, the water is also surprisingly warm. This is thanks to the Leeuwin Current, which flows along the west coast of Australia, creating sea surface temperatures of around 23°C in summer and about 18°C in winter. This allows tropical marine species, such as coral, to live around the island, while also making it much more inviting to wade into the water and enjoy the vast range of aquatic activities the island is known for.

Image Family time at Longreach Bay

Family time at Longreach Bay

### A brief history of tourism

With the lure of bright white beaches, striking turquoise water, and gorgeous temperate weather, it wasn’t long before the island became a tourist destination.

1902 saw the first ferries carry tourists to the island — but only on Sundays. The first public jetty was built in 1906, just to the south of [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) settlement where the Army Groyne stands today.

It was 1907, though, when the island became a recreation and holiday destination. It’s a role that the island has played ever since, only shutting to the public in [wartime](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/military-maritime-history), in 1914 and from 1940–1945.

The [surfing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) boom in the 1950s brought even more visitors to the island, and it became a surfing hot spot, known for its long, rolling barrels.

### It wasn’t always a holiday destination

We acknowledge that [Wadjemup’s history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/history/aboriginal-history) can be particularly distressing.

Following European discovery and settlement, the island began a sorrowful chapter, with the construction of the Rottnest Island Aboriginal Establishment — an Aboriginal prison and forced labour camp that incarcerated 3,700 Aboriginal boys and men over its 93-year lifespan. A sordid time in the island’s story, it’s one that can’t be ignored.

Visitors to Wadjemup can learn more about this history at [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum). With a range of exhibits that tell the rich, complex, and often uncomfortable history of the island, it’s a place to stop, reflect, and understand what has come before you.

# Seals & Sea Lions

## Spot seals and sea lions in the wild

Catching a glimpse of a long-nosed fur seal (manyin in Noongar) or the rare Australian sea lion (manyini in Noongar) at Wadjemup / Rottnest Island is one of Western Australia’s most exciting [wildlife encounters](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/wildlife-encounters-at-wadjemup). You’ll find these charismatic marine mammals basking on sun-warmed rocks or gliding effortlessly through the water around the island year-round.  
  
Whether you’re exploring [on foot](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot), [by bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike) or as part of a guided experience, spotting these marine mammals adds another layer to the island’s coastal story. It’s a chance to slow down, look out across the water, and feel more deeply connected to the wild rhythms of Wadjemup.

### Where to See Seals and Sea Lions on Rottnest Island

Although seals and sea lions can be seen around the island at any time of year, [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) offers the best chance for reliable sightings.  
  
The Cathedral Rocks viewing platform provides the most dependable vantage point, allowing you to watch them safely from above. Look for them floating in the sheltered waters below or resting on the offshore rocks. Binoculars are available to help you get an even closer view.

This area forms part of the West End Demersal [Sanctuary Zone.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/learn/sustainability/marine-sanctuary-zones) As a protected haven rich in tropical fish and marine life, it’s an important feeding and resting site for both seals and sea lions.

Nearby Green Island, within the Green Island Sanctuary Zone, is another key habitat for Australian sea lions. Its undisturbed seagrass meadows attract small fish species, providing essential feeding grounds for marine mammals. You’ll often see young male sea lions lounging around the island’s rocky shoreline here.

[Keep Your Distance

If you spot a seal or sea lion, ensure you keep your distance and do not approach them on land and in the water. If you see a marine animal in distress, contact the rangers on (+61 8) 9372 9788.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/contact-us)

### Spot the Difference

While Australian sea lions and long-nosed fur seals both belong to the pinniped family, several key differences make them easy to tell apart, once you know what to look for.

#### Australian Sea Lions

The Australian sea lion is Australia's only native seal species and can be found along the southern and western coastlines from Western Australia’s Abrolhos Islands to South Australia’s Kangaroo Island. They are considered one of the rarer seal species globally, and while no breeding colonies exist on Wadjemup, the individuals spotted around the island are typically young males using the area as a feeding and resting ground.

###### Spot them by their:

* Blunt snout and tightly rolled external ears
* Large body size, weighing up to 300 kg
* Large front flippers and tail flippers
* Males have chocolate brown to black fur with an off-white back of the head and neck
* Females have silvery-grey fur with yellowish-cream bellies

#### Long-Nosed Fur Seals

Rottnest Island is home to a resident colony of long-nosed fur seals. While they primarily breed in New Zealand, they also inhabit parts of Australia’s southern coastline, with Cathedral Rocks being one of the most dependable viewing spots on the island.

These seals spend about half their lives on land, resting on rocky platforms and in protected bays. They gather in colonies, known as rookeries, and are especially active during their summer breeding season.

###### Spot them by their:

* Pointed nose with visible ear flaps
* Smaller than sea lions, weighing up to around 180 kg
* Big eyes and long whiskers
* Dark brown fur made up of two layers

Image Eco Express

### Eco Express Boat Tours with Rottnest Express

**Operating September to April**

If you’re visiting between September and April, the [Eco Express Adventure Boat Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours) may offer the chance to spot seals and sea lions up close in their natural environment. As you cruise along the rugged coastline, keep an eye out for these playful mammals resting on rocky outcrops or gliding through the water as the boat slows for a clearer view.

[Find out more](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/eco-express-boat-tours)

### Frequently Asked Questions

Where is the best place to see seals and sea lions on Rottnest Island?

The Cathedral Rocks viewing platform at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) is the most reliable spot to see long-nosed fur seals and Australian sea lions on the island. From here, you can often watch them swimming below or resting on the nearby rocky outcrops.

Are there any tours on the island for spotting seals and sea lions?

While there are no tours dedicated specifically to seal or sea lion viewing, you may spot them on the [Eco Express Adventure Boat Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/eco-express-boat-tours), which travels to West End where they often gather. They can also be seen during a number of [hiking](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective), [e-bike](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours), and [bus tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour) that pass through [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end).

What other wildlife will I see on Rottnest Island?

You can expect to see [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas), [birdlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching), and [marine life](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/guide-to-marine-life-at-rottnest-island--what-you-can-see) like tropical fish and bottlenose dolphins throughout the year. [Warmer months](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/summer) increase sightings of reptiles, then during [winter,](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) various frog species repopulate around the wetlands. From August until December, you may even spot [whales migrating](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) around the island.

Can I swim with the seals?

Swimming with the long-nosed fur seals at Cathedral Rocks is not permitted. Visitors may use the purpose-built viewing platform at Cathedral Rocks to see wildlife from a safe distance.

# Take a Rottnest Island Tour Together in Winter

With cooler temperatures and an ever-changing landscape, embrace the opportunity to explore the island together on a guided tour.

5 minutes

Image 

Choose a Segway tour

**Let the experienced guides of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island take you and your favourite person on an adventure filled with winter wonder and island insights.**

[Winter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter) reveals a renewed landscape that’s just waiting to be explored. Invigorating temperatures invite you to circumnavigate the island’s dramatic coastlines, dappled boorn boodja (woodlands) and sweeping kabikarning (salt lakes).

When the temperature dips, so too do warm weather crowds that flit frequently between the island and the mainland. As winter wanderers, relish the stillness and explore further with guided tours available throughout winter on Rottnest Island. Tours are the perfect way to gain deeper knowledge and a unique perspective. From walks to wheels, rail to trails, here are the top land-based tours that connect you with all that’s here.

### WALKING TOURS

If you’re wondering which Rottnest Island tours are the best during the cooler months, well, that’s entirely up to you and your fellow explorer. But a simple place to start is with your own two feet.

#### Trek the trails with The Hike Collective

Fall into a peaceful rhythm with a [guided hiking tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective). Tours range from 4 km to 16 km in length, providing a welcome way to link up with like-minded explorers and reach idyllic island locations together. Let your legs take you further, powered by smatterings of soft sunlight and refreshingly cool air. Whichever tour you take, it’s bound to be filled with [wildlife sightings](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/uniquely-winter-wildlife-experiences-on-wadjemup), including the famous [kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island) and [djerap (birds)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching).

#### Connect to culture with Go Cultural Aboriginal Tours & Experiences

Slow down for moments of reflection alongside local Noongar guide and Traditional Owner, Walter McGuire. This award-winning [guided walking tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) offers an essential experience to better understand the cultural significance of Wadjemup. Tours run for one or two hours and commence with a sand ceremony at the main settlement, before Walter guides you on an enriching walk filled with traditional song and language.

Image 

[Hike along the salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-wonders-along-the-wadjemup-bidi)

Image Walter McGuire

[Walter McGuire from Go Cultural Tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences?tab=see-do)

#### Ascend 38 m above the island on the Wadjemup Lighthouse tour

Take part in an energising [daily tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour) that sees you soar up a 155-step spiral staircase. As you both wind your way to the viewing platform, your guide will set the scene of past engineering feats, and use of this functioning lighthouse in showing the way for lost sailors. At the top, take a deep breath of crisp air and appreciate 360-degree views of the seasonal scenery, from revitalised green foliage to rolling waves over the expansive Indian Ocean. You’ve taken time out of your busy lives to be here, and it’s worth savouring.

#### Travel back in time with daily Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnel tours

Escape passing rain showers and head underground with the Rottnest Voluntary Guides. Hear the soft echoes of anticipatory footsteps as the tour takes you through the [underground tunnels](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour) that lead to the gun’s ammunition supply and engine room. Examine the 9.2-inch naval gun: the only intact emplacement of its type left in Australia. On clear days, park up at a nearby picnic table and enjoy panoramic island views and a pre-packed bite to eat.

Invigorated to continue the adventure with additional walking tours? Explore all the tours offered by the knowledgeable [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours).

#### Explore Wadjemup with Aboriginal Guides

Winter invites a quieter, more reflective connection to Wadjemup, and there's no better way to experience it than through Aboriginal-led cultural tours with [Dooga Waalitj Healing](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences). Immerse yourself in stories of Country, culture and resilience that feel even more deeply connected to the landscape around you. Join a [guided walking tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) and explore significant sites, hear generations-old stories and gain insight into the island’s layered history.

#### Step into culture with Koorda's Crew

The winter seasons of Makuru and Djiiba are the perfect time for young explorers to immerse themselves in Wadjemup’s natural and cultural landscape with [Koorda’s Crew](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda). Beginning at the North Thomson Bay shade shelter, the 50-minute Wadjemup Bush Kaardijin (Knowledge) Tour connects children aged 4 to 12 with native plants, wildlife and their traditional uses, while uncovering the stories and deep cultural connections woven through the island.

### TWO-WHEELED TOURS

#### Cruise around on and off-road with Segway Tours WA

Awaken your senses with chilled coastal breezes that caress your cheeks as you embark on a [two-wheeled tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa). The Settlement Explorer tour is a 1-hour journey covering the main settlement before heading out to The Basin and Bathurst Lighthouse. Along the way, hear historic facts and enjoy the ever-changing landscape.

Explore a little longer on the Fortress Adventure tour with 1.5 hours of off-road exploration as you appreciate the military history of [Bickley Battery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bickley-battery) while soaking in the surrounding coastline.

The Coastal Explorer tour takes you on a 2-hour journey of discovery that explores the island's history while showcasing its natural beauty. Travel through key locations including Thomson Bay, The Quod, Heritage Common, Bathurst Lighthouse, Geordie Bay, Longreach Bay, and the salt lakes.

#### Journey along the coastline with Paul’s Eco E-Bike tours

Wadjemup’s winter winds are no match for [electric bicycles](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours). Embrace the peaks and valleys of your journey in complete comfort. For the complete island experience, join the 4-hour tour that takes you to the wild and wonderful [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/weather/winter). Keep a watchful eye out for [maamoong (whale)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching) sightings as they migrate around these waters during the winter months.

If your day is busy with other adventures, the 2-hour guided sunset tour is a tranquil way to farewell the day. Glide your way as a group to Ricey Beach to capture sight of the soft winter sun casting golden shades in the sky as it sets on another winter’s day.

### BUS AND TRAIN TOURS

#### Travel to Oliver Hill with a Captain Hussey Train Tour

Reconnect with your inner child with a ride on this [historic train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour). Anchored by decades-old rails, the service travels to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) and back to the settlement throughout each day, offering comfortable transportation with shelter from passing seasonal showers. Share gleeful grins and take in the scenery of the island’s southside as you make your way to this significant Australian World War II heritage site.

#### Swing by iconic sites with Discover Rottnest

If you’re visiting when the weather takes a wet or blustery turn, [bus tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) ensure the adventure continues. Departing twice daily, this [90-minute tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/discover-rottnest-bus-tour) with guided commentary takes you past the most iconic locations of the island, stopping at [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end). Bundle up and hop out here hand-in-hand to observe and explore before boarding once again to make the cosy return trip to the settlement, discussing all that you’ve encountered.

#### Explore more with Quokka Coaches

Additional [bus tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) transport you to different expanses of the island, allowing ample opportunities to see seasonal sights. The Bayseeker Island tour departs twice daily and runs for just under two hours. Highlights along the way include stops at [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) and [Henrietta Rocks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/henrietta-rocks).

Those with a desire to delve into the military history of the island will appreciate the Grand Island tour, which departs once daily. Over four hours, you’ll discover stories of the past during the underground [Oliver Hill Guns and Tunnels tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill-gun---tunnels-tour), in addition to exploring the settlement, Wadjemup Lighthouse and more.

# Winter Island Nights Made for Two

You’ve just spent a lovely winter’s day exploring the island; but as the sun slips below the water, your island experience is just getting started.

4 minutes

Image 

Stargazing

**As the sun sets on a dazzling winter’s day, there’s a unique atmosphere to Wadjemup / Rottnest Island that starts to stir. Seize the seasonal opportunity to reconnect with one another and embrace all that’s on offer during an overnight stay.**

Golden-tinged clouds at dusk; illuminating night skies; intimate dining experiences… Wadjemup in winter sets a dreamy backdrop to an evening getaway with the one you love. So slow down, rug up and ease into the romantic rhythms of island life.

### Find a moment of zen together

Reserve yourselves two yoga mats alongside the seasoned yogis at [Evolve in You Yoga](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/evolve-in-you-yoga). Sessions run in the late afternoons, offering yoga, mindfulness and meditation as the soft winter sun slips slowly out of the sky. Feel your breath deepen and mind unwind as you stretch your body in the crisp winter air.

### SEE A SPECTACULAR WINTER SUNSET

As the days get shorter and colder, the skies surrounding the island often become brighter and bolder. Surprise your other half with a decadent cheeseboard and a bottle of local red from the General Store in the [main settlement](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) or from [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store). Then, simply sip, snack and watch the sky glow from the comforts of the courtyard, deck or balcony of your [accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay). Or, slip out into the evening with a thermos of warming tea to enjoy the sky-show from a different vantage point.

#### Best sunset spots:

**Bathurst Lighthouse and Pinky Beach:** Find yourself a spot at the base of this [iconic lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/bathurst-point-lighthouse) and experience uninterrupted views over the vast Indian Ocean. [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island) is close by for a meal and drinks with a delightful view.

**Vlamingh Lookout:** Here, you’ll have panoramic views of the island’s rocky headlands transforming into bush dotted with pink-tinted [kabikarning (salt lakes)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes). During winter, the revitalising winds add a level of thrill to the experience.

**Garden Lake:** Pair this show-stopping evening spectacle with a moreish Mediterranean meal from [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest): the aptly named restaurant that overlooks Garden Lake. Sip a glass of wine while the shadows and sunset hues illuminate the still waters of surrounding salt lakes.

Remember to Bring a Torch

When exploring after dark, remember to take a torch. If you have children joining you, ensure they are always supervised.

### Share an intimate dining experience

**Going out:** Enjoy one another’s company over warming winter dishes. [Geordie's Cafe & Art Gallery](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordies-cafe-art-gallery) and [Frankie’s on Rotto](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/frankie-s-on-rotto) feature classic spreads in a cosy setting. Share a grazing board or small plates while you bond over a beverage. Hearty, wallet-friendly favourites like pizzas, pasta, curries and burgers are also on the menu at these laidback island spots.

For refined flavours and mood lighting, look no further than the Italian fare served at [Isola Bar e Cibo](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/isola-rottnest) or the South East Asian eats available at [Lontara](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/lontara). Both venues are fully enclosed and heated for optimum cosiness as you watch the waves lap the shores of Thomson Bay. [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest) also beckons with the warmth of underfloor heating and sheltered seating.

**Staying in:** Make the most of moody weather with a homemade meal. As rain softly taps the windows, slowly chop, stir and savour a night that demands nothing but your presence. Fresh, local ingredients can be picked up or ordered online from the General Store in the [main settlement](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) or from [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store).

### Reconnect by the fire

While away a cool night together beside flickering crimson flames. Clear nights call for cosying up by the outdoor fire pits at [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) or [Pinky’s Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island); beverage in one hand, your partner’s in the other. To make the evening sweeter still, ask the friendly staff at Pinky’s for a few complimentary marshmallows to roast.

The indoor fireplace will also be roaring at [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest), and at [Sunsets Bar & Dining](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/sunsets-rottnest). Grab a drink to wind down a day well spent together. When seated around a crackling fire, you can’t help but let intimate conversation flow.

### Bundle up indoors

Wrap yourself in blankets and beloved company at your [island accommodation](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay). Lay back and discuss the day over a shared drop of wine. Or take advantage of your time away from all responsibilities and languish in bed with a movie. Serene stays for two can be enjoyed at all island accommodation – after all, it’s who you’re with that makes the experience. But for those seeking a haven for deep relaxation, look to boutique offerings such as [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup). This accommodation offers a tranquil retreat alongside the peaceful, picturesque surrounds of Garden Lake. [Samphire Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/samphire-rottnest) is also a favourite for visiting couples, offering spacious and modern rooms in the coastal surrounds of Thomson Bay.

### Bust out a board game

Put the phones aside and stir up some good old-fashioned competitive spirit. Come prepared and bring a deck of cards, or there are board games available to buy at The General Store in the [main settlement](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/general-store) and at [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/geordie-bay-general-store). Spend hours tucked away indoors as you challenge each other to “just one more round”.

### Cosy up in front of a film

After a day exploring in the cool air, come and curl up in front of a good movie in the heritage-listed Picture Hall. [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf) run favourite films and brand-new blockbusters throughout the winter season for weary wanderers to while away an evening. Don’t forget to swing by the candy bar first for some warm, buttery popcorn!

### Still winter night stargazing

Head out hand-in-hand for a spot of stargazing in the sharp night air. Away from the strong city lights, the skies above Wadjemup sparkle on clear winter evenings. And the serenity of the cool season captures a sense of welcome isolation – you feel like you’re the only people around.

Simply step outside your accommodation to see the show or make an evening of it by setting up a spot at Vlamingh Lookout. Pack a thermos, park up and let all sense of time disappear into the inky skies as you take in each other’s company, and the natural wonder of Wadjemup in winter.

* 40 Ways to Spend Winter on Wadjemup

# 40 Ways to Spend Winter on Wadjemup

There’s no shortage of things to see and do on the island when the temperature dips. In fact, many unique seasonal experiences emerge.

5 minutes

Image Hike along the lakes

Hike along the lakes

**Embrace the cool change and all the opportunities to experience a different side of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island that come with it.****Here’s your guide to enjoying all that the island has to offer during winter:**

### First Things First

**1. Stay overnight:** With so much to see and do you may like to think about extending your visit and enjoying a [cosy night or two away](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay) from the mainland.

### Wildlife spotting

**2. Quokkas:** Cool weather increases [kwoka (quokka)](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas) activity and welcomes the arrival of quokka joeys. Visitors in August will delight in the sight of tiny joeys peeking out of their mothers’ pouches. Visit the best [quokka spotting locations](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-spotting-quokkas-on-rottnest-island).

**3. Whales:** Keep your eyes to the coastline! Sightings of these majestic creatures can begin as early as June, with migration season in full force from August. [Find where to spot them](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/whale-watching).

**4. Birds:** Winter rains bring bursting birdlife to the island, particularly around ngobar (coastal) areas and the balyan boodja (wetlands). [Discover the birds you may encounter](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching).

### Outdoor activities for all

**5. Hiking:** Take to the trails of the [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/winter-wonders-along-the-wadjemup-bidi) while the rejuvenating cooler days allow you to cover extra steps with ease.

**6. Coastal walks:** The [bays and beaches](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities) take on a lively energy during winter. Witness it for yourself on a wonderfully wind-swept walk.

**7. Cycling:** Without the intensity of the summer sun, [power your way](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/cycle-your-way-around-the-island) to the furthest reaches of the island your legs can take you.

**8. Fishing:** [Cast a line](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/fishing) and relish in the stillness as you anticipate your catch of the day.

**9. Surfing:** With multiple swell directions and strong conditions, the [island has breaks](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/surfing) to rival Margaret River without the hours spent driving to get there.

**10. Golf for big kids and little:** Bring your buddies for a [9-hole round](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-island-golf-course) surrounded by nature, or tackle the 18 thrilling holes of the [mini golf course](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf).

**11. Lawn bowls:** The golf course isn’t the only green that beckons; slip off your shoes and enjoy some casual competition on a clear day.

**12. Snorkelling and diving:** Appreciate the thrill of slipping into the [waters of Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/your-guide-to-snorkelling-the-warm-waters-of-wadjemup) in a wetsuit to see the tropical delights that lie beneath the waves.

**13. Pickleball:** Serve up some fun and discover the joy of [pickleball](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rotto-rackets-sports) at the Bathurst Point Tennis Courts, a sport suitable for all ages and abilities.

### Cosy indoor experiences

**14. Wander the museums:** Rain or shine, any day is ideal for immersing yourself in the culture and history housed at [Wadjemup Museum](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/wadjemup-museum) and [Pilot Boathouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pilot-boathouse).

**15. Get your game on:** Kids and kids at heart will be enticed by the bright lights and endless fun of the arcade at [Rottnest Movies & Mini Golf](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf).

**16. Savour winter dining:** With winter in full swing, indulge in seasonal menus and special dining experiences, from hearty Sunday roasts to exclusive wine-paired dinners, served across the island's [cafes and restaurants](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/eat-drink).

**17. Sip on mulled wine:** [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) will be serving up glasses of warming wine to enjoy around the outdoor firepits, in addition to their expansive drinks menu.

### Take a tour

**18. Cycling tours:** Take in the ever-changing island views as you pedal. Take it easy with [Paul's Eco E-Bike tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/paul-s-eco-e-bike-tours) for a cruisey guided journey.

**19. Bus tours:** Appreciate the island scenery while staying cosy, as you cover major habitats from the [comfort of your seat](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bus) with commentary along the way.

**20. Quokka Coaches Island Explorer hop-on-hop-off bus:** Explore at your own pace with this [shuttle service](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) that stops at 19 different locations around the island.

**21. Wadjemup Lighthouse tour:** Join the Rottnest Voluntary Guides and ascend this [iconic structure](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) together, listening to tales along the way.

**22. Oliver Hill Gun & Tunnels tour:** The Rottnest Voluntary Guides also run tours that take you underground to learn about the [island’s intricate military history](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill).

**23. Train tour:** Pair your Oliver Hill visit with a trip on the [Captain Hussey train](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/captain-hussey-historical-train-tour), which takes you from the settlement to this historic site and back again.

**24. Scenic flight tours:** Take to the skies with [Rottnest Air-Taxi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-air-taxi) for unparalleled views of the island and all that surrounds, including migrating whales (for lucky travellers).

**25. Segway Tours WA:**Glide around to areas you’re yet to discover on a [scenic tour or off-road experience](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/segway-tours-wa).

**26. Free walking tours:** These [free guided tours](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours) are run by the Rottnest Voluntary Guides daily (weather permitting), and detail the wildlife, heritage, and sustainability of the island.

### Discover Aboriginal History

**27. Go Cultural Aboriginal Tours & Experiences walking tour:** Join Noongar guide, Walter McGuire, on an [award-winning walking tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/go-cultural-aboriginal-tours-experiences) and heighten your understanding of Wadjemup and its history.

**28. Koorda's Crew Tours and Workshops:** Give the kids an opportunity to [explore Wadjemup's Aboriginal culture](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/koorda) through stories, hands-on fun, and imagination.

**29. Mirliny Cultural Yarning Experience:** Join a [yarning circle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mirliny-cultural-yarning-experience) to learn about Noongar Creation Stories and the Noongar six seasons.

**30. Dooga Waalitj Healing Cultural Experiences:** Discover the heart and spirit of Wadjemup with [Aboriginal guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/dooga-waalitj-healing-cultural-experiences) who share culture, history, and stories of truth and reconciliation.

### Natural winter wonders

**31. Observe the full salt lakes:** Bask in the beauty of the [kabikarning (salt lake) systems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) after the winter rains as they transition to richer hues.

**32. Head to a lookout:** Let the landscape unfold below and beyond you from one of the island’s [main vantage points](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-top-five-lookouts-on-wadjemup-rottnest-island).

**33. Visit the West End:** The [most western point of the island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) is a haven for [winter wildlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/uniquely-winter-wildlife-experiences-on-wadjemup), including birds, migrating whales and long-nosed fur seals. Wander the boardwalk and pause at the lookouts for the best vantage points for wildlife spotting.

**34. Marvel at a sunset:** Embrace the end of a winter day and [watch the sun slip](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/the-best-sunset-locations-on-rottnest-island) below the Indian Ocean horizon before you return home. Or extend your stay to enjoy the experience in unhurried glory.

### For the Stay-Overs

**35. Indulge in a massage:** Unwind in your accommodation with a massage from the relaxation experts at [Mobile Massage on Rottnest Island by Golden Bees](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/mobile-massage-on-rottnest-island-by-golden-bees).

**36. Watch a movie:** Rug up with warm, buttery popcorn and a blockbuster in the heritage-listed Picture Hall at [Rottnest Movies](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/rottnest-movies-mini-golf).

**37. Swap stories by the fire:** The flames will be dancing and crackling into the evenings inside [Hotel Rottnest](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/hotel-rottnest) and [The Lodge Wadjemup](https://www.rottnestisland.com/stay/accommodation/the-lodge-wadjemup) as well as in the outdoor firepits outside [Bayside Bar](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/bayside-bar) and [Pinky's Rottnest Island](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/hire/pinkys-rottnest-island).

**38. Spend the night in:** Make the most of your accommodation by cooking a hearty meal or having a takeaway, busting out a board game and enjoying the company of your people.

**39. Stargaze:** Wander out into the crisp night air and peer up into a star-speckled sky. The glow of each star burns brightly without the competition of city lights. Remember to take a torch!

**40. Catch a sunrise:** Watch the magic that unfolds across the morning sky before you make your way back to the mainland with a sense of renewed energy.

# Experience the Northern Beaches on the Karlinyah Bidi

### Follow the scenic trail along Wadjemup’s northern coast

The Karlinyah Bidi meanders along Wadjemup / Rottnest Island’s northern coastline.

Discover beautiful beaches with powdery white sand, and calm, blue, lagoon-like beaches hidden away from the busier bathing spots. While only 5.7 km one-way, the Karlinyah Bidi features some of the more rugged conditions on the Wadjemup Bidi, making it a must-do trail for keen hikers. Depending on your experience and the prevailing conditions, it can take anywhere between one and three hours — so plan accordingly.

Winding its way from [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), and ending at Narrow Neck, the Karlinyah Bidi is for those looking to discover a diversity of terrain and scenery. Feel grounded in the island, and connected with the land. Cutting inland from Little Parakeet Bay, hikers are treated to spectacular views of Lake Baghdad and Lake Vincent [salt lakes](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) before reaching the coast again. [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay) provides a calm resting stop, shielded from the southerly winds.

Curving down past Catherine Bay and [City of York Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/city-of-york-bay), the trail then leads to [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach). But be aware: here it delivers some of the most rugged hiking conditions on the island. During the stormy seasons, it’s recommended to avoid the trail completely and walk along the paved road instead. But the challenging landscape gives way to exceptional scenery around the water’s edge at Stark Bay, where you can gaze out to the horizon and watch the sun as it dips towards the rolling surf.

The trail ends at Narrow Neck — what happens next is up to you. Choose to continue on to explore Wadjemup’s West End, or if you’re feeling energetic, you can take up your next leg of the Wadjemup Bidi on the Wardan Nara Bidi.

### Where to start the Karlinyah Bidi

The Karlinyah Bidi can be walked both ways, both east to west and west to east. Starting at [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay) trailhead, it takes hikers around the northern beaches, arriving at Narrow Neck. To begin your Karlinyah Bidi journey, simply take the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer bus](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and get off at Stop 18. The hike finishes near the [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay) bus stop, Stop 13.

### Explore the Karlinyah Bidi with Smartreka Digital Maps

Embark on your adventure with confidence using the WA Parks Foundation’s Smartreka digital maps, your guide to exploring the stunning Wadjemup Bidi trails.

With your smartphone’s built-in GPS, Smartreka maps display your real-time location, making it easy to navigate the island’s diverse landscapes. These interactive maps also highlight key features along the way, including trail access points, scenic lookouts, cultural landmarks, and essential amenities.

Whether you're a first-time visitor or a seasoned explorer, let Smartreka help you make the most of your Wadjemup Bidi hiking experience.

### Frequently Asked Questions

What do I need to bring on this hike?

The Karlinyah Bidi gives hikers an experience of Wadjemup at its most rugged, so make sure you wear some robust hiking boots. Bring at least two litres of water, and always wear a hat and sunscreen.

How difficult is the Karlinyah Bidi?

The Karlinyah Bidi covers some of the most challenging terrain on Wadjemup for hikers to experience. Rough surfaces, beach walking, and some steep climbs await you, so it’s recommended to have some bushwalking experience first before trying the Karlinyah Bidi.

Are there any toilets or facilities on the trail?

Despite crossing some tricky ground, hikers on the Karlinyah Bidi can find toilets at City of York Bay, Stark Bay, and Narrow Neck. Fill up your water bottles at Geordie Bay before you leave though, as no water is available on the trail.

Some rubbish bins can be found at bus stops along the way, but it's best to take all your rubbish and recycling with you, and leave no trace upon the trail.

# Wadjemup Lighthouse

### Wadjemup Lighthouse has seen a lot in its lifetime

An integral part of Wadjemup’s maritime history, the Wadjemup Lighthouse was constructed in 1896 at the highest point on the island, as a safeguard against nautical disasters that were, at the time, all too common.

Built to replace the original stone lighthouse that stood in its place, at an impressive 38 metres tall it’s the fourth tallest lighthouse of its kind in Australia.

This taller, more advanced lighthouse ushered in a new age of technology to the island. Featuring a new holophotal revolving light that flashed every 20 seconds, it provided better navigation for passing ships, and helped to reduce the number of vessels that ran aground on the coral shores.

It was connected to electricity in 1936, but it wasn’t until 1990 that it became fully automatic.

With a newer, brighter light, and a range of 26 nautical miles, Wadjemup Lighthouse is still a crucial beacon that helps vessels safely navigate their way towards Fremantle port.

### Where to find Wadjemup Lighthouse

Located at the centre of the island, you can reach the [Wadjemup Lighthouse](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse) on two wheels. ### Climb Wadjemup Lighthouse and experience the inner workings for yourself

Visitors to Rottnest Island have the unique chance to take a guided tour inside Wadjemup Lighthouse.

Climb the tight spiralling staircase, up 155 stairs, as your guide from the Rottnest Island Voluntary Guides Association teaches you about what goes on inside a real working lighthouse. The tour takes you all the way to the top, where you can experience 360-degree views out over the island. Stand at the highest point on Wadjemup; experience the winds whipping across the viewing platform, and gaze in awe at the Indian Ocean that sprawls in every direction.

It’s a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity—one that’s not for the faint-hearted.

[Learn more about the Wadjemup Lighthouse Tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/book-your-trip/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour)

### Frequently Asked Questions

Are the lighthouses on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island operational?

Yes, both lighthouses are operational, and serve an important purpose helping ships safely navigate the waters around Wadjemup. When the sun goes down, you can watch as the lights flash out from each location.

Can I climb the lighthouses?

Bathurst Lighthouse isn’t open to visitors, but visitors can explore Wadjemup Lighthouse on a [guided tour](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/wadjemup-lighthouse-tour). Here you can discover what goes on within the walls of a real working lighthouse. Climb the stairs, making your way to the top to experience breathtaking 360-degree views.

Are there accessible facilities at the lighthouses?

Disabled access is available to get up close to both lighthouses, however no accessible facilities are available inside.

### Before Wadjemup Lighthouse

The current Wadjemup Lighthouse isn’t the first structure to stand where it is now. Constructed on the island in 1842 and completed in 1851, the original lighthouse was a much smaller building. Recognised as the first stone lighthouse constructed and lit in Western Australia, it stood 16 metres tall — half the size of the current lighthouse.

It was built to help the burgeoning Swan River Colony, providing safe passage for vessels travelling past Rottnest Island and into Fremantle Port.

But despite its guiding light, seven ships were wrecked on the reefs around the island between 1878 and 1891 — a clear sign that a taller, more visible lighthouse was needed.

A small square building at the base of Wadjemup Lighthouse is all that remains of the original structure. It provides remembrance not just for the lives lost at sea, but also of the burden carried by the Noongar prisoners incarcerated on the island who were used as labour to build the new structure.

Now, Wadjemup Lighthouse provides a dramatic backdrop to stop and reconnect with the other stories of the island, and a stark reminder of Wadjemup’s chequered past.

# Your guide to hiking the Wadjemup Bidi

Walk along the Wadjemup Bidi and connect to the native environment that surrounds you.

5 minutes

Image Hiking trail

Hiking trail

**Whilst you’ve probably heard of cycling around Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, another amazing way to experience the island is by foot. Rottnest Island has an island-wide network of walk trails that make up the incredible Wadjemup Bidi.**

The [Wadjemup Bidi](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/hiking-the-wadjemup-bidi) is a series of walk trails that take in the spectacular coastal headlands, stunning inland lakes and breathtaking attractions all over the island. The 45 km trail is made up of five sections, with each unique section displaying culturally and environmentally significant landmarks.

> The name for the island in the Noongar language is Wadjemup , which means ‘place across the water where the spirits are’. ‘Bidi’ in Noongar means ‘trail’ or ‘track’.

These connected walk trails allow you to traverse the island either in separate stages, or if you’re keen for an epic adventure, as a whole. The entire trail is 45 km, so you’ll need to spread your hike over a few days if you want to do the whole thing. There are five sections, so you can also just choose to do one or two walks during your time on the island.

### Discover the Salt Lakes on the Gabbi Karniny Bidi

Distance: 9.5 km loop / 3-4 hours

Where to start: [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay)

#### Highlights

* Lakes system
* Migratory birdlife
* Ocean views
* Stunning beaches

This beautiful walk trail meanders through the [lake systems](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/lakes-salt-lakes) and back along the northern coastline — offering you a taste of everything Rottnest Island has to offer. Check out Vlamingh Lookout for some of the best views of the island.  As you wander through the beautiful inland lake systems keeping your eyes peeled for seasonal [migratory birdlife](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/activities/Bird-Watching) and of course, [quokkas](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/quokkas). Don’t miss a stroll along the lakes boardwalk which provides the facade of “walking on water”. Head back along the coast passing [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay), [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), [The Basin](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/the-basin) and [Pinky Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/pinky-beach) before arriving back at the [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) settlement.

### Experience the Northern Beaches on the Karlinyah Bidi

Distance: 5.7 km one way / 2-3 hours

Where to start: [Little Parakeet Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-parakeet-bay) (stop 18) or [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay) (stop 13)

#### Highlights:

* Spectacular coastline
* Native wildlife
* Beautiful beaches

This spectacular trail strolls past beautiful sandy beaches, calm swimming lagoons and eventually, more rugged, wild parts of the island. You’ll traverse the northern coastline, passing incredible beaches like [Little Armstrong Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/little-armstrong-bay) and Catherine Bay. Stop at [City of York](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/city-of-york-bay) to learn about the shipwreck, and then take in the serrated reef that was the cause of its destruction. Carry on past [Ricey Beach](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/ricey-beach), past the gorgeous Stark Bay and finish your hike at [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay).

### Explore West End on the Ngank Wen Bidi

Where to start: Narrow Neck (stop 13)

Distance: 7.8 km loop / 3-4 hours

#### Highlights:

* Rugged and unspoilt coastline
* Vantage point for spotting marine life

This loop trail circumnavigates the spectacular [West End](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/wildlife-nature/west-end) of the island. The trail links Narrow Neck and Cape Vlamingh, the more remote and rugged section of the island. Enjoy secluded beaches like Marjorie Bay and Mabel Cove before arriving at Cathedral Rocks where you can spot our resident long-nosed fur seals from the viewing platform. Stop and admire the waves crashing through the natural arch at Cape Vlamingh and keep your eyes peeled for humpback whales and eagles overhead.

### Relax on Salmon Bay along the Wardan Nara Bidi

Distance: 9.8 km one way / 3-4 hours

Where to start: [Rocky Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/rocky-bay) (stop 13) or Porpoise Bay (stop 4)

#### Highlights:

* Salmon Bay
* WWII gun and tunnels
* Wadjemup Lighthouse

This beautiful trail offers the best of both worlds, taking you from the stunning coastline of Salmon Bay and [Parker Point](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/parker-point) through to the middle of the island to explore the [WWII gun and tunnels](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill). Admire the huge osprey stack at Salmon Point and keep your eyes peeled for our resident osprey. Enjoy incredible views from the Wadjemup Lighthouse and traverse your way back past the world-class surf breaks at [Strickland Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/strickland-bay). Don’t miss Peter Farmer’s Mammong Dreaming sculpture and listen to the story told by Traditional Owner Kerri Anne Winmar via the audio sign.

### Uncover Bickley Battery on the Ngank Yira Bidi

Distance: 10 km one way / 3-4 hours

Where to start: [Thomson Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/thomson-bay) or [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill)

#### Highlights:

* Coastal views
* Bickley Battery
* Train ride back to the settlement

Start at the settlement and head out towards the south east corner of the island. As you walk this trail, you’ll enjoy impressive ocean, coastal and inland views, as well interpretive signage teaching you about the history of Wadjemup.  Enjoy panoramic views from the Jubilee Observation Post and don’t miss “Beachcomber”, the first sculpture installation on the island, made from 80 percent recycled material. This historic trail will take you to [Oliver Hill](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/oliver-hill) to explore the remnants of coastal defence systems installed during WWII. Enjoy a guided tour if you want to know more, and for an extra adventure, head back to the settlement on the train.

[Beware of Snakes

Be aware there are venomous snakes on Wadjemup / Rottnest Island. The dugite is a timid creature, but may bite if harassed. If bitten, seek immediate medical assistance.](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/guides-tips/practical-tips)

### Guided walking tours

If you’re not sure where to start or like the sound of expert commentary paired with your scenic walk, why not join a guided tour with [The Hike Collective](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/the-hike-collective)? Their knowledgeable guides will show you the best of the Wadjemup Bidi in an engaging and relaxed group setting. With multiple tours to choose from, including overnight retreats, it’s the perfect adventure for both hiking enthusiasts and beginners alike.

For those who prefer a self-guided experience, [Smartreka](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/shopping-services/smartreka-digital-maps) offers an innovative way to explore the island at your own pace. Using your smartphone’s built-in GPS capability, you'll be able to see your real-time location plotted on the Smartreka maps, making it easy to navigate the island’s landscapes. You can learn more about Smartreka and how to use it here.

If you’re looking to learn more about different areas of the island, you can also join a free walking tour with the [Rottnest Voluntary Guides](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/rottnest-volunteer-guides-walking-tours). Whether you're keen to meet the wildlife or discover more about the history of the island, you’re sure to find a tour and passionate guide to suit your interests. The tours are run regularly throughout most days and are a great addition to a day trip or to enhance an extended stay. For more information, pop in to say hello to the friendly guides at the Information Booth in the main settlement.

# Fay's Bay

## Breathe in the tranquillity

A small cove at the northernmost tip of Wadjemup / Rottnest Island, what Fay’s Bay lacks in size it makes up for in its beauty. A stretch of soft white sand nestles between high limestone rock outcrops, providing shelter against gusty winds and rougher waters. Wade into the water where the calmer, shallow seabed creates an exceptional family swimming spot. Look further out across the bay, and enjoy stunning blue water that wouldn’t be out of place on any famous tropical island.

Just east of the busier [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), Fay’s Bay is a great little spot to get off the beaten track — but still be close to the gentle hum of activity.

### Look around and discover...

Image 

Glittering blue water

Image 

Soft white sand

Image 

Bright green seagrass beds

Image 

Delightful family snorkelling

### Where to find Fay’s Bay

You can get to Fay’s Bay by foot or by bike. Just minutes from [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), it’s an easy 30-minute [stroll](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-foot) through the centre of the island from Thomson Bay settlement, and less than ten minutes [on a bicycle](https://www.rottnestisland.com/visit/getting-around/by-bike). Or jump aboard the [Quokka Coaches Island Explorer](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/culture-history/quokka-coaches-bus-tour) and hop off at Stop 19, with a short walk to the bay.

Image Snorkelling, Rocky Bay

[Snorkelling](/see-do/beaches-water-activities/snorkelling-diving)

### Discover a different world under the waves

Fay’s Bay is home to rich green seagrass beds, which are able to thrive, safe and protected by a shallow limestone reef. The reef is riddled with caves and channels, providing a twisting, turning playground for schools of colourful fish and sea life.

The calmer waters make it ideal for beginner snorkellers.

So bring your towel and picnic blanket, and set up for the day. Wade out into the cool depths, dive under the shimmering surface, and explore the underwater world of Wadjemup.

[Learn more about snorkelling](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/Snorkelling-Diving)

### Frequently Asked Questions

What facilities are nearby Fay’s Bay?

There are no facilities located at Fay’s Bay, but the Geordie Bay facilities are just a few minutes’ walk away.

Are there accessible facilities at Fay’s Bay?

No, there are no accessible facilities at Fay’s Bay.

Is fishing allowed?

Yes, fishing is allowed at Fay’s Bay. But be sure to stick to local fishing regulations.

What makes Fays Bay a good all-round beach choice on Rottnest Island?

Fay’s Bay is a good all-round beach choice because it brings together calm water, soft white sand and beginner-friendly snorkelling in a small, sheltered cove. It feels quieter than nearby [Geordie Bay](https://www.rottnestisland.com/see-do/beaches-water-activities/geordie-bay), while still being only a short walk from its facilities.
